name: 3/4 Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up that stops about three quarters of the way up, so the abs stay loaded the whole set instead of resting at the top. It mainly works the abs, with help from the hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your arms over your chest or rest your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and curl your head, shoulders and then your back off the floor.
Stop when your torso is about three quarters of the way to upright, before you reach full sitting.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly until your shoulder blades touch the floor, then go again.

name: 45° Side Bend
desc: A side bend done lying sideways on a 45-degree back extension bench, which lets the side of the waist lift the body against gravity. It works the obliques and the rest of the abs.
ins: Set yourself sideways on a 45-degree back extension bench, hip on the pad and feet locked under the foot rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest or put your hands lightly behind your head.
Keeping your body in a straight line, lower your upper body toward the floor by bending at the side of your waist.
Breathe out and lift your torso sideways as high as you can by squeezing the side of your waist.
Do all your reps on one side, then turn over and work the other side.

name: Ab Wheel
desc: An advanced core exercise where you roll an ab wheel forward from your knees and pull it back. It hits the abs hard and also works the lower back to keep your spine steady.
ins: Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel handles with the wheel on the floor under your shoulders.
Tighten your abs and tuck your hips slightly so your lower back stays flat.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, letting your hips and chest move toward the floor as far as you can control.
Stop before your lower back starts to sag, breathing in on the way out.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees using your abs, breathing out as you return.

name: Air Bike
desc: A bodyweight ab move where you pedal your legs while turning your torso so each elbow meets the opposite knee. It trains the abs and obliques, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and lift your shoulders and feet off the floor.
Bend one knee toward your chest while the other leg stretches out just above the floor.
Turn your upper body so the opposite elbow moves toward the bent knee.
Switch legs in a smooth pedaling motion and turn to the other side.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor and breathe out on each twist.

name: All Fours Squad Stretch
desc: A quad stretch done from hands and knees, reaching back to pull one foot toward the glutes. It stretches the front of the thigh and the hip, with light work for the hamstrings and glutes.
ins: Start on your hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Shift your weight onto your left hand and right knee.
Bend your left knee and reach back with your right hand to hold your left foot.
Gently pull the heel toward your glutes until you feel the stretch along the front of the thigh.
Keep your stomach tight so your lower back does not sag, and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Release slowly and switch sides.

name: Alternate Heel Touchers
desc: A lying side-to-side reach where you tap each heel with the hand on the same side. It targets the obliques and keeps the abs working throughout.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat, a little wider than hip width.
Lift your head and shoulders slightly off the floor and let your arms reach long by your sides.
Crunch sideways to tap your right heel with your right hand.
Come back to the middle and crunch to the left to tap your left heel.
Keep your shoulders off the floor the whole set and breathe steadily.

name: Alternate Lateral Pulldown
desc: A lat pulldown done one arm at a time on a cable station with two handles, so each side of the back works on its own. It builds the lats and also works the biceps and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Clip a single handle to each high cable, sit facing the machine and lock your thighs under the pads.
Take one handle in each hand with your arms reaching up and your chest tall.
Pull one elbow down to the side of your ribs while the other arm stays long overhead.
Squeeze your back at the bottom, then let that arm rise slowly under control.
Pull the other arm down the same way and keep switching sides.
Breathe out as you pull and breathe in as the handle goes back up.

name: Ankle Circles
desc: A simple mobility drill where you draw slow circles with your foot. It loosens the ankle joint and warms up the calves and the small muscles that stabilize the ankle.
ins: Sit on a chair or stand holding a wall, and lift one foot off the floor.
Point your toes and slowly draw a big circle with your foot, moving only at the ankle.
Make 10 circles clockwise.
Reverse and make 10 circles counterclockwise.
Keep your leg still and breathe normally.
Switch to the other foot.

name: Ankle Dorsal Flexion
desc: A rehab exercise that pulls the top of the foot up toward the shin. It strengthens the muscles on the front of the lower leg and helps prevent tripping and shin pain.
ins: Sit on a chair or on the floor with your leg straight and your heel resting on the ground.
Relax your foot so the toes point slightly away.
Pull your toes and the top of your foot up toward your shin as far as you can.
Hold for 2 to 3 seconds and feel the front of your lower leg working.
Lower the foot slowly and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Archer Pull Up
desc: An advanced pull-up where you pull toward one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight. It moves you toward a one-arm pull-up by loading one side much more.
ins: Hang from the bar with a very wide overhand grip.
Pull yourself up toward your right hand, bending that arm while the left arm straightens along the bar.
Bring your chin over your right hand and breathe out.
Lower slowly back to the centre hang.
Pull toward the left hand on the next rep and keep alternating.

name: Archer Push Up
desc: An advanced push-up where you lower toward one hand while the other arm slides out straight to the side. It loads one side of the chest and triceps heavily and is a step toward the one-arm push-up.
ins: Set your hands on the floor about twice shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing slightly out, and step back into a push-up position.
Breathe in and bend one elbow to lower your chest toward that hand, keeping the other arm straight.
Shift your weight onto the bent arm while the straight arm only helps with balance.
Breathe out and push back up to the middle.
Alternate sides each rep, or do all reps on one side before switching.
Keep your hips level with your shoulders and avoid twisting.

name: Arm Slingers Hanging Bent Knee Legs
desc: A bent-knee raise done hanging from a pull-up bar with your upper arms resting in padded ab slings. It is an easier version of the straight-leg raise that builds the abs, with the shoulders and back keeping you stable.
ins: Hang a pair of ab slings from a pull-up bar and rest your upper arms in them, elbows bent.
Let your legs hang down and tighten your abs to stop any swinging.
Breathe out and draw your knees up toward your chest, letting your hips curl up slightly at the top.
Pause briefly with your abs squeezed.
Breathe in and lower your legs slowly until they hang straight again.

name: Arm Slingers Hanging Straight Legs
desc: A straight-leg raise done hanging from a pull-up bar with your upper arms supported in padded ab slings. The slings take the load off your grip so the abs can lift your legs, with the shoulders and back holding you steady.
ins: Hook a pair of ab slings on a pull-up bar, slide your arms through and rest your upper arms in them with your elbows bent.
Let your legs hang straight and still, and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs in front of you until they are level with the floor or a little higher.
Avoid swinging; use your abs to do the lift, not momentum.
Breathe in and lower your legs slowly back to a straight hang.

name: Arms Apart Circular Toe Touch
desc: A dynamic toe-touch drill in which you swing wide-open arms in a big circle down to your feet and back up. It loosens the hamstrings, glutes and lower back and challenges balance as the body moves through a large range.
ins: Stand with feet a bit wider than hip-width and your arms spread out to the sides.
Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, sweeping your arms down in a wide arc.
Touch your toes or shins with both hands at the bottom.
Breathe in and continue the circle, sweeping the arms out and up as you rise.
Finish with your arms overhead, then flow straight into the next rep, changing the direction of the circle halfway through.

name: Arms Overhead Full Sit-Up
desc: A full sit-up started with your arms stretched overhead, which lengthens the lever and makes the abs work harder all the way up. The hip flexors and lower back also help control the movement.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat, and your arms straight on the floor above your head.
Tighten your abs and lift your arms slightly off the floor.
Breathe out and swing your arms forward as you curl all the way up until your chest is over your thighs.
Keep your feet on the floor and avoid jerking your head.
Breathe in and roll down slowly, returning your arms overhead.

name: Assisted Chest Dip (kneeling)
desc: A dip done on an assisted dip machine while kneeling on a padded platform that takes part of your body weight. It builds the chest and triceps and is a good stepping stone toward full bodyweight dips.
ins: Pick an assistance level, step up and kneel on the pad, then grip the dip handles with straight arms.
Lean your chest slightly forward and let your elbows point a little out to the sides.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and rise back to the top.
Breathe in on the way down and out as you push up.

name: Assisted Chin Tuck
desc: A chin tuck guided by your fingers on the chin, which helps you feel the correct straight-back motion. It is a gentle way to start training neck posture.
ins: Sit or stand tall and place two fingers on the front of your chin.
Use the fingers to press your chin gently straight back while keeping your eyes forward.
Let your neck muscles do most of the work; the fingers only guide.
Hold the tucked position for 3 to 5 seconds and keep breathing.
Release slowly and repeat.

name: Assisted Hanging Knee Raise
desc: A hanging knee raise done with your arms supported in ab straps, so grip is not the limit. It works the lower part of the abs and the hip flexors.
ins: Hang from a bar with your upper arms resting in ab straps and your legs straight down.
Brace your abs and keep your body still.
Breathe out and draw your knees up toward your chest, tilting your pelvis up slightly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly until they are straight again without swinging.

name: Assisted Hanging Knee Raise With Throw Down
desc: An advanced hanging knee raise where a partner pushes your legs back down after each rep and you stop them with your abs. The arm straps support your upper body so the work goes into the abs and hip flexors.
ins: Hang from a bar with your upper arms resting in ab straps and a partner standing in front of you.
Brace your abs and pull your knees up toward your chest.
At the top, let your partner push your legs firmly back down and forward.
Fight the push with your abs, stop your legs before they swing behind you, and pull them straight back up.
Keep your body from swinging and breathe out each time you lift.

name: Assisted Lying Calves Stretch
desc: A calf stretch done lying on your back, using a towel or strap to pull the foot toward you. It is gentle on the back and also stretches the hamstring.
ins: Lie on your back with both legs straight and loop a towel around the ball of one foot.
Hold the ends of the towel and raise that leg as high as it goes while keeping the knee straight.
Pull the towel gently so your toes come down toward your face.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds and breathe slowly.
Lower the leg and repeat on the other side.

name: Assisted Lying Glutes Stretch
desc: A lying glute stretch where a partner helps press the bent leg toward your chest. The extra help lets you relax fully, which deepens the stretch in the glutes and eases the hamstrings.
ins: Lie on your back and bend your right knee, keeping the left leg straight on the floor.
Your partner kneels beside you and places one hand on your right knee and one on your right shin.
Relax and let your partner slowly push the knee toward your chest and slightly across toward your left shoulder.
Tell your partner to stop as soon as you feel a strong but comfortable stretch in the right glute.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.

name: Assisted Lying Gluteus And Piriformis Stretch
desc: A partner-assisted lying stretch in a figure-four position, aimed at the glutes and the deep piriformis muscle under them. It is useful when the hips feel tight or the buttock area feels stiff after sitting.
ins: Lie on your back, bend both knees and cross your right ankle over your left knee.
Your partner kneels at your feet and holds your left shin and your right knee.
Your partner slowly pushes your left knee toward your chest, which lifts the crossed leg with it.
They can gently press your right knee outward to deepen the stretch in the right glute.
Keep breathing and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then change sides.

name: Assisted Lying Leg Raise With Lateral Throw Down
desc: A partner-assisted leg raise where your partner pushes your raised legs down toward one side and you stop and lift them back. It trains the abs and obliques along with the hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your head near a standing partner's feet and hold their ankles.
Keeping your legs together and straight, raise them up toward your partner's hands.
Let your partner push your legs down and off to one side.
Brace your abs and obliques, stop your legs before they touch the floor, then lift them straight back up.
Alternate the side your partner pushes toward and keep your lower back pressed down.

name: Assisted Lying Leg Raise With Throw Down
desc: A partner-assisted leg raise where your partner throws your legs straight back toward the floor and you stop them with your abs. It builds strong lower-ab control with help from the hip flexors and quads.
ins: Lie on your back with your head near a standing partner's feet and hold their ankles.
Raise your straight legs together until they reach your partner's hands.
Let your partner push your legs straight down toward the floor.
Brace hard, stop your legs a few centimeters above the floor, and bring them back up.
Keep your lower back flat on the floor; if it arches, ask for a lighter push.

name: Assisted Motion Russian Twist
desc: A beginner-friendly Russian twist with a medicine ball, done with your feet on the floor for support. It trains the obliques and abs while the lower back holds your posture.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, heels down, and a medicine ball held at your chest.
Lean back a little with a long, straight spine until you feel your abs switch on.
Turn your shoulders to the right and bring the ball beside your right hip.
Turn back through the middle and take the ball to your left hip.
Let your shoulders lead the turn, not just your arms, and breathe out on each side.

name: Assisted Parallel Close Grip Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up on an assisted machine using the close parallel handles, with a counterweight taking off part of your body weight. It trains the lats, biceps and grip while you build up to full pull-ups.
ins: Set the assistance weight, step onto the platform and kneel on the pad.
Hold the close parallel handles with your palms facing each other.
Start from straight arms with your shoulders pulled slightly down.
Pull your chest up toward the handles, driving your elbows down beside your body.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight again.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Assisted Prone Hamstring
desc: A partner-assisted hamstring curl done lying face down, where a training partner gives light resistance at your ankles instead of a machine. It strengthens the hamstrings and also works the glutes and lower back that keep your hips steady.
ins: Lie face down on a mat with your legs straight and your forehead resting on your hands.
Have your partner kneel at your feet and place their hands on the backs of your ankles.
Bend your knees and pull your heels toward your glutes while your partner pushes back gently.
Keep your hips pressed into the mat the whole time; do not let them lift.
Straighten your legs slowly while your partner keeps a steady, light pressure.
Breathe out as you curl and breathe in as you lower.

name: Assisted Prone Lying Quads Stretch
desc: A partner-assisted quad stretch done lying face down, with the partner bending your knee to bring the heel toward your glutes. It stretches the front of the thigh while you stay completely relaxed.
ins: Lie face down with your legs straight and your forehead resting on your hands.
Your partner kneels beside you and holds your right ankle.
Your partner slowly bends your right knee, bringing the heel toward your glutes.
Keep your hips pressed into the floor and tell your partner when the stretch feels strong but comfortable.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch legs.

name: Assisted Prone Rectus Femoris Stretch
desc: A face-down stretch for the front of the thigh, using a strap, towel or partner to help draw your heel toward your glutes. It targets the long quad muscle that also crosses the front of the hip.
ins: Lie face down with your legs straight and loop a strap or towel around one ankle, or have a partner hold it.
Bend that knee and gently pull your heel toward your glutes.
Press your hips into the floor and keep your knees close together so the stretch stays in the front of the thigh.
Hold for about 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and relaxing into the stretch.
Release gently and repeat on the other leg.

name: Assisted Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up done on a machine that supports part of your body weight, letting you practise the full movement with good form. It strengthens the lats, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Choose the assistance weight and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grip the top handles a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Hang with straight arms and tighten your stomach.
Pull up until your chin passes the handles, thinking of bringing your elbows to your hips.
Come down slowly to a full hang without letting the platform drop you.
Use less assistance over time as you get stronger.

name: Assisted Seated Pectoralis Major Stretch With Stability Ball
desc: A partner-assisted chest stretch done sitting on an exercise ball: a partner gently draws your elbows back to open the chest and the front of the shoulders.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with your feet flat and lace your fingers behind your head.
Have a partner stand behind you and hold the inside of your elbows.
Breathe out as your partner slowly draws your elbows back until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Keep your back upright and your ribs down; tell your partner to stop at a mild, comfortable stretch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then have your partner release gently.

name: Assisted Side Lying Adductor Stretch
desc: A partner-assisted stretch for the inner thigh done while lying on your side, with the partner supporting and lowering the top leg. It loosens the adductors and puts some light stretch on the hamstrings and glutes.
ins: Lie on your side with both legs straight, resting your head on your lower arm.
Your partner stands behind you and holds your top leg under the knee and ankle.
Your partner lifts the top leg up and slightly back while you keep your hips stacked.
Relax the leg fully and tell your partner when you feel the stretch along the inner thigh.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds with slow breaths, then turn over and repeat on the other leg.

name: Assisted Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up with your feet held down by a partner or tucked under a fixed pad, which makes it easier to come all the way up. It builds the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet held by a partner or hooked under a fixed pad.
Cross your arms over your chest or rest your fingertips by your ears.
Tighten your abs, breathe out and curl up until your chest is close to your thighs.
Lead with your chest rather than pulling on your head.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly, letting your back touch the floor bit by bit.

name: Assisted Standing Chin-Up
desc: A chin-up on an assisted machine, where a counterweight takes off part of your body weight. It lets beginners build the lats and biceps through the full movement.
ins: Choose the assistance weight; more weight makes it easier.
Step up and kneel or stand on the platform, then grip the handles with palms facing you.
Start with your arms straight and your shoulders pulled down.
Breathe out and pull until your chin is above the handles.
Lower slowly to straight arms before the next rep.

name: Assisted Standing Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up on an assisted machine with an overhand grip. The counterweight makes it possible for beginners to train the lats through a full range.
ins: Set the assistance weight to a level that lets you do clean reps.
Step onto the platform and take the handles with your palms facing away.
Hang with straight arms and pull your shoulders down.
Breathe out and pull up until your chin clears the handles.
Lower under control, then reduce the assistance as you get stronger.

name: Assisted Standing Triceps Extension (with Towel)
desc: A no-equipment overhead triceps extension where one hand straightens the arm behind your head while the other hand pulls a towel to add resistance. It builds the triceps and is handy for home or travel training.
ins: Stand tall and hold one end of a towel in your right hand with that elbow bent and pointing up beside your head.
Reach your left hand behind your lower back and grab the other end of the towel.
Breathe out and straighten your right arm toward the ceiling while your left hand pulls down to resist.
Keep the right elbow close to your ear and stop when the arm is straight.
Let the right hand sink back behind your head under control while the left hand keeps the towel tight.
Finish your reps, then switch the hand positions.

name: Assisted Wide-Grip Chest Dip (kneeling)
desc: A wide-grip chest dip on an assisted dip machine, kneeling on a pad that pushes up and takes away part of your body weight. It lets beginners learn the dip while working the chest, triceps and shoulders.
ins: Choose the assistance weight; more weight means more help.
Grip the wide dip handles and place your knees on the pad one at a time until you are supported on straight arms.
Lean your chest forward slightly and keep your shoulders down.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower yourself until your upper arms are about level with the handles.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms.
Step off carefully one knee at a time when you finish.

name: Astride Jumps
desc: A jumping drill that lands with the feet wide apart and then jumps them back together. It is simple cardio that works the legs and calves.
ins: Stand with your feet together and hands on your hips or arms by your sides.
Bend your knees slightly and jump, landing with your feet wide apart.
Land softly with knees bent and pointing in the same direction as your toes.
Jump again and bring your feet back together.
Keep a steady, bouncy rhythm and breathe evenly.

name: Back And Forth Step
desc: A light stepping drill that moves one foot forward and back while the other stays put, switching legs as you go. It warms up the legs and keeps the heart rate up at low impact.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Step your right foot forward and shift your weight onto it, bending the knee slightly.
Push off the right foot to bring it back beside the left.
Step the right foot backward, touch down, and bring it back again.
Swing your arms naturally, keep a steady pace, then switch to the left leg.

name: Back Extension
desc: A back extension on a hyperextension bench with the hips on the pad and the feet locked in. It builds the lower back muscles along the spine and also works the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Set the pad so it sits just below your hip bones and lock your heels under the foot rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest or lightly touch your ears.
Bend forward at the hips, lowering your upper body with a straight back.
Raise your body until it forms a straight line from head to heels.
Stop there instead of leaning back past straight, then lower slowly.
Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.

name: Back Extension (Machine)
desc: A seated back extension machine where you push a pad backward by straightening your torso. It strengthens the lower back muscles along the spine, with the glutes and hamstrings helping.
ins: Sit in the machine with your feet on the platform and the back pad across your upper back.
Fasten the belt if there is one and cross your arms over your chest.
Start leaning forward with a neutral spine.
Push back against the pad until your torso is upright or slightly past.
Return slowly to the forward position.
Breathe out as you push back and in as you return.

name: Back Extension On Exercise Ball
desc: A lower back raise done face down over a stability ball. It strengthens the muscles along the spine and also works the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie face down with your hips and belly on the ball and brace your feet wide on the floor or against a wall.
Cross your arms over your chest and let your upper body round down over the ball.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your chest until your body is in a straight line.
Breathe out as you rise and stop before you arch past straight.
Lower back down slowly while breathing in.

name: Back Lever
desc: An advanced static hold where you hang face down below a bar or rings with your body straight and level. It strengthens the shoulders, upper back, biceps and core.
ins: Hang from a bar or rings and tuck your knees up so you can roll backward between your arms.
Keep turning until you hang upside down with your arms behind you.
Slowly extend your legs and lower your body until it is straight and level with the floor, facing down.
Squeeze your glutes and stomach and hold, breathing steadily.
Tuck your knees to return the way you came and drop down safely.

name: Back Pec Stretch
desc: A two-part standing stretch that first rounds the upper back with the hands clasped in front, then opens the chest with the hands clasped behind. It loosens the lats, shoulders and chest.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Clasp your hands in front of you and push them forward, rounding your upper back.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds while breathing slowly.
Release, then clasp your hands behind your back.
Straighten your arms, lift your hands slightly and open your chest.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds, then relax.

name: Backward Jump
desc: A two-foot jump backward, which is harder to coordinate than jumping forward. It builds power in the quads, glutes and hamstrings and trains balance when landing in a direction you cannot see.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and make sure the space behind you is clear.
Bend into a quarter squat and bring your arms forward in front of you.
Swing your arms down and back as you jump backward off both feet.
Land on the balls of your feet first, then let your heels come down as your knees bend.
Keep your chest over your knees on landing so you do not fall back, then reset.

name: Backwards Run
desc: Running backward with short, controlled steps. It challenges coordination and balance and works the quads and calves in a different way from forward running.
ins: Pick a flat, clear area and check behind you before starting.
Stand tall with a slight forward lean and arms bent at your sides.
Reach back with one foot and land on the ball of the foot.
Push off and continue with short, quick backward steps, pumping your arms.
Glance over your shoulder often, keep your core tight, and breathe steadily.

name: Balance Board
desc: A balance drill where you stand on a wobble or rocker board and keep it level. It trains the quads, calves and hips to make small, quick corrections and improves ankle and knee control.
ins: Put the board on a flat, non-slip floor next to a wall or rail you can touch if needed.
Step on with both feet, placed evenly either side of the center, and bend your knees a little.
Shift your weight until the board is level and neither edge touches the floor.
Hold that position, keeping your chest up and your core tight, and let your ankles and knees make the small adjustments.
When it gets easy, try holding with your eyes closed or doing slow shallow squats on the board.
Breathe steadily and step off carefully when you finish.

name: Band Alternating Biceps Curl
desc: A standing biceps curl with a resistance band, lifting one arm at a time. The band gets harder toward the top, so the biceps work hardest where they are most contracted.
ins: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your back straight.
Breathe out and curl your right hand up toward your shoulder.
Breathe in and lower it slowly while keeping tension on the band.
Curl the left hand the same way and keep alternating.

name: Band Alternating V-Up
desc: A V-up done one leg at a time while holding a resistance band anchored behind your head. It trains the abs to lift your upper body and legs together, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Anchor a band low behind your head, lie on your back and hold the band in both hands with your arms straight overhead.
Keep your legs straight on the floor and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and lift your upper body and one straight leg at the same time, reaching your hands toward that foot.
Lower back down slowly with control, breathing in.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating each rep.

name: Band Assisted Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up with a resistance band looped over the bar and under your knee or foot, giving you a push at the bottom. It builds the lats, biceps and grip while you work toward unassisted pull-ups.
ins: Loop a resistance band around the pull-up bar and pull it through itself so it is secure.
Grab the bar overhand, then place one knee or foot into the bottom of the band.
Hang with straight arms and your stomach tight.
Pull up until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly, letting the band stretch without bouncing you back up.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Band Assisted Wheel Rollerout
desc: An ab wheel rollout with a resistance band pulling the wheel back toward you, which makes the hardest part easier. It builds abdominal strength on the way to full rollouts, with the lower back working to hold your spine still.
ins: Anchor a band low in front of you and loop it around the ab wheel handle, then kneel holding the handles with the wheel under your shoulders.
Tighten your abs and keep your lower back flat.
Breathe in and roll the wheel forward slowly, letting the band stretch as your body lowers.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Breathe out and pull the wheel back toward your knees with your abs, letting the band help.

name: Band Bench Press
desc: A bench press done lying on a bench with a resistance band looped behind your back or under the bench. The band gets harder as you push, so the chest and triceps work most at the top.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with the band passing under the bench or behind your upper back and a handle or end in each hand.
Start with your hands beside your chest, elbows bent and angled slightly away from your body.
Press both hands straight up until your arms are fully extended.
Lower slowly back to your chest, keeping tension on the band.
Exhale as you press and keep your wrists straight.

name: Band Bent-Over Hip Extension
desc: A glute kickback done bent forward at the hips with a resistance band around your foot. It isolates the glutes and also works the hamstrings and lower back muscles that hold your trunk steady.
ins: Anchor a band low behind you, loop it around one foot and step forward until it is lightly stretched.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and rest your hands on your thighs or a support.
Stand on the other leg with a soft knee and brace your core.
Push the banded leg straight back by squeezing your glute until it lines up with your body.
Hold for a second, then let the leg come forward slowly.
Breathe out as you push back; switch legs after your set.

name: Band Bicycle Crunch
desc: A bicycle crunch with a resistance band looped around your feet, adding resistance each time a leg pushes out. It works the abs and obliques, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Loop a small band around both feet, lie on your back and rest your hands lightly behind your head.
Lift your shoulders and feet off the floor with your knees bent.
Push one leg out straight against the band while turning to bring your opposite elbow toward the bent knee.
Switch sides in a steady pedaling motion, keeping your lower back pressed down.
Breathe out each time you twist and avoid pulling on your neck.

name: Band Close-Grip Pulldown
desc: A pulldown using a resistance band anchored overhead, with the hands close together. It works the lats with help from the biceps and forearms and is easy to do at home.
ins: Anchor a band high, above head height, and kneel or sit facing it.
Hold the band with both hands close together and your arms reaching up.
Sit or kneel tall with your stomach tight.
Pull the band down toward your upper chest, keeping your elbows close.
Let your arms rise slowly against the band's pull.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Band Close-Grip Push-Up
desc: A close-grip push-up with a resistance band across your upper back for extra load. The band adds resistance as you press up, making the triceps work harder at the top.
ins: Hold an end of a resistance band in each hand and wrap it across your upper back.
Get into a push-up position with your hands pinning the band ends to the floor, about shoulder-width or narrower.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the floor, elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and push up against the band until your arms are straight.
Keep your body straight and your hips from sagging.

name: Band Concentration Curl
desc: A seated concentration curl with a resistance band anchored under your foot. Bracing the elbow on your thigh isolates the biceps.
ins: Sit on a bench with feet wide and step on one end of a resistance band with one foot.
Hold the other end in the hand on the same side and rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh.
Breathe out and curl your hand up toward your shoulder against the band.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Band Fixed Back Close Grip Pulldown
desc: A kneeling or seated pulldown with a band anchored overhead, hands close together. It works the lats and arms with very little equipment.
ins: Anchor a band securely above you and kneel or sit facing it.
Hold the band with your hands close together, arms straight up.
Sit tall and tighten your stomach.
Breathe out and pull your hands down to your upper chest, elbows driving down and slightly forward.
Return slowly until your arms are straight overhead.

name: Band Fixed Back Underhand Pulldown
desc: A standing pulldown with a resistance band anchored above you, using an underhand grip. It is a simple home option for training the lats and biceps.
ins: Anchor a band securely above head height, such as over a pull-up bar.
Stand facing the anchor and hold the band with your palms facing you, arms reaching up and forward.
Step back until the band has light tension and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and pull your elbows down to your sides, bringing your hands to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats, then let your arms return up slowly against the band.

name: Band Front Lateral Raise
desc: A band raise done at an angle between the front and the side, with the band anchored under your feet. Lifting in this angle works the front and side shoulders in a joint-friendly line.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand at your sides.
Turn your arms so they point slightly forward, halfway between the front and the side.
Breathe out and raise your arms along that angle to shoulder height, thumbs up.
Hold for a second while keeping your shoulders down.
Breathe in and lower slowly against the band's pull.

name: Band Front Raise
desc: A front raise with a resistance band anchored under your feet. The band gets harder as you lift, so the front shoulders work most at the top.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band and hold an end in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Stand tall and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and raise your arms straight in front of you to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping some tension on the band.

name: Band Hip Lift
desc: A glute bridge with a mini band just above your knees, pushing your knees out against it as you lift your hips. The band adds work for the side glutes on top of the main glute and hamstring work.
ins: Place a mini band just above your knees and lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Rest your arms by your sides and press your knees out slightly against the band.
Push through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top while keeping your knees pressed out.
Lower your hips slowly to just above the floor.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Band Horizontal Pallof Press
desc: An anti-rotation core exercise where you press a band straight out from your chest while it tries to twist you toward its anchor. It strengthens the abs and obliques, with the glutes helping to keep your hips square.
ins: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it, far enough away that the band is tight.
Hold the band with both hands at the middle of your chest, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly soft.
Tighten your abs and glutes, then breathe out and press your hands straight out in front of you.
Hold for a second without letting your shoulders or hips turn toward the anchor.
Bring your hands back to your chest slowly, and switch sides after the set.

name: Band Jack Knife Sit-Up
desc: A jackknife sit-up where you fold your straight arms and legs up to meet over your hips while holding a band anchored behind your head. It works the full length of the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Anchor a band low behind your head, lie flat and hold it with both hands, arms straight overhead.
Keep your legs straight and together, and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and lift your arms, upper body and legs at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Balance briefly at the top with your body folded into a V.
Breathe in and lower your arms and legs back to the floor slowly.

name: Band Kneeling One Arm Pulldown
desc: A one-arm pulldown done kneeling with a band anchored overhead. It trains each lat separately, with the biceps and mid back helping.
ins: Anchor a band above head height and kneel facing it.
Hold the band in one hand with your arm reaching up and slightly forward.
Kneel tall with your hips forward and your stomach braced.
Pull your elbow down to your side, bringing your hand to shoulder level.
Return slowly to the stretched position, then switch arms after your set.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Band Kneeling Twisting Crunch
desc: A kneeling crunch against a band anchored overhead, with a twist so each elbow travels toward the opposite knee. It works the abs and puts extra focus on the obliques.
ins: Anchor a band high, kneel facing away from it and hold the ends beside your head.
Keep your hips stacked over your knees and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and curl down, turning your torso so one elbow moves toward the opposite knee.
Squeeze your side for a moment at the bottom.
Breathe in, rise back up slowly, then twist to the other side on the next rep.

name: Band Lying Hip External Rotation
desc: A rehab-style exercise lying face down with one knee bent, rotating the hip by moving the foot inward against a band. It strengthens the deep hip rotators and the back of the gluteus medius that control the hip.
ins: Anchor a band at ankle height to the side of the leg you will work and loop it around that ankle.
Lie face down with your forehead on your hands and bend that knee to 90 degrees, so the band pulls the foot outward.
Keep both hips flat on the floor and your thighs still.
Rotate your hip to bring the foot in toward the middle, across toward the other leg, against the band.
Let the foot return out slowly to the start.
Breathe steadily; do slow reps, then switch sides.

name: Band Lying Hip Internal Rotation
desc: A mobility exercise lying face down with one knee bent, moving the foot outward against a band to rotate the hip inward. It improves internal rotation of the hip and gently works the glutes and surrounding thigh muscles.
ins: Anchor a band at ankle height on the side opposite the leg you will work and loop it around that ankle.
Lie face down and bend that knee to 90 degrees, so the band pulls the foot inward.
Keep both hips pressed into the floor and the knee in place.
Let the foot move out to the side, rotating the hip inward against the band.
Go only as far as your hip allows without your pelvis lifting, then return slowly.
Breathe steadily; finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Band Lying Straight Leg Raise
desc: A lying leg raise with a resistance band anchored past your feet and looped around your ankles, so lifting your legs takes more effort. It works the lower abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Anchor a band low beyond your feet, loop it around both ankles and lie on your back with your legs straight.
Place your hands at your sides or under your lower back and press your lower back down.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs together until they point almost straight up.
Breathe in and lower them slowly against the band's pull.
Stop just above the floor before starting the next lift.

name: Band One Arm Overhead Biceps Curl
desc: A one-arm band curl done with the arm raised out to the side at shoulder height, curling your hand toward your head. It trains the biceps in a raised-arm position and works the shoulder to hold the arm up.
ins: Anchor a resistance band at about shoulder height and stand side-on to it.
Hold the free end in the hand nearer the anchor and raise that arm out to the side, level with your shoulder, palm facing up.
Breathe out and curl your hand toward the side of your head, keeping the elbow at shoulder height.
Squeeze the biceps for a second.
Breathe in and straighten the arm slowly; switch sides after the set.

name: Band One Arm Single Leg Split Squat
desc: A Bulgarian split squat with a resistance band under your front foot, holding the band in one hand at your shoulder. The one-sided load adds a core challenge while the quads and glutes of the front leg do the main work.
ins: Stand about two steps in front of a bench and place the middle of a band under your front foot.
Hold the band's other end in the hand on the same side as your front foot, at shoulder height.
Rest the top of your back foot on the bench and use your free hand on a support if needed.
Lower straight down by bending the front knee until the thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through the front heel to rise against the band, keeping your torso upright and not leaning toward the band.
Breathe out as you rise; finish all reps, then switch legs and hands.

name: Band One Arm Standing Low Row
desc: A standing one-arm row with a band anchored low, pulling back toward your hip. It works the upper back on each side, with the biceps and shoulders helping and the core keeping you still.
ins: Anchor a band low, near the floor, and hold it in one hand.
Step back into a split stance and hinge slightly forward with a flat back.
Start with your arm straight toward the anchor.
Row your hand to your hip, keeping your elbow close and your shoulders square.
Return slowly, finish your reps, then switch sides.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Band One Arm Twisting Chest Press
desc: A standing one-arm chest press with a resistance band, adding a rotation of the torso as you press. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps along with the rotational core muscles.
ins: Anchor the band at chest height, stand with your back to the anchor and hold the band in one hand beside your chest.
Step forward until the band is tight and set your feet in a staggered stance.
Press your hand forward and slightly across your body, rotating your torso toward the opposite side as you reach.
Return slowly, letting your torso turn back and your hand come back to your chest.
Finish your reps, then switch arms; breathe out on each press.

name: Band One Arm Twisting Seated Row
desc: A seated one-arm band row where you add a turn of the upper body as you pull. It trains the upper back and shoulders and brings in the obliques, with the biceps assisting.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs out and loop a band around your feet, or anchor it in front of you.
Hold the band in one hand with your arm straight and your torso turned slightly toward that arm.
Pull your hand back to your side while rotating your chest away from the anchor.
Keep your back tall and your hips still on the floor.
Turn back and extend your arm slowly, then switch sides after your set.
Breathe out as you pull and turn, and in as you return.

name: Band Pull Through
desc: A hip hinge where you face away from a low-anchored band, holding it between your legs, and drive your hips forward to stand. It trains the glutes and hamstrings and is a simple way to practice the hinge at home.
ins: Anchor a band low behind you, face away and hold it with both hands between your legs.
Walk forward until the band is tight and set your feet a little wider than hip-width.
Soften your knees and push your hips back, letting the band draw your hands back through your legs.
Keep your back flat and stop when you feel your hamstrings stretch.
Snap your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, arms straight.
Breathe in as you hinge and out as you stand.

name: Band Push Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up where you press a resistance band forward as you rise, with the band anchored behind you. It mainly works the abs, while the shoulders and chest work to push the band.
ins: Anchor a band low behind you, lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, and hold the ends near your chest.
Tighten your abs and tuck your chin slightly.
Breathe out and sit up, pressing your hands forward against the band until your arms are straight.
Pause briefly at the top with your back tall.
Breathe in, bring your hands back to your chest and roll down slowly to the floor.

name: Band Reverse Fly
desc: A reverse fly where you pull a resistance band apart in front of your chest. It strengthens the rear shoulders and the upper back and is good for posture.
ins: Stand tall and hold a band in front of your chest with both hands, arms straight and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows soft and your shoulders down.
Breathe out and pull the band apart by moving your arms out to the sides until the band touches your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Breathe in and let your arms come back together slowly.

name: Band Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A reverse wrist curl using a resistance band anchored under your foot. It trains the wrist extensors and is easy to do at home.
ins: Sit on a chair or bench and step on the middle of a resistance band with one foot.
Hold the other end with your palm facing down and rest that forearm on your thigh, wrist past the knee.
Let the band pull your hand down so the wrist bends toward the floor.
Breathe out and lift the back of your hand as high as you can.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Finish the set, then switch hands.

name: Band Seated Hip External Rotation
desc: A seated rehab exercise where you rotate your hip by pulling your foot inward against a band while your thigh stays still. It strengthens the small deep hip muscles, including the side glutes, that control hip rotation.
ins: Sit tall on the edge of a bench with your knees bent to 90 degrees and feet off or lightly on the floor.
Loop a band around one ankle and anchor it to the outside of that leg so it pulls the foot outward.
Hold the bench and keep the thigh still on the seat.
Rotate your hip to swing your foot inward toward the other leg against the band, keeping the knee in place.
Return the foot slowly to the start.
Breathe steadily; do slow, controlled reps, then switch sides.

name: Band Seated Hip Internal Rotation
desc: A seated mobility exercise where you rotate your hip inward by swinging your foot outward against a band while your thigh stays still. It improves internal hip rotation and gently works the glutes and thigh muscles.
ins: Sit tall on the edge of a bench with your knees bent to 90 degrees.
Loop a band around one ankle and anchor it on the inside of that leg so it pulls the foot inward.
Hold the bench and keep your thigh and knee still.
Rotate your hip to move the foot outward, away from the other leg, against the band.
Return slowly to the start, staying within a pain-free range.
Breathe steadily; finish your reps, then switch legs.

name: Band Seated Twist
desc: A seated rotation where you turn your torso away from a resistance band anchored at your side. It strengthens the obliques and the rest of the abs.
ins: Anchor a band at chest height and sit on the floor side-on to it, knees slightly bent.
Hold the band with both hands in front of your chest, arms nearly straight.
Sit tall, tighten your abs and breathe out as you turn your shoulders away from the anchor.
Keep your hips still so the turn comes from your trunk.
Return slowly to the middle, and switch sides after the set.

name: Band Shoulder Press
desc: An overhead press using a resistance band anchored under your feet. It is a joint-friendly way to train the shoulders and triceps at home or as a warm-up.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with feet hip-width apart and bring the ends up to your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Brace your stomach and stand tall.
Breathe out and press your hands straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your lower back from arching.
Breathe in and lower your hands slowly to your shoulders.

name: Band Shrug
desc: A shrug with a resistance band under your feet, a simple way to train the upper traps at home or while travelling. The shoulders assist.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip-width apart.
Hold the ends at your sides with straight arms; shorten your grip on the band for more tension.
Stand tall with your chin level.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the squeeze briefly, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Band Side Triceps Extension
desc: A one-arm triceps extension done across the body against a resistance band anchored to your side. It isolates the triceps, with the shoulder working to keep the upper arm raised.
ins: Anchor the band at chest height and stand side-on to it, holding the free end in the hand farther from the anchor.
Raise that upper arm out to the side at shoulder height and bend the elbow so your hand sits in front of your chest.
Keep the upper arm still and straighten the elbow, pushing your hand out to the side against the band.
Squeeze the back of your arm when it is fully straight.
Let the band pull your hand back slowly to the start, then switch sides after your set.

name: Band Single Leg Calf Raise
desc: A single-leg calf raise with a resistance band looped under the foot and held at shoulder height. The band adds load as you rise, making it a good home calf exercise.
ins: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with one foot and hold both ends at your shoulders.
Lift the other foot off the floor and lightly touch a wall if you need balance.
Stand tall with your stomach tight.
Breathe out and rise onto the ball of your standing foot as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Band Single Leg Reverse Calf Raise
desc: A seated calf exercise for one leg where you point your foot against a resistance band. It strengthens the calf and ankle with no standing load, which suits beginners and rehab.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front of you.
Loop a resistance band around the ball of that foot and hold the ends with both hands.
Pull the band snug so your toes start pointing toward you.
Breathe out and press the ball of your foot away, pointing your toes as far as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and let the band slowly pull your foot back.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Band Single Leg Split Squat
desc: A Bulgarian split squat with a resistance band under your front foot and the ends held at your shoulders. The band gets harder as you stand, strengthening the quads and glutes of the front leg.
ins: Stand about two steps in front of a bench and place the middle of a band under your front foot.
Bring the band ends up to your shoulders, one in each hand.
Rest the top of your back foot on the bench and stand tall.
Bend the front knee and lower straight down until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Push through the front heel to stand back up against the band.
Breathe out as you rise; finish all reps on one leg, then switch.

name: Band Squat
desc: A squat with a resistance band under your feet and the ends held at your shoulders, so the resistance grows as you stand. It is a portable way to strengthen the glutes and quads.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bring the ends up to the front of your shoulders, palms facing forward or toward each other.
Sit your hips back and down into a squat, keeping your chest up and heels flat.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Drive through your feet to stand against the band, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand.

name: Band Squat Row
desc: A combination move where you hold a band anchored in front of you, squat down, then row the band to your ribs as you stand. It works the glutes and legs together with the back muscles.
ins: Anchor a band at about chest height and stand facing it, holding one end in each hand with arms straight.
Step back until the band is slightly tight and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down with your chest up, keeping your arms reaching forward.
Drive up through your feet and, as you stand, pull your elbows back past your ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then extend your arms as you lower into the next squat.
Breathe in as you squat and out as you stand and row.

name: Band Standing Crunch
desc: A standing crunch against a resistance band anchored above you. It works the abs, with the obliques helping to steady your trunk.
ins: Anchor a band high, stand facing away from it and hold the ends beside your head.
Set your feet hip-width apart and soften your knees.
Breathe out and round your upper body down toward your hips, squeezing your abs.
Keep your hands fixed by your head and your hips still.
Breathe in and slowly roll back up to standing.

name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
desc: A standing row with a resistance band anchored at chest height, pulled toward your face with your elbows high. It targets the rear shoulders and the upper back.
ins: Anchor a band at chest height and hold an end in each hand, palms facing down.
Step back until the band is tight and stand with your arms straight in front of you.
Breathe out and pull your hands toward your face, lifting your elbows out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly.

name: Band Standing Twisting Crunch
desc: A standing crunch against a band anchored above you, with a twist that brings one elbow toward the opposite hip. It works the abs and puts extra focus on the obliques.
ins: Anchor a band high, stand facing away from it and hold the ends beside your head.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your abs tight.
Breathe out and curl down while rotating, bringing one elbow toward the opposite hip.
Squeeze your side at the bottom for a moment.
Breathe in, return to upright slowly and twist the other way on the next rep.

name: Band Step-Up
desc: A step-up onto a box with a resistance band under the stepping foot and the ends held at your shoulders. It strengthens the glutes and quads of the working leg with resistance that peaks at the top.
ins: Place a sturdy box or step in front of you and loop the middle of a band under one foot.
Hold the band ends at your shoulders and put that same foot fully on the box.
Lean slightly forward and push through the heel on the box to stand up on it.
Stand tall at the top, bringing the other foot up beside it.
Step back down slowly with the trailing foot, keeping control with the working leg.
Breathe out as you step up; complete your reps, then switch legs.

name: Band Stiff Leg Deadlift
desc: A stiff-leg deadlift with a resistance band under your feet, keeping your legs nearly straight as you fold forward. It stretches and strengthens the hamstrings and works the glutes and lower back.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip-width apart and hold an end in each hand in front of your thighs.
Straighten your legs, leaving only a slight bend in your knees.
Push your hips back and fold forward, lowering your hands toward your shins.
Keep your back flat and stop when your hamstrings are fully stretched.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand up against the band.
Breathe in as you fold and out as you stand.

name: Band Straight Back Stiff Leg Deadlift
desc: A band stiff-leg deadlift that puts the focus on holding a perfectly flat back, stopping the moment your spine would start to round. It trains the glutes and hamstrings while teaching good hinge posture.
ins: Stand on a band with your feet hip-width apart, holding the ends at your thighs.
Pull your shoulders back, lift your chest and brace your core so your back is long and flat.
Unlock your knees slightly and push your hips back, sliding your hands down your thighs.
Lower only until you feel your back about to round or your hamstrings are tight, usually around the knees.
Squeeze your glutes and push your hips forward to stand tall.
Breathe in as you hinge and out as you rise.

name: Band Twisting Overhead Press
desc: A band press where you rotate your upper body toward one side as you press the opposite arm overhead. It trains the shoulders together with core rotation and coordination.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Brace your stomach and keep your hips facing forward.
Breathe out and press one hand up while turning your chest toward the opposite side.
Breathe in and return to the center as you lower your hand.
Press with the other arm while turning the other way, and keep alternating.

name: Band Two Legs Calf Raise (Band Under Both Feet)
desc: A two-leg calf raise with a resistance band under both feet and the ends held at your shoulders. It adds resistance to the standing calf raise without any weights.
ins: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with both feet hip-width apart.
Hold one end in each hand and bring your hands up to your shoulders so the band is taut.
Stand tall with your knees straight but soft.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Keep your hands still at your shoulders throughout.

name: Band Underhand Pulldown
desc: A pulldown with a resistance band anchored overhead, using an underhand grip so the elbows stay close. It works the lats with strong help from the biceps.
ins: Anchor a band above head height and sit or kneel facing it.
Hold the band with your palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Start with your arms reaching up and your chest tall.
Pull down toward your upper chest, keeping your elbows in front and close.
Let your arms rise slowly against the band.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Band V-Up
desc: A full V-up where you lift your straight legs and upper body together while holding a resistance band anchored behind your head. It works the entire front of the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Anchor a band low behind your head, lie flat and hold the band with both hands, arms straight above your head.
Keep your legs straight and together and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and raise both legs and your upper body at once, reaching your hands toward your shins.
At the top, balance on your hips for a moment with your body in a V.
Breathe in and lower your legs and back slowly, stopping before they rest fully on the floor.

name: Band Vertical Pallof Press
desc: A Pallof press variation where you press a side-anchored band straight up overhead instead of forward. It challenges the abs and obliques to resist twisting, with the glutes helping to keep you planted.
ins: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side-on to it, stepping out until the band is tight.
Hold the band with both hands at your chest, feet shoulder-width apart and knees soft.
Tighten your abs and glutes, then breathe out and press your hands straight up overhead.
Keep your ribs down and your body square, without leaning or turning toward the anchor.
Lower your hands slowly back to your chest, and switch sides after the set.

name: Band Wrist Curl
desc: A palms-up wrist curl using a resistance band held under your foot. It strengthens the inner forearm and grip with very little equipment.
ins: Sit on a chair and step on one end of a resistance band.
Hold the band with your palm facing up and rest your forearm on your thigh, wrist past the knee.
Let the band draw your hand down so your wrist bends back.
Breathe out and curl your palm up toward your forearm.
Pause, then breathe in and return slowly.
Switch hands after the set.

name: Band Y-Raise
desc: A band raise where you lift your arms up and out into a Y shape over your head. It strengthens the lower traps and the shoulders and helps posture.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band and hold an end in each hand in front of your thighs, thumbs up.
Stand tall and pull your shoulders down and back.
Breathe out and raise your arms up and out until they form a Y above your head.
Hold for a second without arching your lower back.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Barbell Alternate Biceps Curl
desc: A standing biceps curl with a barbell where you emphasize one arm at a time by shifting the effort from side to side. It builds the biceps and grip.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, arms straight.
Pin your elbows to your sides and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and curl the bar up, letting your right arm drive the lift while the left arm assists.
Lower the bar slowly to full arm extension.
On the next rep let the left arm lead, and keep alternating without swinging your torso.

name: Barbell Bench Front Squat
desc: A front squat with the barbell across the front of your shoulders, lowered until you lightly touch a bench behind you. The bench sets a consistent depth while the quads do most of the work, helped by the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Place a bench behind you and set the bar on the front of your shoulders, elbows high and pointing forward.
Stand a short step in front of the bench with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace your core and sit down and back until your glutes just touch the bench.
Keep your elbows up and your chest tall so the bar does not roll forward.
Without resting on the bench, drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
Breathe out near the top and reset before the next rep.

name: Barbell Bench Press
desc: The classic flat bench press with a barbell, the main compound lift for overall chest size and pressing strength. The triceps and front shoulders help drive the bar.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width, pull your shoulder blades together and unrack it over your chest.
Breathe in and lower the bar under control to your mid-chest, elbows angled about 45 degrees from your body.
Touch lightly without bouncing, then press the bar up and slightly back to over your shoulders.
Breathe out near the top and keep your hips and upper back on the bench the whole time.

name: Barbell Bench Squat
desc: A back squat performed to a bench or box, so you sit back until you touch it and then stand up. It builds the quads and glutes and teaches a controlled, repeatable depth.
ins: Set the bar on a rack at upper-chest height and place a bench a short step behind where you will stand.
Duck under the bar, rest it on your upper back, grip it just outside your shoulders and lift it off the rack.
Step back until the bench is just behind your heels, feet about shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace and sit your hips back and down until you lightly touch the bench.
Keep your chest up and your knees pushed out, then drive up through your feet to stand.
Breathe out at the top; rack the bar carefully after your last rep.

name: Barbell Bent Arm Pullover
desc: A pullover lying across a flat bench with a barbell and bent elbows. It stretches and works the lats, with help from the chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell over your chest with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees and keep that angle fixed for the whole set.
Breathe in and lower the bar back past your head in an arc until you feel a stretch along your sides.
Keep your lower back on the bench and your belly tight.
Breathe out and pull the bar back over your chest using your lats, not by straightening your arms.

name: Barbell Biceps Curl (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A standing barbell curl with an arm blaster holding your elbows at your sides. It isolates the biceps strictly so the weight can't be swung up.
ins: Put on the arm blaster and grip a barbell underhand at about shoulder width.
Stand tall with your arms straight and your elbows against the plate.
Breathe out and curl the bar up until your forearms are nearly vertical.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Clean And Press
desc: A full-body lift that brings the barbell from the floor to your shoulders in one fast pull, then presses it overhead. It develops power through the legs and hips and strength in the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, hips back, back flat and hands just outside your knees.
Push the floor away to lift the bar past your knees, then snap your hips forward to drive it upward.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on the front of your shoulders with your elbows high and knees bent.
Stand up tall, take a breath and tighten your glutes and core.
Press the bar straight overhead until your arms lock out, moving your head back slightly to let it pass.
Lower the bar to your shoulders, then to your thighs and the floor with control, breathing out as you press.

name: Barbell Clean-Grip Front Squat
desc: A front squat using the clean grip, with the bar on the front of your shoulders and your fingers under it, elbows pointed forward. It loads the quads and glutes while asking a lot of the upper back and core to stay upright.
ins: Set the bar on a rack at shoulder height and step in so it touches the front of your shoulders.
Hold it with your fingertips just outside your shoulders and push your elbows up and forward.
Lift the bar off the rack, take two steps back and set your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Breathe in, brace and squat straight down, keeping your torso upright and elbows high.
Go as deep as you can while your heels stay down, then drive up through your feet.
Breathe out as you finish standing.

name: Barbell Close-Grip Bench Press
desc: A bench press with the hands set closer than shoulder width, which shifts much of the work onto the triceps while the chest and front shoulders help.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and feet planted on the floor.
Grip the bar a little narrower than shoulder width and unrack it over your chest.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up until your arms lock out.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and your shoulder blades pulled together the whole set.

name: Barbell Decline Bent Arm Pullover
desc: A pullover done on a decline bench with the elbows kept bent, which puts a long stretch on the lats. It works the lats first, with the chest and triceps helping.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your legs hooked under the pads and your head at the low end.
Hold a barbell over your chest with a shoulder-width grip and bend your elbows a little.
Keeping that elbow bend fixed, lower the bar back past your head in a wide arc.
Go only as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.
Pull the bar back up over your chest by driving with the lats.
Breathe in as you lower and breathe out as you pull back up.

name: Barbell Decline Close Grip To Skull Press
desc: A triceps press done on a decline bench that blends a close-grip press with a skull crusher: you lower the bar toward your forehead and press it back up. It trains the triceps with help from the chest and shoulders.
ins: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back with a barbell held at a close grip over your chest.
Bend your elbows and lower the bar in a slight arc toward your forehead, letting your upper arms tilt back a little.
Stop just above your forehead with your elbows pointing toward your feet.
Breathe out and press the bar back up and over your chest, straightening your arms fully.
Move slowly on the way down; use a spotter if the weight is heavy.

name: Barbell Decline Pullover
desc: A barbell pullover done on a decline bench, lowering the bar in an arc behind your head. The decline angle increases the stretch on the chest and lats while the triceps hold the arm position.
ins: Secure your legs on a decline bench and lie back holding a light barbell with a narrow overhand grip above your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower the bar in an arc past your head until you feel a strong stretch through your chest and sides.
Pull the bar back along the same arc to above your chest.
Breathe in as the bar goes back and out as it comes up; use a light weight and move slowly.

name: Barbell Decline Wide-Grip Press
desc: A decline barbell press with a wide grip that puts the outer and lower chest under heavy load. The wider hands shorten the range and reduce the triceps' share of the work.
ins: Secure your feet on a decline bench and lie back under the bar.
Hold the bar with your hands clearly wider than shoulder width and lift it off the rack.
Lower it with control until it lightly touches your lower chest, elbows flaring naturally out to the sides.
Press back up by squeezing your chest, stopping just short of locking your elbows hard.
Keep your shoulder blades pinched back and breathe out as you press.

name: Barbell Decline Wide-Grip Pullover
desc: A decline-bench pullover using a wide grip and nearly straight arms, which keeps the lats working through a long arc. The chest and triceps assist.
ins: Secure your legs on a decline bench and lie back with your head at the low end.
Hold the bar with a grip clearly wider than your shoulders, arms almost straight above your chest.
Lower the bar back beyond your head in a slow arc, keeping your arms long.
Stop at a deep stretch under your arms without arching your back off the bench.
Sweep the bar back to above your chest using your lats.
Breathe in on the way back and out on the way up.

name: Barbell Drag Curl
desc: A barbell curl where you drag the bar up along the front of your body while pulling your elbows back. Keeping the bar close takes the front shoulders out and puts more load on the biceps.
ins: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, bar resting on your thighs.
Breathe out and pull your elbows back behind you as you curl, so the bar slides up your stomach.
Keep the bar in contact with or just off your body until it reaches your lower chest.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top for a second.
Lower the bar along the same path back to your thighs.

name: Barbell Floor Calf Raise
desc: A barbell calf raise done with your feet flat on the floor rather than on a step. The shorter range makes it a simple, stable way to load the calves.
ins: Rest a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet hip-width apart on flat ground.
Stand tall with your knees straight but soft and your stomach tight.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second, keeping your weight over your big toes.
Breathe in and lower your heels until they just touch the floor.
Start the next rep without resting your full weight on your heels.

name: Barbell Front Chest Squat
desc: A front squat where you hold the bar on the front of your shoulders with your arms crossed over it instead of the clean grip. It works the quads and glutes and suits lifters who lack the wrist flexibility for a clean grip.
ins: Set the bar on a rack at shoulder height and step in so it sits on the front of your shoulders.
Cross your arms over the bar, placing each hand on the opposite shoulder, and lift your elbows level with the floor.
Lift the bar off, step back and place your feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace and squat down, keeping your chest up and elbows high so the bar stays in place.
Drive up through your whole foot to standing.
Breathe out at the top and keep your elbows up between reps.

name: Barbell Front Raise
desc: A standing raise where you lift a barbell straight out in front of you to shoulder height. It builds the front of the shoulders.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell against your thighs with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Brace your stomach and keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and lift the bar forward and up until your arms are level with the floor.
Hold for a second without leaning back.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your thighs.

name: Barbell Front Raise And Pullover
desc: A lying barbell combo that moves the bar in one long arc from your thighs, over your chest and back behind your head. It works the chest and lats through a big stretch and also trains the front shoulders and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a light barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip, resting it on your thighs with straight arms.
Keeping your arms almost straight, lift the bar up in an arc until it is over your chest.
Continue the arc past your face and lower the bar behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Pull the bar back along the same path to over your chest, then lower it to your thighs.
Brace your stomach so your lower back does not arch, and breathe in as the bar goes behind your head.

name: Barbell Front Squat
desc: A squat with the barbell resting on the front of your shoulders. The forward load keeps your torso upright and puts strong emphasis on the quads and glutes while challenging the core.
ins: Rack the bar at shoulder height and step under so it rests on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat.
Hold it with a grip that lets your elbows point forward and up.
Walk it out and set your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Take a breath, brace and squat down between your knees, keeping your chest tall.
Stop when your hips are below your knees or your back starts to round, then stand up.
Breathe out at the top and keep your elbows lifted the whole set.

name: Barbell Full Squat
desc: A back squat taken to full depth, with your hips dropping well below your knees. It trains the glutes, quads and hamstrings through their longest range and builds hip and ankle mobility.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back from a rack and step out with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little.
Grip the bar firmly and squeeze your shoulder blades together to make a shelf for it.
Breathe in, brace and sit straight down, letting your knees travel forward over your toes.
Keep going until your hips are as low as they can go with your heels down and back flat.
Drive up through your feet, keeping your chest up so your hips and shoulders rise together.
Breathe out near the top.

name: Barbell Full Squat (back Pov)
desc: A full-depth barbell back squat, going all the way down until the hips are well below the knees. It trains the glutes and quads through their whole range, with the hamstrings, calves and core working hard to keep you stable.
ins: Unrack the bar onto your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out a little.
Breathe in deeply and brace your stomach as if about to be pushed.
Bend your knees and hips together and sink straight down, keeping your heels on the floor.
Go as deep as you can while your back stays flat, ideally until your hamstrings touch your calves.
Breathe out and drive up hard, keeping your knees pushed out over your toes.

name: Barbell Full Squat (side Pov)
desc: A deep barbell back squat, the same lift seen from the side, where the bar path and back angle are easiest to check. It builds the glutes and quads, with the hamstrings, calves and core supporting the lift.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back, step out of the rack and place your feet shoulder-width apart.
Pick a spot on the floor a few meters ahead to keep your head steady.
Breathe in, brace and lower yourself so the bar moves straight down over the middle of your foot.
Keep your chest and hips moving at a steady angle, without your hips shooting up or back.
Reach full depth, then breathe out and stand up along the same straight line.

name: Barbell Full Zercher Squat
desc: A deep squat with the barbell held in the bend of the elbows in front of the body. It hits the glutes and quads hard while forcing the upper back and core to stay strong and upright.
ins: Set the bar in a rack at about hip height.
Squat down slightly, hook the bar into the crease of your elbows and hold your hands together near your chest.
Stand up with the bar, step back and set your feet a bit wider than shoulder-width.
Breathe in, brace and sit down between your heels as deep as you can with your chest up.
Keep the bar close to your body and your elbows tucked in.
Breathe out and drive up to standing, then rack the bar when done.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge Two Legs On Bench
