desc: A glute bridge with both feet on a bench and a barbell resting across the hips for extra load. It builds strong glutes and hamstrings while the core keeps the body steady.
ins: Sit on the floor in front of a bench and roll a padded barbell over your legs to rest on your hip crease.
Lie back and place both heels on the bench with knees bent about 90 degrees.
Hold the bar with both hands to keep it steady.
Brace and breathe out as you push your heels into the bench to lift your hips and the bar.
Stop when your body is straight from shoulders to knees and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the bar nearly touches the floor.

name: Barbell Good Morning
desc: A hip hinge with the barbell on your upper back, bowing forward and standing back up. It strengthens the hamstrings and lower back and teaches you to move from the hips.
ins: Rest a light bar on your upper back and stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees softly bent.
Brace your core and keep your back flat from head to hips.
Push your hips straight back and let your chest lower toward the floor.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings or your torso is close to level with the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand up.
Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.

name: Barbell Guillotine Bench Press
desc: An advanced bench press variation where the bar is lowered toward the base of the neck with the elbows flared wide. It stretches the upper and outer chest hard, so it is done with light weight and a spotter.
ins: Set up on a flat bench with a wide grip and use a much lighter load than your normal bench press.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your upper chest with your elbows pointing out to the sides.
Lower the bar slowly toward the top of your chest, just below the collarbone, keeping your elbows flared.
Stop a few centimetres above your body and press back up along the same path.
Always have a spotter, never bounce the bar, and breathe out as you press.

name: Barbell Hack Squat
desc: A squat where you hold the barbell behind your legs at arm's length and stand up with it. Keeping the load behind you keeps your torso upright and puts the work on the quads and glutes.
ins: Place the bar on the floor and stand in front of it with your heels a few centimeters away.
Squat down, reach behind you and grip the bar with your palms facing back, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your chest, flatten your back and take a breath.
Drive through your feet and stand up, sliding the bar up the backs of your legs.
Pause tall at the top, then bend your knees and lower the bar along the same path.
Breathe out as you reach the top.

name: Barbell High Bar Squat
desc: The classic barbell back squat with the bar high on the traps. Your torso stays more upright and the knees travel forward, which makes it strongly quad- and glute-focused while the core holds you stable.
ins: Set the bar in a rack at upper-chest height and step under it.
Rest the bar on top of your traps, grip it just outside your shoulders and pull your elbows down.
Unrack it, step back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Breathe in, brace, and bend at the knees and hips at the same time, keeping your chest up.
Let your knees move forward over your toes and sink until your hips drop below your knees.
Breathe out and push the floor away to stand up, keeping the bar over mid-foot.

name: Barbell Incline Close Grip Bench Press
desc: A barbell bench press on an incline bench using a narrow grip. It emphasizes the triceps while the upper chest and front shoulders also work.
ins: Lie on an incline bench and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Plant your feet and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your upper chest, keeping your elbows tucked near your sides.
Breathe out and press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows throughout.

name: Barbell Incline Reverse-Grip Press
desc: A press on an incline bench with the barbell held in an underhand grip. The reversed grip keeps the elbows close and puts emphasis on the triceps and upper chest.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie back with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar with palms facing you at about shoulder width and unrack it with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your upper chest with your elbows tucked close to your sides.
Breathe out and press it back up to full arm extension.
Keep your wrists firm and straight; a spotter helps with the unusual grip.

name: Barbell Incline Row
desc: A barbell row done lying face down on an incline bench, so your chest is supported and your lower back stays out of it. It focuses on the upper back, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and place a barbell on the floor under its top end.
Lie face down with your chest on the pad and your feet planted.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width and let it hang with straight arms.
Row the bar up toward the bench, leading with your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower it slowly to a full stretch without lifting your chest off the pad.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way down.

name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
desc: A small, controlled movement on an incline bench where you push a barbell up using only your shoulder blades, with your arms kept straight. It strengthens the serratus muscles along the ribs that keep the shoulder blades stable.
ins: Lie on a bench set to about 45 degrees and hold a barbell straight above your shoulders with a shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows locked for the whole set; the arms do not bend at any point.
Let your shoulder blades sink back toward the bench so the bar drops a few centimetres.
Push the bar toward the ceiling by spreading your shoulder blades and reaching your shoulders forward.
Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly; breathe out as you reach up.

name: Barbell Jefferson Squat
desc: An old-school squat where you straddle the barbell and hold it between your legs, one hand in front and one behind. It trains the glutes, quads and inner thighs and challenges your core against an uneven, rotating load.
ins: Stand over the middle of the bar so it runs between your legs, feet wider than your shoulders and turned out.
Squat down and grip the bar with one hand in front of your body and the other behind it.
Flatten your back, lift your chest and brace your core.
Drive through your feet and stand up, keeping your hips and shoulders square instead of twisting.
Lower back down under control until the bar nearly touches the floor.
Breathe out as you stand; switch which leg is forward and which hand is in front on the next set.

name: Barbell Jm Bench Press
desc: An advanced triceps lift that sits between a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher: the bar travels toward your chin while your elbows move forward. It loads the triceps heavily, with the chest and shoulders assisting.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold the bar slightly narrower than shoulder width with straight arms over your chest.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, letting the bar travel down and slightly toward your chin.
Let your elbows drift forward toward your feet so your forearms end up resting near your upper arms.
Stop a few centimeters above your chin and throat.
Breathe out and press back up along the same path until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Jump Squat
desc: A jump squat with a light barbell across your upper back. It builds explosive power in the glutes, quads and calves and should only be done with a weight you can land softly with.
ins: Rest a light bar on your upper back and stand with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold the bar tightly against your back so it cannot bounce.
Dip into a quarter to half squat, keeping your chest up.
Jump straight up as hard as you can by extending your hips, knees and ankles together.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and sink back into the squat to absorb the landing.
Reset your stance and breathe before each jump.

name: Barbell Lateral Lunge
desc: A side lunge with a barbell on your upper back: you step out wide to one side, sit into that hip and push back to the center. It works the glutes, quads and inner thighs and trains side-to-side strength.
ins: Rest a barbell on your upper back and stand with your feet together.
Take a big step out to one side, toes pointing forward or slightly out.
Sit your hips back over the stepping leg and bend that knee while the other leg stays straight.
Keep your chest up and the bent knee in line with your toes.
Push off the bent leg to bring your feet back together.
Breathe out as you push back; alternate sides or finish one side first.

name: Barbell Leg Twist Press
desc: A lying core exercise where you hold a barbell pressed up over your chest while rotating your raised legs from side to side. It works the abs and obliques, while the shoulders, triceps, chest and glutes keep the bar and your body stable.
ins: Lie on your back on the floor and press a light barbell up over your chest with straight arms, hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lift your legs with your knees bent at about a right angle over your hips, knees and feet together.
Keeping the bar steady and your shoulders down, slowly lower both knees to one side as far as you can control.
Breathe out and use your abs to bring your legs back to the center.
Lower your legs to the other side, and keep the range small if your lower back lifts or the bar wobbles.

name: Barbell Low Bar Squat
desc: A barbell back squat with the bar placed low on the rear shoulders, a style many powerlifters use. The hips sit back more and the torso leans further forward, so the glutes, hamstrings and quads all share the load.
ins: Set the bar in a rack at mid-chest height and step under it.
Rest the bar across the back of your shoulders, below the top of the traps, with a fairly wide grip.
Lift the bar off the rack, take two short steps back and set your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in deeply, brace your stomach and push your hips back as your knees bend.
Lean your chest forward enough to keep the bar over the middle of your feet and go down until your hips are just below your knees.
Breathe out and drive up, keeping your back flat until you stand tall.

name: Barbell Lunge
desc: A forward lunge with a barbell on your upper back. Each leg works on its own, building the glutes and quads and improving balance and hip stability.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back from a rack and stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Take a long step forward with one foot.
Lower straight down until your back knee almost touches the floor and your front shin is roughly vertical.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee in line with your toes.
Push through your front heel to step back to the start.
Alternate legs, breathing in as you lower and out as you push back.

name: Barbell Lying Back Of The Head Tricep Extension
desc: A lying barbell triceps extension in which the bar travels past your forehead to behind the top of your head. Letting the upper arms tilt back slightly adds stretch to the long head of the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your head near the end and hold a barbell over your chest, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Tilt your arms back a little so the bar sits above your face rather than your chest.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar in an arc behind the top of your head.
Keep your elbows pointing up and roughly shoulder-width apart.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to bring the bar back over your face.

name: Barbell Lying Close-Grip Press
desc: A lying barbell press with the hands close together and the elbows kept tight to the body. It builds the triceps, with the chest and front shoulders helping.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and take the bar with your hands about a fist's width inside shoulder width.
Hold it straight above your chest with your shoulder blades squeezed together.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your lower chest, brushing your elbows past your ribs.
Breathe out and drive the bar back up, focusing on straightening your elbows.
Keep your hips on the bench and your feet planted.

name: Barbell Lying Close-Grip Triceps Extension
desc: A lying triceps extension with the hands close together on the bar. The narrow grip keeps the elbows in and isolates the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell above your chest with your hands about 15 cm apart.
Tilt your arms back slightly so the bar sits over your eyes.
Breathe in and bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward the top of your head.
Keep your elbows pointing up and close together rather than flaring out.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to bring the bar back up.

name: Barbell Lying Extension
desc: A lying barbell extension where the bar is lowered past your forehead to behind the top of your head. The longer path stretches the triceps more than a standard skull crusher.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your head near the end and hold the bar over your chest at shoulder width, palms facing away.
Let your upper arms angle back slightly toward your head and lock them in that position.
Breathe in and bend your elbows so the bar travels down behind the top of your head.
Go as low as you can control while feeling a stretch in the back of your arms.
Breathe out and straighten your elbows to return the bar above your face.

name: Barbell Lying Lifting (on Hip)
desc: A barbell hip thrust: you rest your upper back on a bench and lift a barbell sitting across your hips. It isolates the glutes strongly, with help from the hamstrings and quads.
ins: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the edge of a bench and roll a padded bar over your hips.
Bend your knees and plant your feet flat, about hip-width apart, so your shins will be vertical at the top.
Hold the bar in place with both hands, tuck your chin and brace your core.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower your hips under control, breathing out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Barbell Lying Preacher Curl
desc: A barbell curl done lying face down on a high bench with your arms hanging over the end, which removes any body swing and keeps steady tension on the biceps.
ins: Lie face down on a raised flat bench so your shoulders are at the end and your arms hang straight down.
Have the barbell on the floor or handed to you and grip it underhand at shoulder width.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your forehead without lifting your upper arms.
Squeeze at the top for a moment.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight again.

name: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension
desc: A lying barbell triceps extension with a shoulder-width grip, lowering the bar toward the crown of your head. It isolates the triceps through a full range.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and press a barbell up over your chest with a shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling and your upper arms fixed.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar toward the top of your head.
Stop when your forearms are about level with the bench.
Breathe out and extend your elbows to bring the bar back to the start.

name: Barbell Narrow Stance Squat
desc: A back squat with your feet set close together. The narrow stance shifts more work onto the quads while the glutes and hamstrings still assist.
ins: Take the bar on your upper back from a rack and step out.
Set your feet about hip-width apart or slightly closer, toes pointing forward.
Breathe in, brace and bend your knees, letting them travel forward over your toes.
Keep your chest up and your heels down as you lower as far as you can control.
Push up through your whole foot to standing.
Breathe out at the top.

name: Barbell One Arm Bent Over Row
desc: A one-arm row where you hold a barbell at its middle in one hand while bent forward. Balancing the bar adds a grip and control challenge while the upper back and lats do the main work.
ins: Stand beside a loaded barbell and grip it in the exact middle with one hand.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and rest your free hand on your thigh or a bench.
Let the bar hang below your shoulder, keeping it level.
Pull it toward your hip, keeping your elbow close and your shoulders square.
Lower it slowly until your arm is straight, then finish your reps and switch sides.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Barbell One Arm Floor Press
desc: A one-arm barbell press done lying on the floor, where the floor limits the range and puts the focus on the lockout. It trains the triceps and challenges your core to keep the bar balanced.
ins: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent and hold a barbell in one hand at its center, arm straight above your chest.
Use your free hand on the floor or on the bar's end to keep it level at first.
Breathe in and lower the bar until the back of your upper arm rests on the floor.
Breathe out and press the bar back up until your arm is straight.
Keep the bar level and your wrist straight; switch arms after your set.

name: Barbell One Arm Side Deadlift
desc: A one-hand deadlift with a barbell held at its center beside your leg, like carrying a suitcase. It works the glutes, hamstrings and quads while your core fights to keep you from leaning to the side.
ins: Place the bar beside one foot, running front to back, and stand next to its middle.
Squat down and grip the bar exactly at its center so it balances front to back.
Flatten your back, square your shoulders and brace your core.
Stand up by driving through your feet, keeping your torso straight and not tilting toward the bar.
Lower it the same way, hips back and knees bent, until it nearly touches the floor.
Breathe out as you stand; finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Barbell One Arm Snatch
desc: An explosive lift where you pull a barbell from the floor to overhead with one hand in a single fast movement. It trains shoulder power, the traps and full-body coordination, and needs a strong, stable core.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart over a light barbell and grip it in the middle with one hand.
Squat down with a flat back, chest up and your free arm out for balance.
Drive hard through your legs and extend your hips to send the bar upward close to your body.
Pull your elbow high, then punch your arm straight overhead as you drop into a quarter squat under the bar.
Stand up tall with the bar locked out and balanced over your shoulder.
Lower it under control to your shoulder, then to the floor, and switch hands after your set.

name: Barbell One Leg Squat
desc: A single-leg squat with a barbell on your upper back, often done down to a bench for safety. It builds strength and balance in the quads and glutes of one leg at a time.
ins: Set a bench behind you and rest a light bar on your upper back.
Shift your weight onto one leg and lift the other foot just off the floor in front of you.
Brace your core and slowly sit back and down on the standing leg until you touch the bench.
Keep your knee tracking over your toes and your chest up.
Drive through the heel of the standing leg to rise without pushing off with the free foot.
Breathe out as you stand; finish one side before switching.

name: Barbell Overhead Squat
desc: A squat with the barbell locked out overhead in a wide grip. It trains the quads and glutes while demanding strong shoulders, upper back, core and good ankle and hip mobility.
ins: Hold the bar overhead with a wide grip, arms straight and the bar over the middle of your feet.
Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out.
Push the bar up toward the ceiling and squeeze your shoulder blades so your arms stay locked.
Breathe in, brace and squat down slowly, keeping the bar directly over your feet.
Go only as deep as you can while the bar stays stable and your chest stays up, then stand.
Breathe out at the top; drop the bar behind you if you lose it.

name: Barbell Palms Down Wrist Curl Over A Bench
desc: A reverse wrist curl with a barbell, forearms resting on a bench and palms facing down. It strengthens the muscles on the top of the forearm that lift the back of the hand.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay your forearms across it with your wrists just past the edge.
Hold a light barbell with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar lower slowly so your knuckles point toward the floor.
Lift the back of your hands up as high as you can, moving only at the wrists.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly; keep your forearms pressed into the bench and breathe normally.

name: Barbell Palms Up Wrist Curl Over A Bench
desc: A barbell wrist curl with palms up and forearms supported on a bench. It builds the muscles on the inner forearm and improves grip.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and rest your forearms on it, wrists hanging over the edge.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms facing up.
Let the bar roll down toward your fingers while keeping hold of it.
Curl the bar back into your palm and then bend the wrists up as far as they go.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly without lifting your forearms off the bench.

name: Barbell Pendlay Row
desc: A strict bent-over barbell row where each rep starts from the floor with the back level. It builds power and thickness in the upper back.
ins: Stand with the barbell over your mid-foot and grip it overhand a little wider than your shoulders.
Hinge until your back is about level with the floor, knees bent and back flat.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and pull the bar quickly to your lower chest.
Keep your back angle the same and do not let your body rise.
Lower the bar back to the floor, let it settle, and reset before the next rep.

name: Barbell Pin Presses
desc: A bench press started from safety pins set just above your chest in a power rack. Pressing from a dead stop in the top half of the lift builds lockout strength, which relies heavily on the triceps.
ins: Set a flat bench in a power rack and place the pins a few centimeters above your chest when lying down.
Load the bar on the pins, lie under it and grip it about shoulder-width or a little wider.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and plant your feet.
Breathe out and press the bar off the pins until your arms are straight.
Lower it under control back onto the pins, let it settle fully, then press again.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
desc: A curl done on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the angled pad. The support stops you from cheating and keeps the biceps working through the bottom of the movement.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and rest the backs of your upper arms on the pad, armpits snug against its top.
Hold a barbell underhand at shoulder width with your arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Stop just before your forearms are vertical to keep tension on the biceps.
Breathe in and lower slowly, stopping just short of locking your elbows.

name: Barbell Press Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up where you hold a barbell on your chest and press it overhead as you reach the top. It works the abs hard and adds work for the shoulders and chest.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet anchored, holding a light barbell across your chest with an overhand grip.
Brace your abs and sit up in one smooth curl.
As you come up, press the bar straight above your head until your arms are locked out.
Lower the bar back to your chest and roll down slowly to the floor.
Breathe out as you sit up and press, and breathe in on the way down.

name: Barbell Prone Incline Curl
desc: A barbell curl done lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging in front. Because your upper arms hang vertically, the biceps work hardest at the top of the curl.
ins: Set a bench to about 45 degrees and lie chest-down on it with your feet on the floor.
Let your arms hang straight down and hold a barbell with an underhand shoulder-width grip.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your shoulders while your upper arms stay vertical.
Squeeze hard at the top for a second.
Lower slowly back to straight arms.

name: Barbell Pullover
desc: A lying barbell pullover that moves the bar from above the chest to behind the head and back. It stretches and strengthens the lats and also works the chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell above your chest with a shoulder-width grip.
Keep a small, fixed bend in your elbows and brace your stomach.
Lower the bar back over your head in a smooth arc until your arms are roughly in line with your body.
Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.
Pull the bar back over your chest along the same path.
Breathe in as the bar travels back and out as it returns.

name: Barbell Pullover To Press
desc: A lying barbell movement that joins a pullover with a close-grip press in one rep. The pullover stretches and works the lats, and the press brings in the chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your feet on the floor and hold a barbell over your chest with a grip about shoulder-width.
Bend your elbows and lower the bar back over your face and behind your head in an arc.
Stop when you feel a good stretch under your arms, keeping your lower back on the bench.
Pull the bar back over your face and lower it to your lower chest.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are straight to finish the rep.
Breathe in as the bar goes back and breathe out as you press.

name: Barbell Rack Pull
desc: A partial deadlift pulled from safety pins or blocks set around knee height. The shorter range lets you handle heavier loads to strengthen the lockout, the glutes, hamstrings and upper and lower back.
ins: Set the bar on rack pins or blocks just below or at knee level.
Stand close with the bar touching your legs and your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge to grip the bar just outside your legs, flatten your back and pull your shoulders down.
Breathe in, brace and drive your hips forward to stand up tall with the bar.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without leaning back.
Lower the bar back to the pins under control and breathe out after each rep.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
desc: A rear shoulder move where you hold a barbell behind your back and lift it away from your body. It works the rear delts along with the traps and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Stand tall and hold a light barbell behind your hips with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Lean forward very slightly from the hips and keep your arms straight.
Breathe out and lift the bar backward and up, away from your body, by squeezing your shoulder blades.
Stop when you feel the back of your shoulders working hard; the range is short.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly back to your hips.

name: Barbell Rear Delt Row
desc: A bent-over barbell row with a wide grip and flared elbows that shifts the work to the rear shoulders. The upper back and biceps help.
ins: Hold a barbell with an overhand grip wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees a little and hinge forward until your chest is close to level with the floor, back flat.
Breathe out and pull the bar toward your upper chest, keeping your elbows out wide.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar until your arms are straight, without rounding your back.

name: Barbell Rear Lunge
desc: A lunge where you step backward instead of forward while holding a barbell on your upper back. Stepping back is easier on the knees and works the glutes and quads of the front leg.
ins: Take the bar on your upper back from a rack and stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot well back, landing on the ball of the foot.
Bend both knees and lower until the back knee hovers just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee over your ankle.
Drive through the front heel and step the back foot forward to stand.
Alternate legs each rep, breathing in on the way down and out on the way up.

name: Barbell Rear Lunge (Same Leg, Forward Lean)
desc: A reverse lunge with a barbell on your upper back, done for all reps on one leg before switching, with a slight forward lean. Staying on one side and hinging a little keeps constant tension on the front leg's glute.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and land on the ball of that foot.
Lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, letting your chest lean slightly forward over the front thigh.
Keep most of your weight in the front heel.
Push through the front heel to bring the back foot forward to the start.
Repeat on the same leg for all reps, then switch, breathing out as you rise.

name: Barbell Reverse Close-Grip Bench Press
desc: A close-grip barbell bench press using an underhand grip. Turning the palms toward you keeps the elbows tight to the body, shifting work to the triceps and upper chest.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar underhand with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and plant your feet.
Unrack the bar with straight arms over your chest; use a spotter, as this grip is less secure.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and press the bar back up until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Reverse Curl
desc: A barbell curl done with an overhand grip, palms facing down. It shifts more work to the forearms and the brachialis while still training the biceps.
ins: Stand tall holding a barbell with palms facing down at shoulder width, arms straight.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your wrists flat in line with your forearms.
Breathe out and curl the bar up until your forearms point toward the ceiling.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly to the starting position without letting your shoulders roll forward.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over barbell row using an underhand grip, which lets the elbows stay close and brings the biceps in more. It trains the upper back and lats.
ins: Hold the bar with your palms facing forward, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips to about 45 degrees, knees soft and back flat.
Let the bar hang at arm's length in front of your knees.
Pull the bar to your lower stomach, keeping your elbows tucked by your sides.
Squeeze your back at the top, then lower slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Decline Bench Press
desc: A decline barbell bench press with an underhand grip, palms facing your head. It targets the lower chest and triceps and needs a spotter because the grip is less secure.
ins: Secure your feet on a decline bench and lie back under the bar.
Grip the bar underhand, slightly wider than shoulder width, and have a spotter help you unrack it.
Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up to straight arms in a steady line.
Keep your thumbs wrapped around the bar, breathe out on the press and rack it with your spotter's help.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench Press
desc: An incline barbell press with an underhand grip that strongly targets the upper chest. Because the grip feels unusual, it is best done with moderate weight and a spotter.
ins: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie back under the bar with your feet flat.
Grip the bar underhand about shoulder-width apart and unrack it with a spotter's help.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, elbows tucked close to your sides.
Press the bar back up over your shoulders.
Keep your wrists straight and breathe out as you press.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench Row
desc: A chest-supported barbell row on an incline bench using an underhand grip. It builds the upper back and puts extra work on the biceps.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie face down on it with your chest on the pad.
Hold a barbell below you with palms facing forward, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar toward your lower ribs, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight again.

name: Barbell Reverse Grip Skullcrusher
desc: A lying barbell triceps extension done with an underhand grip. Turning the palms toward you changes the feel at the elbow and wrist and still isolates the triceps, with the forearms working to hold the bar.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell over your chest with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your upper arms vertical and your elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar slowly toward your forehead.
Stop just above your forehead without letting your elbows drift out.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press the bar back up.

name: Barbell Reverse Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl done with an overhand grip on a barbell. The pad locks your upper arms in place so the forearms and brachialis take on more of the work alongside the biceps.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench with the backs of your upper arms flat on the pad.
Hold a barbell with palms facing down at shoulder width, arms almost straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms.
Stop when your forearms are near vertical.
Lower slowly and with control; use a lighter weight than for a normal preacher curl.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A seated forearm exercise where you raise a barbell by bending the wrists backward with your palms facing down. It targets the muscles on the top of the forearm that also help with grip and elbow health.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat and knees bent at about a right angle.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, palms down, and rest your forearms along your thighs.
Slide forward until your wrists are just past your knees.
Breathe out and raise your knuckles up as high as your wrists allow.
Pause briefly, then breathe in and let the bar sink back down under control.
Use a light weight; your forearms should not lift off your legs.

name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl (Kneeling Over Bench)
desc: A kneeling version of the reverse wrist curl where your forearms rest on a flat bench and you lift a barbell with the backs of your hands. It builds the top of the forearm and the wrist extensors.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay your forearms across it, hands just past the edge.
Hold a light barbell with an overhand grip, palms facing the floor, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let your wrists bend down so the bar hangs below the bench line.
Breathe out and lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling, moving only at the wrists.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and lower the bar slowly.
Keep your forearms pressed into the bench the whole time.

name: Barbell Rollerout
desc: A kneeling rollout with a loaded barbell, used like an ab wheel. It trains the abs to resist arching while the lower back stays stable.
ins: Kneel on a mat with a barbell loaded with round plates on the floor in front of your knees.
Grip the bar at shoulder width with your shoulders stacked over it.
Brace your abs and roll the bar forward slowly, letting your hips follow.
Go only as far as you can keep your lower back from sagging.
Breathe out and pull the bar back under your shoulders using your abs.

name: Barbell Rollerout From Bench
desc: An advanced rollout where you kneel on a bench and roll a loaded barbell out along the floor. The raised start makes the abs work harder to keep your back from sagging, with the shoulders and triceps helping.
ins: Load a barbell with round plates on the floor in front of a flat bench and kneel on the end of the bench.
Hold the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip, arms straight under your shoulders.
Brace your abs, tuck your hips slightly and roll the bar forward as far as you can control.
Keep your back flat and do not let your hips drop toward the floor.
Pull the bar back toward the bench with your abs, breathing out as you return.

name: Barbell Seated Behind Head Military Press
desc: A seated overhead press where the barbell is lowered behind your head instead of in front. It hits the side and front shoulders hard and needs good shoulder mobility, so use a light weight.
ins: Sit on an upright bench with your feet flat and take the bar from the rack onto your upper back, hands wider than shoulder width.
Sit tall, brace your stomach and keep your head slightly forward.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up until your arms are straight.
Breathe in and lower it slowly behind your head to about ear level, not lower.
Stop the set if you feel any pinching in the shoulder.

name: Barbell Seated Bradford Rocky Press
desc: A seated press where the barbell travels from the front of your shoulders, just over your head, to behind your neck and back again. It keeps steady tension on the shoulders because the arms never fully lock out.
ins: Sit tall on a bench and hold a barbell at your upper chest with an overhand grip a bit wider than your shoulders.
Brace your stomach and keep your feet flat.
Press the bar up just high enough to clear the top of your head.
Lower it behind your head to the top of your neck.
Press it back over your head and lower it to the front of your shoulders.
Keep the movement smooth and breathe out on every press.

name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise
desc: A seated calf raise with a barbell resting across your lower thighs. Because the knees stay bent, it focuses on the deeper calf muscle under the main calf.
ins: Sit on a bench and place the balls of your feet on a weight plate or low block, heels hanging off.
Rest a padded barbell across your thighs just above your knees and hold it in place.
Let your heels sink below the block for a full stretch.
Breathe out and push through the balls of your feet to lift your heels as high as you can.
Squeeze at the top for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly back to the stretch.

name: Barbell Seated Calf Raise (Hip-Width Stance)
desc: A barbell calf raise done sitting, with the bar across your knees to load the calves. The bent-knee position shifts more of the work to the deep calf muscle.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench with your feet hip-width apart and toes on a raised plate.
Place a barbell, wrapped in a pad or towel, across the bottom of your thighs and steady it with your hands.
Lower your heels toward the floor until you feel the calves stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Pause at the top, keeping your feet straight.
Breathe in and lower under control.

name: Barbell Seated Close Grip Behind Neck Triceps Extension
desc: A seated overhead triceps extension with a barbell held in a narrow grip and lowered behind your neck. The overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps, making it a strong builder for the back of the arm.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a barbell overhead with your hands about a fist apart, palms facing forward.
Point your elbows toward the ceiling and keep them close to your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar slowly behind your neck.
Stop when you feel a deep stretch in the back of your arms, without letting the elbows flare.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift the bar back overhead.

name: Barbell Seated Close-Grip Concentration Curl
desc: A seated concentration curl with a barbell held at a narrow grip, elbows braced against the inner thighs. Bracing the arms keeps the effort on the biceps.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wide and lean forward slightly.
Hold a barbell underhand with your hands close together and rest the backs of your arms against your inner thighs.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest without moving your elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Seated Good Morning
desc: A good morning done sitting on a bench with the barbell on your upper back, bending forward from the hips and back up. Sitting removes the legs from the lift so the lower back, glutes and hamstrings do the work.
ins: Sit at the end of a flat bench with your feet wide and flat on the floor.
Rest a light bar on your upper back and hold it just outside your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your back flat and your chest up.
Lean forward from the hips, bringing your chest toward the bench as far as your back stays flat.
Squeeze your glutes and lower back to rise back to upright.
Breathe in as you lean forward and out as you sit up.

name: Barbell Seated Overhead Press
desc: A seated barbell press from the front of the shoulders to overhead. Sitting takes the legs out of it so the shoulders and triceps do the work.
ins: Sit on an upright bench with back support and hold the bar at your upper chest, hands just outside shoulder width.
Plant your feet, brace your stomach and keep your back against the pad.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly so it passes your face.
Finish with your arms straight and the bar over the middle of your head.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your upper chest.

name: Barbell Seated Overhead Triceps Extension
desc: A seated overhead triceps extension with a barbell, where you lower the bar behind your head and press it back up. Working overhead puts the long head of the triceps on a deep stretch.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a barbell overhead with a narrow overhand grip.
Keep your elbows close to your head and pointing forward.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Go down until you feel a stretch in the back of your arms.
Breathe out and straighten your arms back overhead, keeping your back against the pad.

name: Barbell Seated Twist
desc: A seated rotation with a barbell resting across your upper back. It works the obliques and abs, with the lower back holding you upright.
ins: Sit on the end of a flat bench with your feet planted and a light barbell resting on your upper back.
Hold the bar wide with both hands and sit tall.
Keeping your hips still, turn your shoulders to one side in a controlled motion.
Return to the middle and turn to the other side.
Keep the pace slow and steady; do not swing the bar.

name: Barbell Shrug
desc: A standing barbell shrug that lifts the shoulders straight up toward the ears. It builds the upper traps and also strengthens the grip.
ins: Stand tall holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip just outside your hips.
Keep your arms straight and your chin level.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second and squeeze your traps.
Lower your shoulders all the way down slowly for a full stretch.
Avoid rolling your shoulders; move straight up and down.

name: Barbell Side Bend
desc: A standing side bend with a barbell held across your upper back. It strengthens the obliques and the muscles along the lower back.
ins: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and a light barbell resting across your upper back.
Hold the bar with both hands and brace your abs.
Bend straight sideways to the right, keeping your chest facing forward.
Use the left side of your waist to pull yourself back to upright.
Repeat to the left, and avoid leaning forward or twisting.

name: Barbell Side Split Squat
desc: A side split squat with a barbell on your back, staying in a wide stance and lowering toward one leg for a full set before switching. It loads the quads and glutes of the bent leg and stretches the inner thigh of the straight one.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back and take a wide stance, toes turned slightly out.
Brace your core and keep your chest tall.
Bend one knee and sit your hips back toward that heel while the other leg stays straight.
Lower until the working thigh is near parallel, keeping its knee in line with your toes.
Press through that foot to rise back to the wide stance.
Complete all reps on that side, then switch, breathing out as you push up.

name: Barbell Side Split Squat (Alternating)
desc: A wide-stance side squat with a barbell on your back where you shift from one side to the other every rep. The alternating pattern trains the quads, glutes and inner thighs of both legs and builds lateral hip mobility.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back and stand with your feet about twice shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Shift your hips toward one foot, bending that knee while the other leg stays straight.
Lower until the bent thigh is close to parallel with the floor, keeping your chest up and that heel down.
Push through the bent leg to return to the center.
Shift straight into the same movement on the other side.
Keep alternating, breathing in as you lower and out as you push back.

name: Barbell Single Leg Deadlift
desc: A one-leg hip hinge holding a barbell, with the free leg reaching straight back. It builds the glutes and hamstrings of the standing leg and demands strong balance and a steady lower back.
ins: Stand on your right leg holding a light barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Keep a small bend in the right knee.
Breathe in and hinge forward at the hips while your left leg lifts straight behind you.
Keep your hips square to the floor and your back flat as the bar slides down toward your shin.
Breathe out and drive the right hip forward to stand, lowering the back leg.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Barbell Single Leg Split Squat
desc: A split squat with your rear foot raised on a bench and a barbell on your upper back, often called a Bulgarian split squat. It builds the quads and glutes of the front leg and challenges balance.
ins: Stand about two steps in front of a bench with the bar on your upper back.
Reach one foot back and rest its top on the bench.
Lower straight down by bending the front knee until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Keep your torso upright and the front knee tracking over the middle of your foot.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up.
Breathe out as you rise; finish all reps before switching legs.

name: Barbell Sitted Alternate Leg Raise
desc: A seated leg raise where a light barbell resting across your thighs adds load as you lift one straight leg at a time. It works the lower abs and the hip flexors.
ins: Sit tall on the end of a bench with a light barbell resting across your lower thighs, holding it in place with both hands.
Lean back very slightly and tighten your abs, keeping your back straight.
Straighten one leg and lift it as high as you can, pressing that thigh up against the bar.
Breathe out as you lift, then lower the foot slowly back to the floor.
Switch legs on each rep.

name: Barbell Sitted Alternate Leg Raise (Pause at Top)
desc: A seated alternating leg raise with a light barbell across your thighs for extra resistance, keeping each raised leg straight and controlled. It trains the lower abs and hip flexors and also works the front of the thigh to keep the knee locked.
ins: Sit upright near the edge of a bench, rest a light barbell across your thighs and steady it with your hands.
Brace your abs and keep your chest lifted.
Lock one knee straight and raise that leg until it is about level with the bench.
Hold for a moment, breathing out, then lower it slowly without letting it drop.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating each time.

name: Barbell Skier
desc: A dynamic straight-arm move where you drive your hips forward and sweep a barbell up in front of you, like pushing off with ski poles. It works the front shoulders, with the triceps and core helping.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a light barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip.
Soften the knees and push your hips back, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward and swing the bar up in front of you with straight arms to about eye level.
Control the bar at the top without leaning back.
Let it swing back down as you hinge again and flow straight into the next rep.

name: Barbell Speed Squat
desc: A back squat with a light barbell where you lower under control and stand up as fast as possible. It trains rate of force development in the glutes and quads and sharpens squat technique.
ins: Load the bar to roughly half of what you would normally squat and set it on your upper back.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and brace your core.
Lower at a steady, controlled pace to your normal squat depth.
Without bouncing, reverse and drive up as fast as you can while keeping good form.
Finish tall without letting the bar leave your back.
Breathe in before each rep and out at the top; keep sets short so every rep stays fast.

name: Barbell Split Squat (Bar at Hips)
desc: A split squat holding a barbell at arm's length in front of your hips instead of on your back. Carrying the bar low keeps the setup simple and works the quads and glutes, with the hamstrings, inner thighs, calves and abs helping.
ins: Deadlift a barbell up to your hips with an overhand grip just outside your thighs.
Step one foot forward into a long split stance, back heel raised.
Keep your arms straight, your shoulders back and the bar level.
Breathe in and lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor.
Breathe out and drive through the front foot to rise, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Finish the set, then switch the front leg.

name: Barbell Split Squat (Bar on Back)
desc: A split squat with the barbell across the upper back, staying in a fixed split stance. It builds the quads and glutes of the front leg, with the hamstrings and calves helping you balance.
ins: Unrack a barbell onto your upper back and step back from the rack.
Step one foot forward into a long stance, back heel lifted and feet about hip-width apart side to side.
Breathe in, brace and lower your back knee straight toward the floor.
Keep your torso upright and the front knee in line with the toes.
Breathe out and push through the front heel to rise without stepping.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Barbell Squat (on Knees)
desc: A kneeling squat: you kneel with a barbell on your upper back, sit your hips back toward your heels and drive them forward to tall kneeling. It isolates the hip drive, working the glutes along with the quads and hamstrings.
ins: Put a pad or folded mat under your knees inside a rack and set the bar at a height you can reach while kneeling.
Kneel with your knees hip-width apart, rest the bar on your upper back and hold it firmly.
Brace your core and sit your hips back toward your heels, keeping your chest up.
Go down until your glutes are just above your heels.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward until you are kneeling tall.
Breathe in as you sit back and out as you drive up.

name: Barbell Squat Jump Rear Lunge (No Step)
desc: A barbell combo performed on flat ground: a squat jump in place, then a step back into a reverse lunge. It develops power and strength in the quads and glutes, with the hamstrings and calves working throughout.
ins: Rest a light barbell across your upper back and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace and lower into a squat.
Breathe out and jump straight up, holding the bar firmly against your back.
Land softly with bent knees and sink right into the next movement.
Step one foot back into a reverse lunge, then push through the front foot to stand.
Repeat, alternating the lunge leg.

name: Barbell Squat Jump Step Rear Lunge
desc: An explosive combo with a barbell on the back: a squat jump onto a low step, followed by stepping back down into a reverse lunge. It builds quad and glute power and works the hamstrings, calves, inner thighs and abs; it needs a light bar and good control.
ins: Place a light barbell on your upper back and stand about a foot in front of a low, stable step.
Brace your stomach and dip into a quarter squat.
Jump up and forward onto the step, landing softly on both feet with knees bent.
Step back down to the floor one foot at a time.
Step one foot back into a reverse lunge, lower with control, then push back to standing.
Reset and repeat, switching the lunge leg each time.

name: Barbell Standing Ab Rollerout
desc: A very advanced rollout started from standing, where you roll a loaded barbell out until your body is nearly flat. It demands strong abs plus stable shoulders and lower back.
ins: Stand behind a barbell loaded with round plates, then bend down and grip it at shoulder width with straight arms.
Brace your abs hard and round your upper back slightly.
Roll the bar forward slowly, keeping your hips in line and your knees straight.
Stop at the furthest point you can hold without your lower back sagging.
Pull the bar back toward your feet with your abs until you return to the start, breathing out on the way back.

name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
desc: A standing wrist curl done with the barbell held behind your back. It works the forearm flexors that close the wrist and support a strong grip.
ins: Stand tall with a barbell behind you, held at arm's length against the back of your thighs.
Grip it with your palms facing backward and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar roll down toward your fingers so your wrists open.
Breathe out and curl the bar back up by bending your wrists toward your forearms.
Keep your arms straight and still; only the wrists move.
Lower slowly and breathe in on the way down.

name: Barbell Standing Bradford Press
desc: A standing press where the barbell moves in a short arc from the front of your shoulders, over your head, to behind your neck and back. It keeps the shoulders under constant tension.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell at your upper chest with a grip a bit wider than your shoulders.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your lower back stays neutral.
Press the bar up just enough to pass over your head and lower it behind your neck.
Press it back over your head and bring it down to the front again.
Breathe out on each press and keep the bar close to your head.

name: Barbell Standing Close Grip Curl
desc: A standing barbell curl with the hands set narrower than shoulder width, which tends to bring more of the outer biceps into play.
ins: Stand tall and hold a barbell underhand with your hands about 15 cm apart.
Let the bar hang against your thighs and keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your upper chest.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning back.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Barbell Standing Close Grip Military Press
desc: A standing barbell press with your hands closer than shoulder width. The narrow grip puts more work on the front shoulders and triceps.
ins: Take the bar from a rack at upper chest height with your hands just inside shoulder width.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, elbows slightly in front of the bar, stomach braced.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly so it clears your face.
Finish with arms straight and the bar over the middle of your head.
Breathe in and lower it slowly to your upper chest.

name: Barbell Standing Concentration Curl
desc: A barbell curl done bent forward at the hips with the arms hanging straight down, so the upper arms can't help. It works like a concentration curl for both biceps at once.
ins: Hold a barbell underhand at shoulder width and stand with your feet wider than your hips.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward until your torso is close to parallel with the floor, arms hanging straight down.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your chest, keeping your upper arms pointing at the floor.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping your back flat throughout.

name: Barbell Standing Front Raise Over Head
desc: A front raise that keeps going past shoulder height until the barbell is overhead. It works the front shoulders through a long range and also involves the upper back.
ins: Stand tall and hold a light barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Brace your stomach and keep your arms straight with soft elbows.
Breathe out and lift the bar in front of you, past shoulder height, until it is over your head.
Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar along the same path to your thighs.

name: Barbell Standing Leg Calf Raise
desc: A standing barbell calf raise performed with the balls of your feet on a raised edge. The extra range lets you stretch and squeeze the calves fully.
ins: Set a barbell on your upper back as you would for a squat and step onto a sturdy block or plate with the balls of your feet.
Stand tall with your knees straight but not locked, feet hip-width apart.
Lower your heels below the edge until the calves stretch.
Breathe out and drive up onto your toes as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Keep your body upright and avoid bouncing at the bottom.

name: Barbell Standing Reverse Grip Curl
desc: A standing barbell curl with a reverse, palms-down grip. It strengthens the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the bar with palms down at shoulder width.
Tuck your elbows against your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar to shoulder height, keeping your knuckles facing up.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to your thighs.

name: Barbell Standing Rocking Leg Calf Raise
desc: A barbell calf exercise where you rock from your heels onto your toes in one smooth motion. Lifting the toes trains the front of the shin, and rising onto the toes trains the calves.
ins: Rest a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet hip-width apart on flat ground.
Shift your weight back onto your heels and lift your toes off the floor.
Rock forward and rise up high onto the balls of your feet.
Pause briefly at the top, then rock back through flat feet onto your heels again.
Keep your body straight and move from the ankles, not the hips.
Breathe steadily and use a light weight until the rhythm feels stable.

name: Barbell Standing Twist
desc: A standing twist with a light barbell on your upper back. It warms up and trains the obliques while the lower back keeps the spine tall.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, knees soft, and a light barbell resting across your upper back.
Hold the bar wide and brace your abs.
Turn your shoulders to one side while your hips stay facing forward.
Rotate back through the middle to the other side.
Move with control rather than momentum and keep breathing.

name: Barbell Standing Wide Grip Biceps Curl
desc: A standing barbell curl with your hands set wider than shoulder-width. The wide grip tends to emphasize the inner, short head of the biceps.
ins: Stand tall and grip a barbell underhand with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Let the bar hang at your thighs with your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest without leaning back.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Standing Wide Military Press
desc: A standing barbell press with a grip much wider than your shoulders. The wide grip shortens the press and shifts more work to the side shoulders.
ins: Take the bar from a rack at upper chest height with your hands well outside shoulder width.
Stand with feet hip-width apart, squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your upper chest.

name: Barbell Standing Wide-Grip Curl
desc: A standing barbell curl with the hands placed wider than shoulder width, which puts more emphasis on the inner part of the biceps.
ins: Stand tall holding a barbell underhand with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Keep your elbows by your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without lifting your elbows.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to the start.

name: Barbell Step-Up
desc: Stepping up onto a box or bench with a barbell across your upper back. It trains the glutes and quads of the stepping leg and builds single-leg balance.
ins: Stand facing a sturdy box or bench about knee height with a light bar on your upper back.
Place one whole foot firmly on the top of the box.
Lean slightly forward and drive through that heel to stand up on the box.
Bring the trailing foot up only at the end, without pushing off with it.
Step down slowly with the trailing foot first, controlling the descent with the top leg.
Breathe out as you step up; alternate legs or finish one side first.

name: Barbell Stiff Leg Good Morning
desc: A good morning done with your knees nearly straight, which puts a strong stretch and load on the hamstrings. It also strengthens the glutes and lower back and suits experienced lifters with good hamstring flexibility.
ins: Rest a light bar on your upper back and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Straighten your legs, leaving only a tiny bend so your knees are not locked hard.
Brace your core and set your back flat.
Hinge forward by pushing your hips back until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Breathe in as you fold and out as you rise; stop short if your back starts to round.

name: Barbell Sumo Deadlift
desc: A deadlift with a very wide stance and your hands gripping the bar inside your legs. The upright torso shares the work between the glutes, quads, hamstrings and inner thighs while easing stress on the lower back.
ins: Stand with your feet much wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out, and the bar over your mid-foot.
Push your knees out over your toes and grip the bar with your hands inside your legs, about shoulder-width apart.
Drop your hips, lift your chest and flatten your back; take a big breath and brace.
Push the floor apart with your feet and stand up, keeping the bar close to your body.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes, then lower the bar the same way.
Breathe out at the top or once the bar is back down.

name: Barbell Thruster
desc: A barbell front squat that drives straight into an overhead press in one movement. It works the shoulders, legs and glutes together and is a demanding full-body exercise.
ins: Hold a barbell at the front of your shoulders with a grip just outside shoulder width, elbows up, feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and squat down with your chest up until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Drive up hard through your whole foot.
As your hips straighten, carry that drive into pressing the bar overhead, breathing out.
Lower the bar to your shoulders as you sink into the next squat.

name: Barbell Upright Row
desc: A classic barbell upright row where you pull the bar from your thighs to chest height with your elbows leading. It builds the side shoulders and traps.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip a little narrower than your shoulders.
Stand tall with your stomach tight.
Breathe out and raise your elbows up and out, pulling the bar up close to your body.
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height and the bar is at your chest.
Breathe in and lower the bar under control.

name: Barbell Upright Row (Close Grip)
desc: An upright row done with a close grip, pulling the barbell up the front of your body toward your chin. It works the side shoulders and traps, with the biceps helping.
ins: Stand tall and hold a barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip, hands about a fist apart.
Brace your stomach and keep the bar close to your body.
Breathe out and lead with your elbows to pull the bar up to your upper chest.
Keep your elbows higher than your wrists at the top and stop if your shoulders pinch.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your thighs.

name: Barbell Upright Row (Shoulder-Width Grip)
desc: A shoulder-friendly upright row with a shoulder-width grip and a shorter pull that stops at the lower chest. It targets the side shoulders while going easier on the shoulder joint.
ins: Hold a barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Stand tall, brace your stomach and relax your neck.
Breathe out and pull your elbows out to the sides, lifting the bar to your lower chest.
Pause briefly with your elbows level with your shoulders, not above them.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Barbell Weightlifting Complex
desc: A barbell complex that links a power clean, a front squat and a push press into one continuous set. It builds whole-body power and strength, led by the quads and glutes with the shoulders, traps and abs working hard.
ins: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, grip it just outside your legs and set a flat back.
Pull the bar from the floor, extend your hips explosively and catch it on the front of your shoulders in a partial squat.
From that position, breathe in and squat all the way down with elbows high, then stand up.
Dip your knees slightly and drive up with your legs to push the bar overhead, locking your arms.
Lower the bar to your shoulders, then to your hips and back to the floor under control.
Rest briefly and repeat the whole sequence.

name: Barbell Wide Bench Press
desc: A flat barbell bench press with the hands set well outside shoulder width. The wide grip puts more stretch and load on the chest and less on the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted and grip the bar about one and a half times shoulder width.
Set your shoulder blades back and down, then unrack the bar over your chest.
Lower the bar slowly to the middle of your chest, letting your elbows travel out to the sides.
Press back up powerfully until your arms are straight but not forcefully locked.
Inhale on the descent and exhale as you drive up; keep the weight moderate to protect your shoulders.

name: Barbell Wide Reverse Grip Bench Press
desc: A flat barbell bench press with a wide underhand grip, an advanced variation that loads the chest, especially the upper part. The unusual grip needs light weight and a spotter.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet planted.
Take an underhand grip clearly wider than your shoulders and unrack the bar with a spotter.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Press it back up until your arms are extended, keeping the bar steady.
Start with a light weight, breathe out on each press and keep your back on the bench.

name: Barbell Wide Squat
desc: A back squat with a stance wider than shoulder-width and toes turned out. The wide position brings in more glutes and inner thighs alongside the quads.
ins: Set the bar on your upper back from a rack and step out.
Place your feet well wider than your shoulders with your toes turned out to match.
Breathe in, brace and squat down, pushing your knees out in line with your toes.
Keep your shins fairly vertical and your chest up as you reach parallel or a bit below.
Drive up through your heels and mid-foot to stand.
Breathe out at the top.

name: Barbell Wide-Grip Upright Row
desc: An upright row with a wide grip, which puts more of the load on the side shoulders and less on the traps. It is usually easier on the shoulder joint than a narrow grip.
ins: Hold a barbell at your thighs with an overhand grip about one and a half times shoulder width.
Stand tall with your stomach braced and chest up.
Breathe out and drive your elbows out to the sides to lift the bar toward your lower chest.
Stop when your upper arms are level with the floor.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your thighs.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl
desc: The classic seated barbell wrist curl with palms facing up. It builds the inner forearm muscles that bend the wrist and help you hold heavy weights.
ins: Sit at the end of a bench with your feet flat and rest your forearms on your thighs.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, palms up, so your wrists sit just past your knees.
Open your hands slightly and let the bar roll down toward your fingertips.
Close your fingers and breathe out as you curl your wrists up as high as possible.
Pause at the top, then breathe in and lower under control.
Keep your forearms flat on your legs the whole set.

name: Barbell Wrist Curl (Kneeling Over Bench)
desc: A kneeling barbell wrist curl with your forearms supported on a flat bench and palms facing up. It isolates the forearm flexors on the inner side of the arm.
ins: Kneel next to a flat bench and lay your forearms across it with your hands hanging off the far side.
Hold a barbell with your palms up and hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar lower toward the floor so your wrists bend back.
Breathe out and curl your palms up toward you as far as they go.
Squeeze for a moment, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Keep your elbows and forearms pinned to the bench.

name: Barbell Zercher Squat
desc: A squat with the barbell held in the crook of your elbows in front of your body. It works the glutes and quads hard while making the upper back and core work to keep you upright.
ins: Set the bar in a rack at about the height of your lower ribs.
Hook the bar in the bend of both elbows, clasp your hands together and pull it close to your body.
Lift it off, step back and set your feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in, brace and squat down, keeping your chest up and your upper back tight.
Go as low as you can with a flat back, then drive up through your feet.
Breathe out at the top; pad the bar if it hurts your arms.

name: Basic Toe Touch
desc: A simple standing stretch where you fold forward from the hips and reach toward your toes. It lengthens the hamstrings and calves and gently stretches the glutes and lower back.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Breathe in and raise your arms overhead.
Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, reaching your hands down toward your toes.
Let your head and neck relax and bend your knees a little if you cannot reach comfortably.
Hold for a few breaths, then roll up slowly to standing.

name: Battling Ropes
desc: A conditioning drill where you whip two heavy ropes up and down in fast waves. It raises your heart rate while working the shoulders, grip and core.
ins: Stand facing the anchor and hold one rope end in each hand with the ropes slightly slack.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart, bend your knees and hips into a half squat, and brace your stomach.
Move your arms up and down quickly, one after the other, to send waves down the ropes.
Keep the movement coming from your shoulders and keep your back flat.
Breathe steadily and keep going for the set time, then rest.

name: Bayesian Curl (cable)
desc: A standing curl with a straight bar on a low cable. The cable keeps tension on the biceps through the whole movement.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing it, close enough that the cable runs straight up.
Hold the bar underhand at shoulder width with your arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your chest, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Bear Crawl
desc: Crawling forward on hands and feet with the knees hovering just off the ground. It challenges the core, shoulders and coordination while raising the heart rate.
ins: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck your toes and lift your knees about a hand's width off the floor.
Move your right hand and left foot forward a short step at the same time.
Then move your left hand and right foot forward.
Keep your back flat, hips low and knees off the floor, and breathe steadily as you crawl.

name: Behind Head Chest Stretch
desc: A simple standing stretch with your hands laced behind your head, opening the elbows and chest backward. It relieves tightness in the chest and the front of the shoulders.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and lace your fingers behind your head.
Point your elbows out to the sides.
Draw your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together, lifting your chest.
Hold the stretch for about 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Relax and repeat two or three times without pushing your head forward.

name: Bench Dip (knees Bent)
desc: A beginner-friendly dip using a bench behind you, with knees bent and feet flat on the floor so your legs share some of the load. It builds the triceps.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands beside your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Walk your feet out until your hips are just off the bench, knees bent at about 90 degrees.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor, keeping your back close to the bench.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Bench Dip On Floor
desc: A beginner dip with your hands on a bench behind you and your feet on the floor with knees bent. It builds the triceps while the chest and front shoulders help.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench, put your hands next to your hips with fingers forward, and plant your feet on the floor with knees bent.
Lift your hips off the bench and move them just in front of it so your arms hold your weight.
Bend your elbows straight back and lower your hips toward the floor until your elbows reach about a right angle.
Keep your back close to the bench and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms and breathe out as you rise.

name: Bench Hip Extension
desc: A body-weight hip extension where you lie face down on a bench with your hips at the end and lift your straight legs behind you. It strengthens the glutes and hamstrings with little load on the spine.
ins: Lie face down on a flat bench so your hips are at the end and your legs hang toward the floor.
Hold the sides of the bench to keep your upper body still.
Squeeze your glutes and lift both legs together until they are in line with your body.
Keep your legs straight and do not swing or arch your lower back to get higher.
Lower your legs slowly until your feet are close to the floor.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Bench Press (Dumbbell)
desc: A bench press on a flat bench using a dumbbell in each hand. It builds the chest, triceps and front shoulders, and lets each arm work on its own through a deeper range than a barbell.
ins: Sit on a flat bench with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them up beside your chest.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Lower them slowly until they are level with your chest and your elbows sit just below the bench.
Press back up, letting the dumbbells move slightly toward each other at the top.
Keep your feet flat and shoulder blades pulled back; breathe in on the way down and out on the press.

name: Bench Pull-Ups
desc: A beginner pulling exercise lying under a bar that rests across two benches, pulling your chest up to it. It trains the lats and upper back with your own body weight.
ins: Lay a sturdy bar across two benches so it is stable, and lie on your back under it.
Grip the bar overhand a little wider than your shoulders.
Straighten your legs or bend your knees and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Breathe out and pull your chest up to the bar.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Bent Knee Lying Twist
desc: A gentle lying twist where you let both bent knees fall slowly from side to side. It loosens the lower back and hips and stretches the glutes and the sides of the waist.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and together.
Stretch your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms down.
Breathe out and let both knees lower slowly to the right while your shoulders stay on the floor.
Pause when you feel a comfortable stretch, then breathe in and bring the knees back to the middle using your stomach.
Lower them to the left and keep alternating slowly.

name: Bent Over One Arm Row (Cable)
ref: Cable One Arm Bent Over Row
desc: A one-arm cable row done bent forward, so the cable keeps tension on the back through the whole pull. It works the upper back and lats, with help from the biceps and forearms.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley and hold it in one hand.
Step back, stagger your feet and hinge forward with a flat back, resting your free hand on your knee.
Let your working arm reach toward the pulley with a slight stretch in your back.
Row the handle to your hip, keeping your elbow close and your torso still.
Return slowly to the stretch, then finish your reps and switch arms.
Breathe out as you row and in as you reach.

name: Bent Over One Arm Row (Dumbbell)
desc: A one-arm dumbbell row with one hand and knee supported on a bench, a staple for building the lats and upper back. The biceps and forearms help.
ins: Put one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, with your other foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in your free hand with your arm straight below your shoulder.
Keep your back flat and parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower it slowly until your arm is straight, then switch sides after your set.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Bent Over Row (Barbell)
desc: A classic free-weight row where you hinge forward and pull a barbell to your body. It builds thickness in the upper back and lats, with the biceps and grip working hard too.
ins: Hold the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width, feet hip-width apart.
Soften your knees and push your hips back until your chest leans well forward, back flat.
Let the bar hang under your shoulders with straight arms and a tight stomach.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight, without standing up.
Breathe out as you pull and breathe in as you lower.

name: Bent Over Row (Dumbbell)
desc: A bent-over row with a dumbbell in each hand, pulling both at once. It builds the upper back and lats and lets each arm move freely, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge forward from the hips with soft knees until your chest is well forward and your back is flat.
Let the dumbbells hang under your shoulders with your palms facing each other.
Row both dumbbells up to your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower them slowly to straight arms without standing up.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Bent Over Row (Plate loaded)
desc: A row on a chest-supported T-bar machine where you lie face down on the angled pad. It builds upper back thickness while protecting the lower back.
ins: Step onto the foot platform and lie with your chest on the angled pad.
Take the handles with a grip that feels natural and let your arms hang straight.
Pull the handles up toward your chest by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Bicep Curl (Barbell)
desc: The classic standing curl with a straight barbell. It is a basic mass builder for the biceps that also works the forearms.
