ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold the bar with palms facing forward, hands about shoulder width.
Let the bar hang against your thighs and tuck your elbows to your sides.
Breathe out and bend your elbows to bring the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Bicep Curl (Cable)
desc: A standing curl with a straight bar on a low cable. The cable keeps tension on the biceps through the whole movement.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing it, close enough that the cable runs straight up.
Hold the bar underhand at shoulder width with your arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your chest, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Bicep Curl (Dumbbell)
desc: A basic dumbbell curl lifting both arms together. It builds the biceps and lets each arm work evenly.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs and your shoulders back.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without swinging.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Bicep plate curl
desc: The classic standing curl with a straight barbell. It is a basic mass builder for the biceps that also works the forearms.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hold the bar with palms facing forward, hands about shoulder width.
Let the bar hang against your thighs and tuck your elbows to your sides.
Breathe out and bend your elbows to bring the bar up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Biceps Leg Concentration Curl
desc: A bodyweight curl in which you hold behind one knee and use your biceps to lift that relaxed leg. Your own leg acts as the weight, so it can be done anywhere.
ins: Sit on a bench or chair with your back straight and feet flat.
Reach down with one hand and grip under the thigh of the same-side leg, just behind the knee, palm facing up.
Relax that leg and keep your elbow against your side.
Breathe out and curl your hand up, lifting the leg with your biceps rather than your hip.
Lower the leg slowly to the floor, finish the set and switch sides.

name: Biceps Narrow Pull-Ups
desc: A pull-up with a narrow underhand grip that makes the biceps do much of the pulling. It is an advanced bodyweight move for the arms and back.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with palms facing you and hands close together.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and tighten your stomach.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward the bar by bending your elbows.
Go up until your chin clears the bar, keeping your elbows in front of you.
Breathe in and lower slowly to a full hang.

name: Biceps Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up done with an underhand, shoulder-width grip and a focus on curling your body up with the arms. It is an advanced exercise that loads the biceps heavily.
ins: Grab a pull-up bar with palms facing you at shoulder width and hang with straight arms.
Set your shoulders down and keep your legs still.
Breathe out and pull yourself up, thinking of squeezing your biceps to bring the bar to your chest.
Pause with your chin above the bar.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are fully straight.

name: Body-Up
desc: A bodyweight triceps move that starts in a forearm plank and pushes up onto straight arms by extending the elbows. It builds the triceps and also challenges the chest, shoulders and core.
ins: Start in a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Shift your weight slightly forward so your hands sit just in front of your elbows.
Breathe out and press your palms into the floor to straighten your elbows, lifting your forearms off the ground.
Keep your hips level and your stomach tight as you rise.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower back onto your forearms.

name: Bodyweight Drop Jump Squat
desc: A plyometric drill in which you step off a low box, land in a squat and immediately jump as high as you can. It trains the glutes, quads and calves to absorb force and spring back quickly.
ins: Stand on the edge of a low box, about knee height or lower.
Step off the box with one foot; do not jump down.
Land on both feet at the same time with knees bent and hips back.
As soon as you touch the floor, swing your arms up and jump straight up as high as you can.
Land softly, reset and climb back onto the box for the next rep.

name: Bodyweight Incline Side Plank
desc: A side plank with your forearm on a bench or step, which raises your upper body and makes the hold easier than on the floor. It strengthens the obliques and the rest of the abs, with the shoulder helping to support you.
ins: Lie on your side next to a bench and place your forearm on it, elbow directly under your shoulder.
Stack your feet, or stagger them for more balance, with your legs straight.
Tighten your abs and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Hold without letting your hips drop or roll forward, breathing steadily.
Lower your hips with control and switch sides.

name: Bodyweight Kneeling Triceps Extension
desc: A bodyweight triceps extension done from your knees, lowering your forearms to the floor and pushing back up. It works like a skull crusher using your own weight, with the chest and shoulders helping.
ins: Kneel on a mat and place your hands on the floor in front of you, shoulder-width apart, with your body leaning forward in a straight line from knees to head.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Bend your elbows to lower your forearms to the floor, letting your body move forward.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your elbows and lift back up.
Move your hands farther forward to make it harder.

name: Bodyweight Side Lying Biceps Curl
desc: A no-equipment biceps exercise done lying on your side, curling the top arm while your other hand presses against the wrist to create resistance. It teaches you to contract the biceps hard without weights.
ins: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your head resting on your bottom arm.
Keep your top upper arm against your side with the palm facing forward.
Place the fingers of your bottom hand on the top wrist if you can reach, or simply tense the arm hard.
Breathe out and curl the top hand toward your shoulder, squeezing the biceps as hard as you can against the resistance.
Breathe in and lower the forearm slowly, then switch sides after the set.

name: Bodyweight Squatting Row
desc: A bodyweight row holding a sturdy post, combined with a squat. It trains the upper back and shoulders, and the legs keep you working through the whole body.
ins: Grip a sturdy post with both hands at about chest height.
Lean back with straight arms and sit down into a squat.
Drive through your heels to stand and pull your chest toward the post as you rise.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top and breathe out.
Sit back down into the squat, letting your arms straighten.

name: Bodyweight Squatting Row (with Towel)
desc: A bodyweight row with a towel around a sturdy post, combined with a squat. It works the upper back while the legs help you move.
ins: Loop a towel around a sturdy post and hold one end in each hand.
Step back with straight arms and sit down into a squat.
Push through your heels to stand up and pull your chest toward the post at the same time.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Lower back into the squat with straight arms.

name: Bodyweight Standing Calf Raise
desc: A calf raise using only your body weight. It is a beginner-friendly way to build calf strength and ankle stability anywhere.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart near a wall or chair for light support.
Stand tall with your stomach tight and knees straight but soft.
Breathe out and rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second, keeping your ankles from rolling out.
Breathe in and lower your heels slowly to the floor.
Stand on a step edge to make it harder.

name: Bodyweight Standing Close-Grip One Arm Row
desc: A one-arm bodyweight row where you hold a sturdy upright post close to your body and lean back. It works one side of the upper back at a time.
ins: Stand facing a sturdy vertical post or door frame and grip it with one hand at chest height.
Walk your feet in close to the post and lean back until your arm is straight.
Keep your body straight and your free hand on your hip.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward your hand, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Lower yourself back slowly.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Bodyweight Standing Close-Grip Row
desc: A bodyweight row holding a sturdy upright post with both hands close together and leaning back. It is an easy way to train the upper back without equipment.
ins: Stand facing a sturdy post or door frame and grip it with both hands, one just above the other, at chest height.
Walk your feet toward the base and lean back until your arms are straight.
Keep your body in one line from head to heels.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower yourself back slowly to straight arms.

name: Bodyweight Standing One Arm Row
desc: A one-arm bodyweight row holding a sturdy post or door frame and leaning back. It trains each side of the upper back and the biceps without weights.
ins: Grip a sturdy post or door frame with one hand at about waist height.
Place your feet close to it and lean back until your arm is straight.
Turn your body slightly so your shoulders stay square and your stomach is tight.
Breathe out and pull yourself toward the post until your hand is near your ribs.
Lower back slowly.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Bodyweight Standing One Arm Row (with Towel)
desc: A one-arm bodyweight row using a towel wrapped around a sturdy post. The towel makes your grip work harder while you train one side of the upper back.
ins: Wrap a towel around a sturdy post and hold both ends together in one hand.
Stand close to the post and lean back until your arm is straight.
Keep your body straight and your stomach tight.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward your hand, driving your elbow back.
Lower yourself back slowly.
Finish the set and switch hands.

name: Bodyweight Standing Row
desc: A beginner bodyweight row holding a sturdy post or door frame with both hands and leaning back. The more you lean back, the harder it gets.
ins: Grip a sturdy post or door frame with both hands at chest height.
Walk your feet in and lean back until your arms are straight.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward your hands, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower back slowly; step your feet closer to make it harder.

name: Bodyweight Standing Row (with Towel)
desc: A two-hand bodyweight row using a towel looped around a sturdy post. It works the upper back and shoulders and challenges your grip.
ins: Loop a towel around a sturdy post and hold one end in each hand.
Step your feet in and lean back until your arms are straight.
Keep your body straight and your stomach tight.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward the post, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself back slowly to straight arms.

name: Bottoms-Up
desc: A reverse crunch where your legs point to the ceiling and you lift your hips straight up off the floor. It focuses on the lower abs and obliques with help from the hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides, palms down.
Raise your legs until they point straight up, knees slightly soft.
Breathe out and use your abs to lift your hips off the floor, pushing your feet toward the ceiling.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor without letting your legs drop.
Keep the lift small and controlled rather than swinging.

name: Box Jump Down With One Leg Stabilization
desc: A landing drill where you step off a box and catch yourself on one leg, holding the position still. It builds ankle and knee stability along with calf and leg strength.
ins: Stand on a low box or step with your feet together.
Step forward off the box with one foot.
Land on that single leg on the ball of the foot, then let the heel settle as the knee bends.
Keep your knee in line with your toes and your hips level.
Hold the landing still for 2 to 3 seconds while breathing steadily.
Step back up and repeat, alternating legs or finishing one side first.

name: Boxing Jab
desc: A fast, straight punch thrown with the lead hand. It trains shoulder speed and endurance and makes a good cardio drill when done in rounds.
ins: Stand in a boxing stance with your lead foot forward and both fists up by your face.
Keep your elbows in and your chin slightly down.
Extend your lead arm straight out in front of you, turning the fist palm-down as your arm straightens.
Breathe out sharply with each punch.
Snap the hand straight back to your face and keep throwing for the round time.

name: Boxing Left Uppercut
desc: A boxing punch where the left fist drives upward from a short dip, powered by the legs and a turn of the hips. It trains the abs and trunk rotation, with the shoulders, triceps, glutes and quads joining in.
ins: Stand in a boxing stance with your left foot forward, knees soft, hands up by your cheeks and chin down.
Dip slightly by bending your knees and shifting a little weight onto your left side.
Push off the floor and turn your hips and chest to the right as you drive your left fist upward.
Keep your left elbow bent and close to your body so the punch travels straight up, not in a wide arc.
Breathe out sharply as you punch, then bring your fist straight back to guard.
Reset your stance before the next punch.

name: Boxing Right Cross
desc: A straight punch thrown with the rear right hand, driven by turning the hips and back foot. Repeated as a drill, it is upper-body cardio that also works the shoulders, chest and core.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance: left foot forward, right foot back, knees soft, hands up by your chin.
Turn your right hip and shoulder forward while pivoting on the ball of your right foot.
Extend your right arm straight toward the target, turning the palm down as the arm straightens.
Keep your left hand up guarding your face and breathe out sharply as you punch.
Bring the right fist straight back to your chin and reset your stance.
Repeat at a steady pace, staying light on your feet.

name: Boxing Right Uppercut
desc: A rising punch thrown with the right hand, coming up from below toward the target's chin. As a cardio drill it works the shoulders, arms and core, powered by the legs and hips.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your left foot forward and hands guarding your chin.
Dip slightly by bending your knees and shift a little weight onto your right side.
Drive up through your legs and turn your right hip forward.
Swing the right fist upward with the elbow bent about 90 degrees and the palm facing you.
Breathe out on the punch, keep the left hand guarding, and bring the right fist straight back to your chin.
Repeat at a steady rhythm without leaning too far forward.

name: Bridge - Mountain Climber (cross Body)
desc: A mountain climber from a straight-arm plank in which each knee drives across toward the opposite elbow. It works the abs and obliques while the shoulders, triceps, glutes and legs keep the plank steady.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight from head to heels.
Tighten your abs and keep your hips level with your shoulders.
Drive one knee across your body toward the opposite elbow.
Return that foot to the floor and drive the other knee across the other way.
Keep alternating at a controlled pace without bouncing your hips, breathing steadily.

name: Broad Jump To Vertical
desc: A combination jump: a long two-foot jump forward, followed straight away by a maximum jump upward from the landing. It builds explosive power in the quads, glutes, hamstrings and calves and teaches quick transitions.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Swing your arms back, dip into a quarter squat and jump forward as far as you can.
Land on both feet with your knees bent and hips back.
Without pausing, swing your arms up and jump straight up as high as you can.
Land softly, reset your feet and repeat.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
desc: A split squat with your rear foot resting in the foot strap of a suspension trainer. The unstable rear foot forces the front leg's quads and glutes to work harder and challenges balance.
ins: Adjust the suspension trainer so the foot cradle hangs about knee height and stand facing away from the anchor.
Place the top of one foot in the cradle behind you and hop the other foot forward into a long split stance.
Keep your chest up and your hands on your hips or in front for balance.
Bend the front knee and lower straight down while the back leg extends behind you.
Push through the front heel to rise, keeping the strap steady.
Breathe out as you rise; finish all reps, then switch legs.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Smith machine)
desc: A Bulgarian split squat in the Smith machine, with the bar on your back and your rear foot raised on a bench. The fixed bar lets you focus on driving with the front leg's quads and glutes without worrying about balance.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and put a bench about two steps behind it.
Rest the bar on your upper back, unrack it and place the top of one foot on the bench behind you.
Position your front foot so your knee stays over the middle of the foot at the bottom.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Drive through the front heel to rise.
Breathe out as you rise; finish all reps, then switch legs.

name: Burpee
desc: A full-body conditioning move that links a squat, a plank and a jump in one flowing rep. It drives your heart rate up and works the legs, chest and shoulders.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands flat on the floor just in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back into a plank, keeping your back straight and stomach tight.
Jump your feet forward again so they land just behind your hands.
Explode up into a jump, reaching your arms overhead.
Land softly with bent knees and flow into the next rep, breathing out on each jump.

name: Burpee Broad Jump
desc: A burpee with your chest to the floor, finished by a two-foot jump forward instead of straight up, so each rep moves you down the floor. A HYROX station that works the whole body, especially the quads, glutes and chest.
ins: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Squat down, put your hands on the floor and jump or step your feet back into a plank.
Lower your chest and thighs to the floor, then push back up to the plank.
Jump or step your feet forward to just behind your hands.
Swing your arms back, then drive them forward and jump forward as far as you comfortably can, landing on both feet with your knees bent.
Go straight into the next burpee where you land, keeping a steady pace.

name: Butt-Ups
desc: A forearm plank in which you push your hips up into an upside-down V and lower them back to a straight line. It works the abs, with the hip flexors and lower back helping to control the movement.
ins: Get into a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your body straight from head to heels.
Tighten your abs and squeeze your glutes before you start.
Press through your forearms and lift your hips high so your body forms an upside-down V, breathing out as you rise.
Pause briefly at the top with your legs straight.
Lower your hips slowly back to the plank line without letting them sag below it.

name: Butterfly Yoga Pose
desc: A seated yoga stretch with the soles of the feet together and the knees dropped out to the sides. It opens the inner thighs and groin and gently loosens the hips.
ins: Sit on the floor and bring the soles of your feet together in front of you.
Pull your heels in toward your body as far as is comfortable.
Hold your feet or ankles and sit up tall.
Let your knees sink toward the floor; you can press them down lightly with your elbows.
Breathe slowly and hold for 30 to 60 seconds, leaning forward from the hips for a deeper stretch.

name: Cable Alternate Shoulder Press
desc: A standing cable press where you push one handle overhead at a time from two low pulleys. The cables keep tension on the shoulders, and alternating sides makes your core work to stay steady.
ins: Stand between two low pulleys and bring both handles up to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Set your feet hip-width apart and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press one handle straight up until your arm is straight.
Lower it back to your shoulder slowly while the other hand stays in place.
Press with the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Cable Alternate Triceps Extension
desc: A cable triceps extension done one arm at a time, alternating sides. Working each arm alone helps even out strength differences.
ins: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and stand facing the machine.
Take the handle in your right hand with your elbow bent and pinned to your side.
Breathe out and push the handle down until your arm is straight.
Let it rise slowly until your forearm is just above level with the floor.
Do one rep with the right arm, then switch the handle to your left hand and keep alternating.

name: Cable Assisted Inverse Leg Curl
desc: A Nordic-style hamstring curl where you hold a cable handle at your chest, with the cable coming from behind you, so the stack takes some of your weight. The cable lets you control the lowering and the return, building strong hamstrings with help from the glutes and calves.
ins: Set a cable pulley high and attach a single handle or a rope.
Kneel on a pad facing away from the machine with your ankles secured under a bench or held by a partner.
Hold the handle against your chest with both hands and keep a straight line from your knees to your head.
Breathe in and slowly lean forward from the knees, letting the cable support part of your weight.
Breathe out and pull with your hamstrings to bring your body back upright, using a lighter weight on the stack as you get stronger.

name: Cable Bar Lateral Pulldown
desc: The standard lat pulldown on a cable machine with a long straight bar. It builds width in the lats and works the biceps, rear shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Sit at the pulldown station with your thighs locked under the pads.
Take the long bar with an overhand grip wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight and your lats stretch.
Breathe out as you pull and in as the bar goes up.

name: Cable Bench Press
desc: A bench press done lying on a flat bench between two low cable pulleys. The cables keep tension on the chest all the way through the press, including at the top.
ins: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys, grab a handle in each hand and lie back.
Start with your hands beside your chest, palms facing your feet and elbows below the bench line.
Press both handles straight up until your arms are extended above your chest.
Let your hands come slightly closer at the top and squeeze your chest for a moment.
Lower slowly back to the start, breathing in, and breathe out as you press.

name: Cable Close Grip Curl
desc: A standing cable curl using a straight bar with your hands close together. The cable keeps constant tension on the biceps, and the narrow grip leans toward the outer head.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and grip it underhand with your hands close together.
Stand facing the machine with your arms straight and elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze at the top while keeping your elbows still.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Cable Concentration Curl
desc: A standing concentration curl on a low cable, bending forward so the working arm hangs straight down. It isolates the biceps of one arm under constant cable tension.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, hold it in one hand and step back a little.
Bend forward at the hips and rest your free hand on your knee, letting the working arm hang straight down.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward your shoulder, keeping the upper arm still.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after the set.

name: Cable Concentration Extension (on Knee)
desc: A seated one-arm cable triceps extension with your elbow resting on your knee. Bracing the elbow keeps the work on the triceps and stops the shoulder from helping.
ins: Set a pulley high, place a bench beside the machine and sit facing sideways to it.
Hold the handle in the hand nearest the machine and rest that elbow on top of your knee, forearm angled up toward the pulley.
Breathe out and straighten your arm by pushing the handle down and forward.
Keep the elbow planted on your knee the whole time.
Let the handle return slowly until your elbow is fully bent, then switch arms after the set.

name: Cable Cross-Over Lateral Pulldown
desc: A pulldown between two high pulleys where each hand takes the cable from the opposite side, so the pull comes down at an angle across the body. It works the lats along with the biceps, rear shoulders and mid back.
ins: Set both pulleys high with a single handle on each.
Grab the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left, so the cables cross in front of you.
Kneel or sit in the middle with your arms reaching up and your chest tall.
Pull both elbows down and out to your sides until your hands reach shoulder level.
Squeeze your shoulder blades down and together, then let the handles rise slowly.
Breathe out on the pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Cross-Over Variation
desc: A standing cable crossover from high pulleys where the hands sweep down and cross past each other in front of the body. Crossing the hands adds extra squeeze for the inner and lower chest.
ins: Set both pulleys high, take a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
Lean your torso slightly forward with a soft bend in your elbows and your arms open wide.
Sweep your hands down and inward in a wide arc until they cross in front of your hips.
Pause with the crossover and squeeze your chest hard; switch which hand goes on top each rep.
Let your arms open back up slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest, breathing in as they open.

name: Cable Crunch
desc: A kneeling crunch with a rope on the high pulley, where you curl your ribs down toward your hips against the cable. It is a popular way to load the abs, with the obliques assisting.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the machine.
Hold the rope ends beside your head with your hips high and still.
Breathe out and curl your chest down toward your knees by rounding your spine, not by bending at the hips.
Squeeze your abs at the bottom for a second.
Let the cable pull you slowly back up until your back is long again.

name: Cable Deadlift
desc: A deadlift performed with a straight bar or handle attached to a low cable pulley. The cable keeps steady tension through the whole lift, working the glutes, hamstrings, quads and lower back.
ins: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and stand facing the machine, close enough that the cable runs straight up.
Set your feet hip-width apart, hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, pull your shoulders down and brace your core.
Push through your feet and stand up, driving your hips forward at the top.
Lower by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, keeping tension on the cable.
Breathe out as you stand and in as you lower.

name: Cable Decline Fly
desc: A cable fly performed lying on a decline bench placed between two low pulleys. The head-down angle targets the lower part of the chest.
ins: Set a decline bench between two low pulleys, hold a handle in each hand and lie back with your feet secured.
Raise your arms over your chest with palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Let the handles travel apart in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring the handles back together over your lower chest by squeezing your pecs, keeping the elbow bend fixed.
Breathe in as your arms open and out as they close.

name: Cable Decline One Arm Press
desc: A one-arm cable press performed lying on a decline bench next to a low pulley. It focuses on one side of the lower chest at a time and helps fix strength differences between sides.
ins: Place a decline bench beside a low pulley, hold the handle in the hand nearest the machine and lie back with your legs secured.
Start with the handle beside your lower chest, elbow bent below the bench line.
Press the handle straight up until your arm is fully extended.
Lower it slowly back to your chest while keeping your torso still.
Complete your reps, turn around to work the other arm, and breathe out on each press.

name: Cable Decline Press
desc: A cable press where the hands drive forward and down at a decline angle, putting most of the work on the lower chest. The triceps and front shoulders help finish each press.
ins: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height, take a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
Start with the handles beside your chest, elbows bent and a little below shoulder level.
Breathe out and press the handles forward and slightly downward until your hands meet in front of your lower ribs.
Squeeze your chest for a second without locking your elbows.
Breathe in and let the handles come back slowly to your chest, keeping your torso still.

name: Cable Decline Seated Wide-Grip Row
desc: A seated cable row with a wide bar where you sit on a bench angled so the cable pulls from below, giving a long reach forward. It targets the upper back, helped by the biceps and forearms.
ins: Place a low-angled bench in front of the low pulley and attach a wide bar.
Sit facing the machine with your feet braced on the platform and grab the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Sit tall with your arms straight and your shoulders reaching forward.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, flaring your elbows out and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your back from rounding.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Drag Curl
desc: A cable curl in which the bar is dragged up along the front of your body as your elbows move back. Keeping the bar close takes the front shoulder out and focuses on the biceps.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and grip it underhand at shoulder width.
Stand close to the machine with the bar resting against your thighs.
Breathe out and curl the bar up while pulling your elbows back, so the bar slides up your body.
Stop when the bar reaches your lower chest and squeeze your biceps.
Breathe in and lower the bar along the same path, bringing your elbows forward to your sides.

name: Cable Floor Seated Wide-Grip Row
desc: A cable row done sitting directly on the floor with a wide bar, which keeps the focus on the upper back and rear shoulders. The biceps and forearms help.
ins: Attach a wide bar to a low pulley and sit on the floor facing it with your knees slightly bent.
Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip and sit up straight.
Keep your torso still and pull the bar to your upper stomach, elbows out to the sides.
Squeeze between your shoulder blades for a moment.
Straighten your arms slowly, letting your shoulders move forward without rounding your back.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Forward Raise
desc: A front raise using a straight bar on a low pulley, with you facing away from the machine and the cable running between your legs. It works the front shoulders with steady cable tension.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley, stand facing away from the machine and hold the bar at your thighs, palms down, with the cable between your legs.
Step forward until the weight lifts and stand tall with your stomach braced.
Breathe out and raise the bar in front of you with straight arms to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower it slowly, keeping tension on the cable.

name: Cable Front Raise
desc: A one-arm cable front raise done facing away from a low pulley, lifting the handle forward with a straight arm. It isolates the front of the shoulder.
ins: Stand facing away from a low pulley and hold the handle in one hand beside your hip, palm facing back.
Take a small step forward, stand tall and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and raise the handle in front of you with a straight arm to shoulder height.
Hold for a second without twisting your body.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Cable Front Shoulder Raise
desc: A cable front raise done facing the machine, lifting a rope or bar from a low pulley up to eye level with both hands. It works the front shoulders, with the traps and biceps helping.
ins: Attach a rope or straight bar to a low pulley, face the machine and hold it with both hands at your thighs.
Step back until the weight lifts, then stand tall with your stomach braced.
Breathe out and raise your straight arms up to eye level.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly.

name: Cable Hammer Curl (with Rope)
desc: A hammer curl on a low cable using a rope, with the palms facing each other. It works the biceps, brachialis and forearms with steady cable tension.
ins: Attach a rope to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Hold one end of the rope in each hand with thumbs up and arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the rope toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Pull the rope ends slightly apart at the top and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Cable High Pulley Overhead Tricep Extension
desc: An overhead triceps extension using a straight bar on a high cable while facing away from the machine. The overhead angle and constant cable tension work the triceps through a long range, especially the long head.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, grip it with palms down and turn so your back faces the machine.
Step forward into a split stance, lean slightly forward and bring your hands behind your head with elbows pointing forward.
Breathe out and straighten your arms forward and up until they are in line with your body.
Keep your upper arms still beside your head as you extend.
Breathe in and let your hands return slowly behind your head.

name: Cable High Row (kneeling)
desc: A kneeling cable row from a high pulley where you pull a bar down and in toward your upper chest. It works the upper back and lats, with the biceps and rear shoulders assisting.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and kneel facing it, a little way back.
Grab the bar overhand at shoulder-width so your arms reach up and forward.
Kneel tall with your hips forward and your stomach tight.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Pause with your shoulder blades squeezed, then extend your arms slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you reach back up.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
desc: A standing cable exercise where you pull one leg in across the front of the other against the cable's resistance. It strengthens the inner thigh muscles that bring the legs together.
ins: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and fasten it around the ankle nearest the machine.
Stand side-on to the machine and step away until the cable is tight with your strapped leg slightly out to the side.
Hold the machine or a rail for balance and stand tall with your core tight.
Pull the strapped leg in and across in front of your standing leg, keeping it straight.
Pause briefly, then let the leg return out to the side slowly.
Breathe out as you pull in; finish your reps, then turn around for the other leg.

name: Cable Incline Bench Press
desc: An incline press on a bench placed between two low cable pulleys. It loads the upper chest with steady cable tension from bottom to top.
ins: Set an incline bench at about 30 to 45 degrees between two low pulleys and sit back holding a handle in each hand.
Start with the handles beside your upper chest and your elbows pointing down and slightly out.
Press the handles up and slightly inward until your arms are straight above your shoulders.
Hold briefly at the top while squeezing your upper chest.
Lower back under control, breathing in, and breathe out on each press.

name: Cable Incline Bench Row
desc: A row done lying chest-down on an incline bench in front of a low cable pulley. Supporting the chest takes the lower back out and focuses the work on the upper back and rear shoulders.
ins: Place an incline bench facing a low pulley and attach two handles or a short bar.
Lie on the bench with your chest on the pad and take the handles with straight arms.
Pull your elbows back past your body while keeping your chest on the pad.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out at the end of the pull.
Let your arms stretch forward slowly and with control.

name: Cable Incline Fly
desc: A cable fly on an incline bench between two low pulleys. It trains the upper chest with constant tension, especially in the squeezed position.
ins: Put an incline bench between two low pulleys, grab the handles and lie back with your feet on the floor.
Raise your hands above your upper chest, palms facing in and elbows softly bent.
Let your arms open slowly out to the sides until your hands are about level with your chest.
Hug the handles back up and together, keeping the same elbow angle throughout.
Inhale while opening and exhale while closing.

name: Cable Incline Fly (on Stability Ball)
desc: An incline cable fly done with your upper back on a stability ball instead of a bench. The unstable support makes your core and hips work hard while the upper chest does the fly.
ins: Place a stability ball between two low pulleys, hold a handle in each hand and roll down until your upper back rests on the ball.
Keep your feet wide and your hips a little lower than your shoulders so your torso is on an incline.
Start with your arms above your chest, palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Open your arms wide in an arc until your chest is stretched, then pull them back together over your upper chest.
Keep your stomach tight so the ball stays still, and breathe out as your hands come together.

name: Cable Incline Pushdown
desc: A straight-arm pulldown done lying back on an incline bench with your head toward a high cable. It isolates the lats, with the triceps and shoulders helping hold the arms straight.
ins: Place an incline bench in front of a high pulley with a straight bar attached.
Lie back on the bench with your head toward the machine and take the bar overhead with straight arms.
Brace your stomach and keep your lower back on the pad.
Keeping your elbows almost locked, pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then let the bar travel back overhead slowly.
Breathe out as you pull down and in as the bar returns.

name: Cable Incline Triceps Extension
desc: A triceps extension done on an incline bench with a cable from a low pulley behind you. The incline places the triceps on a long stretch at the bottom.
ins: Set an incline bench in front of a low pulley with the top of the bench facing the machine and attach a straight bar or rope.
Lie back on the bench and take the attachment over your head with your elbows bent and pointing up.
Breathe out and straighten your arms forward and up until they point above your chest.
Keep your upper arms still and near your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbows slowly to let the attachment return behind your head.

name: Cable Judo Flip
desc: A rotational cable pull that copies the motion of a judo throw, pulling a high cable down and across your body. It trains the abs and obliques to create rotation, with the shoulders helping.
ins: Set a handle on a high pulley and stand side-on to the machine, feet wider than your shoulders.
Reach up and grab the handle with both hands above the shoulder nearest the machine.
Brace your abs and pull the handle down and across your body toward your far hip, turning your torso as you go.
Let your back foot pivot so your hips turn with you, like finishing a throw.
Return slowly against the cable to the start, finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Cable Kickback
desc: A triceps kickback using a low cable, done bent over one arm at a time. The cable keeps tension on the triceps even at the start of the movement.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, take it in one hand and step back facing the machine.
Hinge forward with a flat back and lift your working elbow so the upper arm is beside your torso, forearm hanging down.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back until it is fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps for a second.
Breathe in and let the forearm return slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Cable Kneeling Triceps Extension
desc: An overhead triceps extension done kneeling with your back to a cable machine and a rope attachment. It trains the triceps, especially the long head, while kneeling keeps your lower body out of it.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley, take the ends and kneel facing away from the machine.
Bring your hands behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing forward.
Lean your torso slightly forward and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and straighten your arms forward and up, spreading the rope ends at the finish.
Breathe in and let your hands return behind your head slowly, keeping your elbows still.

name: Cable Lateral Pulldown (with Rope Attachment)
desc: A lat pulldown using a rope instead of a bar, which lets your hands spread apart at the bottom for a stronger squeeze. It works the lats, biceps and forearms.
ins: Attach a rope to the high pulley and sit with your thighs under the pads.
Hold one end of the rope in each hand with your palms facing each other.
Sit tall with your chest up and your arms reaching overhead.
Pull the rope down toward your upper chest, spreading the ends apart as your elbows come down.
Squeeze your back, then let the rope rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way up.

name: Cable Lateral Pulldown With V-Bar
desc: A lat pulldown using a V-shaped close-grip handle with the palms facing each other. It works the lats through a long range with help from the biceps and forearms.
ins: Attach the V handle to the high pulley and sit with your thighs under the pads.
Grip both sides of the handle with your palms facing each other and arms straight.
Lean back slightly and pull the handle to your upper chest, elbows driving down.
Squeeze your lats and breathe out at the bottom.
Let the handle rise slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Cable Low Fly
desc: A standing cable fly that pulls from low pulleys upward to chest or shoulder height. The upward path puts most of the work on the upper chest.
ins: Set both pulleys at the lowest position, take a handle in each hand and stand in the middle with a staggered stance.
Let your arms hang down and slightly back with palms facing forward and elbows softly bent.
Sweep your hands up and inward until they meet in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze your chest at the top for a second without shrugging your shoulders.
Lower your arms slowly back to the start, breathing in, and breathe out as you lift.

name: Cable Low Seated Row
desc: A seated row from the low pulley with your feet braced, one of the main exercises for a stronger mid and upper back. The biceps and forearms assist.
ins: Sit at the low row station with your feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Hold the handle with straight arms and sit upright with your chest up.
Pull the handle to your stomach, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together without leaning back.
Let your arms straighten slowly, keeping your back straight.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Lying Bicep Curl
desc: A cable curl done lying on your back with your feet toward a low pulley. Lying down removes any body swing and keeps the biceps working against steady tension.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and lie on your back on the floor or a flat bench with your feet toward the machine.
Hold the bar underhand with your arms straight along your body and your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top without lifting your elbows.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Cable Lying Close-Grip Curl
desc: A cable curl done lying on your back with a low pulley at your feet and the hands close together. Lying down removes any swinging so the biceps do all the work.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and lie on your back on the floor or a bench with your feet toward the machine.
Hold the bar underhand with your hands close together and arms straight down by your thighs.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your chest with your upper arms resting on the floor or bench.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Cable Lying Extension Pullover (with Rope Attachment)
desc: A lying cable movement that starts as a triceps extension behind the head and finishes as a pullover, using a rope. It works the lats and triceps together, with the shoulders helping.
ins: Set a rope on a low pulley and lie on a flat bench with your head toward the machine.
Reach back and hold the rope behind your head with your elbows bent and pointing up.
Straighten your elbows so the rope moves up toward the ceiling.
Keeping your arms straight, pull the rope over your chest down toward your hips.
Reverse the path slowly: arms back overhead, then bend the elbows to the start.
Breathe out as you pull over and in as you return.

name: Cable Lying Fly
desc: A fly done lying on a flat bench between two low cable pulleys. Unlike dumbbells, the cables keep the chest loaded even when the hands are together at the top.
ins: Place a flat bench between two low pulleys, hold a handle in each hand and lie back.
Extend your arms above your chest with palms facing each other and a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower your arms out to the sides in a smooth arc until you feel a good stretch in your chest.
Bring your hands back together above your chest by squeezing your pecs.
Keep your shoulders down against the bench and breathe out as you close.

name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension (Rope)
desc: A lying cable triceps extension using a rope from a low pulley behind your head. The cable keeps the triceps under tension through the whole range.
ins: Attach a rope to a low pulley and lie on a flat bench with your head toward the machine.
Hold the rope with palms facing each other and press your arms up so your hands are over your chest.
Tilt your upper arms back slightly toward the machine and keep them fixed.
Breathe in and bend your elbows so your hands come down beside your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms, pulling the rope ends slightly apart at the top.

name: Cable One Arm Curl
desc: A standing curl using one cable handle from a low pulley. Training one arm at a time helps you focus on the squeeze and fix side-to-side differences.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Hold the handle underhand in one hand with the arm straight and elbow at your side.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top while keeping your elbow from moving forward.
Breathe in and lower slowly; finish the set and switch arms.

name: Cable One Arm Decline Chest Fly
desc: A single-arm cable fly done lying on a decline bench, which focuses the stretch and squeeze on the lower chest of one side at a time.
ins: Place a decline bench beside a low pulley, lie back with your feet locked in and take the handle in the hand nearest the cable.
Raise the handle above your chest with a soft bend in the elbow and rest your free hand on your stomach.
Breathe in and open your arm out to the side in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Breathe out and sweep the handle back over your chest as if hugging a tree, keeping the elbow angle fixed.
Finish all reps, then turn the bench around and train the other side.

name: Cable One Arm Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm cable fly performed with your upper back supported on an exercise ball. The unstable base makes your core and hips work to hold you steady while the chest does the fly.
ins: Set a pulley at about chest height when you are lying on the ball, hold the handle and roll down until your upper back rests on the ball.
Lift your hips so your body forms a flat line from knees to shoulders, feet planted wide.
Start with the arm extended above your chest and a slight bend in the elbow.
Breathe in and lower the arm out to the side until your chest feels stretched.
Breathe out and pull the handle back over your chest, keeping your hips high the whole time.
Do all your reps, then switch sides.

name: Cable One Arm Incline Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm cable fly done with your back on an exercise ball in an angled, half-reclined position so the pull works the upper chest. The ball adds a balance challenge for the core and hips.
ins: Set a low pulley, grab the handle and sit on the ball, then walk your feet out until your mid and upper back rest on the ball with your hips lower than your shoulders.
Hold the handle low beside you with the arm open and the elbow slightly bent.
Breathe out and sweep the arm up and across until your hand is above your upper chest.
Pause and squeeze the top of your chest.
Breathe in and lower slowly back to the open position without letting the ball roll.
Finish the set, then repeat with the other arm.

name: Cable One Arm Incline Press
desc: A standing one-arm cable press that drives the hand forward and upward, working the upper chest with help from the front shoulder and triceps. Training one side at a time also challenges your core to resist twisting.
ins: Set the pulley low, hold the handle in one hand and face away from the machine in a staggered stance.
Bring the handle to the side of your chest with the elbow bent and slightly below shoulder height.
Brace your stomach and breathe out as you press the handle forward and up at about a 30 degree angle.
Stop just short of locking the elbow and squeeze your chest.
Breathe in and lower the handle back to your chest under control, keeping your hips and shoulders square.
Complete the set, then switch arms.

name: Cable One Arm Incline Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A single-arm incline cable press done with your back resting on an exercise ball in a half-reclined position. It works the upper chest while the ball forces your core and hips to keep you stable.
ins: Set a low pulley behind you, take the handle in one hand and roll back on the ball until it supports your mid and upper back, hips slightly dropped.
Bring the handle beside your chest with the elbow bent.
Breathe out and press the handle up and slightly forward over your upper chest.
Keep your feet wide and your stomach tight so the ball does not roll.
Breathe in and lower the handle back to your chest slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: Cable One Arm Lateral Bent-Over
desc: A one-arm cable fly done while bent forward at the hips, sweeping the handle down and across the body. It isolates one side of the chest at a time.
ins: Set a pulley at shoulder height, hold the handle in the hand nearest the machine and step away until the cable is tight.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back so your torso is angled toward the floor.
Start with your working arm out to the side, elbow slightly bent.
Pull the handle down and across in an arc until your hand is under your chest, squeezing that side of the chest.
Let the arm return slowly, finish all reps, then switch sides; breathe out on each pull.

name: Cable One Arm Lateral Raise
desc: A one-arm lateral raise from a low pulley, pulling the handle across your body and out to the side. It isolates the side shoulder and gives tension even at the bottom.
ins: Stand side-on to a low pulley and take the handle in the hand farther from the machine.
Hold the machine with your other hand, stand tall and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and raise the handle out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
Keep a soft bend in the elbow and avoid leaning away to swing it up.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Cable One Arm Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm preacher curl using a low cable. The pad fixes the upper arm and the cable keeps tension on the biceps through the whole range.
ins: Place a preacher bench in front of a low pulley and attach a single handle.
Rest the back of one upper arm on the pad and hold the handle underhand with your arm nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the handle toward your shoulder.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Cable One Arm Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm cable chest press done lying with your upper back on an exercise ball and hips lifted. It builds the chest and triceps while your core works to stop the ball rolling and your body twisting.
ins: Set the pulley around ball height, hold the handle and lie back so your head and upper back rest on the ball, hips up level with your knees.
Start with the handle beside your chest and the elbow pointing down and out.
Breathe out and press the handle straight up over your chest.
Keep your hips level and both shoulders on the ball; do not let the pulling side rotate.
Breathe in and bring the handle back to your chest slowly.
Switch sides after the set.

name: Cable One Arm Pulldown
desc: A single-arm pulldown on a high cable. Working one side at a time lets you get a full stretch and a strong squeeze in each lat.
ins: Attach a single handle to the high pulley and kneel or sit facing it.
Grip the handle with one hand, arm straight overhead.
Pull your elbow down to your side, bringing the handle toward your shoulder.
Squeeze your lat at the bottom and breathe out.
Let the handle rise slowly to a full stretch.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Cable One Arm Reverse Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm preacher curl on a low cable using an overhand grip. The fixed upper arm and palm-down grip train the brachialis and forearms alongside the biceps.
ins: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley with a single handle attached.
Rest one upper arm on the pad and grip the handle with your palm facing down.
Breathe out and curl the handle up, keeping your wrist straight.
Pause at the top and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Cable One Arm Straight Back High Row (kneeling)
desc: A kneeling one-arm row from a cable set around chest height, keeping your back upright and still. It trains the upper back on each side separately, with the biceps and rear shoulder helping.
ins: Set a single handle at about chest height and kneel facing the machine.
Hold the handle in one hand with your arm straight and your torso upright.
Tighten your stomach and keep your hips and shoulders facing forward.
Pull the handle to the side of your chest, driving your elbow straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back, then extend your arm slowly.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch, breathing out on each pull.

name: Cable One Arm Tricep Pushdown
desc: A single-arm triceps pushdown on a high cable. Working one side at a time lets you focus on the triceps of each arm and fix strength differences between them.
ins: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and grip it with one hand, palm facing down.
Stand close to the machine with your elbow pinned to your side and bent to about a right angle.
Breathe out and push the handle down until your arm is fully straight.
Squeeze the triceps for a moment at the bottom.
Let the handle rise slowly back to the start without moving your elbow, then switch arms.

name: Cable Overhead Curl
desc: A standing curl between two high pulleys with your arms raised out to the sides, like a double-biceps pose. It trains the biceps in a raised-arm position, with the shoulders working to hold the arms up.
ins: Stand in the middle of a cable crossover with a single handle on each high pulley.
Take a handle in each hand, palms facing up, and raise your arms out to the sides at about shoulder height.
Breathe out and curl both handles toward the sides of your head, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze your biceps at the end of the curl.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly back out to the sides.

name: Cable Overhead Curl On Exercise Ball
desc: An overhead cable curl between two high pulleys while sitting on an exercise ball. It trains the biceps in a raised-arm position, and the ball adds work for your core and balance.
ins: Place an exercise ball in the middle of a cable crossover with single handles on the high pulleys.
Sit tall on the ball with feet wide and take a handle in each hand, arms raised to the sides, palms up.
Breathe out and curl both handles toward your head without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze at the top while keeping the ball still.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly back out.

name: Cable Palm Rotational Row
desc: A standing cable row in which your hand turns from palm-down to palm-up as you pull. It works the upper back and adds load to the biceps and forearms.
ins: Set a single handle at about waist height and stand facing the machine.
Take the handle with your palm facing down and step back until the cable is tight, knees soft.
Pull the handle toward your waist and turn your palm up as your elbow passes your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the end and breathe out.
Return slowly, turning the palm down again as your arm straightens.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Cable Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl done with a cable instead of free weights, which keeps tension on the biceps even at the bottom of the movement.
ins: Place a preacher bench in front of a low pulley and attach a straight or EZ-style bar.
Sit with the backs of your upper arms on the pad and take the bar underhand.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your face.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without lifting your arms off the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.

name: Cable Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A two-arm cable chest press done in a bridge position on an exercise ball. The chest, shoulders and triceps press the handles while the glutes and core keep the hips up and the ball still.
ins: Place the ball between two low pulleys, take a handle in each hand and lie back with your upper back on the ball.
Push your hips up so your body is flat from knees to shoulders and your feet are hip-width apart.
Start with the handles at the sides of your chest, elbows bent.
Breathe out and press both handles up until your arms are nearly straight over your chest.
Breathe in and lower them slowly to chest level, keeping your hips from sagging.

name: Cable Pull Through (with Rope)
desc: A hip hinge where you face away from a low cable, holding a rope between your legs, and drive your hips forward to stand. It trains the glutes and hamstrings and is a good way to learn the hip hinge.
ins: Attach a rope to the low pulley, face away from the machine and hold one end of the rope in each hand between your legs.
Walk forward a few steps until the cable is tight and set your feet a little wider than hip-width.
With soft knees and a flat back, push your hips back and let the rope pull your hands back between your legs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand tall, keeping your arms straight.
Breathe in as you hinge back and out as you stand.

name: Cable Pulldown
desc: A basic cable pulldown from a high pulley, the go-to move for building the lats when pull-ups are too hard. The biceps and forearms help.
ins: Sit at a high pulley with your knees under the pads and hold the bar a bit wider than your shoulders.
Start with straight arms and your chest lifted.
Pull the bar down to your collarbone, thinking of putting your elbows in your back pockets.
Keep your torso nearly upright; avoid swinging back.
Return the bar slowly to the top.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Pulldown (pro Lat Bar)
desc: A lat pulldown using a bent lat bar with angled or parallel grips at the ends, which many people find easier on the wrists and shoulders. It works the lats, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Attach the angled lat bar to the high pulley and sit with your thighs secured.
Hold the grips at the ends of the bar and sit tall.
Pull the bar down in front of your face toward your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down to your sides and squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Let the bar return slowly until your arms are fully straight.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you let it up.

name: Cable Pulldown Bicep Curl
desc: A biceps curl on a high cable, facing the machine with your arms reaching up and forward. The high angle keeps the biceps under tension in a raised-arm position, with the shoulders helping to hold the arms up.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley, grip it underhand and step back until your arms reach up and forward.
Kneel or stand with your stomach tight and your upper arms fixed at about head height.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your forehead by bending only your elbows.
Squeeze your biceps when the bar is close to your head.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly back to the start.

name: Cable Pushdown (Straight Arm, Forward Lean)
desc: A standing straight-arm pulldown with a bar on a high cable, done with a slight forward lean. It isolates the lats without the biceps taking over, with the triceps and shoulders keeping the arms straight.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and stand facing it, about an arm's length away.
Grab the bar overhand at shoulder-width and step back to feel tension.
Hinge slightly forward with soft knees and straight arms.
Sweep the bar down in an arc to your thighs, keeping your elbows locked.
Squeeze your lats, then let the bar rise slowly to eye level.
Breathe out on the way down and in on the way up.

name: Cable Pushdown (with Rope Attachment)
desc: A triceps pushdown on a high cable using a rope, letting you spread your hands at the bottom for a stronger contraction.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing it with a slight forward lean.
Hold the rope ends with thumbs up and elbows pinned to your sides, forearms about level with the floor.
Breathe out and push the rope down until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope ends apart at the bottom and squeeze the triceps.
Breathe in and let the rope rise slowly back to the start without moving your elbows.

name: Cable Rear Delt Row (stirrups)
desc: A one-arm cable row with a single handle, pulled high with the elbow flared so the rear shoulder does most of the work. The upper back and biceps assist.
ins: Set a single handle on a pulley at chest height and hold it in one hand, arm straight, palm facing down.
Stagger your feet, step back until the weight lifts and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and pull the handle toward your shoulder, keeping your elbow high and out to the side.
Squeeze the back of your shoulder for a second at the end.
Breathe in and let your arm straighten slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Cable Rear Delt Row (with Rope)
desc: A seated cable row with the rope attachment, pulled to your face with high, wide elbows. It shifts the work to the rear shoulders and the upper back.
ins: Attach a rope to the seated row cable, sit down with your feet on the platform and hold the rope ends with palms facing down.
Sit tall with your arms straight and your stomach braced.
Breathe out and pull the rope toward your face, lifting your elbows out to the sides at shoulder height.
Pull the rope ends apart at the end and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Breathe in and let your arms straighten slowly without leaning back.

name: Cable Rear Drive
desc: A cable move where you drive your arm back from in front of you to beside your hip, finishing with a straight elbow. It works the triceps with help from the rear shoulder and back.
ins: Attach a single handle to a pulley set at about chest height and stand facing the machine.
Hold the handle in one hand with your arm reaching forward and slightly bent.
Breathe out and drive your elbow back past your torso, then straighten your arm so your hand finishes beside your hip.
Squeeze the triceps hard with the arm straight and slightly behind you.
Breathe in and let the handle return forward slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Cable Rear Pulldown
desc: A pulldown that brings the bar down behind the head instead of to the chest. It hits the lats, rear shoulders and mid back, but needs good shoulder mobility, so use a light weight.
ins: Sit at the pulldown machine and take a wide overhand grip on the long bar.
Lean your head slightly forward, keeping your back upright.
Pull the bar down behind your head to about the top of your neck.
Keep the motion smooth and stop if your shoulders feel pinched.
Let the bar rise slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Reverse Crunch
desc: A reverse crunch done lying on the floor with a low cable attached to your feet, which adds resistance as you curl your hips up. It targets the lower abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Attach ankle straps to a low pulley and lie on your back with your feet toward the machine and the straps around your ankles.
Lift your legs so your knees are bent at about a right angle over your hips, and hold the floor or a fixed object behind your head.
Tighten your abs, breathe out and curl your hips off the floor, pulling your knees toward your chest.
Pause for a second with your abs squeezed.
Breathe in and lower your hips slowly, letting the cable draw your knees back to the start.

name: Cable Reverse Curl
desc: A cable curl with an overhand grip on a straight bar from a low pulley. It emphasizes the forearms and brachialis while still working the biceps.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing it.
Hold the bar with palms facing down at shoulder width, arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up with your elbows fixed at your sides.
Keep your wrists flat as you reach the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly back to straight arms.

name: Cable Reverse Grip Triceps Pushdown (sz-Bar) (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A cable triceps pushdown with an EZ bar held palms-up while wearing an arm blaster. The underhand grip brings in the inner part of the triceps and forearms, and the arm blaster locks the elbows in place.
ins: Put on the arm blaster with your elbows resting against its sides.
Attach an EZ-style bar to a high pulley and grip it underhand with your palms facing up.
Stand close to the machine with your elbows bent and pressed into the arm blaster.
Breathe out and press the bar toward your thighs until your elbows are straight.
Let it rise slowly back up, keeping your wrists firm.

name: Cable Reverse One Arm Curl
desc: A standing one-arm cable curl with an overhand grip. The palm-down position trains the biceps together with the brachialis and the top of the forearm.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley and grip it with one hand, palm facing down.
Stand facing the machine with your arm straight and your elbow tucked against your side.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward your shoulder, keeping your wrist straight.
Pause at the top without letting your elbow drift forward.
Breathe in and lower the handle slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Cable Reverse Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl with a cable and an overhand grip. The pad fixes your upper arms while the forearms and brachialis work hard alongside the biceps.
ins: Place a preacher bench in front of a low pulley with a straight bar attached.
Sit with your upper arms flat on the pad and hold the bar with palms facing down.
Breathe out and curl the bar up while keeping your wrists straight.
Stop when your forearms are near vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly to almost straight arms.

name: Cable Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A reverse wrist curl using a low cable pulley, which keeps tension on the forearm through the whole range. It trains the wrist extensors on the top of the forearm.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and sit on a bench facing the machine.
Hold the bar with your palms facing down and rest your forearms on your thighs, wrists past your knees.
Let the cable pull your hands down so your wrists bend toward the floor.
Breathe out and raise the backs of your hands as high as you can.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and return slowly against the cable's pull.
Keep the movement at the wrists only.

name: Cable Reverse-Grip Pushdown
desc: A triceps pushdown on a high cable done with an underhand grip. Turning the palms up changes the angle and brings more of the inner triceps into play.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and grab it with your palms facing up at about shoulder width.
Stand upright with your elbows tucked to your sides and forearms angled up.
Breathe out and push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom.
Breathe in and let the bar rise slowly to about chest height.

name: Cable Reverse-Grip Straight Back Seated High Row
desc: A seated row from a high cable using an underhand grip, pulling toward the upper chest while the back stays upright. It trains the upper back and lats, with strong help from the biceps.
ins: Set a straight bar on a high pulley and sit facing it on a bench or the floor.
Grab the bar with your palms facing up, hands about shoulder-width.
Sit tall with your arms straight up and forward.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, keeping your back straight and your elbows close.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then let the bar return slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Rope Crossover Seated Row
desc: A seated cable row with two ropes taken from opposite low pulleys so the cables cross in front of you. The changing angle hits the upper back and keeps the arms working too.
ins: Sit on the floor or a low bench centred between two low pulleys of a crossover station.
Take the rope on the left with your right hand and the rope on the right with your left hand so the cables cross.
Sit tall with your chest up and arms straight in front of you.
Pull both elbows back to your sides and squeeze your shoulder blades together, breathing out.
Return slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your back upright.

name: Cable Rope Elevated Seated Row
desc: A seated row with a rope attachment while you sit on a raised seat or box, so the pull comes from slightly below. It trains the upper back, biceps and forearms.
ins: Attach a rope to a low pulley and sit on a box or raised bench facing it.
Hold one end of the rope in each hand with your arms straight and your chest up.
Pull the rope toward your stomach, spreading the ends apart as your hands reach your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Straighten your arms slowly without letting your back round.

name: Cable Rope Extension Incline Bench Row
desc: A chest-supported rope row on an incline bench facing a low pulley, finishing with the rope pulled apart. It targets the upper back and rear shoulders.
ins: Place an incline bench in front of a low pulley with a rope attached.
Lie chest-down on the bench and hold one end of the rope in each hand, arms straight.
Pull the rope toward your upper chest, leading with your elbows out to the sides.
Pull the ends of the rope apart at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades, breathing out.
Let your arms straighten slowly back to the start.

name: Cable Rope Hammer Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl with a rope on a low cable using a neutral, thumbs-up grip. It works the biceps, brachialis and forearms with constant tension.
ins: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley and attach a rope.
Rest your upper arms on the pad and hold the rope ends with your palms facing each other.
Breathe out and curl the rope up toward your face.
Squeeze at the top without lifting your elbows.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are nearly straight.

name: Cable Rope High Pulley Overhead Tricep Extension
desc: An overhead triceps extension with a rope on a high cable, facing away from the machine. The rope lets your hands spread apart at the end for a stronger squeeze on the triceps.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley, hold one end in each hand and turn your back to the machine.
Take a split stance, lean slightly forward and bring the rope behind your head with elbows pointing forward.
Breathe out and straighten your arms forward, spreading the rope ends apart at the end.
Keep your elbows close to your head throughout.
Breathe in and let the rope come back slowly behind your head.

name: Cable Rope Incline Tricep Extension
desc: A triceps extension with a rope on a low cable while lying back on an incline bench, head toward the machine. The incline keeps the triceps under stretch and tension through the whole movement.
ins: Place an incline bench in front of a low pulley with a rope attached, and lie back with your head toward the machine.
Reach back and take the rope with both hands, then raise your elbows so your upper arms point up and slightly back.
Breathe out and straighten your arms until your hands are above your face.
Keep your upper arms still and your elbows close together.
Breathe in and bend your elbows slowly to let the rope return behind your head.

name: Cable Rope Lying On Floor Tricep Extension
desc: A triceps extension with a rope on a low cable while lying flat on the floor, head toward the machine. The floor steadies your body so the triceps do the work.
ins: Attach a rope to a low pulley and lie on your back on the floor with your head toward the machine.
Hold the rope with both hands and raise your upper arms so they point straight up, elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten your arms until your hands are over your chest.
Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling and close together.
Breathe in and slowly bend your elbows to lower the rope beside your head.

name: Cable Rope One Arm Hammer Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm hammer preacher curl holding a rope on a low cable. Working one side at a time with a thumbs-up grip trains the biceps, brachialis and forearm of each arm.
ins: Set a preacher bench in front of a low pulley with a rope attached.
Rest one upper arm on the pad and hold the rope near its knot with your palm facing in.
Breathe out and curl the rope up, keeping your thumb pointing up.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Cable Rope Seated Row
desc: A classic seated cable row using a rope attachment. It builds thickness in the upper back and also works the biceps and forearms.
ins: Attach a rope to the low pulley, sit on the seat and place your feet on the platform with knees slightly bent.
Hold the rope ends with palms facing each other and sit up tall.
Pull the rope to your stomach, driving your elbows back close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out without leaning far back.
Return slowly until your arms are straight and you feel your back stretch.

name: Cable Russian Twists (on Stability Ball)
desc: An advanced Russian twist done with your upper back on a stability ball while you rotate a cable handle from side to side. It challenges the obliques, abs and lower back to stay stable on an unstable base.
ins: Set a handle at chest height and lie with your upper back on a stability ball, side-on to the machine, hips lifted in a bridge.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms straight above your chest.
Keeping your hips level, rotate your shoulders away from the machine, rolling slightly across the ball.
Rotate back to center under control without letting the cable yank you.
Finish your reps, then turn around and work the other side.

name: Cable Seated Chest Press
desc: A seated chest press using cables, usually on a bench placed between two pulleys or on a cable press station. The cables keep tension on the chest the whole way, with the shoulders and triceps assisting.
ins: Set the pulleys at about chest height when seated, place a bench between them and sit with a handle in each hand.
Sit tall with your back against the pad or upright, feet flat, and bring the handles to the sides of your chest.
Breathe out and press the handles straight forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Let your hands come slightly closer together at the end and squeeze your chest.
Breathe in and let the handles return slowly to chest level.

name: Cable Seated Crunch
desc: A seated crunch against a high cable, done on a bench with the rope held by your head. It loads the abs with the obliques helping.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and sit on a bench facing away from the machine.
Hold the rope ends at the sides of your head and sit tall.
Breathe out and curl your upper body forward and down, bringing your ribs toward your hips.
Pause briefly while your abs are fully squeezed.
Uncurl slowly back to tall sitting without letting the weight jerk you.

name: Cable Seated Curl
desc: A biceps curl on a low cable done while seated facing the machine. Sitting stops you from using your legs or back, so the biceps do the lifting.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and sit on the floor or a low bench facing the machine.
Grip the bar underhand with your arms straight and your elbows at your sides, back upright.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Cable Seated High Row (v-Bar)
desc: A seated cable pull from a high pulley with a V-shaped handle, angled between a pulldown and a row. It works the lats along with the biceps, rear shoulders and mid back.
ins: Attach a V-handle to a high pulley and sit facing it a little way back.
Hold the handle with straight arms reaching up and forward.
Lean back just slightly and lift your chest.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your back, then extend your arms slowly.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Seated Neck Extension (with Head Harness)
desc: A seated neck extension using a cable attached to a head harness. The cable keeps tension steady through the whole movement for the back of the neck.
ins: Attach a head harness to a low cable and sit on a bench facing the machine.
Lean forward slightly with a straight back and let the cable pull your chin toward your chest.
Rest your hands on your thighs and keep your shoulders still.
Pull your head back slowly until you are looking slightly up.
Pause, then let your head return under control; exhale as you pull back.
