name: Cable Seated Neck Flexion (with Head Harness)
desc: A seated neck flexion using a cable and head harness, pulling the chin down toward the chest. It strengthens the muscles at the front of the neck.
ins: Attach a head harness to a cable at about head height and sit facing away from the machine.
Sit tall and let the cable draw your head back slightly.
Place your hands on your thighs and keep your torso still.
Bring your chin down toward your chest against the cable.
Pause, then return slowly; keep the weight light and breathe out as you flex.

name: Cable Seated One Arm Alternate Row
desc: A seated cable row with a separate handle in each hand, pulling one arm at a time. Working each side alone helps even out strength in the upper back, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Set two single handles on low pulleys, or on a dual-cable row, and sit facing them with your feet braced.
Hold one handle in each hand with your arms straight and your back upright.
Pull one handle to the side of your stomach while the other arm stays straight.
Return it slowly, then pull with the other arm.
Keep your torso still and avoid twisting toward the working side.
Breathe out on each pull and in as the arm goes forward.

name: Cable Seated One Arm Concentration Curl
desc: A seated one-arm concentration curl on a low cable with your elbow braced against your inner thigh. It isolates each biceps tightly with steady cable tension.
ins: Sit on a bench in front of a low pulley with a single handle attached, feet wide.
Take the handle in one hand and brace the back of that arm against your inner thigh.
Breathe out and curl the handle up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Cable Seated Overhead Curl
desc: An overhead cable curl done seated on a bench between two high pulleys. Sitting keeps your torso still so the biceps work with the arms held up and out.
ins: Place a bench in the middle of a cable crossover with single handles on the high pulleys.
Sit tall and take a handle in each hand, raising your arms out to the sides with palms up.
Breathe out and curl both handles toward your head, keeping your upper arms level.
Squeeze your biceps at the end of the curl.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly back out.

name: Cable Seated Rear Lateral Raise
desc: A seated bent-over raise between two low pulleys, pulling the crossed cables out to the sides. It isolates the rear shoulders with the upper back helping.
ins: Sit at the end of a bench placed between two low pulleys and hold the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left.
Lean forward with a flat back until your chest is close to your thighs.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows.
Stop when your arms are in line with your shoulders and squeeze for a second.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly so the cables cross again.

name: Cable Seated Shoulder Internal Rotation
desc: A light cable exercise where you rotate your forearm in toward your stomach while seated, with the elbow fixed at your side. It strengthens the rotator cuff muscles that turn the shoulder inward and is common in shoulder rehab.
ins: Sit side-on to a cable set at elbow height and hold the handle in the hand closest to the machine.
Bend your elbow to 90 degrees and tuck it against your side; a small rolled towel there helps.
Breathe out and rotate your forearm in across your stomach, keeping your elbow in place.
Pause briefly, then return slowly until your forearm points forward or slightly out.
Use a light weight, then switch sides after your set.

name: Cable Seated Twist
desc: A seated rotation against a cable set at chest height, turning your torso away from the machine. It strengthens the obliques and teaches the trunk to rotate under control.
ins: Set a handle at chest height and sit side-on to the machine on a bench or the floor, far enough away to keep tension on the cable.
Hold the handle with both hands in front of your chest, arms almost straight.
Sit tall, tighten your abs and breathe out as you turn your shoulders away from the machine.
Keep your hips still so the movement comes from your trunk.
Return slowly to the start, and switch sides after the set.

name: Cable Seated Wide-Grip Row
desc: A seated cable row with a wide bar, which shifts more of the work to the upper back and rear shoulders than a narrow handle. The biceps and forearms help.
ins: Attach a long bar to the low pulley and sit with your feet on the platform.
Grip the bar overhand, hands wider than your shoulders.
Sit upright with straight arms and a slight bend in your knees.
Row the bar to your lower chest with your elbows pointing out.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Shoulder Press
desc: A cable overhead press using two low pulleys, pressing both handles up at once. The cables keep the shoulders under even tension from bottom to top.
ins: Sit on a bench placed between two low pulleys and bring both handles to shoulder height, palms forward.
Sit tall with your feet flat and your stomach braced.
Breathe out and press both handles up until your arms are straight and the handles are close together over your head.
Keep your lower back from arching.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly to shoulder height.

name: Cable Shrug
desc: A shrug using a bar on a low cable, which keeps steady tension on the traps from bottom to top. It builds the upper traps.
ins: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley and stand close, holding it in front of your thighs.
Stand tall with straight arms and your stomach tight.
Raise your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your shoulders are fully down.
Keep your arms straight; the movement comes only from the shoulders.

name: Cable Side Bend
desc: A standing side bend holding a handle from a low pulley. It trains the obliques with steady tension through the whole movement.
ins: Stand side-on to a low pulley and hold the handle in the hand nearest the machine, arm straight.
Place your other hand on your hip and stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Let the cable pull you into a slight side bend toward the machine.
Use the far side of your waist to bend the other way, past upright.
Return under control, finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Cable Side Bend Crunch (bosu Ball)
desc: An advanced side crunch where you lie on your side over a BOSU and crunch against a cable. It strengthens the obliques through a long range of motion.
ins: Place a BOSU dome-up beside a low pulley and lie with your hip on the dome, feet away from the machine and braced against something solid.
Hold the cable handle with your top hand beside your head.
Breathe out and crunch sideways, lifting your upper body off the dome toward your top hip.
Lower back over the dome slowly to feel a stretch along your side.
Complete your reps, then turn over for the other side.

name: Cable Side Crunch
desc: A standing crunch to the side against a high cable, pulling your elbow down toward your hip. It focuses on the obliques.
ins: Stand side-on to a high pulley and hold the handle beside your head with the hand nearest the machine.
Brace your abs with your feet hip width apart and knees soft.
Breathe out and crunch sideways, pulling your elbow down toward your hip on the far side.
Hold the squeeze for a moment.
Straighten back up slowly, finish the set, then work the other side.

name: Cable Squat Row (with Rope Attachment)
desc: A cable row with a rope that combines a squat and a row. It works the lats and upper back while the legs and core stay active.
ins: Attach a rope to a cable set at about chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Step back until the cable is tight and sit down into a squat with your arms straight.
Drive up through your heels to stand and, as you rise, row the rope to your lower ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Straighten your arms as you sit back into the squat for the next rep.

name: Cable Squatting Curl
desc: A cable curl performed while holding a deep squat, with the backs of your upper arms resting on your inner thighs. The squat holds the arms still for the biceps and also works the legs.
ins: Attach a straight bar or handle to a low pulley and stand facing it with feet a little wider than your hips.
Grip the bar underhand and sit down into a deep squat, resting the backs of your upper arms on your inner thighs.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your shoulders, keeping your chest up.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly while staying in the squat.

name: Cable Standing Back Wrist Curl
desc: A behind-the-back wrist curl using a low cable, done standing with your back to the machine. It strengthens the forearm flexors with steady cable tension.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand with your back to the machine.
Reach behind you and hold the bar at arm's length with your palms facing backward.
Step forward slightly so the cable has tension and your wrists open.
Breathe out and curl the bar up by bending your wrists, keeping your arms straight.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Stand tall and avoid leaning forward to help the movement.

name: Cable Standing Calf Raise
desc: A standing calf raise using a low cable pulley for resistance. The cable keeps tension on the calves at every point of the lift.
ins: Attach a handle or a hip belt to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Hold the handle at your side with a straight arm, or clip the belt around your hips.
Place the balls of your feet on a low step with heels off.
Lower your heels until your calves stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping your body upright.

name: Cable Standing Cross-Over High Reverse Fly
desc: A standing reverse fly with both pulleys set high, pulling the crossed cables out and down to your sides. It targets the rear shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Set both pulleys above head height and hold the left cable in your right hand and the right cable in your left.
Stand in the middle with your arms crossed in front of your face and elbows slightly bent.
Brace your stomach and breathe out as you sweep your arms out and down until they are level with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Breathe in and bring your arms back up and across slowly.

name: Cable Standing Crunch
desc: A standing crunch with your back to a high cable and the rope held by your head. It trains the abs while teaching you to curl the spine rather than hinge at the hips.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing away from the machine, holding the rope ends beside your head.
Step forward until the cable has tension and set your feet hip width apart.
Breathe out and curl your ribs down toward your hips, rounding your back slightly.
Keep your hips and legs still so the abs do the work.
Uncurl slowly to tall standing.

name: Cable Standing Crunch (with Rope Attachment)
desc: A standing crunch using a rope on a high pulley, rounding your trunk down against the cable's pull. It works the abs, with the obliques helping to keep you steady.
ins: Attach a rope to the high pulley, hold one end in each hand and stand facing away from the machine with the rope beside your ears.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly soft.
Breathe out and curl your chest down toward your hips, rounding your back and squeezing your abs.
Keep your hips still and your hands fixed by your head so your arms do not do the pulling.
Breathe in and slowly uncurl back to upright.

name: Cable Standing Fly
desc: A cable fly done standing between two pulleys, a common finisher for chest workouts. It trains the chest through a wide arc with tension kept on the muscle the whole time.
ins: Set the pulleys a little above shoulder height, grab both handles and step forward into a split stance.
Lean slightly forward, keep your chest proud and let your arms open wide with a slight elbow bend.
Draw your hands together in front of your lower chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze for a moment, then open your arms slowly until your chest is stretched.
Breathe out as you bring the hands in and keep your torso still throughout.

name: Cable Standing Hip Extension
desc: A standing cable kickback where you push one straight leg back against a low cable. It isolates the glutes, with help from the hamstrings.
ins: Fasten an ankle strap to a low pulley and around one ankle, then face the machine.
Hold the frame with both hands and step back until the cable is slightly tight.
Stand on the other leg with a soft knee and lean forward a little, keeping your core tight.
Push the strapped leg straight back by squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back.
Pause at the top, then let the leg return forward slowly.
Breathe out as you kick back; switch legs after your set.

name: Cable Standing Inner Curl
desc: A one-arm standing cable curl where you curl the handle in toward the middle of your body. Curling across the body changes the angle on the biceps and keeps tension steady.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley and stand side-on to the machine, holding the handle in the hand farther from it.
Let the arm hang straight with the palm facing forward and the elbow at your side.
Breathe out and curl the handle up and slightly in toward your opposite shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch sides after the set.

name: Cable Standing Lift
desc: A low-to-high diagonal cable lift, the reverse of a wood chop. It trains the obliques and abs to rotate and the lower back to stay strong.
ins: Set a handle on a low pulley and stand side-on to the machine, feet wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees a little and hold the handle with both hands near the hip closest to the machine.
Breathe out and drive the handle up and across your body to above the opposite shoulder, keeping your arms fairly straight.
Turn your hips and pivot your back foot as you finish high.
Lower the handle slowly along the same path, finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Cable Standing One Arm Triceps Extension
desc: A one-arm overhead triceps extension done standing with your back to a low cable. Working one arm at a time with constant cable tension builds the long head of the triceps.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, take it in one hand and turn your back to the machine.
Raise the hand behind your head so the elbow is bent and pointing up beside your ear.
Stand in a staggered stance and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and straighten your arm toward the ceiling.
Breathe in and let the handle lower behind your head slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Cable Standing One Leg Calf Raise
desc: A single-leg calf raise with a low cable providing resistance. It strengthens each calf on its own and trains ankle balance.
ins: Attach a handle to a low pulley and hold it in one hand, standing beside or facing the machine.
Stand on the same-side foot on a low step with the heel off, other foot lifted behind.
Hold the machine frame with your free hand for balance.
Lower your heel for a full stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, and switch sides after the set.

name: Cable Standing Pulldown (with Rope)
desc: A standing pulldown on a high cable with a rope, pulling the rope down to your chest while bending the elbows. The bent-elbow pull works the biceps together with the shoulders and back.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand facing it, a step back, with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the rope ends with your thumbs up and arms reaching up and forward.
Breathe out and pull the rope down toward your upper chest, bending your elbows and keeping them in front of you.
Squeeze your biceps and upper back at the bottom.
Breathe in and let your arms straighten back up slowly.

name: Cable Standing Rear Delt Row (with Rope)
desc: A standing cable row with the rope attachment at chest height, pulled toward your face with the elbows high. It works the rear shoulders, traps and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Set a rope on a pulley at chest height and hold the ends with palms facing down.
Step back until your arms are straight, stand with feet hip-width apart and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and pull the rope toward your face, raising your elbows out to the sides.
Spread the rope ends apart at the end and hold for a second.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly.

name: Cable Standing Reverse Grip One Arm Overhead Tricep Extension
desc: A standing one-arm overhead triceps extension on a low cable using an underhand grip. Working one arm overhead isolates the triceps long head, and the palm-up grip changes the feel at the wrist.
ins: Attach a single handle to a low pulley, stand with your back to the machine and take the handle with one hand, palm facing up.
Raise that arm so the elbow points to the ceiling and the handle sits behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arm overhead.
Keep the upper arm close to your head and still.
Lower the handle slowly behind your head, then switch arms after your set.

name: Cable Standing Row (v-Bar)
desc: A standing cable row with a V-handle set around chest height. It trains the upper back while your legs and core keep you steady, with the biceps and shoulders assisting.
ins: Attach a V-handle to a cable at about chest height and hold it with both hands.
Step back until your arms are straight and the weight lifts off the stack.
Stand with your knees soft and your feet hip-width apart, chest up.
Pull the handle to your stomach, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your back, then straighten your arms slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Standing Shoulder External Rotation
desc: A light standing cable exercise where you rotate your forearm outward with the elbow pinned to your side. It strengthens the rotator cuff muscles that turn the shoulder outward and is often used for injury prevention.
ins: Stand side-on to a cable at elbow height and hold the handle in the hand farther from the machine.
Bend that elbow to 90 degrees and keep it against your side with your forearm across your stomach.
Breathe out and rotate your forearm outward, away from your body, keeping the elbow in place.
Stop when you feel the end of your comfortable range.
Breathe in and return slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Cable Standing Twist Row (v-Bar)
desc: A standing cable row with a V-handle where you add a turn of the upper body as you pull. It works the upper back and brings in the obliques, with the biceps and shoulders helping.
ins: Set a V-handle at chest height and stand facing the cable with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Step back to straight arms with your knees soft and stomach braced.
Pull the handle toward your stomach while turning your chest to one side.
Let your hips stay mostly forward so the turn comes from your upper body.
Return to the centre with straight arms, then pull and turn to the other side.
Breathe out on each pull and in as you return.

name: Cable Standing Up Straight Crossovers
desc: A cable crossover done standing fully upright rather than leaning forward, with the arms meeting and crossing in front of the body. It trains the chest through a squeeze across the midline.
ins: Set both pulleys at shoulder height, hold a handle in each hand and stand tall in the middle with your feet hip-width apart.
Open your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows and your chest up.
Breathe out and bring your hands together in front of your chest, letting one hand cross past the other.
Squeeze your chest at the crossed position for a second.
Breathe in and let your arms open back out slowly, staying upright without leaning.
Swap which hand crosses on top each rep.

name: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown
desc: The classic straight-arm cable pulldown with a bar, a simple way to feel and isolate the lats. The shoulders and biceps play a supporting role.
ins: Stand facing a high pulley with a straight bar, a step or two back.
Hold the bar overhand at shoulder-width with your arms straight and slightly raised.
Brace your stomach and keep a small bend in your knees.
Push the bar down to your thighs in a wide arc without bending your elbows.
Hold the squeeze for a second, then let the bar return slowly.
Breathe out on the way down and in on the way up.

name: Cable Straight Arm Pulldown (with Rope)
desc: A straight-arm pulldown using a rope on a high cable, letting your hands pass beside your hips at the bottom for a fuller lat squeeze. It isolates the lats, with the biceps and forearms holding the rope.
ins: Attach a rope to the high pulley and hold one end in each hand.
Step back, hinge slightly forward and reach your arms up toward the pulley.
Keeping your arms nearly straight, pull the rope down in an arc toward your thighs.
At the bottom, spread the rope ends to the sides of your hips and squeeze your lats.
Let your arms rise slowly back to the start.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you let it up.

name: Cable Straight Back Seated Row
desc: A seated cable row where the main cue is keeping the back still and straight the whole time, so the upper back does the work instead of momentum. The biceps, forearms and shoulders assist.
ins: Sit at the low pulley with your feet braced and hold the handle with straight arms.
Sit upright with your chest up and shoulders down; this is your fixed position.
Pull the handle to your stomach without leaning back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Straighten your arms slowly while your torso stays upright.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Cable Supine Reverse Fly
desc: A reverse fly done lying chest-down on an incline bench between two low pulleys. Supporting your chest removes momentum so the rear shoulders work strictly.
ins: Set an incline bench between two low pulleys and lie chest-down on it, holding the left handle in your right hand and the right in your left.
Let your arms hang crossed under the bench with a slight bend in the elbows.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a second.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly.

name: Cable Thibaudeau Kayak Row
desc: A lat pulldown with a straight bar where you pull toward one side and then the other, like paddling a kayak. It works each lat through a slightly different angle.
ins: Sit at the pulldown machine with your thighs under the pads and grip the bar about shoulder-width apart.
Pull the bar down toward one side of your chest, letting your torso turn slightly toward that side.
Squeeze the lat on that side and breathe out.
Let the bar rise slowly back to the centre.
Pull toward the other side on the next rep and keep alternating.

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown (v-Bar)
desc: A triceps pushdown on a high cable using a V-shaped bar, which puts the wrists at a comfortable angle and lets you push heavier loads.
ins: Attach the V-bar to a high pulley and hold it with your thumbs on top.
Stand close with your elbows tucked against your sides and forearms about level with the floor.
Breathe out and push the bar down until your arms lock straight.
Pause and squeeze at the bottom.
Breathe in and let the bar rise slowly, keeping your upper arms still.

name: Cable Triceps Pushdown (v-Bar) (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A cable triceps pushdown with a V-shaped handle while wearing an arm blaster. The strap across your neck holds your elbows against your sides so the triceps can't get help from swinging.
ins: Put on the arm blaster so the plate rests against your stomach with your elbows against its sides.
Attach a V-handle to a high pulley and grip it with palms facing each other.
Stand tall close to the machine with your elbows pressed into the arm blaster.
Breathe out and push the handle down until your arms are straight.
Let the handle rise slowly until your forearms are just above parallel to the floor.

name: Cable Tuck Reverse Crunch
desc: A reverse crunch done lying down with ankle straps attached to a low cable, so your legs pull in against resistance. It targets the lower abs with the hip flexors assisting.
ins: Attach ankle straps to a low pulley and lie on your back with your feet toward the machine.
Hold onto something solid behind your head or press your palms into the floor.
Start with your legs nearly straight, then breathe out and tuck your knees in toward your chest.
At the end, curl your hips slightly off the floor to finish the crunch.
Extend your legs slowly against the cable without letting your lower back arch.

name: Cable Twist
desc: A standing cable rotation where you turn your torso while holding a handle out in front of your chest. It strengthens the obliques for twisting power.
ins: Set a handle at chest height and stand side-on to the machine, feet shoulder width apart and knees soft.
Hold the handle with both hands, arms extended in front of your chest.
Brace your abs and rotate your shoulders away from the machine, keeping your arms in front of your chest.
Pause briefly, then return slowly to the start.
Complete your reps and repeat facing the other way.

name: Cable Twist (up-Down)
desc: A diagonal twist where you pull a cable handle from a high pulley down across your body toward the opposite hip. It trains the abs and obliques to rotate with control, with the lower back helping to stabilize.
ins: Set a handle on the high pulley and stand side-on to the machine, feet a little wider than shoulder width.
Reach up and hold the handle with both hands above your near shoulder, arms almost straight.
Tighten your abs and pull the handle down and across your body toward your far hip, turning your chest as you go.
Let your back foot pivot so your knees and hips turn with you, and breathe out as you pull.
Return the handle slowly along the same path to the top.
Finish your set, then switch sides.

name: Cable Twisting Pull
desc: A one-arm cable pull with a rotation of the torso, pulling the handle across from a low pulley while turning away from the machine. It works the lats and shoulders and challenges the core, with the biceps helping.
ins: Set a single handle on a low pulley and stand facing it, holding the handle in one hand.
Step back with your knees soft until your arm is straight and you feel tension.
Brace your stomach and rotate slightly toward the machine to start.
Pull the handle up and back toward your chest while turning your shoulders away from the machine.
Reverse the motion slowly back to the start.
Finish all reps, then switch sides, breathing out on each pull.

name: Cable Two Arm Curl On Incline Bench
desc: A two-arm cable curl done lying back on an incline bench between two low pulleys. The arms start behind your body, which puts the biceps under a deep stretch.
ins: Place an incline bench between two low pulleys with single handles attached.
Sit back on the bench and take a handle in each hand, letting your arms hang down and slightly behind you, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl both handles toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until you feel the stretch again.

name: Cable Two Arm Tricep Kickback
desc: A two-arm triceps kickback using low cables while bent forward. The cables keep tension on the triceps even at full extension, where dumbbells go light.
ins: Stand between two low pulleys and take the left cable in your right hand and the right cable in your left hand so they cross.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back and pull your upper arms back alongside your body, elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten both arms behind you.
Squeeze the triceps hard with your arms fully straight.
Bend your elbows slowly to return, keeping the upper arms in place.

name: Cable Upper Chest Crossovers
desc: A cable crossover pulled from low pulleys up toward shoulder height, which shifts the work to the upper chest and front shoulders.
ins: Set both pulleys at the lowest position, take a handle in each hand and step to the middle with a slight forward stagger.
Let your arms hang down and slightly back with palms facing forward and a small bend in the elbows.
Breathe out and sweep your hands up and in until they meet in front of your face at about chin height.
Squeeze your upper chest briefly, keeping your shoulders down away from your ears.
Breathe in and lower your arms back along the same arc under control.

name: Cable Upper Row
desc: A standing cable row pulled to the upper chest with the elbows high. It focuses on the upper back and rear shoulders.
ins: Set a straight bar on the cable at about chest height and stand facing it.
Grip the bar overhand a little wider than shoulder width and step back until the cable is tight.
Stand tall with soft knees and a tight stomach.
Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows out at shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Straighten your arms slowly with control.

name: Cable Upright Row
desc: An upright row using a straight bar on a low pulley. The cable keeps the side shoulders and traps working throughout the lift.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and hold it at your thighs with an overhand grip at about shoulder width.
Stand close to the machine, tall, with your stomach braced.
Breathe out and pull the bar up close to your body by lifting your elbows out to the sides.
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly.

name: Cable Wide Grip Rear Pulldown Behind Neck
desc: An advanced lat pulldown in which a wide bar is lowered behind the head. It works the lats and upper back but needs good shoulder mobility, so use a light weight.
ins: Sit at the pulldown machine with your thighs under the pads and grip the bar wide with an overhand grip.
Lean your head slightly forward so the bar can pass behind it.
Pull the bar down behind your head to about the base of your neck, elbows pointing down.
Breathe out and squeeze your shoulder blades down and together.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Stop and switch to a front pulldown if you feel any pinching in the shoulders.

name: Cable Wrist Curl
desc: A seated wrist curl on a low cable pulley with your palms facing up. The cable gives constant resistance to the inner forearm muscles.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and sit on a bench facing it.
Hold the bar with your palms up and rest your forearms on your thighs, wrists just past your knees.
Let the cable draw your hands down so your wrists bend back.
Breathe out and curl your palms up toward your forearms.
Squeeze at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Keep your forearms still on your legs.

name: Calf Press on Seated Leg Press
ref: Sled Calf Press On Leg Press
desc: A calf raise done on the 45-degree leg press, pushing the platform with the balls of the feet. It builds the calves under a heavy, back-supported load.
ins: Sit in the leg press with your back flat on the pad and the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, heels off.
Press the platform up until your legs are straight but not locked, then release the safety stops.
Let your heels travel toward you slowly so you feel a stretch in the calves.
Push through the balls of your feet to point your toes and drive the platform away as far as you can.
Squeeze for a second at the top, then lower under control; breathe out as you push.
Lock the safety stops before you take your feet off.

name: Calf Push Stretch With Hands Against Wall
desc: A classic wall calf stretch in a split stance, leaning into the wall with your hands. It loosens tight calves after running or leg training.
ins: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place both palms on it at shoulder height.
Step one foot back and keep it straight with the heel pressed into the floor.
Bend the front knee and lean your weight toward the wall.
Keep your back heel down and your toes pointing forward; hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Breathe out as you sink deeper, then switch legs.

name: Calf Stretch With Hands Against Wall
desc: A classic standing calf stretch with your hands on a wall and one leg stepped back. It lengthens the calf muscles and the back of the lower leg.
ins: Stand facing a wall and place both hands on it at shoulder height.
Step one foot back about a long stride, toes pointing straight ahead.
Keep the back leg straight and press its heel into the floor.
Bend the front knee and lean toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Switch legs.

name: Calf Stretch With Rope
desc: A seated calf stretch where you loop a rope around your foot and pull your toes toward you. It stretches the calf and also the hamstring of the straight leg.
ins: Sit on the floor with both legs straight in front of you.
Loop a rope or towel around the ball of one foot and hold an end in each hand.
Sit tall and keep the knee straight.
Gently pull the rope so your toes come back toward you.
Hold a comfortable stretch for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Release and switch legs.

name: Cambered Bar Lying Row
desc: A chest-supported row lying face down on a high bench, using a cambered bar whose bend lets you pull higher before it touches the bench. It focuses on the upper back with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Lie face down on a high flat bench with the cambered bar on the floor or rack beneath you.
Grab the bar overhand at about shoulder-width and let it hang with straight arms.
Keep your chest on the bench and your legs still.
Row the bar up as high as you can, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower it slowly to a full stretch.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Chair Leg Extended Stretch
desc: A gentle stretch done sitting on the edge of a chair with one leg straight out in front. It eases tight legs and is easy to do at home or at work, mostly through the back of the thigh and the calf.
ins: Sit near the front edge of a sturdy chair with your back straight.
Straighten one leg in front of you with the heel on the floor and toes pointing up.
Keep the other foot flat on the floor with the knee bent.
Place your hands on the bent leg and lean forward from the hips, keeping your back long.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then switch legs.

name: Chest And Front Of Shoulder Stretch
desc: A simple standing stretch that opens the chest and the front of the shoulders, useful after pressing work or long periods of sitting.
ins: Stand tall and clasp your hands together behind your lower back.
Straighten your arms and gently pull your shoulder blades together.
Lift your hands slightly away from your back until you feel a stretch across your chest and the front of your shoulders.
Keep your chin level and your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then release.

name: Chest Dip
desc: A bodyweight dip on parallel bars with the torso leaned forward to bias the chest. It is a demanding pushing exercise that also works the triceps and front shoulders.
ins: Grip the dip bars and jump or step up so you are supported on straight arms.
Lean your chest forward and bend your knees slightly so your body tilts.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself until you feel a stretch in your chest and your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms while keeping the forward lean.
Breathe in going down, out coming up, and stop the descent if your shoulders feel pinched.

name: Chest Dip (on Dip-Pull-Up Cage)
desc: A bodyweight dip on the dip station of a dip and pull-up tower, done with a forward lean so the chest does most of the work. The triceps and front shoulders also work hard.
ins: Grip the dip handles and jump or step up until you are supported on straight arms.
Cross your ankles behind you and lean your torso forward.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower yourself until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows or you feel a strong stretch in your chest.
Keep your elbows angled slightly out and your shoulders down away from your ears.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms while keeping the forward lean.

name: Chest Dip On Straight Bar
desc: A dip performed on a single straight bar in front of you instead of parallel bars. It is harder to balance and works the chest, triceps and front shoulders strongly.
ins: Stand in front of a straight bar at about hip height, grip it with hands shoulder-width apart and jump up so you are supported on straight arms with the bar at your hips.
Lean your chest forward over the bar and bring your legs slightly forward underneath you for balance.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar.
Keep your elbows pointing back and slightly out, not flaring wide.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms.

name: Chest Fly
desc: A seated fly on a pec deck machine, where you bring the arms together in front of your chest against resistance. It isolates the chest with a stable, guided path that suits beginners.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles or pads are at chest height, then sit with your back against the pad.
Hold the handles with a slight bend in your elbows and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a smooth arc.
Squeeze your chest for a moment when they meet.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch, breathing in, and breathe out as you close.

name: Chest Fly (Band)
desc: The standard flat-bench dumbbell fly, an isolation move that stretches and contracts the chest without much help from the triceps. It is usually done with moderate weight after pressing exercises.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand held above your chest, palms facing each other.
Unlock your elbows into a slight bend and keep it the same for the whole set.
Open your arms slowly out to the sides until your hands are about level with your chest.
Pull the dumbbells back up and together as if hugging a large barrel.
Inhale during the lowering and exhale as you bring the weights up.

name: Chest Fly (Cable)
desc: A standing cable fly with the pulleys set at about chest height, so the hands travel straight across in front of the body. It targets the middle of the chest.
ins: Set both pulleys around shoulder or chest height, take the handles and step forward into a split stance.
Open your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in your elbows and your chest up.
Pull your hands forward and together in a horizontal arc until they meet in front of your chest.
Pause and squeeze, keeping your elbows from bending further.
Return slowly to the stretched position while breathing in; breathe out as you bring the hands together.

name: Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
desc: The standard flat-bench dumbbell fly, an isolation move that stretches and contracts the chest without much help from the triceps. It is usually done with moderate weight after pressing exercises.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand held above your chest, palms facing each other.
Unlock your elbows into a slight bend and keep it the same for the whole set.
Open your arms slowly out to the sides until your hands are about level with your chest.
Pull the dumbbells back up and together as if hugging a large barrel.
Inhale during the lowering and exhale as you bring the weights up.

name: Chest Press (Machine)
desc: A seated chest press on a plate-loaded or selectorised machine that guides the handles along a fixed path. It is a simple, safe way for beginners to build the chest, triceps and front shoulders.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest, then sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing down and your elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest, without letting the weight stack touch down.
Breathe out as you push and in as you return.

name: Chest Stretch With Exercise Ball
desc: A kneeling stretch that uses an exercise ball to open up one side of the chest and the front of the shoulder.
ins: Kneel beside an exercise ball and place one forearm or hand on top of it with the arm out to the side.
Keep your other hand on the floor for support and your back flat.
Slowly lower your chest toward the floor and turn it slightly away from the ball, letting the ball roll a little.
Stop when you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest and front of the shoulder.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds with slow breaths, then switch sides.

name: Chest Tap Push-Up
desc: An explosive push-up where you push off the floor and quickly tap your chest with both hands before landing. It builds upper-body power and fast hands.
ins: Start in a push-up position with your hands just wider than your shoulders and your body straight.
Lower your chest close to the floor with your stomach tight.
Push up as hard as you can so your upper body rises off the floor.
Quickly tap your chest with both hands while you are in the air.
Get your hands back to the floor and land with soft elbows, then go into the next rep.
Master clap push-ups before trying this, and stop if you start landing heavily.

name: Chin Tuck
desc: A posture exercise that slides the head straight back to line it up over the shoulders. It strengthens the deep front neck muscles and helps undo forward-head posture.
ins: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and eyes looking straight ahead.
Without tipping your head up or down, glide your chin straight back as if making a double chin.
Feel a gentle stretch at the base of the skull and keep your eyes level.
Hold for 3 to 5 seconds while breathing normally.
Relax back to the start and repeat.

name: Chin Up
desc: A pull-up done with palms facing you. It builds the lats and gives the biceps more work than a regular overhand pull-up.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart and arms straight.
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears and tighten your stomach.
Breathe out and pull yourself up until your chin is above the bar.
Keep your body still and avoid swinging your legs.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are fully straight.

name: Chin-Ups (narrow Parallel Grip)
desc: A chin-up on close parallel handles with the palms facing each other, a strong and shoulder-friendly grip. It trains the upper back and lats with heavy biceps involvement.
ins: Grab close parallel handles with your palms facing each other.
Hang with straight arms, legs together and stomach tight.
Pull yourself up, driving your elbows down close to your ribs.
Bring your chin above your hands with your chest close to the handles.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Circles Knee Stretch
desc: A gentle mobility drill where you circle your knees with your hands resting on them. It warms up the knees, ankles and calves before training.
ins: Stand with your feet together and bend your knees slightly.
Lean forward a little and place your hands on top of your knees.
Slowly move your knees in a circle, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Make 10 smooth circles in one direction.
Reverse and make 10 circles the other way.
Keep the circles small and pain-free and breathe normally.

name: Clap Push Up
desc: An explosive push-up where you push hard enough to lift your hands off the floor and clap before landing. It builds power in the chest, triceps and shoulders.
ins: Get into a push-up position with hands a bit wider than your shoulders and your body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest close to the floor with your stomach tight.
Push up as hard and fast as you can so your hands leave the floor.
Clap your hands quickly in front of your chest.
Land with soft elbows, hands back in place, and sink straight into the next rep.
Stop the set as soon as you cannot get enough height to clap safely.

name: Clock Push-Up
desc: An advanced push-up where you walk your hands around in a circle between reps, using your feet as the centre point like the hand of a clock. It challenges the chest, triceps, shoulders and core from constantly changing angles.
ins: Get into a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight from head to heels.
Do one full push-up, lowering your chest close to the floor and pressing back up.
Walk your hands a step to one side so your body pivots around your feet.
Do another push-up in the new position, then keep stepping and pushing until you have gone around the full circle.
Keep your stomach and glutes tight so your hips never sag, and breathe out on every press.

name: Close Grip Chin-Up
desc: A chin-up with the hands close together and palms facing you. The narrow grip puts even more load on the biceps while still training the lats.
ins: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip, hands a few centimetres apart.
Set your shoulders down and keep your legs still.
Breathe out and pull up, keeping your elbows in front of you, until your chin clears the bar.
Hold for a moment at the top.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
desc: A push-up with the hands placed under or just inside the shoulders and the elbows kept close to the ribs. It shifts the effort toward the triceps.
ins: Get into a push-up position with your hands slightly narrower than your shoulders and your body straight.
Tighten your stomach and glutes so your hips don't sag.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows brushing your sides.
Stop just above the floor.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up (on Knees)
desc: A close-grip push-up done from the knees. It is an easier way to build triceps and chest strength before moving to full close-grip push-ups.
ins: Kneel on a mat and place your hands under your chest, a little narrower than shoulder-width.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your hips in line with your body; don't let them pike up.

name: Cocoons
desc: A lying ab exercise where you go from fully stretched out to curled up in a tight ball, then back. It works the whole abdominal wall with the hip flexors and lower back assisting.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched overhead, both slightly off the floor.
Breathe out and sit up while pulling your knees in to your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins for a moment so your body forms a tight ball.
Breathe in and stretch back out slowly to the long starting position, keeping your arms and legs off the floor if you can.

name: Concentration Curl (Dumbbell)
desc: A seated one-arm curl with the elbow braced against your inner thigh. Bracing the arm stops any swinging and lets you focus on squeezing the biceps.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wide and a dumbbell in one hand.
Lean forward and rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh, arm straight down.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly to a straight arm; switch arms after the set.

name: Converging Chest Press (Machine)
desc: A seated chest press on a plate-loaded or selectorised machine that guides the handles along a fixed path. It is a simple, safe way for beginners to build the chest, triceps and front shoulders.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest, then sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing down and your elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest, without letting the weight stack touch down.
Breathe out as you push and in as you return.

name: Crab Twist Toe Touch
desc: A dynamic move from a crab position where you kick one leg up and reach the opposite hand across to touch it. It works the abs and obliques, with the hip flexors and shoulders also involved.
ins: Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet flat, hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through your hands and feet to lift your hips into a crab position.
Kick one leg up while lifting the opposite hand and reaching it across to touch your toes, breathing out.
Keep your hips lifted and your supporting arm straight as you twist.
Return the hand and foot to the floor, then repeat on the other side.

name: Cross Body Crunch
desc: A crunch with a twist that brings one elbow across your body toward the opposite knee. It works the abs and puts extra focus on the obliques.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and fingertips lightly behind your head.
Breathe out and lift your shoulders while turning to bring your right elbow toward your left knee.
Lift the knee slightly to meet the elbow if you like.
Lower back down with control and repeat to the other side.
Keep your elbows wide and avoid pulling on your neck.

name: Cross-over back (cable)
desc: A reverse fly on the cable crossover station with the pulleys at shoulder height, pulling the handles apart with crossed cables. It isolates the rear shoulders and also works the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Set both pulleys to shoulder height with no handles, and hold the left cable end in your right hand and the right one in your left.
Step back to the middle so the cables cross in front of you and your arms are straight at chest height.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and pull your arms apart and back until they line up with your body.
Breathe in and let your arms come back together slowly.

name: Crunch (hands Overhead)
desc: A floor crunch with your arms stretched straight overhead, which makes the lever longer and the abs work harder. Hip flexors assist lightly.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Stretch your arms overhead, keeping them in line with your ears.
Breathe out and curl your head, arms and shoulders off the floor as one unit.
Keep your arms beside your ears; do not swing them forward to help.
Lower slowly until your shoulders touch the floor.

name: Crunch (Machine)
desc: A crunch performed on a seated ab machine, where you curl forward against an adjustable weight stack. It focuses on the abs, with the obliques helping.
ins: Set the weight, sit on the machine and hook your feet under the foot pads if it has them.
Hold the handles or place your arms on the pads in front of your chest.
Breathe out and curl your chest down toward your hips, rounding your back with your abs.
Squeeze for a second at the bottom without yanking with your arms.
Breathe in and return slowly, stopping before the weight stack touches down.

name: Crunch (on Stability Ball)
desc: A crunch done lying back on a stability ball, which lets your abs move through a bigger range than on the floor. It trains the abs with light hip flexor help.
ins: Sit on a stability ball, then walk your feet forward until your lower and middle back rest on the ball.
Plant your feet wide for balance and place your fingertips by your ears.
Let your upper back drape gently over the ball to stretch your abs.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders up until your abs are fully tight.
Lower slowly back over the ball.

name: Crunch (on Stability Ball, Arms Straight)
desc: A stability ball crunch with your arms held straight up toward the ceiling, reaching higher as you curl. It works the abs and keeps your hands off your neck.
ins: Lie back on a stability ball with it under your middle back and your feet planted wide.
Hold your arms straight up toward the ceiling with your palms together.
Breathe out and crunch up, reaching your hands higher toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your abs at the top without sitting all the way up.
Lower slowly until your back rests over the ball again.

name: Crunch Floor
desc: The basic floor crunch, a short curl of the upper body that works the front of the abs. It is a simple starting point for ab training.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Cross your arms over your chest or place your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and lift your head and shoulder blades off the floor by tightening your abs.
Keep your lower back on the floor and look slightly up, not at your knees.
Lower slowly and keep tension on your abs between reps.

name: Curl-Up
desc: A short, controlled ab exercise where you lift only your head and shoulders off the floor, sliding your hands toward your knees. It works the abs while keeping strain off the lower back and neck.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, palms resting on your thighs.
Tighten your abs and keep your lower back in contact with the floor.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders up, sliding your hands along your thighs toward your knees.
Stop when your shoulder blades clear the floor and hold for a second.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly.

name: Curtsey Squat
desc: A lunge where one leg steps diagonally behind the other, like a curtsey, before you squat down. It works the glutes, especially the outer part, along with the quads and hamstrings.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or clasped at your chest.
Step your right foot back and across behind your left leg.
Breathe in and bend both knees to lower your hips, keeping your chest up.
Keep your front knee over the ankle and your hips facing forward.
Breathe out and push through the front foot to return to standing.
Alternate sides or finish one side first.

name: Cycle Cross Trainer
desc: A seated cross trainer that combines pedaling with pushing and pulling arm handles. It gives low-impact cardio for the legs while the upper body joins in.
ins: Adjust the seat so your knees stay slightly bent at the farthest point of each stride.
Sit with your back against the backrest, feet on the pedals, and hands on the handles.
Start a smooth pedaling motion while pushing and pulling the handles in rhythm.
Keep your core lightly tight and avoid rocking side to side.
Set the resistance to a level you can hold for your planned time, breathing steadily.
Lower the pace for the last few minutes to cool down.

name: Dead Bug
desc: A slow, controlled core exercise where you lie on your back and lower opposite arm and leg while keeping your lower back still. It builds deep core stability and coordination.
ins: Lie on your back with your arms pointing to the ceiling and your knees bent at 90 degrees over your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and brace your abs.
Breathe out and slowly lower your right arm overhead and your left leg toward the floor at the same time.
Stop just above the floor, keeping your lower back still, then return to the start.
Repeat with the left arm and right leg, moving slowly.

name: Deadlift (Barbell)
desc: The classic barbell lift from the floor to standing, driven by the hips. It builds the glutes, hamstrings and lower back, and strengthens your grip and whole posterior chain.
ins: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs, then bend your knees until your shins touch it.
Flatten your back, pull your shoulders down and take a big breath into your belly.
Push the floor away and keep the bar close to your legs as it rises.
Once it passes your knees, push your hips forward and stand tall; do not lean back.
Lower it by pushing your hips back first, then bending your knees once it passes them, and breathe out at the top or after setting it down.

name: Decline Bench Press (Barbell)
desc: A barbell press done on a bench set head-down, which shifts more of the work to the lower chest. The shorter range is often easier on the shoulders.
ins: Lock your legs under the pads of a decline bench and lie back with your eyes under the bar.
Take a grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack the bar, ideally with a spotter's help.
Lower the bar slowly to the lower part of your chest, keeping your elbows tucked a little.
Drive the bar straight back up until your arms are extended over your chest.
Inhale as you lower and exhale as you press.

name: Decline Crunch
desc: A crunch done on a decline bench with your head lower than your hips, which makes the abs work against more gravity. Hip flexors help hold your legs in place.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your feet hooked under the rollers and your head at the low end.
Cross your arms over your chest or put your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders up off the bench, rounding your upper back.
Stop once your abs are fully contracted, before you sit all the way up.
Lower slowly back to the bench.

name: Decline Push-Up
desc: A push-up with your feet raised on a bench or box, which tilts more of your body weight onto your hands. The angle shifts the work toward the upper chest and front shoulders.
ins: Place your feet on a bench or step behind you and set your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Brace your stomach so your body forms a straight line from heels to head.
Bend your elbows and lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
Push the floor away until your arms are straight again.
Inhale as you go down and exhale as you push up; do not let your hips drop.

name: Decline Sit-Up
desc: A full sit-up on a decline bench, rising from lying to upright against the slope. It builds the abs and hip flexors, with the lower back working to control the descent.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your feet hooked under the rollers and your arms crossed on your chest.
Brace your abs and breathe out as you curl up, then keep rising until your chest is near your thighs.
Lead with your chest rather than jerking with your head.
Breathe in and lower slowly, rolling your back down one section at a time.
Stop just before your head touches the bench and go again.

name: Deep Push Up
desc: A push-up done with your hands on dumbbells or handles so your chest can sink below hand level. The extra depth gives the chest a bigger stretch and makes it work harder.
ins: Place two hex dumbbells on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width and grip the handles.
Walk your feet back into a push-up position with your body in one straight line.
Breathe in and lower your chest between the dumbbells until it drops just below your hands.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body and your hips in line.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.

name: Diamond Push-Up
desc: A push-up with your hands touching under your chest so the thumbs and index fingers form a diamond shape. It is one of the hardest bodyweight exercises for the triceps.
ins: Get into a push-up position and place your hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers touching.
Set your feet together or slightly apart and keep your body in a straight line.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward your hands, elbows pointing back.
Go as low as you can while keeping your hips in line.
Breathe out and push back up to straight arms; drop to your knees if needed.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
desc: A calf raise done bent over at the hips with your hands supported, which puts the calves in a stretched position. It targets the calves strongly using body weight.
ins: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step and your heels hanging off.
Hinge forward at the hips and rest your forearms or hands on a bench or bar in front of you.
Keep your back flat and your legs nearly straight.
Lower your heels for a deep calf stretch.
Breathe out and push up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Double Under Jump Rope
desc: An advanced jump rope skill in which the rope passes under the feet twice during a single jump. It is intense cardio that builds calf power, timing and grip endurance.
ins: Warm up with regular single jumps until you have a steady rhythm.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and hands near your hips.
Jump a little higher than usual, staying tall with your legs nearly straight.
Spin the rope with fast wrist flicks so it passes under you twice before you land.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and go straight into the next jump.
Breathe steadily and mix in single jumps when you need to recover.

name: Drop Push Up
desc: A beginner-friendly drop push-up done from the knees: you fall forward from an upright kneeling position, catch yourself on your hands and push back up. It teaches the chest and arms to absorb and return force.
ins: Kneel tall on a mat with your body upright and your hands at chest height.
Keep your body straight from knees to head and let yourself fall forward.
Catch yourself on your hands about shoulder-width apart and bend your elbows to soften the landing.
Lower your chest close to the floor in a knee push-up.
Push hard enough to bring your torso back up to the upright kneeling position.
Start with small falls and move your knees further back as you get stronger.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Biceps Curl
desc: A standing dumbbell curl where your arms take turns lifting. Alternating lets you focus on each biceps and turn the palm up as you lift.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing your thighs.
Breathe out and curl the right dumbbell up, turning your palm to face up as it rises.
Squeeze the biceps at the top with your elbow still at your side.
Breathe in and lower it slowly while turning the palm back in.
Repeat with the left arm and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Biceps Curl (with Arm Blaster)
desc: An alternating dumbbell biceps curl done with an arm blaster. One arm works at a time while the strap keeps both elbows still.
ins: Put on the arm blaster and rest your elbows against the sides of the plate.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight, palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up to your shoulder.
Lower it slowly, then curl the other dumbbell.
Keep alternating without leaning back.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Hammer Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl with two dumbbells held thumbs-up, lifting one arm at a time. It works the biceps, brachialis and forearms with the upper arms locked on the pad.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and rest both upper arms on the pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up, keeping your thumb pointing up.
Squeeze at the top, then lower it slowly to an almost straight arm.
Curl the other dumbbell the same way.
Keep alternating without lifting your elbows off the pad.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Preacher Curl
desc: A dumbbell preacher curl alternating arms, with both upper arms resting on the pad. Working one arm at a time lets you focus on each biceps.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench with both upper arms on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Squeeze, then lower it slowly until the arm is nearly straight.
Curl the other dumbbell the same way.
Keep alternating, moving only at the elbows.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Seated Hammer Curl
desc: A seated hammer curl lifting one dumbbell at a time with a thumbs-up grip. Sitting removes body swing, and the neutral grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearms.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your back straight, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep your elbows close to your body.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up toward your shoulder, thumb pointing up.
Lower it slowly, then curl the other one.
Keep alternating without rocking your torso.

name: Dumbbell Alternate Side Press
desc: A standing dumbbell press where you lean your upper body slightly away from the working arm as you press, one side at a time. It works the shoulders while your side abs keep you stable.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and keep your hips still.
Breathe out and press one dumbbell up while you bend your upper body a little to the opposite side.
Straighten your body as you lower the dumbbell to your shoulder.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Alternating Bicep Curl With Leg Raised On Exercise Ball
desc: An alternating dumbbell curl done sitting on an exercise ball with one foot lifted off the floor. The biceps do the curling while your core, hips and shoulders work hard to keep you balanced.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms forward.
Brace your stomach and lift one foot off the floor, straightening that leg in front of you.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up while keeping your balance.
Lower it slowly, then curl the other dumbbell.
Switch the raised leg halfway through the set.

name: Dumbbell Alternating Seated Bicep Curl On Exercise Ball
desc: An alternating dumbbell curl done seated on an exercise ball. The ball makes your core work to keep you upright while each biceps works in turn.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with your feet flat and wide, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms forward.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows close to your body.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Lower it slowly, then curl the other dumbbell.
Keep alternating without leaning or rolling the ball.

name: Dumbbell Arnold Press
desc: A seated dumbbell press that starts with your palms facing you and turns them forward as you press. The rotation works the front and side shoulders through a long range.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold the dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
Keep your elbows in front of your body and your feet flat.
Breathe out and press up while turning your palms forward and moving your elbows out.
Finish with your arms straight above your shoulders.
Breathe in and reverse the turn as you lower back to the start.

name: Dumbbell Around Pullover
desc: A lying dumbbell exercise where straight arms travel in a big half-circle from your thighs, out to the sides and up past your head. It stretches and strengthens the chest and lats and works the shoulders through a wide range.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a light dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and resting by your thighs, palms facing up.
Keeping your arms nearly straight and low, sweep the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc.
Continue the arc until the dumbbells meet above and behind your head.
Reverse the circle along the same path back to your thighs.
Move slowly, use light weights, and keep your lower back pressed to the bench; breathe steadily.

name: Dumbbell Bench Seated Press
desc: A dumbbell shoulder press done sitting on the end of a flat bench with no back support. It works the shoulders and triceps and makes you hold your posture yourself.
ins: Sit on the end of a flat bench with your feet flat and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward.
Sit up tall and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Keep your back straight and don't lean back.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly to shoulder height.

name: Dumbbell Bench Squat
desc: A squat to a bench while holding dumbbells, sitting back until you touch the seat and then standing. It is a beginner-friendly way to build the glutes and quads with a clear, safe depth target.
ins: Stand a short step in front of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Breathe in, brace and sit your hips back and down until your glutes lightly touch the bench.
Keep your chest up and your knees pushed out in line with your toes.
Without relaxing onto the bench, drive through your heels to stand up.
Breathe out as you stand.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl Lunge With Bowling Motion
desc: A combination move: a curtsy-style lunge, stepping one leg back behind the other as in a bowling delivery, paired with a dumbbell curl. It trains the biceps while the legs, glutes and balance work too.
ins: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms forward.
Step your right leg back and across behind your left, bending both knees as if bowling a ball.
At the bottom of the lunge, breathe out and curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly while staying low.
Push through your front foot to stand up, then repeat stepping back with the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl On Exercise Ball With Leg Raised
desc: A two-arm dumbbell curl done sitting on an exercise ball with one leg lifted. Both biceps work together while your core and hips fight to keep you steady on one foot.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms forward.
Brace your stomach and raise one foot off the floor, leg straight in front of you.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up at the same time.
Squeeze briefly, then lower them slowly.
Switch the raised leg halfway through or between sets.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl With Stork Stance
desc: A dumbbell biceps curl done balancing on one leg, with the other foot resting against your standing leg. It works the biceps and adds a balance challenge for the ankle, hip and core.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with palms facing forward.
Shift your weight onto one leg and place the other foot against the inside of the standing calf or knee.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Lower them slowly while keeping your balance.
Switch legs halfway through the set.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A standing dumbbell biceps curl done with an arm blaster strapped around your neck. The plate keeps your elbows fixed at your sides, so the biceps can't be helped by swinging.
ins: Put on the arm blaster so the plate sits across your stomach and rest your elbows against its sides.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms straight and palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top for a moment.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl Reverse
desc: A standing dumbbell curl with your palms facing down. The overhand grip brings in the brachialis and the top of the forearm along with the biceps.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing back.
Keep your elbows at your sides and your wrists straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, palms still facing down.
Pause at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl Squat
desc: A combination of a dumbbell squat and a biceps curl. The squat works the legs and glutes, and the curl at the top trains the biceps.
ins: Set your feet about shoulder-width apart and let a dumbbell hang at each side.
Breathe in and squat down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, chest up.
Breathe out and drive through your feet to stand up.
At the top, curl both dumbbells to your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly, then start the next squat.

name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl V Sit On Bosu Ball
desc: A dumbbell curl done in a V-sit on a BOSU, leaning back with your feet off the floor. Your core works hard to hold the position while the biceps curl.
ins: Sit on the center of a BOSU dome holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor, knees bent, to form a V shape.
Brace your stomach and let your arms hang with palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, then lower them slowly.
Keep your chest up and your balance steady through the set.

name: Dumbbell Burpee
desc: A burpee done while holding a dumbbell in each hand, often finishing with a press or curl to the shoulders. The added load makes it a tough full-body conditioning exercise.
ins: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Squat down and set the dumbbells on the floor under your shoulders, gripping the handles.
Jump or step your feet back into a plank on the dumbbells, keeping your body straight.
Jump your feet back toward your hands.
Stand up with the dumbbells, keeping your back flat as you lift.
Breathe out as you stand, then lower straight into the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Clean
desc: An explosive lift that pulls two dumbbells from below the knees to the front of your shoulders in one motion. It builds power in the glutes, hamstrings and quads and coordination through the whole body.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to lower the dumbbells just below your knees, back flat.
Jump your hips forward hard, extending your hips, knees and ankles, and shrug the dumbbells up close to your body.
As they rise, pull your elbows up and then quickly rotate them under to catch the dumbbells on your shoulders.
Land in a quarter squat with soft knees, then stand tall.
Lower the dumbbells to your thighs with control and breathe out after each catch.

name: Dumbbell Close-Grip Press
desc: A dumbbell press on a flat bench with the dumbbells held together and palms facing each other. Squeezing them together keeps the elbows in and makes the triceps work hard.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding two dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other and the dumbbells touching.
Press the dumbbells together firmly and keep them in contact for the whole set.
Breathe in and lower them to your mid chest with your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your feet planted and your shoulder blades squeezed together.

name: Dumbbell Complex Push Up Row Clean And Press
desc: A full-body dumbbell complex that links a push-up, a row with each arm, a clean to the shoulders and an overhead press. It works the shoulders, chest, back, legs and core and builds conditioning.
ins: Start in a push-up position holding two dumbbells on the floor under your shoulders, feet wide for balance.
Do one push-up, keeping your body in a straight line.
Row one dumbbell to your ribs, set it down, then row the other.
Step your feet up toward your hands, then clean the dumbbells from the floor to your shoulders by driving through your hips.
Stand tall and press the dumbbells overhead, breathing out.
Lower them to your shoulders, then to the floor, and step back into the push-up position for the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Contralateral Forward Lunge
desc: A forward lunge holding a single dumbbell in the hand opposite the front leg. The uneven load makes the hip of the front leg work harder to stay stable, building the glutes and quads.
ins: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in your left hand at your side.
Step forward with your right foot into a lunge.
Breathe in and lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, keeping your shoulders level.
Do not let your body lean toward the dumbbell side.
Breathe out and push off the right foot to step back to standing.
Finish the set, then switch the dumbbell to the right hand and lunge with the left leg.

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl
desc: A hammer curl where the dumbbell travels across your body toward the opposite shoulder. It trains the brachialis, forearms and biceps from a slightly different angle.
ins: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing in.
Breathe out and curl the right dumbbell up and across your chest toward your left shoulder, thumb on top.
Keep your upper arm close to your body.
Breathe in and lower it along the same path.
Repeat with the left arm toward the right shoulder and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Cross Body Hammer Curl (Pause at Top)
desc: A hammer curl in which each dumbbell is brought across your body toward the opposite shoulder, one arm at a time. It strongly targets the brachialis and forearms along with the biceps.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your thighs.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up and across your chest toward the opposite shoulder, thumb up.
Squeeze briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower it slowly back to your side.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Cuban Press
desc: A three-part dumbbell move that chains a high pull, an outward shoulder rotation and an overhead press. It strengthens the shoulders and the rotator cuff together, so use light weights.
ins: Stand tall and hold light dumbbells at your thighs with an overhand grip.
Pull your elbows up and out until your upper arms are level with your shoulders and your forearms hang down.
Keeping your elbows in place, rotate your forearms up until the dumbbells are above your elbows.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells overhead.
Reverse each step slowly to return to the start.

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
desc: A deadlift using a pair of dumbbells held at your sides or in front of your legs. It is an easy-to-learn version that strengthens the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and the dumbbells on the floor just outside your feet.
Hinge at the hips, bend your knees and grip the dumbbells with your back flat and chest up.
Brace your core and push through your feet to stand up straight.
Keep the dumbbells close to your legs and finish by squeezing your glutes.
Lower them back down by pushing your hips back first, then bending your knees.
Breathe out as you stand and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Decline Bench Press
desc: A dumbbell press on a decline bench that emphasises the lower chest. Using dumbbells allows a natural hand path and a deep stretch at the bottom.
ins: Hook your legs under the pads of a decline bench and lie back holding a dumbbell in each hand at your chest.
Press both dumbbells up over your lower chest until your arms are straight.
Lower them under control to the sides of your lower chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom, then press back up.
Exhale on each press; when finished, bring the dumbbells to your chest before sitting up.

name: Dumbbell Decline Fly
desc: A dumbbell fly on a decline bench, isolating the lower chest. The arms stay slightly bent and open wide to stretch the chest.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured, holding dumbbells above your lower chest with palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep that angle fixed.
Open your arms out to the sides until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest in a wide hugging arc.
Breathe in as you open and out as you close; choose a weight you can control at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Decline Hammer Press
desc: A decline dumbbell press with your palms facing each other in a neutral, hammer-style grip. It targets the lower chest and triceps while being gentle on the shoulders.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and hold the dumbbells at your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your sides rather than flared.
