Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are extended over your lower chest.
Lower them slowly back to the sides of your chest.
Breathe out as you press and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Decline One Arm Fly
desc: A single-arm dumbbell fly on a decline bench that isolates the lower chest of one side and lets you focus on a deep, controlled stretch.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and hold a dumbbell in one hand above your chest, palm facing in.
Place your free hand on the bench or your stomach to stay balanced.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell out to the side in a wide arc, elbow slightly bent.
Stop when your upper arm is about level with your body and you feel the stretch.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbell back up over your chest along the same arc.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Decline One Arm Hammer Press
desc: A one-arm dumbbell press on a decline bench with your palm facing in. The neutral grip and lower arm path shift much of the work to the triceps, with the lower chest and shoulder helping.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured and hold one dumbbell over your chest, palm facing in toward your body.
Put your free hand on your stomach or hold the bench to stay steady.
Lower the dumbbell to the side of your chest, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Breathe out and press it straight back up until your arm is straight.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Decline Shrug
desc: A dumbbell shrug done lying face down on an angled bench, which takes the lower back and leg drive out of the lift. It isolates the traps, with some help from the shoulders and mid back.
ins: Lie face down on an angled bench, chest supported, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let the dumbbells hang straight below your shoulders.
Raise your shoulders toward your ears without bending your elbows.
Pause at the top and squeeze your traps.
Lower your shoulders slowly to a full stretch.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Decline Shrug (Shoulder Blades Back)
desc: A chest-supported dumbbell shrug done face down on an angled bench, where the shoulders pull back toward each other as well as up. It works the traps and the muscles between the shoulder blades, with the shoulders assisting.
ins: Set a bench at a moderate angle and lie face down on it with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down with your palms facing each other.
Keeping your arms straight, pull your shoulders up and back so your shoulder blades meet.
Hold the squeeze for a second at the top.
Let your shoulders sink slowly back down and forward.
Breathe out as you squeeze and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Decline Triceps Extension
desc: A lying dumbbell triceps extension done on a decline bench. The decline keeps tension on the triceps through more of the movement.
ins: Secure your feet on a decline bench and lie back holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing up.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the triceps.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to raise the dumbbells back up.

name: Dumbbell Decline Twist Fly
desc: A decline dumbbell fly that adds a wrist rotation, turning the palms as the arms close and open. The twist increases the squeeze on the lower and inner chest.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with legs secured and hold the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc, turning your palms to face the ceiling as you go down.
Stop when you feel a stretch in your chest, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lift back up in the same arc, rotating your palms back to face each other and then turning your little fingers slightly inward at the top.
Squeeze your chest at the top and breathe out on the way up.

name: Dumbbell Finger Curls
desc: A grip exercise where a dumbbell rolls down to the fingertips and is curled back into the palm. It strengthens the fingers and the forearm muscles that close the hand.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest your forearm on your thigh, palm facing up, holding a dumbbell.
Keep your wrist still and slowly open your fingers so the dumbbell rolls down toward the fingertips.
Stop before it slips, with the handle resting on the last joints of your fingers.
Close your fingers to roll the dumbbell back up into a tight fist.
Squeeze for a moment, then repeat; switch hands after the set.

name: Dumbbell Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A dumbbell fly performed with your upper back on an exercise ball and hips lifted. It stretches and works the chest while the glutes and core hold the bridge.
ins: Sit on the ball with a dumbbell in each hand, then walk your feet out until your head and upper back rest on it.
Lift your hips so your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Press the dumbbells above your chest with palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Breathe in and open your arms out to the sides until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbells back together over your chest without changing the elbow bend.
Keep your hips up throughout; lower them only when the set is over.

name: Dumbbell Forward Lunge Triceps Extension
desc: A forward lunge combined with an overhead dumbbell triceps extension. It trains the triceps while the legs and core work to keep you steady through the lunge.
ins: Stand tall holding one dumbbell with both hands above your head, arms straight.
Step forward into a lunge and lower your back knee toward the floor.
At the bottom, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head, keeping elbows pointing up.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift the dumbbell back overhead.
Push off your front foot to stand up, then lunge with the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
desc: A standing raise that lifts two dumbbells straight in front of you to shoulder height. It is a basic isolation move for the front shoulders.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Brace your stomach and keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and lift both dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Pause for a second at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly without swinging.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise (One Dumbbell, Both Hands)
desc: A front raise holding one dumbbell with both hands. Using both hands keeps the movement steady and works the front shoulders.
ins: Stand tall and hold one dumbbell by its ends with both hands in front of your thighs.
Brace your stomach and keep your arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height.
Hold briefly without leaning back.
Breathe in and lower it slowly to your thighs.

name: Dumbbell Full Can Lateral Raise
desc: A raise done at an angle between the front and the side, with your thumbs pointing up, often called the full can raise. It trains the side shoulders and the rotator cuff in a shoulder-friendly position.
ins: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides, thumbs pointing forward.
Turn your arms so they point slightly forward, about halfway between the front and the side.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells along that angle to shoulder height, thumbs up.
Keep your shoulders down and your elbows almost straight.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Goblet Squat
desc: A squat holding one dumbbell upright against your chest. The front-loaded weight helps you stay upright and sit deep, making it a great squat for learning form while building the quads and glutes.
ins: Hold one dumbbell vertically by the top end with both hands against your chest.
Stand with feet a little wider than shoulder-width and toes slightly out.
Breathe in and sit down between your heels, keeping your elbows pointing down and chest up.
Let your elbows brush the insides of your knees at the bottom.
Breathe out and push through your whole foot to stand tall.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl (Alternating)
desc: A hammer curl done one arm at a time, alternating sides, with the palms facing in. It builds the biceps, brachialis and forearms.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing your body.
Breathe out and curl the right dumbbell up with your thumb pointing up.
Stop near shoulder height and keep the elbow at your side.
Breathe in and lower it slowly.
Curl the left dumbbell the same way and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl On Exercise Ball
desc: A hammer curl done seated on an exercise ball. The neutral grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearms, and the ball keeps your core engaged.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with feet wide, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows tucked.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up with your thumbs pointing up.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly, keeping the ball still.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curls (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A hammer curl with an arm blaster holding your elbows in place. The thumbs-up grip works the biceps together with the brachialis and forearms, and the arm blaster stops any swinging.
ins: Put on the arm blaster with your elbows resting against the plate.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up, keeping your thumbs pointing up.
Pause at the top without letting your elbows leave the plate.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly.

name: Dumbbell High Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done with your upper arms raised out to the sides at shoulder height, like a front double-biceps pose. It trains the biceps at their shortest position, with the shoulders working to hold the arms up.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing up.
Raise your arms out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your shoulders and your arms are straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells toward the sides of your head, keeping your upper arms level.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly back out to the sides; use light weights.

name: Dumbbell Incline Alternate Press
desc: An incline dumbbell press where you press one dumbbell at a time while the other stays held at the top. It works the upper chest, shoulders and triceps and keeps the core engaged throughout.
ins: Set a bench to about 30 degrees and lie back with a dumbbell in each hand pressed up over your upper chest.
Keep your feet flat and your shoulder blades pulled back into the bench.
Breathe in and lower one dumbbell to the side of your chest while the other arm stays straight.
Breathe out and press it back up to meet the other dumbbell.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating sides for the whole set.

name: Dumbbell Incline Biceps Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done seated back on an incline bench so your arms hang behind your body. This puts the biceps on a long stretch at the bottom.
ins: Set a bench to about 45 to 60 degrees and sit back with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down behind your torso with palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up without moving your upper arms forward.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are fully straight and you feel the stretch.

name: Dumbbell Incline Breeding
desc: A beginner-friendly incline dumbbell press done at a slow, steady pace with a short pause at the bottom. It builds the upper chest and teaches control of the dumbbells.
ins: Sit on a bench set to about 45 degrees with your back on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your upper chest.
Take about three seconds to lower them to the sides of your chest, elbows bent to roughly a right angle.
Pause for one second at the bottom without relaxing.
Press back up smoothly, breathing out as you push.

name: Dumbbell Incline Curl
desc: An incline dumbbell curl done one arm at a time. The incline stretches the biceps, and alternating lets you focus fully on each side.
ins: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight and palms forward.
Breathe out and curl the right dumbbell up while the left arm stays down.
Squeeze at the top, then breathe in and lower it slowly to full stretch.
Curl the left dumbbell the same way.
Keep alternating, keeping your head and back against the bench.

name: Dumbbell Incline Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A dumbbell fly done half-reclined on an exercise ball with the hips dropped, creating an incline angle that targets the upper chest.
ins: Sit on the ball holding two dumbbells and walk forward until your mid and upper back rest on it, hips lower than your shoulders.
Hold the dumbbells over your upper chest, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent.
Breathe in and lower the weights out to the sides in a wide arc until your chest is stretched.
Breathe out and squeeze them back up and together over your upper chest.
Keep your feet wide and planted so the ball stays still.

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Curl
desc: A hammer curl done seated on an incline bench, palms facing in. It works the brachialis and forearms from a stretched starting position.
ins: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging and palms facing your body.
Keep your shoulders back against the pad.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up with your thumbs leading.
Stop near shoulder height and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press
desc: An incline dumbbell press with a neutral grip, palms facing each other throughout. It works the upper chest and triceps with less strain on the shoulder joint.
ins: Sit on an incline bench and hold the dumbbells at your upper chest with palms facing each other.
Tuck your elbows in so they point down and slightly forward.
Press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower them slowly back to your upper chest, keeping the palms facing in.
Exhale on the press and inhale as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Incline Hammer Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A neutral-grip dumbbell press done with your upper back on an exercise ball and your hips dropped low, giving an incline angle. It trains the triceps, upper chest and shoulders while your core and legs keep you steady.
ins: Sit on the ball with a dumbbell in each hand, then walk your feet forward until your upper back rests on it.
Let your hips sink a little lower than your shoulders to make an incline, with your feet flat and wide.
Hold the dumbbells over your chest with palms facing each other.
Lower them beside your chest with your elbows tucked close to your body.
Breathe out and press back up, keeping the ball still under you.

name: Dumbbell Incline Inner Biceps Curl
desc: An incline dumbbell curl with the arms turned out so the dumbbells travel up and out to the sides. This angle stresses the inner part of the biceps.
ins: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging and palms facing forward.
Turn your arms slightly out so your hands start a little wider than your shoulders.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up and out toward the outside of your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same path.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Fly
desc: A single-arm dumbbell fly on an incline bench that focuses on the upper chest one side at a time and helps even out strength differences.
ins: Set a bench to about 30 degrees, lie back and hold one dumbbell above your shoulder with your palm facing in.
Hold the side of the bench with your free hand to keep your body square.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell out to the side, elbow softly bent, until you feel a stretch in your upper chest.
Breathe out and bring it back up over your shoulder in a hugging motion.
Complete your reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm incline dumbbell fly performed half-reclined on an exercise ball. It isolates the upper chest on one side while your core works hard against the uneven load.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and roll back on the ball until it supports your mid and upper back, hips slightly dropped.
Set your feet wide and press the dumbbell up over your upper chest, palm facing in.
Breathe in and lower the weight out to the side in an arc, keeping the elbow slightly bent.
Stop at a comfortable stretch and keep your shoulders level on the ball.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbell back over your chest.
Finish the set and repeat with the other arm.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Hammer Press
desc: A one-arm neutral-grip dumbbell press on an incline bench. It works the triceps hard, along with the front shoulder and upper chest, and makes your core resist twisting.
ins: Sit back on an incline bench holding one dumbbell at shoulder level with your palm facing in.
Plant your feet and rest your free hand on your stomach or the bench.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight.
Lower it slowly back to the side of your chest, elbow close to your body.
Keep your torso square to the ceiling, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Hammer Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm neutral-grip press with your upper back on an exercise ball and hips low for an incline. It works the triceps, shoulder and upper chest while your core fights to stop the ball rolling.
ins: Sit on the ball holding one dumbbell, walk your feet out, and settle your upper back on the ball with your hips slightly low.
Spread your feet wide for balance and hold the dumbbell at your shoulder, palm facing in.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up.
Lower it slowly to your shoulder, keeping the elbow tucked.
Keep your hips and shoulders level, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise
desc: A one-arm lateral raise done lying on your side on an incline bench. The angle changes where the movement is hardest, so the side shoulder works more at the bottom of the lift.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie on your side against it, holding a dumbbell in your top hand in front of your thigh.
Brace yourself with your bottom arm and keep your top arm almost straight.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell out and up until your arm is about vertical.
Pause briefly, keeping the movement slow.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell under control, then switch sides after your set.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Press
desc: An incline dumbbell press using one arm at a time, which works the upper chest, front shoulder and triceps and makes your core resist being pulled to one side.
ins: Set a bench to 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with one dumbbell held at the side of your upper chest.
Plant your feet and grip the bench with your free hand.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight above your shoulder.
Keep both shoulder blades pinned to the bench so your body does not roll.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly back to your chest.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A single-arm incline dumbbell press done half-reclined on an exercise ball. It trains the upper chest while your hips and core keep the ball steady against the one-sided load.
ins: Sit on the ball with a dumbbell in one hand and walk your feet out until your mid and upper back rest on it, hips slightly lower than your shoulders.
Bring the dumbbell to the side of your upper chest with the elbow bent.
Breathe out and press it up and slightly back so it ends over your shoulder.
Keep your free hand on your stomach or out to the side for balance.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly to your chest.
Switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Incline Palm-In Press
desc: An incline dumbbell press with palms facing in and the dumbbells pressed together for the whole rep. Squeezing the weights together keeps the inner and upper chest working hard.
ins: Sit on an incline bench holding the dumbbells against your upper chest, palms facing each other and the dumbbells touching.
Squeeze the dumbbells firmly into each other.
Press them straight up while keeping them in contact the whole way.
Lower slowly back to your chest without letting them drift apart.
Breathe out as you press; use a lighter weight than for a regular incline press.

name: Dumbbell Incline Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A two-dumbbell incline press done half-reclined on an exercise ball. It builds the upper chest, front shoulders and triceps and adds a stability challenge for the hips and core.
ins: Sit on the ball holding two dumbbells on your thighs, then walk forward until your mid and upper back are on the ball with your hips dropped a little.
Bring the dumbbells to the sides of your upper chest, palms facing forward.
Breathe out and press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
Keep your feet planted wide and your stomach tight.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells under control back to your chest.

name: Dumbbell Incline Raise
desc: A dumbbell shoulder press done leaning back on a steep incline bench. The angle puts extra work on the front shoulders, with the triceps and traps helping.
ins: Set a bench to a steep incline, sit back against it and bring a dumbbell in each hand to shoulder height, palms forward.
Keep your back and head against the pad and your feet flat.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Pause for a second at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly to shoulder height.

name: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise
desc: A rear shoulder raise done lying chest-down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand. The bench support removes swing so the rear shoulders work cleanly.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest-down on it with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
Turn your palms to face each other and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Incline Shoulder Raise
desc: A short-range movement on an incline bench where you push dumbbells upward using only your shoulder blades while your arms stay locked. It strengthens the serratus muscles that hold the shoulder blades against the ribs.
ins: Lie on a 45-degree incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight above your shoulders.
Keep your elbows locked; only your shoulder blades will move.
Let your shoulder blades pinch back so the dumbbells lower a few centimetres.
Reach the dumbbells toward the ceiling by pushing your shoulder blades apart and forward.
Hold the reach for a second, lower slowly, and breathe out as you push up.

name: Dumbbell Incline Shrug
desc: A dumbbell shrug done lying face down on an incline bench, which changes the angle so the traps pull the shoulders up and slightly back. It targets the traps with the shoulders assisting.
ins: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight and relaxed.
Shrug your shoulders up toward your ears, keeping your elbows straight.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower slowly until your shoulders are fully stretched down.
Breathe out on the shrug and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Incline T-Raise
desc: A raise done lying chest-down on an incline bench, lifting the arms straight out to the sides into a T shape with thumbs up. It strengthens the rear shoulders and the middle back.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest-down on it with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down.
Turn your hands so your thumbs point forward.
Breathe out and raise your arms straight out to the sides until your body forms a T.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold briefly.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Incline Triceps Extension
desc: A triceps extension lying on an incline bench with dumbbells, lowering them beside your head. The incline lets the triceps stretch further than on a flat bench.
ins: Lie on an incline bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand straight above your face, palms facing each other.
Fix your upper arms in place, angled slightly back.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head.
Go down until you feel a deep stretch in the back of your arms.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to bring the dumbbells back up.

name: Dumbbell Incline Twist Curl
desc: An incline dumbbell curl that starts with a thumbs-up grip and turns the palm up as you lift. The twist adds a strong biceps contraction at the top.
ins: Sit back on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging and palms facing your body.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, turning your palms to face up as they rise.
Finish with your little fingers turned slightly higher than your thumbs and squeeze.
Keep your upper arms still against the bench angle.
Breathe in and lower slowly, turning your palms back in at the bottom.

name: Dumbbell Incline Twisted Flyes
desc: An incline dumbbell fly with a twist of the wrists during the lift. It targets the upper chest and adds a stronger contraction at the top.
ins: Lie on an incline bench holding dumbbells above your upper chest with palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in the elbows.
At the bottom, turn your palms to face each other.
Bring the dumbbells back up and together, rotating so your palms face forward again as they meet.
Squeeze your upper chest at the top and exhale on the way up.

name: Dumbbell Incline Two Arm Extension
desc: A two-arm dumbbell triceps extension done lying on an incline bench. The incline angle keeps the triceps under stretch at the bottom of each rep.
ins: Lie back on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your head, palms facing each other.
Point your elbows up and keep your upper arms still.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells slowly behind your head.
Stop when you feel a stretch in the back of your arms.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift the dumbbells back up.

name: Dumbbell Incline Y-Raise
desc: A dumbbell raise lying chest-down on an incline bench, lifting the arms in a Y shape. It strengthens the lower traps, upper back and rear shoulders.
ins: Set a bench to about 30 to 45 degrees and lie on it face down.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging straight and thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms forward and out at an angle so your body and arms form a Y.
Lift until your arms are in line with your body, pulling your shoulder blades down, and breathe out.
Lower slowly with control.

name: Dumbbell Iron Cross
desc: A two-stage raise where you lift the dumbbells to the front, open them out to the sides into a T shape, then reverse. It works the front and side shoulders together.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing down.
Breathe out and raise both dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height.
Keeping them at that height, open your arms out to the sides until your body forms a T.
Bring your arms back to the front at the same height.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells to your thighs.

name: Dumbbell Kickback
desc: A bent-over triceps exercise where you straighten your arms back behind you with dumbbells. It isolates the triceps and is strongest at full extension.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, hinge forward at the hips until your torso is nearly level with the floor, knees slightly bent.
Lift your elbows so your upper arms are beside your torso and parallel to the floor, forearms hanging down.
Breathe out and straighten your arms back until they line up with your torso.
Squeeze the triceps for a second without letting your upper arms drop.
Breathe in and bend your elbows slowly to return.

name: Dumbbell Kickbacks On Exercise Ball
desc: A triceps kickback done lying chest-down on an exercise ball. The ball supports your torso so you can focus on the triceps, while your back and core keep you balanced.
ins: Lie with your stomach and chest on an exercise ball, feet wide on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Raise your upper arms alongside your body with your elbows bent at about a right angle.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back until they are in line with your body.
Squeeze the triceps for a moment at the top.
Bend your elbows slowly to bring the dumbbells back down.

name: Dumbbell Kneeling Bicep Curl Exercise Ball
desc: A preacher-style curl done kneeling behind an exercise ball with the backs of your upper arms resting on top of it. The ball acts as a soft preacher pad, so the biceps work without body swing.
ins: Kneel on a mat behind an exercise ball, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Lean forward and rest the backs of your upper arms on top of the ball, arms angled down in front of it, palms up.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping the ball steady under your arms.

name: Dumbbell Lateral To Front Raise
desc: A combined raise where you lift the dumbbells to the side, sweep them to the front at shoulder height, then lower. It works the side and front shoulders in one continuous movement.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height.
Keep them at that height and sweep them around to the front.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells to your thighs.
On the next rep raise to the front first and sweep out to the side, alternating the direction.

name: Dumbbell Lunge With Bicep Curl
desc: A forward lunge followed by a dumbbell curl at the bottom position. It works the legs and glutes in the lunge and the biceps in the curl.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Step forward and lower into a lunge until both knees are bent at about a right angle.
Hold the lunge, breathe out and curl both dumbbells to your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells slowly.
Push through your front foot to step back to standing, then lunge with the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Lying Alternate Extension
desc: A lying dumbbell triceps extension in which you lower one dumbbell at a time beside your head. Alternating lets you focus on each arm while the other holds still overhead.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand straight above your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Keep your upper arms vertical and still.
Bend one elbow to lower that dumbbell slowly beside your head.
Breathe out and straighten that arm back up.
Switch to the other arm and keep trading sides.

name: Dumbbell Lying Elbow Press
desc: A lying dumbbell press where you lower the weights by bending the elbows and letting them drift toward your feet, then press up. It mixes a press with an extension to load the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, letting them travel down and slightly toward your feet as the dumbbells come toward your shoulders.
Keep your elbows close together rather than flaring to the sides.
Stop when the dumbbells are just above your shoulders.
Breathe out and push the dumbbells back up by straightening your elbows.

name: Dumbbell Lying Extension (across Face)
desc: A one-arm lying triceps extension where the dumbbell is lowered across your face toward the opposite shoulder. The cross-body path isolates the triceps and is easy on the elbow.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in one hand straight above your chest, palm facing your feet.
Support the working upper arm with your free hand if you like.
Breathe in and bend the elbow so the dumbbell travels across your face toward the opposite shoulder.
Stop when the dumbbell is just above that shoulder.
Breathe out and straighten your arm to bring it back up; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
desc: A rotator cuff exercise done lying on your side, rotating a light dumbbell up with your elbow fixed at your side. It strengthens the muscles that turn the shoulder outward and is common in rehab.
ins: Lie on your side and hold a light dumbbell in your top hand.
Bend that elbow to 90 degrees and keep it against your side, with the dumbbell resting near your stomach.
Breathe out and rotate your forearm up toward the ceiling, keeping your elbow in place.
Stop when you reach the end of your comfortable range.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Femoral
desc: A lying leg curl done on a flat bench with a dumbbell held between your feet instead of a machine. It isolates the hamstrings, with some help from the glutes and calves.
ins: Have a partner place a light dumbbell between your feet, or set it there yourself, then lie face down on a flat bench with your knees just off the end.
Squeeze the dumbbell handle firmly between your feet and hold the bench for support.
Bend your knees and curl the dumbbell up toward your glutes, keeping your hips on the bench.
Stop when your shins are about vertical so the dumbbell stays secure.
Lower it slowly until your legs are nearly straight.
Breathe out as you curl and in as you lower; use a light weight you can control.

name: Dumbbell Lying Hammer Press
desc: A flat dumbbell press with palms facing each other in a hammer grip. The tucked elbows make it shoulder-friendly while working the chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding the dumbbells at your chest with palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your torso, pointing toward your feet.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your chest.
Lower them slowly until they lightly touch the sides of your chest.
Breathe out as you press and keep your feet flat on the floor.

name: Dumbbell Lying On Floor Rear Delt Raise
desc: A rear shoulder raise done lying face down on the floor, lifting light dumbbells out to the sides. The floor limits the range and makes it a gentle, controlled exercise for the rear shoulders and upper back.
ins: Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting on a small towel.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with your arms out to the sides in a T, elbows slightly bent.
Breathe out and lift your arms off the floor by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold for one to two seconds at the top.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly to the floor.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Deltoid Rear
desc: A one-arm rear shoulder raise done lying face down on a flat bench, lifting the dumbbell out to the side. Working one arm at a time lets you focus on each rear shoulder.
ins: Lie on your stomach along a flat bench, one dumbbell in your working hand and that arm hanging straight beside the bench.
Rest your other hand on the bench or the floor and keep your chest on the pad.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell out to the side with a slight bend in the elbow until your arm is level with the bench.
Squeeze the back of your shoulder for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Press
desc: A single-arm flat dumbbell press with the palm facing your feet, like one half of a dumbbell bench press. It builds each side of the chest separately and trains core stability.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with one dumbbell held at chest level, palm facing toward your feet.
Brace your stomach and keep both shoulders flat on the bench.
Press the dumbbell up until your arm is straight over your shoulder.
Lower it under control until your elbow is just below the bench line.
Complete the set, then change arms; exhale as you press.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Press (Neutral Grip)
desc: A one-arm dumbbell press on a flat bench done with the palm facing in and the elbow kept close to the body. Working one side at a time challenges the core to stop the torso from twisting.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell beside your chest, palm facing in toward your body.
Place your free hand on your stomach or hold the bench for balance.
Press the dumbbell straight up, keeping your elbow tucked close to your side as it leaves your chest.
Lower slowly back to the side of your chest without letting your torso roll.
Finish your reps, then switch arms; breathe out on each press.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Pronated Triceps Extension
desc: A one-arm lying triceps extension with the palm facing down toward your feet. It isolates the triceps and lets you focus on one side at a time.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold one dumbbell straight above your shoulder with your palm facing your feet.
Keep that upper arm vertical and still.
Breathe in and bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell toward your forehead.
Stop just above your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arm; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise
desc: A rear shoulder raise done lying on your side on a flat bench, lifting the top dumbbell from in front of your chest up toward the ceiling. It isolates the rear shoulder of one arm at a time.
ins: Lie on your side on a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in your top hand, arm hanging in front of your chest.
Bend your knees slightly for balance and keep a small bend in your elbow.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell up and back until your arm points to the ceiling.
Keep your body from rolling backward.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Supinated Triceps Extension
desc: A one-arm lying triceps extension with the palm turned to face you. The turned grip changes how the triceps are loaded and can feel easier on the elbow.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold one dumbbell straight above your shoulder with your palm facing your face.
Keep your upper arm pointing straight up.
Breathe in and bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell beside your head on the same side.
Pause when your forearm is about level with the bench.
Breathe out and straighten the arm; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
desc: A forearm rotation drill where you turn a dumbbell from palm-up to palm-down while lying on a bench. It strengthens the muscles that rotate the forearm inward.
ins: Lie face down on a flat bench and rest one forearm on the bench with your hand just past the end.
Hold a light dumbbell by one end so the heavier side sticks out past your thumb.
Start with your palm facing up.
Breathe out and slowly turn your hand until the palm faces down.
Breathe in and rotate back to palm up under control.
Keep your elbow and forearm still; only the forearm twists. Switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation On Floor
desc: A forearm rotation drill lying on the floor with a dumbbell, turning the palm down. It strengthens the muscles that rotate the forearm and supports elbow and wrist health.
ins: Lie on your back and rest your upper arm on the floor with the elbow bent at 90 degrees, forearm pointing up.
Hold a light dumbbell at one end, or by its handle, with your thumb toward your head.
Slowly rotate your forearm so your palm turns to face down toward your feet.
Keep your elbow and upper arm still on the floor.
Rotate back to the start under control and switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Pullover On Exercise Ball
desc: A dumbbell pullover done lying across an exercise ball, where the weight travels from over your chest to behind your head and back. It stretches and works the chest and lats, with the triceps and shoulders helping.
ins: Lie with your upper back across the ball, hips lifted and feet flat, holding one dumbbell with both hands over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and lock that angle in place.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your arms are roughly in line with your body.
Keep your hips up and your ribs down so your lower back does not arch.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back over your chest using your chest and back.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
desc: A dumbbell row done lying face down on a bench with the elbows flared wide. It targets the rear shoulders and upper back.
ins: Lie face down on a flat bench set high enough that your arms can hang straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing your feet.
Lift the dumbbells by driving your elbows out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
desc: A rear shoulder raise done lying chest-down on a flat bench, holding two dumbbells. Your chest stays supported, so the rear shoulders and upper back do the lifting without help from your lower back.
ins: Lie on your stomach along a flat bench, holding two dumbbells with your arms hanging straight down.
Keep your palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and lift both dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are level with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Lying Single Extension
desc: A one-arm lying dumbbell triceps extension. Training each side alone makes it easy to control the weight and feel the triceps working.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell straight above your shoulder, palm facing in.
Support the working upper arm with your other hand if you like, and keep it vertical.
Breathe in and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell toward the opposite shoulder or beside your head.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back up.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
desc: A forearm rotation drill where you turn a dumbbell from palm-down to palm-up while lying on a bench. It trains the muscles that rotate the forearm outward, which also assist the biceps.
ins: Lie face down on a flat bench with one forearm resting on the bench and your hand just past the end.
Hold a light dumbbell by one end with the weighted side sticking out past your thumb.
Start with your palm facing down.
Breathe out and slowly turn your hand until the palm faces up.
Breathe in and rotate back to palm down with control.
Do not let your elbow lift; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supination On Floor
desc: A forearm rotation drill lying on the floor with a dumbbell, turning the palm up. It trains the muscles that rotate the forearm outward, including the biceps.
ins: Lie on your back with your upper arm on the floor, elbow bent at 90 degrees and forearm pointing up.
Hold a light dumbbell with your palm facing your feet.
Slowly rotate your forearm so the palm turns to face your head.
Keep the elbow pinned to the floor and move only the forearm.
Return slowly to the start and switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supine Biceps Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done lying on your back on a flat bench, with your arms hanging down beside it. Starting with the arms behind the body gives the biceps a deep stretch.
ins: Lie on your back on a flat bench, feet flat on the floor, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor beside the bench, palms facing up.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly back to the stretched position.

name: Dumbbell Lying Supine Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done lying on your back on a flat bench with your arms hanging below the bench. The start position puts the biceps on a full stretch.
ins: Lie on your back on a high flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down toward the floor beside the bench, palms facing up.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms still.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly back to the stretched position.

name: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension
desc: A lying triceps extension with a dumbbell in each hand, lowered beside your head. It is a simple way to isolate the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your ears.
Stop when your forearms are about level with the bench.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift the dumbbells back up.

name: Dumbbell Lying Wide Curl
desc: A lying dumbbell curl with your arms angled out wide from your body. The wide, low arm position stretches the biceps and emphasizes the inner part of the muscle.
ins: Lie on your back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms drop out to the sides at about a 45-degree angle from your body, slightly below the bench, palms up.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping your upper arms in that wide position.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight again.

name: Dumbbell Neutral Grip Bench Press
desc: A flat dumbbell bench press with palms facing each other. The neutral grip keeps the elbows tucked, which brings the triceps in strongly and is kind to the shoulders.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells beside your chest, elbows close to your body.
Breathe out and press them back up until your arms are straight.
Keep the dumbbells moving together and under control.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Bench Fly
desc: A single-arm dumbbell fly on a flat bench that isolates the chest of one side and lets you control the stretch closely.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell over your chest in one hand, palm facing in.
Hold the bench with your other hand and keep your feet flat on the floor.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell out to the side, elbow slightly bent, until your arm is about level with the bench.
Breathe out and sweep the dumbbell back up over your chest.
Keep your hips and shoulders flat on the bench so you do not twist.
Switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Chest Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm chest fly done in a bridge on an exercise ball. Working one side at a time on an unstable surface makes this a demanding chest and core exercise.
ins: Lie with your head and upper back on the ball, hips lifted level with your knees, and hold one dumbbell over your chest.
Place your feet wider than hip-width for a solid base.
Breathe in and open the arm out to the side in a slow arc, elbow softly bent.
Resist the pull of the weight; keep your hips level and do not roll off the ball.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbell back over your chest.
Complete the set, then change arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Concentration Curl (on Stability Ball)
desc: A one-arm concentration curl done sitting on a stability ball. The unstable seat makes your core work while the biceps do the lifting.
ins: Sit on a stability ball with feet wide and flat on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand, lean forward and rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top while keeping your balance on the ball.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Decline Chest Press
desc: A decline dumbbell press done with one arm, focusing on the lower chest and triceps while your core keeps you square on the bench.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your feet hooked in and hold a dumbbell beside your lower chest.
Grip the bench with your free hand.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up over your lower chest until your arm is extended.
Breathe in and lower it slowly, elbow at about 45 degrees from your side.
Keep both shoulders on the bench through every rep.
Switch arms when the set is done.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A single-arm dumbbell fly done with your upper back resting on an exercise ball and your hips held high, training the chest while challenging balance.
ins: Roll down on the ball until your head and shoulders are supported, hips up and feet flat, holding a dumbbell over your chest.
Put your free hand on your hip or stretch it out to the side for balance.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell out to the side, keeping the elbow slightly bent.
Stop when you feel a good stretch across your chest.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbell back up in a wide arc.
Change arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm French Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm overhead dumbbell triceps extension while seated on an exercise ball. It stretches and strengthens the triceps, and the ball makes your core work to keep you upright.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with your feet flat and wide, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Press the dumbbell overhead so your arm is straight and close to your head.
Breathe in and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten the arm, keeping the elbow pointing up.
Keep your back straight and stomach tight, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Hammer Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm hammer curl on a preacher bench. The pad fixes your upper arm while the thumbs-up grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearm.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and rest one upper arm on the pad, holding a dumbbell with your palm facing in.
Start with the arm nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping your thumb pointing up.
Squeeze at the top without lifting the elbow.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Hammer Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm neutral-grip press done in a bridge with your upper back on an exercise ball. It trains the triceps and chest while your glutes and core hold your hips up and stop you rolling.
ins: Rest your upper back on the ball with your feet flat, knees bent and hips lifted level with your knees.
Hold one dumbbell above your chest with your palm facing in.
Lower it to the side of your chest, elbow close to your ribs.
Breathe out and press back up until your arm is straight.
Squeeze your glutes the whole time so your hips stay up, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Incline Chest Press
desc: A one-arm incline dumbbell chest press that works the upper chest on each side separately, with a little rotation of the palm for a natural pressing path.
ins: Lie on a bench set to about 30 degrees with a dumbbell at the side of your upper chest, palm facing your feet.
Hold the bench with your free hand and keep your back flat against the pad.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell up, letting your palm turn slightly inward near the top.
Pause with the arm straight over your shoulder.
Breathe in and lower it back to your chest slowly.
Repeat on the other side.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Kickback
desc: A one-arm triceps kickback with a dumbbell, supporting yourself on a bench. Straightening the arm behind you isolates the triceps.
ins: Place your left knee and left hand on a flat bench and hold a dumbbell in your right hand.
Keep your back flat and lift your right upper arm so it is level with your torso, forearm hanging down.
Breathe out and straighten your right arm back until it is fully extended.
Hold and squeeze for a second.
Breathe in and lower the forearm slowly; switch sides after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise
desc: A standing lateral raise done one arm at a time. It lets you focus on each side shoulder and fix strength differences between sides.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand at your side and your other hand on your hip.
Brace your stomach and keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.
Keep your body upright without leaning.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Lateral Raise With Support
desc: A one-arm lateral raise while holding a post or rack with your free hand and leaning slightly away. The support and lean let the side shoulder work through a longer range.
ins: Stand side-on to a sturdy post and hold it with your near hand at about waist height.
Take a dumbbell in your other hand and lean your body slightly away from the post.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell out to the side until your arm is level with the floor.
Keep your arm almost straight and your stomach tight.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm dumbbell chest press done in a bridge on an exercise ball. It trains the chest and triceps and makes the core work to stop the body from rotating.
ins: Lie with your upper back on the ball, hips lifted and feet planted, holding a dumbbell beside your chest.
Tighten your stomach and glutes to keep your hips level.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is extended.
Breathe in and lower it slowly to the side of your chest.
Do not let the shoulder on the working side lift off the ball.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Prone Curl
desc: A one-arm curl done lying face down on a flat bench with the working arm hanging toward the floor. Lying prone removes any body swing so the biceps do all the work.
ins: Lie face down on a high flat bench, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Let that arm hang straight down off the side of the bench, palm facing forward.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, keeping your upper arm pointing down.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Prone Hammer Curl
desc: A one-arm hammer curl done lying face down on a flat bench. The prone position stops any cheating, and the thumbs-up grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearm.
ins: Lie face down on a high flat bench with a dumbbell in one hand.
Let the arm hang straight down beside the bench with your palm facing in.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, thumb pointing forward and up.
Squeeze at the top while your upper arm stays pointing down.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Pullover On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm dumbbell pullover done lying across an exercise ball. It stretches and strengthens the chest and lats on one side while the core resists twisting.
ins: Lie with your upper back across the ball, hips up, and hold a dumbbell over your chest in one hand with a slight elbow bend.
Rest your free hand on your stomach.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell back past your head in an arc until you feel a stretch along your side and chest.
Keep your ribs down and your hips level.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back over your chest.
Switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Fly (with Support)
desc: A one-arm rear shoulder fly with one hand and knee on a bench for support. Bracing on the bench keeps your back steady so the rear shoulder works on its own.
ins: Put one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, with your back flat and level.
Hold a dumbbell in your free hand, arm hanging under your shoulder, palm facing in.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell out to the side with a slight bend in the elbow.
Stop at shoulder height and squeeze for a second without twisting your body.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch sides after your set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Grip Press
desc: A one-arm dumbbell press done lying on a flat bench with an underhand grip, palm facing your head. The turned grip keeps the elbow tucked and shifts more work to the upper chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing toward your head.
Start with the dumbbell beside your chest and your elbow close to your side.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is extended over your shoulder.
Keep your wrist firm and your elbow tucked as you press.
Breathe in and lower it slowly back beside your chest.
Switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm preacher curl with a dumbbell held palm-down. The pad locks your upper arm in place while the overhand grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearm extensors.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and rest the back of one upper arm on the pad, holding a dumbbell with your palm facing down.
Start with your arm almost straight but not locked.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping your wrist in line with your forearm.
Stop when your forearm is close to vertical and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Spider Curl
desc: A one-arm curl with a palms-down grip done chest-down on an incline bench, arm hanging vertically. It works the brachialis and forearm extensors along with the biceps, with no body swing possible.
ins: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest near the top and a dumbbell in one hand.
Let the arm hang straight down with your palm facing back.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping your palm facing down and your wrist straight.
Squeeze at the top while your upper arm stays vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A single-arm reverse wrist curl with a dumbbell, done seated with your forearm on your thigh. Working one side at a time helps fix strength gaps in the wrist extensors.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest one forearm along your thigh, wrist just past your knee.
Hold a dumbbell with your palm facing down.
Let your hand drop so the wrist bends toward the floor.
Breathe out and lift the back of your hand as high as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Finish all reps, then switch to the other arm.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Seated Bicep Curl On Exercise Ball
desc: A one-arm dumbbell curl seated on an exercise ball. Training one side while balancing on the ball makes your core resist leaning toward the weight.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with feet wide, holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm forward.
Rest your free hand on your thigh and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Squeeze briefly, then lower slowly without leaning to the side.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Seated Hammer Curl
desc: A seated one-arm hammer curl. Sitting keeps your body still, and the thumbs-up grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearm of one arm at a time.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing in.
Keep your back straight and your elbow tucked against your side.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up with your thumb pointing up.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
desc: A seated one-arm wrist movement holding a dumbbell with the thumb on top, tipping the weight up and down. It trains the thumb side of the forearm and the wrist stabilizers.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest one forearm along your thigh with the hand past the knee.
Hold a dumbbell in that hand with your thumb pointing up, like holding a hammer.
Let the front end of the dumbbell tip down toward the floor.
Raise the front end up toward the ceiling by bending the wrist toward the thumb side.
Lower slowly, keep the forearm still on your thigh, then switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Snatch
desc: A powerful one-arm lift where you pull a dumbbell from the floor to overhead in a single fast motion. It is driven by the glutes and legs, with the hamstrings, quads, shoulders and core all working.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a dumbbell on the floor between your feet.
Squat down with a flat back and grip the dumbbell with one hand, the other arm out for balance.
Drive through your legs and extend your hips explosively, keeping the dumbbell close to your body.
As it rises past your chest, pull your elbow high and flip the dumbbell up to lock it out overhead.
Stand tall with the arm straight, then lower it to your shoulder, then your hip, then the floor.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Standing Curl
desc: A standing one-arm dumbbell curl. Working one biceps at a time lets you focus on each side and keep strict form.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing forward.
Keep your elbow close to your side and your shoulders still.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up to your shoulder.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Standing Hammer Curl
desc: A standing one-arm hammer curl. The neutral grip trains the biceps together with the brachialis and forearm, one side at a time.
ins: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm facing your thigh.
Keep your elbow tucked and your torso still.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping your thumb pointing up.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (on Bench)
desc: A one-arm overhead triceps extension done seated on a bench. Working overhead stretches the triceps' long head and builds strength one side at a time.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in one hand straight overhead.
Keep that elbow close to your head and pointing forward.
Breathe in and bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arm back overhead.
Keep your torso still; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Upright Row
desc: An upright row with one dumbbell, pulling it up the front of your body with the elbow leading. It works the side shoulder and traps one side at a time.
ins: Stand tall and hold a dumbbell in one hand in front of your thigh, palm facing you.
Put your free hand on your hip and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and lift your elbow up and out, pulling the dumbbell up close to your body.
Stop when your elbow reaches shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Wrist Curl
desc: A single-arm wrist curl with a dumbbell, palm facing up and forearm resting on your thigh. It isolates the forearm flexors one side at a time.
ins: Sit on a bench and lay one forearm on your thigh with your wrist hanging past the knee.
Hold a dumbbell with your palm facing up.
Let the dumbbell lower so your wrist bends back.
Breathe out and curl your palm up toward your forearm.
Squeeze briefly, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Complete the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Arm Zottman Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm Zottman curl on a preacher bench: curl up palm-up, turn the palm down at the top, and lower palm-down. It trains the biceps on the way up and the forearms and brachialis on the slow way down.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench with one upper arm on the pad, holding a dumbbell with your palm facing up.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
At the top, turn your wrist so your palm faces down.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell slowly with your palm still facing down.
At the bottom, turn your palm back up, finish the set and switch arms.

name: Dumbbell One Leg Fly On Exercise Ball
desc: A dumbbell fly done in a bridge on an exercise ball with one foot lifted off the floor. Balancing on a single leg makes the glutes and core work hard while the chest does the fly.
ins: Lie with your head and upper back on the ball, hips lifted, and hold two dumbbells over your chest, palms facing in.
Straighten one leg in front of you so you are balancing on the other foot.
Breathe in and open your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in the elbows.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
Keep your hips level and the ball still; use a lighter weight than usual.
Halfway through the set or on the next set, switch the supporting leg.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Neutral Wrist Curl
desc: A wrist curl done kneeling beside a bench with your forearms resting on it and a thumbs-up grip. Tipping the dumbbells up with the wrist works the forearms and the muscles at the front of the elbow.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay your forearms across it with your hands just past the edge.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your thumbs pointing up.
Let the front ends of the dumbbells dip down toward the floor.
Breathe out and lift the front ends up as high as you can by moving only your wrists.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping your forearms flat on the bench.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench One Arm Neutral Wrist Curl
desc: A one-arm version of the neutral-grip wrist curl over a bench. Working one side at a time lets you focus on the forearm and the front of the elbow.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and rest one forearm on it, hand just past the edge.
Hold a dumbbell with your thumb pointing up and steady the forearm with your other hand.
Let the front of the dumbbell tip down toward the floor.
Breathe out and raise it as far as your wrist allows without lifting your forearm.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench One Arm Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A one-arm reverse wrist curl with a dumbbell, forearm resting on a bench and palm down. It targets the top of the forearm, which is often weaker than the underside.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay one forearm on it, hand hanging past the edge, palm facing down.
Hold a light dumbbell and let the back of your hand drop toward the floor.
Lift the back of your hand up as high as you can, moving only at the wrist.
Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly.
Keep your forearm flat on the bench the whole time and switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench One Arm Wrist Curl
desc: A one-arm dumbbell wrist curl with your forearm supported flat on a bench, palm up. The bench keeps the arm fixed so the forearm flexors do all the work.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay one forearm on it, palm up, with your hand past the edge.
Hold a dumbbell and let it lower so your wrist bends toward the floor.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up by bending only the wrist.
Hold the top for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly to a full stretch.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A two-handed reverse wrist curl with dumbbells, forearms resting on a bench and palms facing down. It trains the wrist extensors on the top of the forearm.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and rest both forearms on it with your hands past the edge.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand with palms facing down.
Let the dumbbells hang so your wrists bend down.
Breathe out and raise the backs of your hands as high as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Keep your forearms flat on the bench throughout.

name: Dumbbell Over Bench Wrist Curl
desc: A two-handed dumbbell wrist curl with your forearms supported on a bench and palms facing up. It builds the inner forearm and grip strength.
ins: Kneel beside a flat bench and lay both forearms across it, hands past the edge.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up.
Lower the dumbbells so your wrists bend back toward the floor.
Breathe out and curl both wrists up as far as you can.
Squeeze at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Move only at the wrists; keep the elbows down.

name: Dumbbell Palm Rotational Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over dumbbell row where the hands turn from palm-down to palm-up during the pull. It trains the upper back and adds work for the biceps and forearms.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips until your back is nearly level with the floor, knees soft.
Let the dumbbells hang with palms facing behind you.
Row the dumbbells toward your hips and rotate your palms to face forward as they rise.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top and breathe out.
Lower slowly, turning your palms back as your arms straighten.
Keep your back flat for the whole set.

name: Dumbbell Palms In Incline Bench Press
desc: An incline dumbbell press with your palms facing each other and elbows tucked. The narrow, neutral path puts more of the load on the triceps than a regular incline press, with the upper chest and shoulders still helping.
ins: Sit on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level, palms facing each other.
Plant your feet and pull your shoulder blades back against the bench.
Breathe out and press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly to the sides of your chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Stop when your elbows are just below the bench line, then press again.

name: Dumbbell Plyo Squat
desc: A jump squat done holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. The added load builds explosive power in the glutes, quads and calves.
ins: Hold a light dumbbell at each side and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders pulled down so the dumbbells stay still.
Squat down to about half depth, chest up.
Explode upward, pushing through your feet so they leave the floor.
Land quietly on the balls of your feet and bend your knees to absorb the landing.
Pause to reset, breathing out as you jump, then go again.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl Over Exercise Ball
desc: A spider-style curl done with your chest draped over an exercise ball and your arms hanging down in front of it. The arms stay vertical, which keeps tension on the biceps at the top.
ins: Kneel behind an exercise ball and lean forward until your chest and stomach rest on top of it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and let your arms hang straight down in front of the ball, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up, keeping your upper arms pointing at the floor.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping the ball steady with your knees.

name: Dumbbell Preacher Hammer Curl
desc: A hammer curl on a preacher bench with the palm facing in. The pad keeps the upper arm still so the brachialis and forearm work hard with the biceps.
ins: Sit or stand at a preacher bench and rest the back of one upper arm on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell with your thumb pointing up and the arm almost straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping the thumb on top.
Stop when your forearm is near vertical and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A two-dumbbell chest press performed in a bridge on an exercise ball. It builds the chest, shoulders and triceps while the glutes and core hold the position.
ins: Sit on the ball with dumbbells on your thighs and walk out until your head and upper back rest on it.
Lift your hips level with your knees and bring the dumbbells to the sides of your chest.
Breathe out and press both dumbbells up until your arms are straight over your chest.
Breathe in and lower them slowly until your elbows are just below your torso.
Keep your hips from dropping as you get tired.

name: Dumbbell Pronate-Grip Triceps Extension
desc: A seated overhead triceps extension holding one dumbbell with both hands, palms facing down on the handle. It stretches and strengthens the triceps.
ins: Sit upright on a bench and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands gripping the handle, palms facing down.
Keep your elbows close to your head and pointing forward.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Stop when you feel a good stretch in the back of your arms.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to raise it back overhead.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done lying chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging straight. It removes momentum and makes the biceps work hard at the top.
ins: Lie chest-down on a bench set to about 45 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down with palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up while your upper arms stay vertical.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Hammer Curl
desc: A hammer curl done lying chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging straight down. It isolates the biceps, brachialis and forearms with no chance to swing.
ins: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest near the top and a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down with your palms facing each other.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, thumbs pointing up.
Squeeze at the top while your upper arms stay vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
desc: A classic lying exercise where you lower one dumbbell behind your head and pull it back over your chest. It stretches and works the chest and lats together, with the triceps helping to hold the arm position.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold one dumbbell with both hands cupped under the top plate, arms above your chest.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep them at that angle.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until your upper arms are about in line with your body.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest along the same arc.
Breathe in deeply as you lower and out as you pull up; keep your ribs and hips down.

name: Dumbbell Pullover Hip Extension On Exercise Ball
desc: A combination move on an exercise ball: a dumbbell pullover followed by lifting the hips into a bridge. It works the chest and lats, and the hip lift brings in the glutes and core.
ins: Lie with your upper back on the ball, hips lowered toward the floor, holding one dumbbell with both hands over your chest.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbell behind your head in an arc, elbows slightly bent.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbell back over your chest.
With the weight held over your chest, squeeze your glutes and drive your hips up until your body is flat from knees to shoulders.
Lower your hips back down with control to finish the rep.

name: Dumbbell Pullover On Exercise Ball
desc: A classic dumbbell pullover done across an exercise ball. The weight moves in an arc over and behind the head, stretching and working the chest and lats.
ins: Place your shoulders across the ball, hips up and feet flat, and hold one dumbbell under the top plate with both palms.
Start with the dumbbell above your chest and your elbows slightly bent.
Breathe in deeply as you lower the weight behind your head until you feel a stretch in your chest and lats.
Breathe out and bring it back over your chest along the same arc.
Keep your elbows at the same angle throughout; the movement comes from the shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Push Press
desc: An overhead press with dumbbells that uses a quick knee dip and leg drive to start the lift. It lets you handle more weight and builds powerful shoulders and triceps.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and dip a few centimeters by bending your knees, chest up.
Drive up through your legs and press the dumbbells overhead in one smooth movement.
Finish with your arms and legs straight.
Lower the dumbbells to your shoulders under control and reset.

name: Dumbbell Raise
desc: A simple standing dumbbell raise out to the sides with the palms facing down. It works the side shoulders, with the traps and upper back helping to steady the shoulder blades.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides, turning your palms down as you go.
Stop at shoulder height and pause briefly.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly.

name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Row (shoulder)
desc: A bent-over dumbbell row with your elbows pointing out to the sides and the dumbbells pulled toward your chest. This shifts the work to the rear shoulders and upper back.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips until your upper body is almost level with the floor, knees slightly bent.
Let the dumbbells hang under your shoulders with your palms facing behind you.
Breathe out and pull the dumbbells up toward your chest, keeping your elbows wide.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders when your upper arms are level with your back.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping your back flat.

name: Dumbbell Rear Fly
desc: A standing bent-over fly where you open the dumbbells out to the sides with your palms facing each other. It is a classic rear shoulder isolation exercise.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, and hinge forward until your upper body is almost level with the floor.
Let your arms hang with palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders.
Keep your neck in line with your back and don't jerk the weights.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise
desc: A rear shoulder raise done seated on the end of a bench with your chest leaning over your thighs. Sitting stops you from using your legs and hips to swing the weight.
ins: Sit on the end of a flat bench and lean forward until your chest is close to your thighs.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand behind your calves, palms facing each other.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells out to the sides with slightly bent elbows.
Stop when your arms are level with your shoulders and pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise (support Head)
desc: A bent-over rear shoulder raise with your forehead resting on a high bench or pad. Supporting your head keeps your upper body still so the rear shoulders work without swinging.
ins: Set a bench to a high incline, stand behind it, and hinge forward until your forehead rests on the top of the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging down and a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height.
Keep your forehead on the pad and squeeze your shoulder blades briefly.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Rear Lunge
desc: A reverse lunge holding dumbbells, stepping back instead of forward. It works the glutes and quads of the front leg and is gentler on the knees than a forward lunge.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell at each side.
Step one foot back far enough that both knees can bend to about 90 degrees.
Lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your weight in the front heel and your torso upright.
Drive through the front foot and bring the back foot forward to stand.
Alternate legs, breathing out as you come up.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Bench Press
desc: A dumbbell bench press done with an underhand grip, palms facing your head. It keeps the elbows close and puts extra emphasis on the upper chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand and turn your palms to face your head.
Press the dumbbells up over your chest with your arms straight.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Pause briefly when the dumbbells reach chest level.
Breathe out and press them back up, keeping your wrists straight.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Biceps Curl
desc: A standing dumbbell curl with palms facing down. The overhand grip builds the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps.
