ins: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms by your sides and palms facing behind you.
Keep your elbows tucked and wrists straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up with the backs of your hands leading.
Stop near shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench One Arm Row
desc: A one-arm dumbbell row with an underhand grip while lying chest-down on an incline bench. It works the upper back on one side at a time with extra help from the biceps.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie on it face down.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand with your palm facing forward and let the arm hang straight.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back and breathe out at the top.
Lower slowly to a straight arm.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Incline Bench Two Arm Row
desc: A chest-supported row on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing forward. It builds the upper back while the biceps and forearms assist.
ins: Lie face down on a low-incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight.
Turn your palms to face forward.
Pull both dumbbells toward your hips, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Lower the dumbbells slowly without lifting your chest off the pad.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Grip Row
desc: A bent-over dumbbell row with the palms facing forward. It works the upper back and brings the biceps in more than a neutral grip.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees until your back is close to level, keeping it flat.
Pull the dumbbells toward your hips, elbows close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Lower the dumbbells slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Preacher Curl
desc: A one-arm preacher curl with a dumbbell held palm down. It strengthens the forearm and brachialis while the pad keeps the arm fixed.
ins: Rest the back of one upper arm on a preacher pad.
Hold a dumbbell with your palm facing down and the arm almost straight.
Breathe out and curl it up while keeping your wrist in line with your forearm.
Stop when your forearm is near vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Spider Curl
desc: A spider curl with both dumbbells held palms-down, lying chest-down on an incline bench. It trains the brachialis and forearm extensors together with the biceps.
ins: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down with your palms facing back.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up, keeping your palms down and wrists straight.
Pause at the top with your upper arms still vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
desc: A seated reverse wrist curl with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing down. It strengthens the top of the forearm, which often lags behind the inner side.
ins: Sit on a bench with your feet flat and rest your forearms on your thighs.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, palms down, wrists just past your knees.
Let the dumbbells drop so your wrists bend toward the floor.
Breathe out and lift the backs of your hands upward.
Hold briefly, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Choose a light weight so you can control every rep.

name: Dumbbell Rotation Reverse Fly
desc: A bent-over reverse fly where you turn your hands as you lift, from palms facing each other to thumbs pointing forward. The rotation adds work for the rear shoulders and the rotator cuff.
ins: Hinge forward with a flat back and knees slightly bent, holding the dumbbells under your chest with palms facing each other.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides.
As you lift, rotate your hands so your thumbs point forward at the top.
Pause at shoulder height and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Breathe in and lower slowly, turning your hands back to the start.

name: Dumbbell Scott Press
desc: A seated dumbbell press that starts with the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward and elbows flared wide, then presses up and in. It works the side and front shoulders hard at the bottom of the press.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with back support and hold the dumbbells beside your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Point your elbows straight out to the sides so your upper arms are in line with your shoulders.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up and slightly in until your arms are straight.
Breathe in and lower them slowly back to the wide starting position.
Keep your back against the pad throughout.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Front Raise
desc: A seated front raise that lifts one dumbbell at a time. Sitting cuts out body swing, so the front shoulders work strictly.
ins: Sit tall on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and keep your feet flat.
Breathe out and raise one dumbbell in front of you to shoulder height, turning the palm down.
Lower it slowly as you breathe in.
Raise the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Hammer Curl On Exercise Ball
desc: An alternating hammer curl done seated on an exercise ball. The neutral grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearms while the ball keeps your core active.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with feet wide, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms in.
Brace your stomach.
Breathe out and curl one dumbbell up with your thumb pointing up.
Lower it slowly, then curl the other one.
Keep alternating while keeping the ball still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Press
desc: A seated dumbbell press done one arm at a time, while the other dumbbell waits at shoulder height. It builds the shoulders and triceps and helps balance strength between sides.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward.
Keep your back against the pad and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press one dumbbell up until your arm is straight.
Breathe in and lower it back to your shoulder.
Press with the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Seated Alternate Shoulder
desc: A seated alternating dumbbell press where one arm stays locked out overhead while the other lowers and presses. Holding the top position keeps both shoulders working the whole set.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.
Keep one dumbbell overhead and breathe in as you lower the other to shoulder height.
Breathe out and press it back up.
Hold that arm overhead and lower the other one.
Keep alternating with your back against the pad and your stomach braced.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bench Extension
desc: A seated triceps extension holding one dumbbell overhead with both hands. It is a simple way to load the triceps through a long range.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with feet flat and back straight.
Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the top end.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing up and close to your ears.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press it back overhead.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Arm Lateral Raise
desc: A seated lateral raise with your elbows bent at 90 degrees. Bending the arms shortens the lever, which makes it easier to feel the side shoulders and to control the weight.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your elbows bent to 90 degrees at your sides.
Brace your stomach and keep your forearms pointing forward.
Breathe out and lift your elbows out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your shoulders.
Keep your elbows and wrists at the same height at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Alternate Kickback
desc: A triceps kickback done seated on the end of a bench, leaning your chest toward your knees and straightening one arm at a time. Sitting removes leg drive and the lean keeps the upper back working to hold position.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and lean your chest forward over your thighs with a flat back.
Lift your upper arms so they run alongside your body, elbows bent at about a right angle.
Breathe out and straighten one arm back until it is in line with your body.
Squeeze the triceps, then bend the elbow slowly to return.
Do the same with the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bent Over Triceps Extension
desc: A two-arm dumbbell triceps kickback done seated on the end of a bench with your chest leaning over your thighs. Both arms work together, and the seated lean keeps the rest of your body still.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and lean forward from the hips with a flat back.
Raise your upper arms beside your body and bend your elbows to about a right angle.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back at the same time.
Hold the squeeze for a moment with your arms in line with your body.
Bend your elbows slowly to lower the dumbbells.

name: Dumbbell Seated Bicep Curl
desc: A two-arm dumbbell curl done seated with your palms facing up. Sitting removes leg drive and body swing, keeping the work on the biceps.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat and a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Turn your palms to face forward and keep your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Seated Biceps Curl (on Stability Ball)
desc: A seated dumbbell curl on a stability ball. The ball makes you keep a tall, braced posture while the biceps lift.
ins: Sit on a stability ball with feet flat and hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand.
Sit tall, brace your stomach and let your arms hang with palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps while staying balanced.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Seated Biceps Curl To Shoulder Press
desc: A seated combination of a dumbbell biceps curl followed by an overhead shoulder press. It trains the biceps and the shoulders in one flowing movement.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up to your shoulders.
Turn your palms to face forward at shoulder height and push both dumbbells up until your elbows straighten overhead.
Lower the dumbbells back to your shoulders with control.
Breathe in and lower them slowly to your sides to finish the rep.

name: Dumbbell Seated Calf Raise
desc: A seated calf raise with a dumbbell on each knee. It is a simple way to train the deep calf muscle when you do not have a calf machine.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with the balls of both feet on a low block, heels off.
Rest a dumbbell on each thigh just above the knees and hold them in place.
Lower your heels to stretch the calves.
Breathe out and lift your heels as high as you can.
Squeeze for a second at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Cuban Press
desc: A seated version of the Cuban press: an outward shoulder rotation from a raised-elbow position followed by an overhead press. Sitting keeps the body still so the rotator cuff and shoulders work cleanly.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with a light dumbbell in each hand.
Raise your upper arms out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows bent to 90 degrees and forearms pointing down.
Rotate your forearms up until the dumbbells are above your elbows.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells overhead, then lower them back to the 90-degree position.
Rotate your forearms back down and repeat.

name: Dumbbell Seated Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl done sitting on a bench. Sitting makes it harder to swing, so the biceps do more of the work.
ins: Sit on the end of a flat bench with feet planted and a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang beside the bench with palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Keep your torso still and squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Seated Front Raise
desc: A seated front raise lifting both dumbbells together. It isolates the front shoulders without help from leg drive.
ins: Sit tall on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Brace your stomach and keep your back straight.
Breathe out and raise both dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, palms facing down.
Pause briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Hammer Curl
desc: A two-arm hammer curl done seated. The neutral grip works the biceps, brachialis and forearms, and sitting keeps the movement strict.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Sit tall with your elbows tucked.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, thumbs pointing up.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Inner Biceps Curl
desc: A seated dumbbell curl where the dumbbells travel up and out toward the sides. Curling out to the sides stresses the inner part of the biceps.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging and palms facing forward.
Turn your arms slightly outward so your hands start a little wide.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up and out toward the outside of your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top with your elbows still at your sides.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same path.

name: Dumbbell Seated Kickback
desc: A triceps kickback with both arms done while seated and leaning forward. Sitting takes stress off the lower back while the triceps work.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and lean your chest forward over your thighs.
Raise your elbows so your upper arms are tight to your sides and close to level, forearms hanging down.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back until they are fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps at the top.
Breathe in and bend your elbows slowly to return.

name: Dumbbell Seated Lateral Raise
desc: A lateral raise done sitting on the end of a flat bench. Sitting removes leg drive, so the side shoulders do the lifting.
ins: Sit tall on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Brace your stomach and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Keep your wrists level with your elbows at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Lateral Raise (Back Supported)
desc: A seated lateral raise done with your back resting against an upright bench. The back support stops you from leaning, keeping the work on the side shoulders.
ins: Set a bench upright, sit with your back against it and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your feet flat and your head against the pad.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows slightly bent.
Pause briefly without shrugging.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
desc: A seated wrist curl with a thumbs-up grip, forearms resting on your thighs. Lifting the dumbbells with the wrists works the forearms and the muscles at the front of the elbow.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs with your hands just past your knees.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with thumbs pointing up.
Let the front ends of the dumbbells drop toward the floor.
Breathe out and lift them as high as you can using only your wrists.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping your forearms on your thighs.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Arm Bicep Curl On Exercise Ball With Leg Raised
desc: A one-arm dumbbell curl seated on an exercise ball with one leg raised. It trains the biceps while your core and hips work hard to balance against an uneven load.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side, palm forward.
Brace your stomach and lift the opposite foot off the floor, leg straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Lower it slowly while holding your balance.
Finish the set, then switch arm and raised leg.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Arm Kickback
desc: A one-arm triceps kickback done seated and leaning forward. It isolates one triceps at a time without loading the lower back.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in one hand and lean forward with a flat back.
Place your free hand on your knee and raise the working elbow so the upper arm is close to level and tight to your side.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back until it is fully extended.
Squeeze for a second.
Breathe in and lower the forearm slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Arm Rotate
desc: A seated forearm rotation with one dumbbell, turning the palm up and down while the elbow stays fixed. It works the forearm rotators and helps wrist and elbow health.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest one forearm on your thigh with your hand past the knee.
Hold a light dumbbell vertically, like a hammer, by its middle or one end.
Breathe out and rotate your hand until the palm faces up.
Rotate the other way until the palm faces down, moving slowly.
Keep your forearm on your thigh; only the forearm twists.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Arm Shoulder Press
desc: A one-arm dumbbell press done seated on a bench. Sitting removes help from the legs, and pressing with one arm makes the core work to keep you upright.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with your feet flat and hold a dumbbell at shoulder height, palm facing forward.
Rest your free hand on your thigh and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up until your arm is straight.
Keep your body from leaning to either side.
Breathe in and lower slowly to your shoulder, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise
desc: A seated calf raise for one leg at a time with a dumbbell resting on the working knee. The bent knee shifts the focus to the deep calf muscle.
ins: Sit on a bench and place the ball of one foot on a low block or plate, heel hanging off.
Set a dumbbell upright on top of that knee and hold it steady with your hand.
Let your heel drop below the block for a stretch.
Breathe out and push the knee up by rising onto the ball of your foot.
Pause at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise - Hammer Grip
desc: A one-leg seated calf raise where you hold the dumbbell upright on your knee with a neutral, hammer-style grip. The grip makes it easy to keep steady pressure on the working calf.
ins: Sit on a bench with the ball of one foot on a step and the heel hanging off.
Stand a dumbbell on end on top of that knee and grip its handle with your palm facing in.
Press the dumbbell down lightly to keep it steady.
Breathe out and rise onto the ball of your foot as high as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and lower your heel slowly below the step.
Complete the set and switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Seated One Leg Calf Raise - Palm Up
desc: A one-leg seated calf raise with the dumbbell lying across your thigh, held with your palm facing up. It loads one calf at a time from a bent-knee position.
ins: Sit on a bench with the ball of one foot on a step, heel off the edge.
Lay a dumbbell across that thigh just above the knee and hold it with your palm facing up.
Keep your back straight and your foot pointing forward.
Breathe out and raise your heel as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly into a stretch.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Seated Palms Up Wrist Curl
desc: A seated wrist curl with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing up. It targets the inner forearm muscles used in every pulling and gripping lift.
ins: Sit at the end of a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your wrists just past your knees.
Let the dumbbells lower so your wrists bend back.
Breathe out and curl both palms up as high as possible.
Pause, then breathe in and lower under control.
Keep your forearms flat and still.

name: Dumbbell Seated Preacher Curl
desc: A seated one-arm preacher curl with a dumbbell. The pad holds your arm in place so the biceps work without help from the shoulder.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and place the back of one upper arm flat on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell underhand with the arm almost straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Seated Reverse Grip Concentration Curl
desc: A seated concentration curl with the palm facing down. Bracing the elbow on the thigh isolates the arm, and the grip works the forearm and brachialis hard.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with feet wide and a dumbbell in one hand.
Lean forward and rest the back of that upper arm against your inner thigh, palm facing down.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up, keeping your wrist straight.
Stop near shoulder level.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Seated Reverse Grip One Arm Overhead Tricep Extension
desc: A seated one-arm overhead triceps extension with the dumbbell held in an underhand grip. It isolates the triceps through a long range, and the palm-up grip changes the angle at the wrist.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in one hand overhead, palm facing up behind you.
Keep the elbow pointing to the ceiling and the upper arm close to your head.
Breathe in and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back overhead.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press
desc: The standard seated dumbbell shoulder press with back support. It builds overall shoulder size and strength with help from the triceps.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and lift the dumbbells to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Plant your feet and keep your back against the pad.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight above your shoulders.
Don't bang the dumbbells together at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until they are level with your ears or a little lower.

name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press (parallel Grip)
desc: A seated dumbbell press with your palms facing each other. This neutral grip is easier on the shoulders and puts more work on the front shoulders and triceps.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your palms facing each other the whole time.
Breathe in and lower slowly to shoulder height.

name: Dumbbell Shrug
desc: A standing shrug with a dumbbell in each hand, a simple way to build the upper traps. Holding the weights also trains the grip.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep your arms straight and your neck relaxed.
Lift your shoulders straight up as high as you can.
Squeeze your traps at the top for a second.
Lower slowly all the way down.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Dumbbell Side Bend
desc: A standing side bend holding one dumbbell, where you lean toward the weight and pull yourself back up. It strengthens the obliques on the side opposite the dumbbell.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and a dumbbell in one hand at your side.
Rest your free hand on your hip or behind your head.
Slowly bend sideways toward the dumbbell, sliding it down the side of your leg.
Pull yourself back upright using the opposite side of your waist.
Keep your chest facing forward the whole time, then switch hands after your reps.

name: Dumbbell Side Lying One Hand Raise
desc: A lateral raise done lying on your side on the floor or a bench, lifting the top dumbbell up from your hip. Lying down changes the resistance so the side shoulder works hardest at the start.
ins: Lie on your side with your head resting on your bottom arm and a dumbbell in your top hand in front of your thigh.
Keep your legs stacked and your top arm almost straight.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbell up until your arm points just short of the ceiling.
Lower it slowly as you breathe in.
Finish your set, then roll over and work the other side.

name: Dumbbell Side Plank With Rear Fly
desc: An advanced combination where you hold a side plank on one forearm and lift a dumbbell out to the side with the top arm. It trains the rear shoulder and upper back while the core holds the plank.
ins: Lie on your side and set up a side plank on your forearm, elbow under your shoulder.
Hold a light dumbbell in your top hand, starting with it near the floor in front of your chest.
Lift your hips so your body is straight from head to feet and tighten your stomach.
Raise the dumbbell out and up until your arm points to the ceiling, keeping a slight bend in the elbow.
Lower it slowly while keeping your hips up.
Finish the set and switch sides.

name: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Carry
desc: A loaded walk holding one dumbbell straight overhead. It builds shoulder stability and makes your core work hard to keep you upright.
ins: Press a dumbbell overhead with one hand until your arm is straight, biceps near your ear.
Stand tall, brace your stomach and keep your ribs down.
Walk forward with short, steady steps, keeping the dumbbell directly over your shoulder.
Breathe steadily and don't lean to either side.
After the set distance, lower the dumbbell with control and switch hands.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Calf Raise
desc: A one-leg calf raise on a step while holding a dumbbell. Working each leg alone doubles the load on the calf and improves ankle balance.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and stand on a step on the same-side foot, heel hanging off.
Hook the other foot behind your ankle and hold a wall or rail with your free hand.
Lower your heel below the step for a full stretch.
Breathe out and push up onto your toes as high as you can.
Squeeze at the top, then breathe in and lower slowly.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift
desc: A one-leg hip hinge with dumbbells, reaching the weights toward the floor as the free leg extends behind you. It strengthens the glutes and hamstrings one side at a time and trains balance and hip control.
ins: Stand on your left leg with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Soften the left knee and brace your stomach.
Breathe in and tip forward from the hips, letting the dumbbells hang straight down as your right leg extends back.
Stop when your body is close to parallel to the floor or when your back starts to round.
Breathe out and squeeze the left glute to return to standing.
Complete the set, then work the other leg.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift With Stepbox Support
desc: A single-leg deadlift where the toes of the back foot rest lightly on a step behind you like a kickstand. The light support lets you load the glutes and hamstrings of the front leg with more weight and less wobble.
ins: Place a low step about a stride behind you and hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Put most of your weight on your front leg and rest the toes of your back foot on the step.
Soften the front knee and breathe in.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells along the front leg, keeping your back flat.
Breathe out, squeeze the front glute and stand tall.
Finish the set, then switch the working leg.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Deadlift With Stepbox Support (One Dumbbell)
desc: A supported single-leg hip hinge holding one dumbbell on the same side as the working leg, with the back foot resting on a low box. It focuses on the hamstrings and glutes and also trains grip, calves and a steady spine.
ins: Stand on your right leg with the toes of your left foot resting on a low box behind you.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand next to your thigh.
Keep a small bend in the right knee and brace your stomach.
Breathe in and hinge forward, lowering the dumbbell toward the middle of your right shin.
Keep your hips level and stop when you feel a strong stretch in the right hamstring.
Breathe out and push your hips forward to stand; switch sides after your reps.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Split Squat
desc: A Bulgarian split squat holding a dumbbell in each hand, with your rear foot raised on a bench. It strongly works the quads and glutes of the front leg and improves balance.
ins: Stand about two steps in front of a bench holding a dumbbell at each side.
Reach one foot back and rest the top of it on the bench.
Lower by bending the front knee until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor.
Keep your chest up and let the front knee move forward only as far as is comfortable.
Push through the whole front foot to rise back up.
Breathe out as you rise; complete all reps on one leg, then switch.

name: Dumbbell Single Leg Squat
desc: A single-leg squat holding a dumbbell at your chest as a counterweight, lowering toward a box or bench. It builds strength, balance and control in the glutes and quads of one leg.
ins: Stand in front of a box or bench, holding one dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Balance on one leg and lift the other foot slightly forward off the floor.
Push the dumbbell a little forward to counterbalance as you sit back and down on the standing leg.
Lower until you lightly touch the box, keeping the knee over your toes and the heel down.
Drive through the standing heel to stand back up without letting the free foot touch down.
Breathe out as you stand; finish one leg, then switch.

name: Dumbbell Squat
desc: A basic squat holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. It is a simple way for beginners to load the squat and build the glutes and quads.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell hanging at each side.
Brace your core, lift your chest and look straight ahead.
Sit your hips back and bend your knees to lower down, letting the dumbbells hang straight.
Go down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, heels flat.
Push through your feet to stand back up.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Hammer Curl And Press
desc: A standing combination of a hammer curl and an overhead press, alternating arms. It trains the biceps, brachialis and forearms on the curl and the shoulders on the press.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Breathe out and hammer curl one dumbbell up to your shoulder.
Press that dumbbell straight overhead, keeping your palm facing in.
Lower it back to your shoulder, then to your side with control.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating, stomach tight.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Overhead Press
desc: A standing dumbbell press where you push one arm overhead at a time. It works the shoulders and triceps while your core keeps your body from leaning.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe out and press one dumbbell straight up until your arm is straight.
Breathe in and lower it back to your shoulder.
Press the other side and keep alternating, staying upright.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternate Raise
desc: A standing lateral raise done one arm at a time, alternating sides. Resting one arm while the other lifts lets you keep strict form for longer.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Brace your stomach and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise one dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower it slowly.
Raise the other arm and keep alternating without leaning.

name: Dumbbell Standing Alternating Tricep Kickback
desc: A standing dumbbell triceps kickback done one arm at a time. Bending at the hips puts the upper arms in position so the triceps lift the weight back.
ins: Take a dumbbell in each hand, unlock your knees and tip your torso forward from the hips, back flat.
Bring your upper arms up beside your body with elbows bent at about a right angle.
Breathe out and straighten one arm back until it is in line with your body.
Bend it slowly to return, then straighten the other arm.
Keep your upper arms still and your back flat as you alternate.

name: Dumbbell Standing Arnold Press
desc: A standing version of the Arnold press, where you start with palms facing you and rotate them forward as you press. It works the front and side shoulders, and standing makes your core work too.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you and elbows in front.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe out and press up while turning your palms forward and moving your elbows out to the sides.
Finish with your arms straight and palms facing forward over your head.
Breathe in and reverse the turn as you lower back to the start.

name: Dumbbell Standing Around World
desc: A standing move where you sweep light dumbbells in a big circle from your thighs, out to the sides and over your head, then back. It works the shoulders through their full range and improves shoulder control.
ins: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep your arms almost straight and brace your stomach.
Breathe in as you sweep the dumbbells out to the sides and up until they meet over your head.
Breathe out and reverse the circle back down to your thighs.
Move slowly and keep your shoulders away from your ears.

name: Dumbbell Standing Bent Over One Arm Triceps Extension
desc: A standing one-arm triceps kickback with your free hand braced on a bench. Bracing lets you keep a flat back and focus fully on the working triceps.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and put your other hand on a bench, hinging forward until your back is nearly flat.
Raise the working upper arm beside your body with the elbow bent at about a right angle.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back until it is fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps, then lower the dumbbell slowly by bending the elbow.
Finish the set, then switch sides.

name: Dumbbell Standing Bent Over Two Arm Triceps Extension
desc: A standing two-arm triceps kickback while bent forward at the hips. Both triceps work at once, and holding the bent-over position also trains the back.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, soften your knees and hinge forward until your torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Pull your upper arms up beside your body with your elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back at the same time.
Squeeze for a moment with your arms in line with your body.
Bend your elbows slowly to return, keeping your back flat.

name: Dumbbell Standing Biceps Curl
desc: A standing curl with a dumbbell in each hand, both arms together, palms up the whole way. It is a basic biceps builder.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing forward.
Pull your shoulders back and keep your elbows by your ribs.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up until your forearms are near vertical.
Squeeze at the top without leaning back.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Standing Concentration Curl
desc: A standing concentration curl where you bend forward and let one arm hang straight down. Hanging the arm removes momentum and isolates the biceps.
ins: Stand with feet wide, hinge forward at the hips and rest your free hand on your knee or a bench.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and let that arm hang straight down below your shoulder.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your chest without moving the upper arm.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing Front Raise Above Head
desc: A standing front raise that continues all the way overhead with straight arms. It works the front shoulders through a full range, with the traps helping at the top.
ins: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing each other.
Brace your stomach and keep your arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and raise the dumbbells in front of you and keep going until they are over your head.
Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same path.

name: Dumbbell Standing Inner Biceps Curl
desc: A standing dumbbell curl in which the dumbbells travel up and outward, away from your body, with the elbows fixed at your sides. This outward path tends to emphasize the inner, short head of the biceps.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Turn your hands slightly outward so the dumbbells point away from your body, elbows tucked at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbells up and out toward the outside of your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same path.

name: Dumbbell Standing Kickback
desc: A triceps kickback done standing in a bent-over position with a dumbbell in each hand. Both arms straighten back together to isolate the triceps.
ins: With two dumbbells in hand, soften your knees and lean your torso forward to about 45 degrees or lower.
Bring your upper arms up beside your torso and let your forearms hang down.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back until they are in line with your body.
Pause and squeeze the triceps.
Breathe in and lower your forearms slowly without letting your elbows drop.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Concentration Curl
desc: A standing one-arm curl where your free hand supports the working elbow to keep it still. It concentrates the effort on one biceps at a time.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight and palm facing forward.
Cup the working elbow with your free hand to hold it against your side.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell slowly toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Curl (over Incline Bench)
desc: A one-arm curl done standing behind an incline bench with your upper arm draped over the backrest, like a homemade preacher curl. It isolates the biceps.
ins: Set a bench to a steep incline and stand behind it.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand and drape the back of that upper arm over the top of the backrest, arm hanging down the front.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze at the top without lifting your arm off the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly to an almost straight arm; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Curl Over Incline Bench
desc: A one-arm curl done standing behind an incline bench with your upper arm resting over the top of the backrest. The bench works like a preacher pad, keeping the upper arm fixed so the biceps do the work.
ins: Set a bench to a steep incline and stand behind it holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Drape the back of that upper arm over the top of the backrest so your arm hangs down the front, palm facing up.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the arm is nearly straight, then switch arms.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Extension
desc: A one-arm overhead triceps extension done standing with a dumbbell. It works the triceps, especially the long head, and asks your core to stay stable.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and press a dumbbell straight overhead in one hand.
Brace your stomach and keep the elbow close to your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arm back overhead.
Keep your torso upright; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Palm In Press
desc: A standing one-arm press with your palm facing in toward your head. The neutral grip is gentle on the shoulder, and pressing with one arm makes your core work hard.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell at shoulder height in one hand, palm facing in and elbow in front.
Brace your stomach and keep your free hand on your hip.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight up, keeping your palm facing in.
Keep your shoulders level and don't lean away.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Dumbbell Standing One Arm Reverse Curl
desc: A standing one-arm curl with the palm facing down. It builds the forearm and brachialis as well as the biceps, one side at a time.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in one hand, arm straight and palm facing behind you.
Keep the elbow at your side and the wrist straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up with the back of your hand leading.
Stop near shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing Palms In Press
desc: A standing dumbbell press with both palms facing each other throughout. It is a shoulder-friendly way to train the front shoulders and triceps.
ins: Stand tall and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing each other and elbows pointing forward.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your palms facing in the whole time.
Breathe in and lower slowly to your shoulders.

name: Dumbbell Standing Preacher Curl
desc: A standing preacher curl with a dumbbell, leaning over a preacher pad set at standing height. It isolates the biceps and stretches them at the bottom.
ins: Stand behind a preacher bench or standing preacher station and rest the back of one upper arm on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell underhand with the arm nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch arms after the set.

name: Dumbbell Standing Reverse Curl
desc: A standing dumbbell curl with both palms facing down, lifting both arms together. It trains the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps.
ins: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and palms facing behind you.
Pin your elbows to your sides.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, keeping your wrists flat.
Pause near shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Dumbbell Standing Triceps Extension
desc: A standing overhead triceps extension holding one dumbbell with both hands. It stretches and strengthens the triceps through a long range.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands under the top end.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows close to your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift it back overhead.
Avoid arching your lower back as you press.

name: Dumbbell Standing Zottman Preacher Curl
desc: A Zottman curl done standing at a preacher bench with both dumbbells: curl up palms-up, turn the palms down at the top, and lower slowly palms-down. It trains the biceps going up and the forearms going down.
ins: Stand behind a preacher bench and rest the backs of both upper arms on the pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand palms up.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly with palms down.
At the bottom, turn your palms back up before the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Step Up Lunge
desc: A split squat between two benches: the front foot stands on one bench and the rear foot rests on another, so you can drop lower than the floor allows. Holding dumbbells, it builds the quads and glutes through a very deep range and works the inner thighs, hamstrings, calves and abs.
ins: Set two sturdy benches about a stride apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step your front foot onto one bench and rest the top of your rear foot on the bench behind you.
Breathe in and lower straight down between the benches, keeping your chest up.
Go as deep as you can control, letting the front knee travel forward over the toes.
Breathe out and drive through the front heel to rise back up.
Finish the set, then switch legs carefully.

name: Dumbbell Step Up Single Leg Balance With Bicep Curl
desc: A step-up onto a box, finishing balanced on one leg while performing a dumbbell curl. It works the quads, glutes and hamstrings along with the biceps and balance.
ins: Stand facing a box or step holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place one foot on the box and push through it to stand up on top.
Keep the other leg lifted with the knee bent and balance on the box leg.
While balanced, breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, then lower them slowly.
Step back down with control and repeat, switching legs.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
desc: Stepping up onto a box or bench while holding a dumbbell in each hand. It builds the glutes and quads of each leg and improves balance for stairs and climbing.
ins: Stand facing a sturdy box about knee height with a dumbbell at each side.
Place one foot fully on the box.
Press through that heel to lift yourself up until the leg is straight.
Bring the other foot up to meet it, then stand tall at the top.
Step down slowly with the same foot you brought up last, keeping control with the working leg.
Breathe out as you step up; alternate legs or finish one side first.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up Lunge
desc: A combination move: step up onto a box with dumbbells in hand, then step down and back into a reverse lunge. It trains the quads and glutes in two ways in a single rep, with the hamstrings and calves helping.
ins: Stand in front of a box or bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place your right foot fully on the box and push through it to stand on top, bringing the left foot up.
Step down with the left foot, then the right, back to the floor.
Step the right foot back into a reverse lunge, lowering until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through the front foot to return to standing, breathing out as you rise.
Repeat, leading with the same leg for the set, then switch.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up Split Squat
desc: A split squat with the front foot raised on a low step and a dumbbell in each hand. The raised front foot lets you sink deeper, putting more stretch and work on the quads and glutes.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and place your right foot flat on a low step.
Step your left foot back into a long split stance with the heel lifted.
Breathe in and lower until the back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your chest up and your front heel pressed into the step.
Breathe out and push through the front foot to return to the top.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Dumbbell Straight Arm Pullover
desc: A dumbbell pullover done with the arms kept fully straight from start to finish. The long lever increases the stretch and load on the chest and lats.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding one dumbbell with both hands directly above your chest, arms straight.
Brace your stomach and press your lower back gently into the bench.
Keeping your elbows straight, lower the dumbbell back over your head until you feel a stretch along your chest and sides.
Raise it back to above your chest without bending your arms.
Inhale on the way back and exhale on the way up; use a lighter dumbbell than for a bent-arm pullover.

name: Dumbbell Straight Leg Deadlift
desc: A straight-leg dumbbell deadlift where the dumbbells slide down the front of your thighs as your hips move back. It targets the glutes and hamstrings and strengthens the lower back's hold on a flat spine.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand against the front of your thighs, palms facing you, feet hip-width apart.
Soften your knees slightly and pull your shoulders back and down.
Push your hips back and let the dumbbells slide down your thighs, keeping them close to your legs.
Stop just below the knees or when your hamstrings are fully stretched.
Return to standing by driving your hips forward until you are upright.
Breathe in as you hinge and out as you stand.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Pull Through
desc: A wide-stance hip hinge where you swing a dumbbell back between your legs and drive the hips forward to bring it up. It trains the glutes and hamstrings, with work for the inner thighs, quads and lower back.
ins: Stand with feet wide and toes turned out, holding one dumbbell by its end with both hands.
Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length between your legs.
Breathe in, push your hips back and let the dumbbell travel back between your thighs, knees slightly bent.
Keep your back flat and arms long, without squatting deep.
Breathe out and thrust your hips forward, squeezing your glutes, so the dumbbell rises to just in front of your hips.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Pull Through (Bottom Stretch)
desc: A sumo-stance glute exercise: hinge back to reach a dumbbell between your legs, then stand up by squeezing your glutes. It builds the glutes and hamstrings, with the quads and core helping.
ins: Take a wide stance with toes pointed out and hold a dumbbell with both hands in front of your hips.
Soften your knees and tighten your stomach.
Push your hips back and reach the dumbbell down and back between your legs, keeping your back flat.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings and inner thighs at the bottom.
Breathe out and drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes hard at the top.

name: Dumbbell Supported Squat
desc: A squat holding a dumbbell in one hand while the other hand holds a rack or sturdy support. The support lets beginners sit deeper and focus on form while the quads, glutes and hamstrings do the work.
ins: Stand beside a rack or sturdy support and hold it lightly with one hand.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand at your side, feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in and sit your hips back and down, keeping your chest up.
Use the support only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Breathe out and drive through your heels to stand.
Switch the dumbbell to the other hand halfway through, or on the next set.

name: Dumbbell Tate Press
desc: A lying dumbbell triceps exercise where the elbows flare out and the dumbbells are lowered inward to touch your chest. It targets the triceps, especially near lockout.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand pressed above your chest, palms facing your feet.
Turn the dumbbells so their ends point toward each other.
Breathe in and bend your elbows out to the sides, lowering the dumbbells inward until they touch your chest.
Keep your upper arms still.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to push the dumbbells back up.

name: Dumbbell Tricep Kickback With Stork Stance
desc: A triceps kickback done while standing on one leg. Balancing on one foot adds work for the ankle, hips and core on top of the triceps.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, lift one foot and rest it against the inside of your standing leg.
Hinge forward slightly with a flat back and bring your upper arms beside your body, elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten both arms back.
Hold the squeeze briefly, then bend your elbows to return.
Keep your balance and switch standing legs halfway through or between sets.

name: Dumbbell Twisting Bench Press
desc: A dumbbell bench press where you rotate your hands during the movement, from palms facing each other at the bottom to palms facing your feet at the top. The turning action adds triceps and chest work.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand beside your chest, palms facing each other.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up, turning your hands as you go so your palms face your feet at the top.
Bring the dumbbells close together over your chest and squeeze.
Lower them slowly while turning your palms back to face each other.
Keep your elbows from flaring wide as you move.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row
desc: An upright row with a dumbbell in each hand. Dumbbells let your hands move freely, which often feels easier on the shoulders than a barbell.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Breathe out and lift your elbows up and out, pulling the dumbbells up close to your body.
Stop when your elbows are at shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Upright Row (back Pov)
desc: A dumbbell upright row shown from behind, which makes it easy to see your shoulder blades and elbows. It works the side shoulders and traps, with the biceps helping.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Set your shoulders down and keep your stomach braced.
Breathe out and lift your elbows out to the sides, drawing the dumbbells up close to your body.
Stop when your elbows are level with your shoulders, with both sides moving evenly.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly.

name: Dumbbell Upright Shoulder External Rotation
desc: A standing rotator cuff exercise with your upper arm raised to shoulder height and your elbow bent, rotating the dumbbell up and back. It strengthens the outward rotators and helps keep the shoulder healthy for pressing.
ins: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand.
Raise your upper arms out to the sides to shoulder height with elbows bent to 90 degrees and forearms pointing forward.
Breathe out and rotate your forearms up until they point to the ceiling, keeping your elbows in place.
Pause briefly at the top.
Breathe in and rotate back down slowly.

name: Dumbbell W-Press
desc: A seated press that starts with your elbows low and wide so your arms form a W shape. It works the shoulders and triceps and trains you to keep your shoulder blades set.
ins: Sit tall on a bench and hold the dumbbells beside your shoulders, palms forward, elbows pointing down and out.
Squeeze your shoulder blades back and down so your arms form a W.
Breathe out and press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Breathe in and lower them back into the W position.
Keep your back straight and your stomach braced throughout.

name: Dumbbell Waiter Biceps Curl
desc: A curl in which you hold a single dumbbell upright with both palms under the top plate, like a waiter holding a tray. The flat-palm grip keeps steady tension on the biceps throughout.
ins: Stand tall and hold one dumbbell vertically in front of your thighs, both palms cupped flat under the top plate.
Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your chest, keeping it vertical.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Dumbbell Zottman Curl
desc: A dumbbell curl that goes up with palms facing up and comes down with palms facing down. It trains the biceps on the way up and the forearms on the way down.
ins: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight and palms facing forward.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up to shoulder height.
At the top, rotate your wrists so your palms face down.
Breathe in and lower the dumbbells slowly with palms down.
At the bottom, turn your palms forward again before the next rep.

name: Dumbbell Zottman Preacher Curl
desc: A seated Zottman curl on a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Lifting palms-up and lowering palms-down trains the biceps, brachialis and forearms in one movement.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench with both upper arms on the pad, holding a dumbbell in each hand palms up.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up.
Turn your palms to face down at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, resisting the weight with your forearms.
Turn your palms back up at the bottom and repeat.

name: Dumbbells Seated Triceps Extension
desc: A seated overhead triceps extension holding one dumbbell with both hands. It lets you use a heavier weight and stretches the long head of the triceps.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupped under the top plate.
Keep your elbows pointing up and close to your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift it back overhead.
Keep your back against the pad and your ribs down.

name: Dynamic Chest Stretch
desc: A moving warm-up stretch where you swing your arms open and closed across the body to loosen the chest and shoulders. It is best done before upper-body training.
ins: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Swing your arms back gently until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Swing them forward and cross them in front of your chest, alternating which arm goes on top.
Keep the movement smooth and controlled, gradually increasing the range.
Breathe naturally and continue for about 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Elbow Dips
desc: A bench dip performed with your legs straight and heels on the floor. Straight legs put more of your bodyweight on the triceps than the bent-knee version, with the chest and shoulders assisting.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands gripping it beside your hips.
Walk your feet out until your legs are straight and only your heels touch the floor, then slide your hips off the bench.
Breathe in and bend your elbows straight back to lower your hips toward the floor.
Stop when your elbows reach about a right angle, keeping your back close to the bench.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Elbow Lift - Reverse Push-Up
desc: A floor exercise lying on your back where you press the elbows down to lift the upper body. It strengthens the upper back and the backs of the shoulders and suits beginners.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Bend your elbows to 90 degrees with your upper arms by your sides and forearms pointing up.
Press your elbows into the floor to lift your upper back and chest off the mat.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out at the top.
Lower yourself slowly back to the floor.

name: Elbow-To-Knee
desc: A lying crunch where you bring each elbow to the opposite knee in turn. It works the abs with a focus on the obliques.
ins: Lie on your back with your fingertips behind your head and your knees bent, feet flat.
Breathe out, lift your shoulders and bring your left knee up as your right elbow twists toward it.
Touch or nearly touch elbow to knee, then lower both with control.
Repeat with your left elbow and right knee.
Keep your elbows open and the movement slow.

name: Elevator
desc: A hanging drill on a pull-up bar where you raise and lower your body using only your shoulder blades, like an elevator, with your arms straight. It strengthens the upper back and traps and prepares the shoulders for pull-ups.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width and arms straight.
Let your shoulders rise toward your ears in a relaxed hang.
Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and together so your body rises a few centimetres.
Hold for a second and breathe out.
Lower slowly back to the relaxed hang.

name: Exercise Ball Alternating Arm Ups
desc: A beginner exercise lying face down over a stability ball and raising one arm at a time overhead. It trains the lats and shoulders while the core keeps you balanced.
ins: Lie face down with your stomach on the ball, feet on the floor and hands on the floor in front of you.
Tighten your stomach so your body stays steady on the ball.
Lift one arm straight forward in line with your ear, thumb pointing up.
Hold for a second, then lower it with control.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Arms Extended
desc: A back extension over a stability ball with the arms reached straight forward. The long arm position makes the lower back muscles work harder, with help from the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and your feet wide on the floor or braced against a wall.
Reach both arms straight forward past your head.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your chest until your arms, back and legs form one line.
Breathe out as you lift and keep your neck in line with your back.
Lower slowly over the ball.

name: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Hands Behind Head
desc: A back extension over a stability ball with the fingertips behind the head. It strengthens the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and your feet planted wide or against a wall.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your head with elbows out.
Lift your chest off the ball until your body is straight, squeezing your glutes.
Do not pull on your head; keep your chin tucked slightly.
Lower slowly and breathe in on the way down.

name: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Knees Off Ground
desc: A harder ball back extension with the legs straight and knees off the floor, feet braced against a wall. The whole back line works, including the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and press the balls of your feet against a wall, legs straight.
Keep your knees off the floor and cross your arms on your chest.
Lift your chest until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and breathe out at the top.
Lower slowly while keeping your legs straight.

name: Exercise Ball Back Extension With Rotation
desc: A ball back extension with a twist at the top. It strengthens the lower back and adds rotation work for the trunk.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and your feet wide on the floor.
Place your fingertips behind your head.
Lift your chest until your back is straight.
At the top, turn your chest to one side, then back to the middle.
Lower slowly and alternate the side you turn to each rep.

name: Exercise Ball Dip
desc: A dip with your hands on a bench behind you and your feet up on an exercise ball. The unstable ball raises the difficulty for the triceps, chest and shoulders and makes your core work to stay balanced.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands beside your hips, then place your heels on an exercise ball in front of you.
Lift your hips off the bench so your arms and the ball hold your weight, legs straight.
Bend your elbows straight back and lower your hips until your elbows reach about a right angle.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms.
Keep the ball still and your back close to the bench.

name: Exercise Ball Hip Flexor Stretch
desc: A kneeling lunge stretch where you rest your hands on a stability ball for balance. It opens the hip flexors at the front of the hip and also stretches the quads.
ins: Kneel on your right knee with your left foot flat in front, both knees bent about 90 degrees.
Place a stability ball in front of you and rest your hands on top of it.
Tuck your pelvis under slightly and squeeze your right glute.
Shift your hips forward slowly, rolling the ball a little ahead, until you feel the stretch at the front of the right hip.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds with slow breaths, then switch sides.

name: Exercise Ball Hug
desc: A gentle mobility drill where you kneel and drape your body over a stability ball as if hugging it. It rounds and relaxes the spine and opens the upper back and shoulders.
ins: Kneel on a mat with a stability ball in front of you.
Lean forward and wrap your arms around the ball, resting your chest and head on it.
Let your back round softly over the ball and relax your shoulders.
Breathe slowly and feel the space open between your shoulder blades.
Roll the ball gently forward and back or side to side for 30 to 60 seconds.

name: Exercise Ball Lat Stretch
desc: A kneeling stretch using a stability ball to lengthen the lats and the backs of the shoulders.
ins: Kneel on a mat with a stability ball in front of you.
Place both hands on top of the ball, thumbs up.
Roll the ball forward and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Let your chest sink toward the floor until you feel a stretch along your sides and under your arms.
Breathe deeply and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Exercise Ball Lower Back Stretch (pyramid)
desc: A standing forward fold with the hands on a stability ball, making a pyramid shape. It stretches the lats and lower back along with the hamstrings and glutes.
ins: Stand with your feet wide apart and a stability ball on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at the hips and place both hands on the ball.
Roll the ball forward and let your chest drop between your arms, keeping your legs straight.
Push your hips up and back so your body forms a pyramid shape.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then roll the ball back to stand up.

name: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch
desc: A side-lying stretch over a stability ball that lengthens the lats and the whole side of the trunk.
ins: Kneel beside the ball and lie sideways over it so it sits under your ribs and hip.
Straighten your legs and stagger your feet on the floor for balance.
Reach your top arm over your head and let your side curve over the ball.
Breathe into the stretched side and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Come back up slowly and switch sides.

name: Exercise Ball On The Wall Calf Raise
desc: A calf raise holding dumbbells while an exercise ball sits between your lower back and a wall. The ball keeps your posture upright so you can focus on the calves.
ins: Place an exercise ball against a wall and lean your lower back into it.
Walk your feet slightly forward so you stand upright, feet hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of your feet, letting the ball roll slightly up the wall.
Pause at the top, then breathe in and lower your heels slowly.
Keep gentle pressure into the ball the whole time.

name: Exercise Ball On The Wall Calf Raise (tennis Ball Between Ankles)
desc: A dumbbell calf raise with an exercise ball behind your lower back against a wall and a tennis ball held between the ankles. Gripping the ball at the ankles stops the feet rolling outward as you rise.
ins: Lean your lower back into an exercise ball placed against a wall, with your feet a little in front of you.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Place a tennis ball between your ankles and press it gently with both feet.
Rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can without letting the tennis ball drop.
Hold for a second, then lower your heels slowly to the floor.
Exhale on the way up and inhale on the way down.

name: Exercise Ball On The Wall Calf Raise (tennis Ball Between Knees)
desc: A dumbbell calf raise with an exercise ball between your lower back and a wall, and a tennis ball squeezed between the knees. The tennis ball keeps the knees in line so the calves work straight up and down.
ins: Place an exercise ball against a wall and lean your lower back into it, feet slightly in front of you and hip-width apart.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms hanging by your sides.
Put a tennis ball between your knees and squeeze it lightly.
Rise onto your toes as high as you can, letting the ball roll slightly up the wall.
Keep squeezing the tennis ball, pause at the top, then lower your heels slowly.
Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.

name: Exercise Ball One Leg Prone Lower Body Rotation
desc: A balance exercise lying face down over a stability ball, lifting one straight leg and rotating it across behind you by turning your hips. It works the glutes and core and improves hip control and rotational mobility.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and your hands on the floor in front, arms straight.
Lift one leg straight back until it is in line with your body.
Keeping your hands planted, slowly rotate your hips and swing the raised leg across behind you toward the other side.
Go only as far as you can stay balanced on the ball.
Rotate back to the center, lower the leg and repeat with the other leg.
Breathe out as you rotate and keep your core tight the whole time.

name: Exercise Ball One Legged Diagonal Kick Hamstring Curl
desc: An advanced single-leg hamstring curl on a stability ball: from a bridge with one heel on the ball, you roll the ball in, then push it back out on a diagonal. The diagonal path adds extra demand on the glutes and hip stabilizers along with the hamstrings.
ins: Lie on your back with your arms out at your sides and one heel on top of the ball; hold the other leg up toward the ceiling.
Press your heel into the ball and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to heel.
Keeping your hips up, bend the knee and roll the ball in toward your glutes.
Push the ball back out at a diagonal, angling the leg slightly away from your body, until the leg is straight.
Bring the ball back to center and keep your hips level the whole time.
Breathe out as you curl in; finish your reps, then switch legs.

name: Exercise Ball Pike Push Up
desc: An advanced push-up with your shins on an exercise ball: you roll the ball in as you lift your hips into a pike, then do a push-up. It works the chest and shoulders hard and demands strong core control.
ins: Get into a push-up position with your hands on the floor under your shoulders and your shins resting on the ball.
Brace your stomach and lift your hips toward the ceiling, rolling the ball in until your toes are on top of it.
Lower back to a straight plank position with control.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor.
Breathe out and push back up to straight arms.
Keep your back from sagging at any point; reset if the ball drifts sideways.

name: Exercise Ball Prone Leg Raise
desc: A reverse leg raise done face down over a stability ball. It strengthens the lower back and glutes.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and your hands on the floor under your shoulders.
Straighten your legs behind you with your toes resting on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift both legs until they line up with your body.
Breathe out as you lift and avoid swinging.
Lower your legs slowly until your toes lightly touch the floor.

name: Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch
desc: A hamstring stretch done sitting on a stability ball with one leg straight in front. The ball keeps you upright and lets you hinge from the hips, stretching the hamstrings and easing the glutes and lower back.
ins: Sit on top of a stability ball with your feet flat and knees bent.
Walk one foot forward and straighten that leg, resting the heel on the floor.
Sit tall and place your hands on your thighs.
Lean forward from the hips with a flat back until you feel the stretch behind the straight leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly, then switch legs.

name: Exercise Ball Seated Triceps Stretch
desc: A seated stretch for the back of the upper arm, done sitting on an exercise ball. It loosens the triceps and the side of the shoulder after arm or pressing work.
ins: Sit tall on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor.
Raise one arm overhead, bend the elbow and let your hand drop behind your head toward your upper back.
Hold the bent elbow with your other hand and gently ease it back and toward your head.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, keeping your ribs down.
Release slowly and repeat on the other arm.

name: Exercise Ball Supine Triceps Extension
desc: A lying dumbbell triceps extension performed with your upper back supported on an exercise ball. It isolates the triceps while your glutes and core hold your hips up in a bridge.
ins: Sit on the ball with a dumbbell in each hand, walk your feet forward and lie back until your head and upper back rest on it.
Lift your hips level with your knees and press the dumbbells straight up, palms facing each other.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms, keeping your upper arms still.
Keep squeezing your glutes so your hips don't drop.

name: Ez Bar French Press On Exercise Ball
desc: A lying triceps extension with an EZ bar, performed with your upper back on an exercise ball. The angled grip is easy on the wrists, and the ball adds a balance challenge for the core and hips.
ins: Hold an EZ bar on the inner angled grips and lie back on the ball until your upper back and head are supported, hips raised.
Press the bar up over your chest with your arms straight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Keep your elbows pointing up and not flaring out.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press the bar back up.

name: Ez Bar Lying Bent Arms Pullover
desc: A lying pullover with an EZ bar and bent elbows. It stretches and strengthens the lats, with the chest and triceps assisting.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold an EZ bar over your chest with a narrow overhand grip.
Bend your elbows and keep that bend fixed.
Breathe in and lower the bar back behind your head in an arc until you feel your lats stretch.
Keep your lower back on the bench.
Breathe out and pull the bar back over your chest.

name: Ez Bar Lying Close Grip Triceps Extension Behind Head
desc: A lying triceps extension with an EZ bar held in a close grip and lowered behind your head. The extra range behind the head adds stretch to the long head of the triceps.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your head near the end and hold an EZ bar on the inner grips above your face.
Let your upper arms angle slightly back toward your head.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar past your forehead to behind your head.
Feel the stretch in the back of your arms while keeping your elbows narrow.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to bring the bar back above your face.

name: Ez Bar Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over row with an EZ bar held palms-up. It builds the upper back and uses the biceps more than an overhand row, with less wrist strain than a straight bar.
ins: Hold an EZ bar on the angled grips with your palms facing forward.
Hinge at the hips until your back is at about 45 degrees or lower, knees soft and back flat.
Pull the bar toward your lower stomach, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Ez Bar Seated Close Grip Concentration Curl
desc: A seated concentration curl with an EZ bar held in a close grip, both elbows braced against your inner thighs. It isolates both biceps at once with no swing.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet wide and hold an EZ bar underhand on the inner grips.
Lean forward and brace the backs of your upper arms against your inner thighs, arms hanging down.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Ez Bar Standing French Press
desc: A standing overhead triceps extension with an EZ bar. Working overhead stretches the long head of the triceps, and standing makes your core keep your back from arching.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and hold an EZ bar overhead on the inner grips, arms straight.
Tighten your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your lower back stays neutral.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointing forward and close to your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift the bar back overhead.

name: Ez Barbell Anti Gravity Press
desc: A press done lying chest-down on an incline bench, pushing an EZ bar out past your head in line with your body. Fighting gravity in this position strengthens the shoulders and upper back through the top of the overhead range.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie chest-down on it with your head past the top edge.
Hold an EZ bar at the level of your face with an overhand grip, elbows bent and pointing down.
Breathe out and press the bar forward and up in line with your body until your arms are straight.
Keep your chest on the pad and your shoulder blades squeezed.
Breathe in and bring the bar back slowly to your face.

name: Ez Barbell Close Grip Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl with an EZ bar held on the inner, narrow grips. The close grip tends to emphasize the outer part of the biceps while the pad stops any swinging.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench and rest your upper arms on the pad.
Hold an EZ bar underhand on the inner angled grips with your arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chin.
Squeeze your biceps when your forearms are near vertical.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly, stopping just short of locking your elbows.

name: Ez Barbell Close-Grip Curl
desc: A curl with an EZ bar held on the inner, narrow grips. The angled handles ease wrist strain while the close grip works the outer biceps.
ins: Stand tall and hold an EZ bar on the inner angled grips, palms facing up.
Let the bar rest against your thighs and keep your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Ez Barbell Curl
desc: A standing curl with an EZ bar on the outer grips. The bend in the bar is easier on the wrists than a straight bar while still building the biceps.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold an EZ bar on the outer angled grips, palms up.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs and your chest up.
Breathe out and curl the bar toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top without letting your elbows move forward.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Ez Barbell Decline Close Grip Face Press
desc: A decline-bench triceps press with an EZ bar held close, lowering the bar toward your face before pressing it back up. It loads the triceps with help from the chest and shoulders.
ins: Secure your feet on a decline bench and lie back holding an EZ bar on the inner grips above your chest.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to bring the bar down toward your chin and face, letting your elbows travel slightly forward.
Stop a few centimeters above your face.
Breathe out and press the bar back up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Move slowly and use a spotter for heavier sets.

name: Ez Barbell Decline Triceps Extension
desc: A lying triceps extension with an EZ bar on a decline bench. The decline keeps the upper arms in a strong position and keeps steady tension on the triceps.
ins: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured and hold an EZ bar on the inner grips above your chest.
Keep your upper arms vertical to the floor and your elbows pointing up.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Stop just above your head without moving your upper arms.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press the bar back up.

name: Ez Barbell Incline Triceps Extension
desc: A triceps extension on an incline bench with an EZ bar, lowering it behind your head. The incline places the triceps on a deep stretch.
ins: Lie on an incline bench and hold an EZ bar on the inner grips with straight arms above your head.
Keep your upper arms fixed and angled slightly back.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Go as deep as you can control while feeling the stretch.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to raise the bar.

name: Ez Barbell Jm Bench Press
