desc: An advanced triceps press with an EZ bar that blends a close-grip bench press with a skull crusher. The angled grips can be easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
ins: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar on the inner grips with straight arms over your chest.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, letting the bar come down toward your upper chest and chin.
Let your elbows move forward toward your feet so your forearms fold against your upper arms.
Stop just above your chin.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms along the same path.

name: Ez Barbell Reverse Grip Curl
desc: A standing curl with an EZ bar and a palms-down grip. It strengthens the forearms and brachialis along with the biceps, with less wrist strain than a straight bar.
ins: Stand tall holding an EZ bar on the outer grips with palms facing down.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your shoulders, keeping your wrists firm.
Pause at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Ez Barbell Reverse Grip Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl with an EZ bar held palms down. The pad fixes your upper arms, so the forearms and brachialis work hard alongside the biceps.
ins: Sit at a preacher bench with the backs of your upper arms on the pad.
Hold an EZ bar with palms facing down and arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up, keeping your wrists in line with your forearms.
Stop when your forearms are near vertical.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the start.

name: Ez Barbell Seated Curls
desc: A seated biceps curl with an EZ bar. Sitting cuts out body swing, and the angled grip is comfortable for the wrists.
ins: Sit on the end of a bench with your feet flat and hold an EZ bar underhand on the angled grips, resting it on your thighs.
Keep your back straight and your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top for a moment.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly back to your thighs.

name: Ez Barbell Seated Triceps Extension
desc: A seated overhead triceps extension with an EZ bar. The angled grip is comfortable for the wrists, and working overhead stretches the long head of the triceps.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold an EZ bar overhead on the inner grips.
Keep your elbows close to your head and pointing forward.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift it back overhead.
Keep your back against the pad and your ribs down.

name: Ez Barbell Spider Curl
desc: A curl done lying chest-down on the angled side of a preacher bench or on an incline bench, with your arms hanging straight down. It isolates the biceps and gives a hard squeeze at the top.
ins: Lie chest-down on the angled side of a preacher bench or an incline bench so your arms hang straight down.
Hold an EZ bar underhand on the grips.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest, keeping your upper arms vertical.
Squeeze hard at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Ez Barbell Spider Curl (Incline Bench)
desc: A curl done lying chest-down on an incline bench with an EZ bar, arms hanging straight down. The position stops any body movement and keeps tension on the biceps at the top of the curl.
ins: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest near the top edge.
Hold an EZ bar underhand and let your arms hang straight toward the floor.
Breathe out and curl the bar up, keeping your upper arms pointing straight down.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Ez-Bar Biceps Curl (with Arm Blaster)
desc: A standing EZ-bar curl with an arm blaster keeping your elbows fixed. The angled bar is easier on the wrists, and the strap makes the biceps do the lifting without body swing.
ins: Put on the arm blaster and hold an EZ bar underhand on the angled grips.
Stand tall with your arms straight and your elbows pressed against the plate.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to full arm extension.

name: Ez-Bar Close-Grip Bench Press
desc: A flat-bench press with an EZ bar using a close grip on the inner angled handles. The angled grip is easier on the wrists while the triceps do most of the work, helped by the chest and shoulders.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold an EZ bar on the inner angled grips over your chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and plant your feet.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
Keep the bar moving in a straight line over your lower chest.

name: Ez-Barbell Standing Wide Grip Biceps Curl
desc: A standing EZ-bar curl using the wider outer grips. The wide grip tends to bias the inner head of the biceps, while the angled bar is kinder to the wrists than a straight bar.
ins: Stand tall and hold an EZ bar underhand on the outer angled grips.
Let the bar rest at your thighs with your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest without swinging.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Face Pull (Cable)
ref: Cable Kneeling Rear Delt Row (with Rope)
desc: A cable row done kneeling, pulling a rope from a high pulley toward your face with your elbows high. Kneeling stops you from using your legs or leaning back, so the rear shoulders do the work.
ins: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the machine, holding the ends with palms facing down.
Kneel tall with your arms straight and your stomach braced.
Breathe out and pull the rope toward your forehead, driving your elbows out and back.
Spread the rope ends apart and squeeze your shoulder blades at the end.
Breathe in and straighten your arms slowly.

name: Face Pull (Dumbbell)
desc: A bent-over rear shoulder raise done with your elbows bent at about 90 degrees, leading with the elbows. The shorter lever lets you focus on the rear shoulders with a bit more weight.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward with a flat back until your upper body is almost level with the floor.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees with the dumbbells under your chest.
Breathe out and lift your elbows out to the sides and up until your upper arms are level with your back.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders for a second.
Breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Farmers Walk
desc: Walking with a heavy dumbbell in each hand at your sides. It builds grip strength, works the legs and core with every step, and trains you to carry heavy loads with good posture.
ins: Place a heavy dumbbell on each side of your feet.
Bend your knees, keep your back flat and pick them up as in a deadlift.
Stand tall with shoulders pulled back and down and arms straight at your sides.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps, keeping your stomach tight and your body still.
Breathe steadily, and set the dumbbells down carefully at the end of the distance.

name: Finger Curls
desc: A grip exercise where you let a barbell roll down to your fingertips and then close your fingers around it again. It strengthens the finger flexors and crushing grip.
ins: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs, palms up, wrists past your knees.
Hold a barbell with an underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Slowly open your fingers and let the bar roll down to your fingertips.
Close your fingers to roll the bar back into your palms.
Finish with a small wrist curl and squeeze hard.
Keep the bar under control; use a weight you can hold safely at the fingertips.

name: Flag
desc: An advanced hold, often called the human flag, where you grip a vertical pole with both hands and hold your body out sideways, level with the floor. It takes great strength in the abs, obliques and shoulders.
ins: Grip a sturdy vertical pole with both hands, the top hand above your head and the bottom hand about shoulder-width lower, both thumbs pointing up.
Lock the bottom arm straight to push into the pole and pull hard with the top arm.
Jump or kick your legs up and out to the side while tightening your abs and the side of your body facing up.
Straighten your body until it is level with the floor, legs together or spread for an easier version.
Hold while breathing steadily, then lower your legs with control. Build up with tucked knees first.

name: Flexion Leg Sit Up (bent Knee)
desc: A sit-up where you pull your bent knees in toward your chest as your upper body rises, meeting in the middle. It works the upper and lower abs together with the hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs bent and feet just off the floor, arms by your sides.
Breathe out and lift your upper body while pulling your knees in toward your chest.
Meet in a tight tuck, balancing on your hips for a moment.
Lower your back and push your feet away slowly, stopping before they rest on the floor.

name: Flexion Leg Sit Up (straight Arm)
desc: A sit-up with straight arms reaching forward past your knees as your bent legs draw in. It trains the abs and hip flexors, with the quads helping hold the legs.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet slightly off the floor, and your arms straight overhead.
Breathe out and swing your straight arms forward as you sit up and draw your knees in.
Reach your hands past your knees toward your feet at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly back to the start, arms overhead again.

name: Floor Fly (with Barbell)
desc: A fly-style movement lying on the floor using a barbell, where the arms open by rolling the bar out to the sides while the elbows are protected by the floor. It targets the chest and also involves the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, holding a light barbell over your chest with a narrow overhand grip.
Keep your elbows softly bent throughout.
Lower the bar toward your chest in an arc, letting your elbows travel out wide until your upper arms touch the floor.
Pause lightly on the floor, then squeeze your chest to bring the bar back up over your chest.
Breathe out as you lift and keep your lower back relaxed on the floor.

name: Flutter Kicks
desc: A floor exercise where you lie on your back and make small, quick up-and-down kicks with straight legs. It works the hip flexors and lower abs and keeps the glutes and thighs active.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your hands flat under or beside your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor and tighten your stomach.
Lift both heels a few centimeters off the floor.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick, alternating movements, keeping them straight.
Keep your lower back flat the whole time; raise your legs higher if it starts to arch.
Breathe steadily, and kick for a set time or count.

name: Forward Jump
desc: An explosive two-foot jump forward for distance. It builds leg power in the quads, glutes and hamstrings, and trains soft, controlled landings.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
Dip into a quarter squat while swinging your arms back.
Swing your arms forward hard and jump forward as far as you can, pushing off both feet.
Land on both feet with your knees bent and your weight in the middle of your feet.
Hold the landing for a second, then walk back or turn around for the next jump.

name: Forward Lunge
desc: The basic bodyweight forward lunge: step forward, lower, then push back to the start. It builds the glutes and quads and works balance, with the hamstrings and calves supporting.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips.
Step your right foot well out in front of you.
Breathe in and lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Keep your chest up and the front knee over the ankle.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to step back to the start.
Alternate legs or finish one side first.

name: Frankenstein Squat
desc: A front squat in which the barbell rests on the front of the shoulders while your arms stretch straight out in front without gripping it. Any lean or loss of upper-back tightness lets the bar roll, so it teaches a very upright squat for the glutes and quads.
ins: Set an empty or light bar in a rack at shoulder height.
Step under it so the bar rests on the front of your shoulders, close to your throat.
Raise your arms straight out in front at shoulder height, palms down, without holding the bar.
Step back, set your feet shoulder-width apart, breathe in and squat down while keeping your chest tall.
Breathe out and stand up, keeping the arms level so the bar stays in place.

name: Frog Crunch
desc: A crunch done with the soles of your feet pressed together and your knees dropped out to the sides, like a frog. This leg position limits help from the legs so the abs do more of the work.
ins: Lie on your back, bring the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open to the sides.
Reach your arms forward toward your feet or rest your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders up, reaching toward your feet.
Keep your knees relaxed and open; do not push through your legs.
Breathe in and lower slowly back down.

name: Frog Planche
desc: An early planche step where you balance on your hands with straight arms and your bent knees resting against the backs of your upper arms. It teaches the forward lean and balance of the planche while working the abs, shoulders, chest and triceps.
ins: Squat down and place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread.
Rest your knees against the backs of your upper arms, just above the elbows.
Keep your arms as straight as you can and lean your shoulders forward over your hands.
Lift your feet off the floor and balance, tightening your abs to pull your knees in toward your chest.
Hold while breathing steadily, then lower your feet with control.

name: Front And Back Neck Stretch
desc: A gentle neck mobility stretch where you slowly look down and then up. It eases stiffness in the back and front of the neck and the upper traps.
ins: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Slowly lower your chin toward your chest until you feel a stretch along the back of the neck.
Hold for 15 to 20 seconds while breathing slowly.
Bring your head back to neutral, then gently tilt it back to look up at the ceiling.
Stop at a comfortable stretch in the front of the neck and hold for 15 to 20 seconds.
Move slowly and never force the range.

name: Front Groin Kick
desc: A straight, upward kick with the instep or shin aimed low and in front of you. It is a simple, fast kick that works the quads, abs and hip flexors and helps build kicking speed.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your hands up and weight balanced.
Bring the rear knee up quickly toward your chest.
Snap the lower leg forward and up so the top of the foot rises in front of you.
Pull the foot back immediately by bending the knee.
Set the foot down where it started, then repeat or switch legs.

name: Front Leg Hook Kick
desc: A hook kick thrown with the front leg, where the leg extends outside the target and then snaps the heel back across it. It trains the inner and outer thighs, glutes, hamstrings and abs, and builds quick, controlled hips.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your left leg forward and your guard up.
Shift your weight onto your back foot.
Raise your front knee and extend the leg so the foot passes just outside the target.
Pull the heel back sharply across the target by bending the knee.
Recoil the leg and place it back in your stance, staying balanced.
Do your reps, then switch the lead leg.

name: Front Lever
desc: An advanced calisthenics hold where you hang from a bar with straight arms and keep your whole body horizontal, facing up. It demands very strong abs and lats, with the shoulders and forearms working hard to hold the position.
ins: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width apart and hang with straight arms.
Pull your shoulders down and back and tighten your abs and glutes so your body is rigid.
Pressing the bar down toward your hips with straight arms, lift your legs and hips up until your body is level with the floor, facing the ceiling.
Hold the line from shoulders to feet without bending your hips or arms, breathing in short, steady breaths.
Lower slowly back to a hang. If the full hold is too hard, practice with your knees tucked or one leg bent.

name: Front Lever Reps
desc: An advanced calisthenics move where you raise your straight body from a hang up to a horizontal hold under the bar. It builds huge strength in the lats, core and shoulders.
ins: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width.
Pull your shoulder blades down and lock your arms straight.
Tighten your stomach and glutes and lift your straight body until it is level with the floor.
Hold for a moment with your body horizontal, breathing steadily.
Lower slowly back to the hang and repeat; tuck your knees to make it easier.

name: Front Plank With Twist
desc: A forearm plank where you rotate your hips from side to side toward the floor. It trains the obliques and abs while the shoulders hold you steady.
ins: Set up in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Rotate your hips to the right, lowering the right hip toward the floor without touching it.
Rotate back through the middle and lower the left hip toward the floor.
Keep your shoulders still and move at a steady pace, breathing throughout.

name: Front Snap Kick
desc: A quick kick straight forward with the ball of the foot, snapping the lower leg out and back. It strengthens the quads and hip flexors and builds speed and balance on one leg.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your hands up.
Lift the kicking knee high and point it at the target.
Pull your toes back and snap the lower leg forward, hitting with the ball of the foot.
Breathe out sharply as you kick, then snap the leg straight back.
Lower the foot into your stance and repeat, switching legs after your reps.

name: Full Maltese
desc: One of the hardest strength holds in gymnastics: your body is straight and horizontal at hand level, arms spread wide and legs together. It requires extraordinary strength in the abs, shoulders and chest.
ins: Hold rings or parallettes with your arms locked straight and positioned far wider than your shoulders.
Tighten your abs, glutes and legs so your body is one rigid line.
Lean forward and lift your legs together as you lower your chest toward hand height.
Hold your body flat and level with your hands while breathing steadily.
Lower out of the hold with control. Build up through the straddle version first.

name: Full Planche
desc: One of the hardest bodyweight holds: your entire body stays straight and level above the floor, supported only by your straight arms, with your legs together. It takes elite strength in the abs, shoulders, chest and triceps.
ins: Set your hands on the floor or parallettes about shoulder-width apart, elbows locked.
Push the floor away so your upper back rounds slightly, and tighten your whole body.
Lean forward until your shoulders are well in front of your hands.
Lift your legs together behind you until your body forms one straight line parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your abs, glutes and legs to keep the line, hold while breathing steadily, then lower slowly. Build up through the tuck and straddle versions first.

name: Full Planche Push-Up
desc: An elite bodyweight push-up done in a full planche, with your whole body held horizontal off the floor and only your hands touching it. It demands huge strength in the chest, shoulders, triceps and core.
ins: Place your hands on the floor or on low parallettes about shoulder-width apart, fingers turned slightly out.
Lean your shoulders well forward past your hands and lift both feet off the floor, holding your body straight and level.
Keep your arms locked, your shoulder blades spread apart and your glutes and legs squeezed.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your straight body toward the floor, keeping it horizontal.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms without letting your hips drop.
Only attempt this after mastering easier planche holds such as the tuck and straddle planche.

name: Gironda Sternum Chin
desc: An advanced chin-up where you lean back as you rise and pull your lower chest to the bar. It hits the lats hard along with the biceps, rear shoulders and mid back.
ins: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Start pulling up while arching your upper back and leaning your head and shoulders back.
Keep pulling until your lower chest touches the bar, with your body close to horizontal at the top.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together hard at the top.
Lower yourself slowly back to a full hang.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Glute Bridge March
desc: A glute bridge held at the top while you lift one foot at a time in a slow march. Holding the hips level on one leg makes the glutes and hamstrings work harder and challenges core control.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and arms by your sides.
Breathe out and lift your hips into a bridge.
Keeping the hips high and level, lift your right foot a few centimeters off the floor, knee still bent.
Put it down, then lift the left foot.
Keep alternating slowly, breathing steadily and not letting the hips drop or twist.
Lower your hips to the floor when the set is done.

name: Glute Bridge Two Legs On Bench
desc: A glute bridge with both feet up on a bench and the shoulders on the floor. The raised feet increase the range of motion and bring in the hamstrings more along with the glutes.
ins: Lie on your back with your heels on a bench, knees bent about 90 degrees.
Rest your arms on the floor by your sides.
Brace your stomach and breathe out as you press your heels into the bench to lift your hips.
Rise until your knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe in and lower your hips slowly until they almost touch the floor.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
desc: A hamstring exercise on a glute-ham bench where you bend at the knees to pull your body up from horizontal to upright. It is one of the hardest hamstring exercises, with the glutes and lower back working to keep the body straight.
ins: Set the foot plate so your knees rest just behind the pad and lock your ankles under the rollers.
Start with your body horizontal and straight from head to knees, hands crossed on your chest.
Squeeze your glutes and breathe out as you pull with your hamstrings, bending your knees to raise your body.
Keep your hips straight; do not bend at the waist.
Stop when your body is upright, then breathe in and lower slowly back to horizontal.

name: Goblet Squat (Kettlebell)
desc: A squat holding one kettlebell by the horns close to your chest. The front load helps beginners squat deep with an upright torso while working the glutes and quads.
ins: Hold a kettlebell by both sides of the handle at chest height, elbows pointing down.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out a little.
Breathe in and sit down between your heels, keeping your chest up.
At the bottom, let your elbows brush the inside of your knees and push your knees out.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up tall.
Breathe out as you stand.

name: Gorilla Chin
desc: An advanced chin-up where you pull your knees up toward your chest as you rise, combining an upper-body pull with a hanging knee raise. It works the abs hard, with the biceps and forearms doing the pulling.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width and your legs straight.
Brace your abs and pull your chest toward the bar while drawing your knees up to your chest.
Get your chin over the bar with your knees tucked high.
Lower your body and your legs together slowly to a full hang.
Avoid swinging; keep each rep strict.

name: Groin Crunch
desc: A crunch done with the soles of your feet together and knees falling open, which takes the legs out of the movement. It works the abs, with a gentle stretch for the inner thighs.
ins: Lie on your back, put the soles of your feet together and let your knees fall open to the sides.
Place your fingertips by your ears or cross your arms on your chest.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders up off the floor, ribs toward hips.
Keep your knees relaxed and open while you crunch.
Lower slowly and repeat.

name: Hack Calf Raise
desc: A calf raise on the hack squat machine, standing with the shoulder pads on you and the balls of your feet on the platform edge. The machine guides the path so you can push the calves hard.
ins: Step into the hack squat machine facing the backrest or facing away, as your machine allows, and set your shoulders under the pads.
Place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform with heels off.
Stand up to unrack the weight and release the safety handles.
Lower your heels for a full calf stretch, keeping knees soft and still.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, and re-engage the safety handles when done.

name: Hack One Leg Calf Raise
desc: A single-leg calf raise on the hack squat machine. Training one leg at a time builds each calf evenly and adds an ankle stability challenge.
ins: Set up in the hack squat machine with your shoulders under the pads.
Place the ball of one foot on the lower edge of the platform and lift the other foot behind it.
Unrack the weight with a light load and release the safety handles.
Lower your heel for a full stretch, keeping the knee soft.
Breathe out and drive up onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, rack the weight and switch legs.

name: Hack Squat
desc: A squat done on an angled hack squat machine with your back supported by a pad. The guided path lets you train the quads and glutes hard without balancing a bar.
ins: Step into the machine with your back flat on the pad and your shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform, toes slightly out.
Release the safety handles and stand tall.
Bend your knees and lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the platform.
Keep your back and hips against the pad, then drive up through your feet.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you push; re-engage the safeties at the end.

name: Half Knee Bends
desc: Shallow, rhythmic knee bends to about half a squat, done continuously. It gets the heart rate up and warms the thighs and glutes with little strain on the knees.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms out in front for balance.
Push your hips back slightly and bend your knees to about halfway down.
Keep your heels on the floor, chest up, and knees in line with your toes.
Straighten your legs to stand back up without locking the knees.
Move in a steady rhythm, breathing in on the way down and out on the way up.

name: Half Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up where you come up only halfway, to about a 45-degree angle, with your arms reaching forward. It builds the abs with less strain than a full sit-up, with the hip flexors assisting.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, arms straight and reaching toward your knees.
Tighten your abs and tuck your chin slightly.
Breathe out and curl up until your upper body is about halfway to upright.
Pause for a second, keeping your feet flat on the floor.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly.

name: Hammer Curl (Dumbbell)
desc: A dumbbell curl with a neutral, thumbs-up grip, lifting both arms together. It strengthens the brachialis and forearms as well as the biceps.
ins: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your thighs.
Keep your elbows tucked and your wrists straight.
Breathe out and curl both dumbbells up, keeping the palms facing each other.
Squeeze at the top near shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Hamstring Stretch
desc: A standing stretch for the back of the thigh, done with one foot slightly forward and the hips folding over it. It loosens the hamstrings, with some stretch in the glutes.
ins: Stand tall and step your right foot about half a step forward.
Straighten the right leg and lift its toes so only the heel is on the floor.
Bend your left knee a little and put your hands on your hips or left thigh.
Keep your back flat and push your hips back until you feel the stretch behind the right thigh.
Breathe slowly, hold for about 30 seconds, then switch legs.

name: Hands Bike
desc: Arm cycling on an upper body ergometer, where you turn the handles with your hands like pedalling a bike. It raises your heart rate while working the chest, shoulders and arms.
ins: Sit or stand facing the machine and adjust it so the center of the handles is level with your shoulders.
Grip the handles and sit tall with your feet flat and your stomach lightly braced.
Turn the handles in smooth circles, pushing away and pulling back evenly with each arm.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down, and breathe steadily.
Start at an easy pace for a few minutes, then raise the resistance or speed for your workout.
Switch the turning direction partway through to work the muscles differently.

name: Hands Clasped Circular Toe Touch
desc: A mobility drill with the hands clasped in front: you trace a big circle from overhead down to your feet and back up. It warms up the hips, hamstrings and glutes and loosens the spine.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together in front of you.
Breathe in and lift your clasped hands overhead.
Breathe out and lean to one side, then bend forward and bring your hands down toward your toes.
Keep the circle going, sweeping across your feet to the other side.
Breathe in and rise up that side until your hands are back overhead.
Do several circles, then reverse the direction.

name: Hands Reversed Clasped Circular Toe Touch
desc: A dynamic toe-touch with the fingers interlaced behind your back, letting the arms rise overhead as you fold and circle. It stretches the hamstrings and glutes and opens the chest and the front of the shoulders.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and interlace your fingers behind your lower back.
Straighten your arms and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, letting your clasped hands lift up and over toward your head.
Draw a slow circle with your upper body and hands from one side to the other at the bottom.
Breathe in and roll back up to standing, lowering the hands behind you.

name: Handstand
desc: Balancing upside down on your hands with your body stacked in a straight line. It builds strength in the triceps and shoulders and trains balance and core control.
ins: Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers spread, about a hand's length from a wall if you are learning.
Kick one leg up, followed by the other, until your body is upside down and your legs come together.
Push the floor away so your arms are straight and your shoulders are by your ears.
Squeeze your stomach and glutes to keep your body in one straight line.
Breathe steadily and balance by pressing through your fingers, then step down one leg at a time.

name: Handstand Push-Up
desc: An advanced push-up done upside down against a wall, lowering your head toward the floor and pressing back up. It builds strong triceps and shoulders and demands core control.
ins: Place your hands on the floor about shoulder-width apart, a hand's length from a wall, and kick up into a handstand with your heels against the wall.
Tighten your stomach and glutes and keep your body straight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your head slowly toward the floor, elbows angled slightly forward.
Stop when your head lightly touches the floor or a cushion.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.
Come down one leg at a time when you finish.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
desc: A hanging leg raise where you lift your legs up in front of you from a dead hang. It is a demanding move for the lower abs and hip flexors, and grip strength helps.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your legs together.
Pull your shoulders down slightly so you are not hanging loosely.
Breathe out and raise your legs in front of you, curling your hips up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly until they are straight below you.
Stop any swing before the next rep.

name: Hanging Leg Hip Raise
desc: A hanging raise where you lift your legs and then curl your hips up toward your chest. It strengthens the abs, especially the lower part, with the hip flexors and lower back assisting.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away and your arms straight.
Tighten your abs and settle any swinging before you begin.
Breathe out and raise your knees until your thighs are level with the floor.
Continue by tilting your hips up so your knees travel toward your chest.
Lower your legs slowly back to a straight hang without swinging.

name: Hanging Oblique Knee Raise
desc: A hanging knee raise where you bring your knees up and across toward one shoulder. It works the obliques along with the rest of the abs and demands solid grip strength.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Draw your shoulders slightly down and keep your legs still so you are not swinging.
Breathe out and lift your knees up and to one side, rotating your hips so your knees aim at one shoulder.
Lower your legs slowly back to the center under control.
Raise to the other side on the next rep, alternating sides.

name: Hanging Pike
desc: An advanced hanging exercise where you lift straight legs all the way up until your feet reach the bar. It requires very strong abs and hip flexors, plus stable shoulders.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your legs straight and together.
Brace your abs and press the bar down slightly so your shoulders engage.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs up, folding at the hips until your feet touch or near the bar.
Lower your legs slowly back down under full control.
Keep your knees straight throughout; bend them slightly only if your hamstrings are tight.

name: Hanging Straight Leg Hip Raise
desc: A hanging raise where you lift straight legs to horizontal and then curl your hips up so your pelvis rolls toward your chest. It emphasizes the lower abs over the hip flexors.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with your legs straight and together.
Raise your straight legs until they are about level with your hips.
From there, breathe out and curl your pelvis up, lifting your hips and pushing your feet a little higher.
Uncurl your hips first, then lower your legs slowly to the start.

name: Hanging Straight Leg Raise
desc: A strict hanging leg raise with your knees locked straight, lifting until your legs are level with the floor. It works the lower abs and hip flexors.
ins: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, legs straight and together.
Brace your abs and keep your knees locked.
Breathe out and raise your legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly without letting your body swing.

name: Hanging Straight Twisting Leg Hip Raise
desc: A hanging straight leg raise that finishes with a twist, lifting your legs up toward one side and then the other. It trains the obliques along with the lower abs and hip flexors.
ins: Hang from a pull-up bar with your legs straight and together.
Brace your abs to stop any swinging.
Breathe out and raise your straight legs up and toward your right side, rotating your hips.
Lower slowly back to the center.
Repeat toward your left side and keep alternating.

name: Heel Push Kick
desc: A front kick that pushes the target away with the flat of the heel instead of snapping. It builds the quads and glutes and teaches you to drive power forward from the hips.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your hands up.
Lift your kicking knee up to chest height.
Pull your toes back so the heel leads.
Drive the heel straight forward, pushing your hips into the kick.
Breathe out as you push, then pull the knee back and place the foot down.
Repeat, then switch legs.

name: Hex-press
desc: A flat-bench dumbbell press with the two dumbbells pressed together over your chest. Squeezing them together keeps the elbows in and makes the triceps and inner chest work hard.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold two dumbbells over your chest with palms facing each other, touching end to end along their sides.
Squeeze the dumbbells together firmly.
Lower them to your mid-chest, keeping them in contact and your elbows close to your body.
Breathe out and press them back up until your arms are straight.
Keep the squeeze on for the whole set.

name: High Knee Against Wall
desc: Fast high-knee running in place while leaning into a wall with the hands. The wall support lets you focus on driving the knees hard and fast.
ins: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it at chest height.
Walk your feet back slightly so your body leans forward in a straight line.
Drive your right knee up toward your chest, then quickly switch to the left.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep alternating as fast as you can.
Keep your core tight, your back straight, and breathe quickly but steadily.

name: Hip Raise (bent Knee)
desc: A bent-knee hip raise from the floor where you tilt your pelvis and lift your hips by tightening your abs and glutes. It trains the lower abs with the glutes and hamstrings helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat near your hips and arms by your sides.
Flatten your lower back into the floor by tightening your abs.
Breathe out and lift your hips until your body makes a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Keep your ribs down; do not arch your lower back at the top.
Lower your hips slowly back to the floor.

name: Hip Thrust (Barbell)
desc: A hip bridge done on the floor with a barbell resting across your hips. It loads the glutes directly, with the hamstrings helping, and is easy to set up without a bench.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and roll a padded barbell up over your hips.
Lie back, bend your knees and plant your feet flat, hip-width apart, close to your glutes.
Hold the bar with both hands to keep it from rolling.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Pause and squeeze your glutes, then lower your hips slowly to the floor.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Hug Knees To Chest
desc: A gentle stretch lying on your back and hugging both knees into your chest. It loosens the glutes and lower back and is a good warm-up or cool-down.
ins: Lie on your back on a mat with your legs straight.
Bend both knees and bring them up toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins or hold behind your knees.
Pull your knees gently closer to your chest while keeping your head and shoulders relaxed on the mat.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and letting your lower back sink into the floor.
Release your legs slowly back to the mat.

name: Hyght Dumbbell Fly
desc: A dumbbell fly on a flat bench in which the arms open in a wide arc and come back together over the chest. It isolates the chest muscles, with the front shoulders assisting.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand held over your chest, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows slightly and keep that angle for the whole set.
Breathe in and open your arms out to the sides until the dumbbells are about level with the bench.
Breathe out and bring the dumbbells back up in a wide arc as if hugging a large barrel.
Stop just before the dumbbells touch to keep tension on your chest.

name: Hyperextension (on Bench)
desc: A back extension done lying face down on a flat bench with your upper body off the end. It strengthens the lower back muscles along the spine, with the glutes and hamstrings helping.
ins: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the end and your upper body hanging off.
Have a partner hold your ankles, or hook your feet under something stable.
Cross your arms over your chest and let your upper body lower toward the floor.
Lift your upper body until it is in line with your legs, squeezing your glutes.
Lower slowly back down without jerking.
Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.

name: Impossible Dips
desc: An advanced bar exercise in which you lower yourself from straight arms until your forearms rest on the parallel bars, then press back up. It builds very strong triceps and elbow control.
ins: Support yourself on parallel bars with your arms straight and your body upright.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself slowly, letting your elbows move back until your forearms lie along the bars.
Pause briefly with your weight on your forearms and your stomach tight.
Breathe out and press your palms into the bars to straighten your elbows and lift back to straight arms.
Lean slightly forward as you press to keep your balance over your hands.

name: Inchworm
desc: A full-body mobility drill where you walk your hands out from standing into a plank and then walk your feet back in. It warms up the core and shoulders and stretches the hamstrings.
ins: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge forward and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees only as much as you need.
Walk your hands forward one at a time until you reach a high plank with your body straight.
Hold the plank briefly with your abs tight and hips level.
Keeping your legs as straight as you can, walk your feet in toward your hands, then roll up to standing.

name: Inchworm (Traveling)
desc: A traveling version of the inchworm: you walk your hands out to a plank and your feet up to your hands repeatedly, moving forward across the floor. It warms up the core and shoulders and stretches the hamstrings.
ins: Stand at one end of a clear space with your feet hip-width apart.
Fold forward, place your hands on the floor and walk them out until you reach a high plank.
Hold the plank for a moment with your abs tight and your hips level.
With your legs as straight as possible, take small steps to walk your feet up toward your hands.
Without standing up, walk your hands out again and keep traveling forward for the set distance.

name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
desc: A barbell press on a bench angled upward, which shifts emphasis to the upper chest and front shoulders. It is a staple for building a fuller upper chest.
ins: Set the bench to about 30 to 45 degrees and sit back with your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, squeeze your shoulder blades back and unrack it.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just under the collarbone, with control.
Press the bar straight up until your arms are extended above your shoulders.
Breathe in on the way down, breathe out as you press, and keep your back on the pad.

name: Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell)
desc: A dumbbell press on a bench angled upward, focused on the upper chest. Each arm moves independently, which helps even out strength between sides.
ins: Set an incline bench to 30 to 45 degrees, sit back and kick the dumbbells up to the sides of your upper chest.
Press them up until your arms are straight above your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until they are level with your upper chest.
Drive them back up without clanging them together at the top.
Keep your back on the pad and breathe out on each press.

name: Incline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
desc: An incline bench press in a Smith machine that targets the upper chest and front shoulders. The guided bar suits beginners and lifters training alone.
ins: Set an incline bench at 30 to 45 degrees under the Smith bar so the bar lines up with your upper chest.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unhook it.
Lower the bar slowly to just below your collarbone.
Press it straight up until your arms are extended.
Breathe out as you press and keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench.

name: Incline Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
desc: A dumbbell fly on an incline bench that isolates the upper chest. The arms open wide with a fixed elbow bend, then squeeze back together.
ins: Lie on an incline bench and hold the dumbbells above your upper chest, palms facing each other.
Set a slight bend in your elbows and lock that angle in.
Let the dumbbells travel apart in a wide arc until your chest feels stretched.
Bring them back together over your upper chest by squeezing your pecs.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you lift; avoid going so deep that your shoulders hurt.

name: Incline Chest Press (Machine)
desc: A seated incline chest press on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine. The fixed path makes it easy to learn while it works the upper chest, shoulders and triceps.
ins: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Grip the handles, keep your feet flat and your shoulder blades pulled back.
Breathe out and press the handles up and forward until your arms are almost straight.
Breathe in and let the handles come back slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
Do not let the weight stack touch down between reps.

name: Incline Close-Grip Push-Up
desc: A close-grip push-up with your hands on a raised surface such as a bench. The incline makes it easier than a floor push-up while still targeting the triceps.
ins: Place your hands shoulder-width apart or a little narrower on the edge of a bench or sturdy box.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Breathe in and lower your chest to the edge, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your hips in line; use a higher surface to make it easier.

name: Incline Leg Hip Raise (leg Straight)
desc: A leg raise on an incline bench with your head at the high end, where straight legs lift and your hips curl up off the pad. It focuses on the lower abs with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on an incline bench with your head at the top and hold the bench behind your head.
Keep your legs straight and together, just off the pad.
Breathe out and raise your legs until they point up, then curl your hips off the bench.
Lower your hips first, then your legs, slowly.
Stop before your legs rest on the bench so your abs stay working.

name: Incline Push Up Depth Jump
desc: An explosive push-up drill where you push off a raised surface, drop your hands to the floor, and absorb the landing before pushing back up. It develops power in the chest, triceps and shoulders.
ins: Set up in a push-up position with your hands on a low box or step and your body straight.
Push explosively off the box so your hands leave it and move out to land on the floor on either side.
Land with soft elbows and let your chest sink toward the floor to absorb the impact.
Immediately push hard off the floor to bring your hands back up onto the box.
Keep your stomach braced so your hips stay in line, and breathe out sharply on each push.

name: Incline Push-Up
desc: A push-up with your hands on a bench or box so your body is angled upward, making it easier than a floor push-up. It is a good way for beginners to build chest and triceps strength with proper form.
ins: Place your hands on the edge of a sturdy bench a little wider than your shoulders and walk your feet back.
Make a straight line from head to heels and tighten your stomach.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest to the edge of the bench.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
Breathe in going down and out going up; use a lower surface as you get stronger.

name: Incline Push-Up (on Box)
desc: A push-up with your hands on a box or bench so your body is angled upward. It is easier than a floor push-up and is a good way to build chest, shoulder and triceps strength.
ins: Place your hands on the edge of a stable box or bench, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body is straight from head to heels.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your chest to the edge of the box.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees and your stomach tight.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Use a lower box as you get stronger.

name: Incline Reverse Grip Push-Up
desc: An incline push-up with the hands turned so the fingers point back toward your feet. The reverse grip keeps the elbows tucked and puts extra work on the lower chest and triceps.
ins: Place your hands on a bench about shoulder-width apart with your fingers pointing toward your feet.
Walk your feet back into a straight plank with your body angled up.
Lower your chest toward the bench, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Press back up to straight arms.
Exhale as you press and keep your wrists comfortable; widen the hands slightly if they strain.

name: Incline Row (Dumbbell)
desc: A dumbbell row done lying face down on an incline bench, so the chest is supported and you can focus only on pulling. It works the upper back, with the biceps and rear shoulders helping.
ins: Set a bench to a low incline and lie face down with your chest on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging straight down.
Row both dumbbells up, bringing your elbows back past your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower slowly to straight arms, keeping your chest on the bench.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Incline Scapula Push Up
desc: A small-range push-up done with the hands on a raised surface, where the arms stay straight and only the shoulder blades move. It trains the serratus muscles along the ribs that keep the shoulder blades stable.
ins: Place your hands on a bench or box at shoulder-width and walk your feet back into an inclined plank with straight arms.
Keep your body in a straight line and your elbows locked but not hyperextended.
Breathe in and let your chest sink between your shoulders so your shoulder blades come together.
Breathe out and push the bench away, spreading your shoulder blades apart and rounding your upper back slightly.
Move slowly and keep your arms straight throughout.

name: Incline Twisting Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up on a slanted bench with a twist at the top, bringing one shoulder toward the opposite knee. It works the abs and the obliques.
ins: Lie on a slanted sit-up bench with your feet hooked under the rollers and your head at the low end.
Cross your arms on your chest or put your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and sit up, turning as you rise so your right shoulder heads toward your left knee.
Turn back to center and lower slowly.
Alternate the direction of the twist each rep.

name: Intermediate Hip Flexor And Quad Stretch
desc: A deeper half-kneeling stretch that uses a rope or strap around the back foot to pull the heel toward the glutes. It stretches the hip flexors and quads together, so it suits people who already have some flexibility.
ins: Loop a rope or strap around your right ankle and kneel on your right knee on a soft surface, left foot flat in front.
Hold the rope over your right shoulder with your right hand.
Tuck your pelvis under and squeeze your right glute to start the stretch at the front of the hip.
Gently pull the rope to bring your right heel toward your glutes.
Keep your chest up and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Release the rope slowly, then switch sides.

name: Inverse Leg Curl (bench Support)
desc: A body-weight hamstring curl where you anchor your feet under a bench and lower your body forward from your knees, then pull yourself back up. It is a demanding hamstring exercise that also works the glutes and calves.
ins: Kneel on a pad with your heels hooked under a secure bench or have the bench held steady.
Keep your body straight from knees to head, with your hips pushed forward and glutes squeezed.
Slowly lean forward from the knees, resisting with your hamstrings as long as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands when you can no longer control the descent.
Push lightly off the floor and pull with your hamstrings to return to upright kneeling.
Breathe out as you pull back up; keep your hips from bending throughout.

name: Inverse Leg Curl (on Pull-Up Cable Machine)
desc: A Nordic-style hamstring curl done kneeling on the seat of a pull-up or pulldown station with the ankles locked under the leg pad. You lower your body forward with control, which builds very strong hamstrings and works the glutes and calves.
ins: Kneel on the seat of the station facing away from the machine, with your ankles hooked under the leg pad.
Keep a straight line from your knees to your head and cross your arms or hold them ready in front.
Breathe in and slowly lean forward from the knees, fighting the fall with your hamstrings.
Lower as far as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands if needed.
Pull with your hamstrings, using a small push from the hands if needed, to return upright while breathing out.

name: Inverted Row
desc: A bodyweight row where you hang under a bar with your body straight and pull your chest up to it. It strengthens the upper back and is a good step toward pull-ups, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Set a bar at about hip height and lie underneath it.
Grab the bar overhand, slightly wider than your shoulders, with straight arms.
Straighten your legs and lift your hips so your body is one straight line resting on your heels.
Pull your chest to the bar, driving your elbows back.
Lower slowly to straight arms without letting your hips sag.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Inverted Row (Bent Knees, Shoulder Blade Squeeze)
desc: An easier inverted row done with the knees bent and feet flat, which takes some body weight off the arms. It trains the upper back, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Set a bar about waist height in a rack or smith machine.
Lie underneath and grab the bar with an overhand grip a bit wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees and plant your feet flat, lifting your hips so your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower yourself slowly until your arms are straight.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way down.

name: Inverted Row Bent Knees
desc: An easier inverted row with the knees bent and feet on the floor. It trains the upper back and biceps and prepares you for harder rowing and pull-up work.
ins: Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at about waist height and lie under it.
Grip the bar overhand slightly wider than your shoulders.
Bend your knees, plant your feet and lift your hips so your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Breathe out and pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly to straight arms without letting your hips sag.

name: Inverted Row On Bench
desc: A beginner inverted row done lying under a sturdy bench and pulling your chest up to it. It builds the upper back using your own body weight.
ins: Lie on your back under a solid flat bench that will not tip.
Grip the long edges of the bench with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees, feet flat, and lift your hips so your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Breathe out and pull your chest up toward the bench, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Inverted Row With Straps
desc: An inverted row using suspension straps, which lets your hands turn freely and adds a balance challenge. It builds the upper back, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Hang the straps from a high anchor and hold one handle in each hand.
Walk your feet forward and lean back until your arms are straight and your body is at an angle.
Brace your stomach and glutes so your body stays straight from head to heels.
Pull your chest up to your hands, turning your palms in and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight; walk your feet further forward to make it harder.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Iron Cross Stretch
desc: A lying stretch where you keep your arms out wide like a cross and swing one straight leg over your body to the opposite side. It stretches the glutes, outer hip and lower back and adds gentle spinal rotation.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms stretched out to the sides at shoulder height.
Raise one straight leg toward the ceiling.
Lower that leg across your body toward the opposite hand, letting your hips turn.
Keep both shoulders on the floor and go only as far as is comfortable.
Hold briefly while breathing out, then bring the leg back up and down to the start.
Repeat with the other leg, alternating sides.

name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press (Machine)
desc: A seated chest press on a plate-loaded or selectorised machine that guides the handles along a fixed path. It is a simple, safe way for beginners to build the chest, triceps and front shoulders.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest, then sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing down and your elbows slightly below shoulder height.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Let them come back slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest, without letting the weight stack touch down.
Breathe out as you push and in as you return.

name: Isometric Chest Squeeze
desc: A no-equipment exercise where you press your palms together in front of your chest and hold the squeeze. It activates the chest without any movement and is easy to do anywhere.
ins: Stand or sit tall and bring your palms together in front of your chest, elbows out to the sides.
Keep your shoulders down and your wrists straight.
Press your palms into each other as hard as you can, feeling your chest tighten.
Hold the squeeze for 10 to 20 seconds while breathing steadily; do not hold your breath.
Relax for a few seconds, then repeat.

name: Isometric Wipers
desc: A challenging static push-up drill where you hold a wide push-up and slowly shift your weight from one hand to the other like a windscreen wiper. It builds strength and endurance in the chest, triceps, shoulders and core.
ins: Start in a push-up position with your hands set much wider than your shoulders.
Lower halfway down and hold that height.
Shift your body toward one hand, bending that elbow while the other arm straightens.
Slide slowly across to the other hand without rising up, then back again.
Keep your hips level and your stomach tight, and breathe steadily throughout.

name: Jack Burpee
desc: A burpee that swaps the vertical jump for a jumping jack at the top. It raises your heart rate fast and works the legs, shoulders, arms and core.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides.
Squat down, place your hands on the floor and jump your feet back into a plank.
Keep your body in a straight line, then jump your feet back in toward your hands.
Stand up and go straight into one jumping jack, opening your feet and swinging your arms overhead.
Bring your feet and arms back together and drop into the next rep.
Land softly and breathe steadily; slow down if your plank starts to sag.

name: Jack Jump
desc: The classic jumping jack: jump the feet out while raising the arms overhead, then jump back. It is a full-body warm-up and cardio move.
ins: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet out a little wider than your shoulders while swinging your arms out and up overhead.
Land lightly on the balls of your feet with soft knees.
Jump your feet back together and lower your arms to your sides.
Keep a quick, steady rhythm and breathe evenly throughout.

name: Jackknife Sit Up
desc: A sit-up where your straight arms and straight legs lift at the same time and meet over your hips, folding your body like a pocket knife. It works the whole abdominal wall and the hip flexors.
ins: Lie flat with your legs straight and your arms stretched overhead.
Brace your abs and press your lower back into the floor.
Breathe out and lift your arms and legs together, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Balance on your hips for a moment at the top.
Lower your arms and legs slowly at the same time.

name: Janda Sit-Up
desc: A slow sit-up where you actively pull your heels down into the floor, which tightens the hamstrings and reduces how much the hip flexors can help. It isolates the abs and is harder than it looks.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat; a partner can hold the backs of your ankles, or hook your heels against a fixed low support.
Pull your heels down and back into the floor and keep that pressure the whole rep.
Cross your arms on your chest, breathe out and curl up very slowly.
Rise only as far as you can while keeping your heels pressing down.
Lower slowly back to the floor.

name: Jump Box Over
desc: A plyometric drill where you jump up onto a box and then hop down the far side, moving over it. It builds leg power and coordination, mainly in the quads, with the glutes, hamstrings, calves and abs helping.
ins: Stand next to a low, sturdy box with feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Jump up onto the box, landing softly with both feet flat and knees bent.
Step or hop down on the far side, landing gently.
Turn around and repeat in the other direction, breathing out on each jump.

name: Jump Rope
desc: Jumping rope with small, quick hops as the rope passes under the feet. It is efficient cardio that also builds calf strength, coordination and footwork.
ins: Pick a rope length where the handles reach your armpits when you stand on its middle.
Hold the handles at hip height with elbows close to your sides.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your whole arms.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep your knees slightly bent, your body tall, and your breathing relaxed.
Start with short rounds and rest between them as needed.

name: Jump Squat
desc: A squat followed by a powerful jump, using an arm swing to help drive you upward. It builds explosive leg power in the glutes, quads and calves and works as a conditioning exercise.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Squat down while swinging your arms back behind you.
Swing your arms forward and up as you jump as high as you can.
Land softly with bent knees, hips back and knees in line with your toes.
Reset your stance and repeat.
Breathe out as you jump and in as you land and lower.

name: Jump Squat (Hands on Hips)
desc: A continuous body-weight jump squat with the arms kept on the hips or behind the head, so the legs produce all the power. It develops explosive strength in the glutes, quads and calves and raises the heart rate.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place your hands on your hips.
Squat down until your thighs are close to parallel, chest up.
Jump straight up as high as you can, using only your legs.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, then let your heels settle and bend your knees.
Flow straight into the next squat and jump without pausing.
Breathe out on each jump and keep a steady rhythm.

name: Kettlebell Advanced Windmill
desc: A deep kettlebell windmill where you hold a bell overhead and fold sideways until your free hand reaches the floor. It builds strong, flexible obliques and very stable shoulders.
ins: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and turn both feet about 45 degrees away from that arm.
Lock your eyes on the kettlebell and keep the arm straight and vertical.
Push your hips toward the kettlebell side and fold sideways, sliding your free hand down the inside of your front leg to the floor.
Keep the overhead arm stacked over your shoulder as you go down.
Drive back up to standing by squeezing your hips and side, then finish your reps and switch arms.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Hang Clean
desc: An explosive kettlebell drill where you pull the bell from just above the knee into the rack position at your shoulder, switching hands each rep. It builds grip, forearms, shoulders and hip power.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand at arm's length in front of your thigh.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back so the bell lowers to just above your knee.
Drive your hips forward hard and let the bell rise close to your body.
Pull your elbow down and rotate your hand so the bell settles softly against your forearm at shoulder height.
Lower the bell back to the hang, switch hands at the bottom, and repeat on the other side.
Breathe out on each drive and keep your core tight.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Press
desc: A standing kettlebell press alternating arms. The offset weight of the kettlebell sitting on your forearm challenges shoulder stability and your core.
ins: Clean two kettlebells to the rack position so they rest on the outside of your forearms at shoulder height.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press one kettlebell straight up until your arm is straight, wrist firm.
Lower it back to the rack under control.
Press the other arm and keep alternating.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Press On Floor
desc: A floor press with a kettlebell in each hand, pressing one arm at a time. The floor limits the range to protect the shoulders while the chest and triceps do the work.
ins: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, holding a kettlebell in each hand with your upper arms resting on the floor.
Press one kettlebell straight up until that arm is fully extended.
Lower it back down until your elbow touches the floor.
Press the other kettlebell up, and keep alternating sides.
Keep your wrists straight with the bell resting on the back of your forearm, and breathe out on each press.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Renegade Row
desc: An advanced row done from a push-up position on two kettlebells, rowing one at a time while the other arm holds you up. It works the upper back while the core and shoulders fight to keep the body from twisting.
ins: Place two kettlebells shoulder-width apart and hold their handles in a push-up position.
Spread your feet wider than hip-width for balance and brace your stomach and glutes.
Push one hand into the floor and row the other kettlebell up to your ribs.
Keep your hips level and avoid turning your body toward the lifting side.
Set the kettlebell down with control and row with the other arm.
Breathe out on each row and in as you set it down.

name: Kettlebell Alternating Row
desc: A bent-over row holding a kettlebell in each hand and pulling them up one at a time. It trains the upper back on each side, with the biceps and forearms helping and the lower back holding the position.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in each hand and hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back.
Let both kettlebells hang under your shoulders.
Row one kettlebell to your ribs while the other stays down.
Lower it slowly, then row the other side.
Keep your torso still and your hips level the whole time.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Kettlebell Arnold Press
desc: An Arnold press with kettlebells, rotating the arms from palms facing you to palms facing forward as you press. It works all parts of the shoulder through a long range.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in each hand in front of your shoulders, palms facing you and elbows in front.
Stand tall with your stomach braced.
Breathe out and press up while turning your palms forward and opening your elbows out.
Finish with your arms straight overhead.
Breathe in and reverse the turn as you lower to the start.

name: Kettlebell Bent Press
desc: An old-school strength lift where you press a kettlebell overhead by bending your body down and away from it rather than pushing it up with the arm alone. It trains the obliques, shoulders and triceps together.
ins: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder and turn your feet about 45 degrees away from that side.
Rest the elbow against your side so the bell sits on your forearm.
Lean your body sideways and forward away from the bell, letting your arm straighten under it as your torso goes down.
Once your arm is locked straight, keep your eyes on the bell and stand back up under it.
Lower the bell to your shoulder with control, finish your reps, then switch sides.

name: Kettlebell Bottoms Up Clean From The Hang Position
desc: An advanced kettlebell clean from a hang where the bell finishes upside down, bottom up, in front of your shoulder. Balancing it trains grip, the biceps and shoulder stability.
ins: Stand with a kettlebell in one hand hanging between your legs, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge slightly at the hips with a flat back to load the hang position.
Drive your hips forward and pull the bell up close to your body.
Squeeze the handle hard and catch the bell upside down in front of your shoulder, elbow tucked and forearm vertical.
Hold it steady for a moment, then lower it back to the hang with control; switch arms after the set.

name: Kettlebell Double Alternating Hang Clean
desc: A clean with two kettlebells where you bring one bell up to the rack position at a time while the other hangs. It builds the arms, grip and shoulders while the hips drive the movement.
ins: Stand with a kettlebell in each hand hanging in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge slightly at the hips with a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and pull one bell up close to your body, rotating your hand so the bell rests on the back of your forearm at your shoulder.
Keep the other bell hanging still.
Lower the racked bell back to the hang with control, then clean the other one.
Keep alternating sides, breathing out on each drive.

name: Kettlebell Double Jerk
desc: An explosive lift that drives two kettlebells overhead using a double knee dip, finishing in a locked-out stand. It builds shoulder power, triceps strength and full-body timing.
ins: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, feet hip-width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly, keeping your upper body upright.
Drive up hard through your legs to launch the kettlebells upward.
As they rise, dip under them a second time to lock your arms out.
Stand up fully with the kettlebells overhead, then lower them to the rack with control.

name: Kettlebell Double Push Press
desc: An overhead press with two kettlebells that uses a short knee dip and leg drive to help start the press. It lets you move more weight than a strict press and builds shoulder and triceps strength.
ins: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your stomach and dip a few centimeters by bending your knees, chest up.
Drive through your legs and use that push to press the kettlebells overhead.
Finish with your arms straight and legs straight.
Lower the kettlebells to the rack under control and reset.

name: Kettlebell Double Snatch
desc: An advanced explosive lift that swings two kettlebells from between your legs straight to overhead in one movement. It builds shoulder power, grip and hip drive.
ins: Stand with feet a little wider than hip-width with two kettlebells on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and swing both kettlebells back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward and pull the kettlebells up close to your body.
Punch your hands up so the kettlebells turn over softly onto your forearms as your arms lock overhead.
Lower them back down in front of you and into the next swing with control.

name: Kettlebell Double Windmill
desc: A windmill using two kettlebells, one held overhead and one hanging in the low hand. It loads the obliques and abs while challenging shoulder stability and stretching the hamstrings.
ins: Hold one kettlebell locked out overhead and another hanging in your other hand.
Turn your feet about 45 degrees away from the overhead arm.
Watch the top bell, push your hips toward it, and fold sideways to lower the bottom bell along the inside of your front leg.
Go as low as you can with a long spine and a straight overhead arm.
Stand back up with control, finish your reps, then switch the bells to the other side.

name: Kettlebell Extended Range One Arm Press On Floor
desc: A one-arm kettlebell floor press with an extra reach at the top, where the shoulder lifts off the floor to add range. It strengthens the chest and triceps and also trains the muscles that move the shoulder blade.
ins: Lie on the floor with knees bent and hold one kettlebell at your chest, upper arm on the floor.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your elbow is locked.
At the top, reach the kettlebell further toward the ceiling so your shoulder lifts slightly off the floor.
Let the shoulder settle back down, then lower the kettlebell until your elbow touches the floor.
Finish the set, switch arms, and breathe out as you press and reach.

name: Kettlebell Figure 8
desc: A kettlebell drill where you pass the bell between your legs in a figure-eight pattern while holding a half squat. It trains the abs to stabilize while the shoulders and forearms handle the passes.
ins: Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders, sit your hips back into a half squat and keep your back flat.
Hold a kettlebell in your right hand in front of you.
Pass the bell back between your legs to your left hand, which reaches around from behind your left leg.
Bring it forward around the left leg, then pass it back through the middle to your right hand behind the right leg.
Keep tracing the figure eight smoothly, chest up and abs braced.

name: Kettlebell Front Squat
desc: A front squat holding one or two kettlebells in the rack position at your chest. It trains the glutes and quads while keeping your torso upright and your core working.
ins: Clean the kettlebells to your chest so each rests on the back of your forearm, wrists straight and elbows tucked in.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Breathe in, brace and squat down between your knees, keeping your chest tall.
Go as deep as you can while your heels stay down and your back stays flat.
Drive up through your feet to standing.
Breathe out at the top and keep the bells close to your body.

name: Kettlebell Hang Clean
desc: A kettlebell clean that starts from a hanging position just above the knees, bringing the bell to the rack position at your chest. It develops hip power in the hamstrings and glutes and teaches a smooth catch.
ins: Stand with the kettlebell in one hand, arm straight, and hinge so the bell hangs just above your knees.
Keep your back flat and your shoulder pulled down.
Drive your hips forward quickly so the bell floats up close to your body.
As it rises, keep your elbow close and rotate your hand around the handle so the bell lands softly on the back of your forearm.
Finish standing tall with the bell at your chest, wrist straight, then let it drop back to the hang and hinge.
Breathe out as your hips snap forward; switch hands after your set.

name: Kettlebell Lunge Pass Through
desc: A lunge in which you pass a kettlebell under your front thigh from one hand to the other on every rep. It works the glutes and quads while adding a coordination and core challenge.
ins: Stand tall holding a kettlebell in one hand at your side.
Step forward into a lunge, lowering until your back knee is just above the floor.
At the bottom, pass the kettlebell under your front thigh to your other hand.
Push through the front heel and step back to standing.
Lunge with the other leg and pass the bell back under that thigh.
Keep your chest up and your core tight, breathing out as you rise.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Clean And Jerk
desc: A two-part lift with one kettlebell: clean it from between your legs to your shoulder, then jerk it overhead with a quick double dip. It builds power in the shoulders, hips and core.
ins: Stand over a kettlebell, hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip it with one hand.
Swing it back between your legs, then snap your hips forward to bring it up into the rack at your shoulder.
Dip slightly at the knees and drive up hard to launch the kettlebell upward.
Drop under it with a second small dip to lock your arm out, then stand tall.
Lower it to the rack and then back between your legs, and switch hands after your set.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Floor Press
desc: A one-arm press with a kettlebell done lying on the floor. The floor limits how far the elbow drops, so it is shoulder-friendly while still working the chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand with the handle in your palm and the bell resting on the back of your forearm.
Rest your upper arm on the floor at about 45 degrees from your body.
Breathe out and press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is locked out over your shoulder.
Keep your wrist straight and your knuckles pointing to the ceiling.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your upper arm touches the floor lightly.
Finish the set, then switch arms.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Jerk
desc: A one-arm kettlebell jerk from the rack position using two quick knee dips. It trains explosive shoulder strength and teaches you to get under the weight fast.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at one shoulder, feet hip-width apart.
Dip slightly by bending your knees, keeping your chest up.
Drive up through your legs to launch the kettlebell.
Bend your knees again to drop under it and lock your arm out overhead.
Stand tall, then lower the kettlebell back to the rack and switch arms after your set.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Military Press To The Side
desc: A one-arm kettlebell press where you lean your upper body slightly away from the working arm as it rises. It works the shoulder through a strong pressing angle and trains your side abs.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at one shoulder and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your stomach and keep your hips square.
Breathe out and press the kettlebell up while bending your upper body a little to the opposite side.
Finish with your arm straight and your eyes on the kettlebell.
Breathe in, straighten up as you lower it to the rack, and switch sides after your set.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Push Press
desc: A one-arm overhead press that uses a short knee dip and leg drive to start the kettlebell moving. It builds shoulder and triceps strength with help from the legs.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in the rack position at one shoulder, feet hip-width apart.
Brace your stomach and dip a little at the knees, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your legs and press the kettlebell overhead in one smooth movement.
Finish with your arm and legs straight.
Lower the kettlebell to the rack under control, and switch sides after your set.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Row
desc: A one-arm row with a kettlebell, usually with the free hand resting on a bench or knee. It builds the upper back and lats, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Stand in a split stance and rest your free hand on a bench or your front thigh.
Hold the kettlebell in your other hand, arm hanging straight below your shoulder.
Keep your back flat and your stomach braced.
Row the kettlebell to your hip, elbow brushing past your side.
Lower slowly to a full stretch, then switch sides after your set.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way down.

name: Kettlebell One Arm Snatch
