desc: An explosive one-arm lift that takes a kettlebell from a swing between your legs straight to overhead. It develops shoulder power, grip and strong hip drive.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hinge at the hips and grip a kettlebell on the floor with one hand.
Swing it back between your legs with a flat back.
Snap your hips forward and pull the kettlebell up close to your body.
Punch your hand up so the kettlebell turns over softly onto your forearm as your arm locks overhead.
Bring it back down in front of you into the next swing, and switch hands after your set.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Carry
desc: A loaded walk holding a kettlebell locked out overhead. It strengthens shoulder stability, the upper back and the core, and improves overhead posture.
ins: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder and press it overhead until your arm is straight, with the bell resting on the back of your forearm.
Stand tall with your ribs down, stomach braced and wrist straight.
Walk forward with slow, even steps, keeping the kettlebell stacked over your shoulder.
Breathe steadily and keep your hips level.
After the set distance, lower the kettlebell with control and switch arms.

name: Kettlebell Pirate Supper Legs
desc: A kettlebell drill, often called pirate ships, where you hold one kettlebell with both hands and swing it in an arc from side to side at shoulder height. It works the front and side shoulders and your grip while the core keeps you steady.
ins: Stand with feet wider than shoulder width and hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands, arms straight down in front of you.
Brace your stomach and keep your knees slightly bent.
Swing the kettlebell up in an arc to one side until it reaches about head height, letting your body turn a little.
Let it swing back down past your hips and up to the other side.
Keep your arms straight and breathe steadily as you continue side to side.

name: Kettlebell Pistol Squat
desc: A full single-leg squat with the other leg held straight out in front, holding a kettlebell at your chest for counterbalance. It demands strength, balance and mobility in the glutes, quads and ankles.
ins: Hold a kettlebell by the horns at your chest and stand on one leg.
Lift the other leg straight out in front of you, just off the floor.
Push the kettlebell slightly forward and slowly squat down on the standing leg as low as you can control.
Keep your heel flat, your knee over your toes and the free leg off the floor.
Drive through the standing foot to rise back up, staying balanced.
Breathe out as you stand; use a box to limit depth until you can do the full range.

name: Kettlebell Plyo Push-Up
desc: An explosive push-up that moves sideways over a kettlebell, with one hand on the bell and the other on the floor. It builds upper-body power and coordination in the chest, triceps, shoulders and core.
ins: Set a kettlebell on the floor and get into a push-up position with one hand on its handle and the other on the floor.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight.
Push up explosively so both hands leave their spots, and move sideways over the kettlebell.
Land with the opposite hand on the handle and the other on the floor, absorbing the landing with bent elbows.
Go straight into the next rep in the other direction, breathing out on each push.

name: Kettlebell Seated Press
desc: A one-arm kettlebell press done seated on a bench. Sitting takes the legs out, so the shoulder has to press strictly and the core keeps you upright.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with feet flat and hold a kettlebell in the rack position at one shoulder.
Brace your stomach and keep your back straight.
Breathe out and press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is straight.
Keep your body from leaning to the side.
Breathe in and lower it to the rack slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Kettlebell Seated Two Arm Military Press
desc: A seated press with a kettlebell in each hand, pressing both at once. Sitting removes leg drive, so the shoulders and triceps must do all the work.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with feet flat and hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders.
Brace your stomach and keep your back straight.
Breathe out and press both kettlebells straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your wrists straight and avoid leaning back.
Breathe in and lower them slowly to the rack.

name: Kettlebell Seesaw Press
desc: A kettlebell press where one arm lowers as the other presses up, like a seesaw. It keeps the shoulders working continuously and challenges coordination and core stability.
ins: Hold a kettlebell in each hand, one in the rack position and the other pressed overhead.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and your stomach braced.
Lower the top kettlebell while pressing the bottom one up at the same time.
Pass the two at about head height and keep the movement smooth.
Keep alternating, breathing steadily and staying upright.

name: Kettlebell Sumo High Pull
desc: A powerful pull from a wide sumo stance where you drive the kettlebell from the floor up to chest height with your elbows high. It works the traps and shoulders, with the glutes and hamstrings supplying the power.
ins: Stand with your feet wide, toes turned out, and a kettlebell on the floor between them.
Squat down with a flat back and grab the handle with both hands.
Drive through your heels and stand up fast, pushing your hips forward.
As you rise, pull the kettlebell up close to your body, elbows high and out, until the handle is near your chest.
Lower it under control back to the floor along the same path.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Kettlebell Swing
desc: A ballistic hip hinge where you swing a kettlebell from between your legs to chest height by snapping your hips forward. It builds power and endurance in the glutes and hamstrings and works the core.
ins: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and the kettlebell on the floor a step in front of you.
Hinge down, grip the handle with both hands and tilt the bell back toward you.
Hike it back between your legs, keeping your back flat and the bell high in your groin area.
Drive your hips forward hard and squeeze your glutes so the bell floats up to about chest height.
Let it fall back and hinge again as your forearms meet your thighs, then go straight into the next swing.
Breathe out sharply at the top of each swing; your arms guide the bell, they do not lift it.

name: Kettlebell Thruster
desc: A kettlebell front squat that flows straight into an overhead press using the drive from your legs. It works the shoulders, quads and glutes together and raises your heart rate.
ins: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, feet shoulder-width apart.
Breathe in and squat down with your chest up until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Drive up hard through your feet.
As you stand, use that momentum to press the kettlebells overhead, breathing out.
Lower the kettlebells to your shoulders as you go into the next squat.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up (squat Style)
desc: A Turkish get-up that rises from lying to standing with a kettlebell locked out overhead, using a squat instead of a lunge to stand up. It works the glutes, quads, shoulders and core and builds stability through the whole body.
ins: Lie on your back holding the kettlebell straight up over your shoulder in one hand, with the same-side knee bent and foot flat.
Keeping your eyes on the bell, roll up onto the opposite elbow and then onto that hand.
Drive through your bent leg to lift your hips, then sweep the straight leg under you so both feet are flat on the floor in a low squat.
With the arm locked overhead, stand up out of the squat, pushing through both feet.
Reverse the steps slowly: squat down, place the free hand on the floor, extend the leg, lower to the elbow and then to your back.
Breathe steadily throughout; switch arms after each set.

name: Kettlebell Two Arm Clean
desc: A clean with one kettlebell held in both hands, swinging it from between your legs up to your chest. It trains hip power, the traps and grip, and is a simple way to learn the clean.
ins: Stand with feet a little wider than hip-width and grip one kettlebell by the handle with both hands.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and swing it back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward and pull the kettlebell up close to your body, elbows high.
Turn your hands around the handle so it lands softly at your chest, held by the sides of the handle.
Lower it back between your legs with control and repeat.

name: Kettlebell Two Arm Military Press
desc: A strict standing press with a kettlebell in each hand, pressing both up at once. It builds shoulder and triceps strength with no help from the legs.
ins: Hold two kettlebells in the rack position at your shoulders, feet hip-width apart.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes and lock your knees softly.
Breathe out and press both kettlebells straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your wrists straight and the bells close to your head at the top.
Breathe in and lower them slowly to the rack.

name: Kettlebell Two Arm Row
desc: A bent-over row with a kettlebell in each hand. It builds the upper back and also trains grip and forearms.
ins: Stand with a kettlebell on each side of your feet.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees and a flat back, and grab the handles.
Pull both kettlebells toward your hips, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top and breathe out.
Lower them slowly without letting your back round.

name: Kettlebell Windmill
desc: A kettlebell windmill where you hold the bell overhead and hinge sideways toward your front foot. It strengthens the obliques and teaches shoulder stability overhead.
ins: Press a kettlebell overhead with one arm and turn your feet about 45 degrees away from it.
Keep your eyes on the bell and your overhead arm straight.
Shift your hips toward the bell side and hinge sideways, reaching your free hand down your front leg toward your foot.
Lower only as far as you can with a long, straight spine.
Rise back up by driving your hips forward, then switch arms after your reps.

name: Kick Out Sit
desc: A ground-based flow move where you start on hands and feet, kick one leg through under your body and sit your hips toward the floor. It works the hamstrings, glutes and quads and improves hip mobility and coordination.
ins: Start on your hands and feet with your knees hovering a few centimeters off the floor, back flat.
Lift one hand and the opposite foot off the floor.
Rotate your hips and kick that leg through under your body toward the lifted hand's side, straightening it out in front.
Lower your hips toward the floor so you are briefly in a side sitting position, supported on one hand and one foot.
Pull the leg back through and return to the hands-and-feet start.
Repeat to the other side, breathing out as you kick through.

name: Kipping Muscle Up
desc: A gymnastic move where you use a leg and hip swing to go from hanging below a bar to supporting yourself above it. It works the lats, biceps, triceps, shoulders and core, and needs solid strict pull-ups and dips first.
ins: Hang from a bar with a false or regular overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Build a controlled swing by pushing your chest forward, then kicking your legs forward.
At the front of the swing, snap your hips up and pull the bar hard toward your hips.
As your body rises, quickly lean your chest over the bar and turn your elbows up.
Press down until your arms are straight above the bar.
Lower back to a hang with control and reset before the next rep.

name: Knee Raise (Captain's Chair)
desc: A straight-leg raise done on a captain's chair station, with your forearms on the pads and your back against the backrest. It works the abs and hip flexors without your grip giving out first.
ins: Step onto the captain's chair, rest your forearms on the pads, hold the handles and press your back against the backrest.
Let your legs hang straight and tighten your abs.
Breathe out and lift your straight legs in front of you until they are level with the floor.
Pause for a second without leaning your shoulders back.
Breathe in and lower your legs slowly, stopping before they swing.

name: Knee Touch Crunch
desc: A crunch where you reach both hands up your thighs until your fingertips touch your knees at the top. The reach gives you a clear target and keeps the focus on the abs, with the hip flexors helping a little.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, palms resting on the front of your thighs.
Tighten your abs and tuck your chin slightly.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders off the floor, sliding your hands up until your fingertips touch your knees.
Hold the squeeze for a moment.
Breathe in and lower slowly, sliding your hands back down.

name: Kneeling Jump Squat
desc: An advanced power drill where you kneel with a barbell on your back and jump explosively from your knees onto your feet, landing in a squat. It builds hip explosiveness in the glutes, quads and hamstrings.
ins: Kneel on a soft mat with your knees hip-width apart and toes tucked under, a light barbell on your upper back.
Hold the bar tight to your back and sit your hips slightly back toward your heels.
Swing your hips forward explosively to jump up off your knees.
Pull your feet under you and land flat-footed in a squat, knees in line with your toes.
Stand up from the squat, then carefully return to kneeling for the next rep.
Breathe out as you jump; master it with no weight before using a bar.

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch
desc: A floor stretch from a kneeling position that lengthens the lats and the backs of the arms.
ins: Kneel on all fours on a mat.
Walk your hands forward and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Keep your arms straight and press your palms into the floor.
Let your chest sink down until you feel the stretch along your sides.
Walk both hands to one side to deepen the stretch on the opposite side, then switch.
Hold each position for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.

name: Kneeling Plank Tap Shoulder
desc: A plank held on your hands and knees in which you lift one hand at a time to tap the opposite shoulder. It is a beginner version of shoulder taps that trains the abs to stop your hips twisting, while the shoulders and triceps support you.
ins: Kneel on a mat with your hands under your shoulders, then walk your knees back until your body is straight from head to knees.
Tighten your abs and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, keeping your hips square to the floor.
Place the hand back down and tap with the other hand.
Keep alternating slowly, breathing steadily.

name: Kneeling Push-Up
desc: A push-up done from the knees instead of the toes, which lowers the load so you can build chest, shoulder and triceps strength with good form.
ins: Kneel on a mat and place your hands on the floor a little wider than your shoulders.
Walk your hands forward until your body forms a straight line from knees to head.
Tighten your stomach and glutes so your hips do not bend.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
Breathe out and push back up to straight arms.

name: Korean Dips
desc: An advanced dip done on a straight bar held behind your back. Your body slides forward and down in front of the bar, which places a big stretch on the chest and front shoulders and demands good shoulder mobility.
ins: Stand with your back to a straight bar at about hip height and grip it behind you with hands shoulder-width apart, palms facing forward.
Press up onto straight arms with your feet off the floor and the bar behind your hips.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, letting your body move forward and down while the bar stays behind you.
Lower until the bar is near your mid-back or you reach your comfortable shoulder range.
Breathe out and press back up and slightly backward to straight arms.
Build up slowly; stop at any pinching pain in the front of the shoulder.

name: L-Pull-Up
desc: An advanced pull-up done while holding your legs straight out in front in an L shape. It trains the lats and biceps and adds heavy core work.
ins: Hang from the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Lift your straight legs until they are level with the floor, making an L shape.
Keeping your legs up, breathe out and pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang while your legs stay level.
Bend your knees if you cannot keep your legs straight.

name: L-Sit On Floor
desc: A hold where you press yourself up on your hands from a seated position and keep your straight legs lifted level with the floor, forming an L shape. It builds strong abs and hip flexors and also works the arms and shoulders.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight together and your hands flat beside your hips.
Lock your elbows and press down through your palms, pushing your shoulders down away from your ears.
Tighten your abs and lift your hips and legs off the floor, keeping your knees straight.
Hold your legs level with the floor and your toes pointed, breathing steadily.
Lower with control. If your hands are too low to lift off, use parallettes or yoga blocks, or bend your knees.

name: Landmine 180
desc: A rotational landmine exercise where you swing the top of a barbell in an arc from one hip to the other. It trains the abs and obliques to turn the body, with the legs helping.
ins: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine holder or a corner and stand facing the other end.
Hold the end of the bar with both hands at chest height, arms nearly straight, feet wider than your shoulders.
Rotate your shoulders and hips together to bring the bar down in an arc toward your right hip, pivoting your left foot.
Brace and reverse the motion, swinging the bar up and over to your left hip.
Keep your arms long and let your trunk, not your arms, drive the arc.

name: Landmine Lateral Raise
desc: A one-arm lateral raise using the free end of a barbell anchored in a landmine. The bar's arc keeps tension on the side shoulder through the whole lift.
ins: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine or a corner and stand side-on to it.
Bend down and grip the free end with the hand farther from the bar, holding it in front of your opposite hip.
Stand tall with a soft bend in your elbow and your stomach braced.
Breathe out and raise the bar end up and out to the side until your arm reaches shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower slowly across your body, then switch sides after your set.

name: Lat Pulldown (Cable)
ref: Cable Lat Pulldown Full Range Of Motion
desc: A lat pulldown done through the longest possible range, from a full overhead stretch to the bar at the upper chest. It builds the lats and teaches control at both ends.
ins: Sit at the pulldown with your thighs under the pads and grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders.
Let your arms straighten fully and your shoulders rise to feel a stretch in your lats.
Start by pulling your shoulders down, then bend your elbows and pull the bar to your upper chest.
Breathe out and squeeze your shoulder blades down and back.
Return slowly all the way to the stretched position.

name: Lat Pulldown (Machine)
desc: A plate-loaded or selectorized pulldown machine where you pull the handles down in front of you along a fixed path. It builds the lats with help from the biceps, rear shoulders and mid back.
ins: Adjust the seat and thigh pad so you are locked in and the handles are just within reach.
Grab the handles with your arms straight and your chest up.
Pull the handles down in front of you until they reach shoulder level.
Squeeze your lats and shoulder blades at the bottom.
Let the handles rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
desc: A two-arm lateral raise between two low pulleys with the cables crossed in front of you. It keeps tension on the side shoulders through the whole lift.
ins: Stand between two low pulleys and hold the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left, so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand tall, brace your stomach and keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe in and lower your arms slowly across your body.

name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
desc: The standard standing lateral raise, lifting dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height. It is the main isolation exercise for the side shoulders and adds width to the upper body.
ins: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and a slight bend in your elbows.
Brace your stomach and relax your neck.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down.
Breathe in and lower slowly, taking about two seconds.

name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
desc: A lateral raise on a seated machine where pads on your arms guide the lift out to the sides. The fixed path keeps the work on the side shoulders and is easy to learn.
ins: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot points, then sit with your chest against the pad if there is one.
Place your arms against the pads with your elbows slightly bent and hold the handles lightly.
Breathe out and raise your arms out to the sides by pushing through your elbows until they reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly without shrugging.
Breathe in and lower slowly without letting the weight stack touch down.

name: Lean Planche
desc: A planche progression done from a push-up position with your feet on the floor, leaning your shoulders far forward over your hands. It trains the abs to keep your body rigid and builds the shoulder, chest and triceps strength needed for harder planche holds.
ins: Get into a high plank with your hands about shoulder-width apart and fingers turned slightly out.
Lock your elbows and push the floor away so your upper back rounds slightly.
Shift your weight forward onto your toes until your shoulders are in front of your hands.
Keep your body straight with abs and glutes tight, holding as far forward as you can control while breathing steadily.
Shift back to a normal plank to rest, and lean a little farther as you get stronger.

name: Left Hook (boxing)
desc: A boxing punch thrown with the left arm in a short, curved path toward the side of the target. It builds shoulder speed and power and uses the whole body through the hip and foot turn.
ins: Stand in a boxing stance with your left foot forward, knees soft and both hands up guarding your face.
Bend your left elbow to about 90 degrees and lift it to shoulder height.
Turn your left foot, hips and shoulders together to swing the fist in a tight arc across your body.
Breathe out sharply as the punch lands, keeping your right hand by your chin.
Bring the left hand straight back to guard and reset your stance.

name: Leg Extension (Machine)
desc: A seated machine exercise where you straighten your knees against a padded lever. It isolates the quads and is a common beginner and rehab movement.
ins: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the pad rests on the front of your lower shins.
Sit back firmly and hold the side handles.
Straighten your legs until your knees are fully extended, squeezing your thighs.
Pause for a second at the top without locking your knees hard.
Lower the pad slowly to about a 90-degree knee bend.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Leg Pull In Flat Bench
desc: A seated knee tuck on the end of a flat bench, pulling your knees in toward your chest while leaning back. It works the lower abs and hip flexors.
ins: Sit on the end of a flat bench and hold its edges just behind your hips.
Lean back slightly and stretch your legs out straight, feet off the floor.
Breathe out and pull your knees in toward your chest while bringing your chest slightly forward.
Push your legs back out slowly without letting your feet touch the floor.

name: Leg Up Hamstring Stretch
desc: A lying stretch where you raise one straight leg and hold it behind the thigh. Your back stays supported on the floor, so it is a safe way to loosen the hamstrings and the lower glutes.
ins: Lie on your back with both legs straight on the floor.
Lift your right leg toward the ceiling and hold the back of the thigh or calf with both hands.
Keep the left leg flat and the back of your head on the floor.
Gently pull the right leg toward you, keeping the knee as straight as you comfortably can.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs.

name: Lever Alternate Leg Press
desc: A machine leg press where each leg pushes in turn rather than both together. Alternating sides builds the quads, glutes and hamstrings evenly and lets you focus on one leg at a time.
ins: Adjust the seat so your knees are bent about 90 degrees with both feet on the platforms.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and hold the side handles.
Breathe out and press one foot forward until that leg is nearly straight.
Breathe in and let it return slowly under control.
Repeat with the other leg and keep alternating.

name: Lever Alternating Narrow Grip Seated Row
desc: A seated machine row with narrow handles, pulling with one arm and then the other. It trains each side of the upper back separately, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and rest your chest on the pad.
Hold both narrow handles with straight arms.
Pull one handle back to your side, keeping your elbow close.
Return it slowly to straight, then pull with the other arm.
Keep your chest on the pad and avoid twisting.
Breathe out on each pull and in as the arm extends.

name: Lever Assisted Chin-Up
desc: A chin-up with the palms facing you on an assisted machine that takes off part of your body weight. It builds the lats and biceps while you work toward unassisted chin-ups.
ins: Set the assistance weight and kneel or stand on the platform.
Hold the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder-width.
Start from straight arms with your stomach tight.
Pull up until your chin clears the bar, elbows driving down in front of you.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Lever Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over row using a barbell anchored at one end, often called a landmine row, so the bar moves in an arc. It works the upper back with the biceps and forearms, and is easier on the lower back than a free barbell row.
ins: Anchor one end of a barbell in a corner or landmine base and load the free end.
Straddle the bar facing the plates and hinge forward with a flat back and soft knees.
Hold the bar just behind the plates with both hands, or use a V-handle under the bar.
Pull the bar end up toward your chest, driving your elbows back.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Lever Bent-Over Row With V-Bar
desc: A bent-over row on a lever or T-bar machine using a V-shaped close-grip handle. It builds thickness in the middle of the upper back.
ins: Attach the V handle to the lever arm and stand over it with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees and a flat back, and grip the handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Lower slowly to a full stretch while keeping your back flat.

name: Lever Bicep Curl
desc: A biceps curl on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine with an arm pad. The machine guides the path so you can focus on the biceps.
ins: Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Grip the handles with palms facing up.
Breathe out and curl the handles toward your shoulders.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and return slowly without letting the weight stack touch down.

name: Lever Calf Press
desc: A calf press on a plate-loaded lever machine, pushing a footplate with the balls of the feet. It lets you load the calves heavily with little balance demand.
ins: Sit or lie in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the footplate.
Straighten your legs to take the weight, keeping a slight bend in the knees.
Let the footplate bring your toes back toward you until the calves stretch.
Press through the balls of your feet to push the plate as far as you can.
Hold the top briefly, return slowly, and breathe out on each press.

name: Lever Chest Press (Slow Negative)
desc: A machine chest press done seated, where the machine controls the path so you can focus on pushing with your chest. It trains the pecs with help from the triceps and front shoulders and suits all levels.
ins: Set the seat height so your hands meet the handles at mid-chest level and plant your feet on the floor.
Press your shoulder blades back into the pad and hold the handles firmly.
Drive the handles away from you in a smooth press, stopping just before your elbows lock.
Control the return for about two seconds until your hands are back beside your chest.
Exhale during the press and keep your head against the backrest.

name: Lever Deadlift
desc: A deadlift done on a plate-loaded lever machine with handles at your sides, which guides the path of the lift. It is a beginner-friendly way to train the glutes, hamstrings and quads with less balance demand.
ins: Load the machine and stand on the platform with your feet hip-width apart between the handles.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the handles, arms straight.
Flatten your back, lift your chest and brace your core.
Push through your feet and stand up, driving your hips forward at the top.
Lower the handles by pushing your hips back and bending your knees until the weight nearly touches down.
Breathe out as you stand and in as you lower.

name: Lever Decline Chest Press
desc: A decline chest press on a machine, with the handles moving forward and down. It focuses on the lower chest and triceps in a stable, guided path.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with the lower part of your chest and sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with your elbows bent and pointing down and out.
Breathe out and press the handles forward and down until your arms are nearly straight.
Squeeze your chest at the end without locking your elbows.
Breathe in and return the handles slowly to the start.

name: Lever Donkey Calf Raise
desc: A donkey calf raise on a dedicated machine, where a pad rests on your hips while you lean forward. It loads the calves in a stretched position with a stable setup.
ins: Step into the donkey calf machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform, heels off.
Lean forward, hold the handles and position the pad across your lower back or hips.
Straighten your legs to lift the weight off the stack, keeping knees soft.
Lower your heels for a deep stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the stretch.

name: Lever Gripless Shrug
desc: A shrug machine where pads rest on your shoulders or arms so you don't need to grip anything. Because the hands are free, the traps can work hard without grip strength limiting you.
ins: Set the machine so the pads sit on top of your shoulders or under your arms when you stand or sit tall.
Let your arms hang relaxed and keep your back straight.
Lift your shoulders straight up against the pads as high as you can.
Pause and squeeze your traps at the top.
Lower slowly until your shoulders are fully down.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Lever Gripper Hands
desc: A grip machine exercise where you squeeze two handles together. It builds crushing grip strength in the hands and forearms.
ins: Sit or stand at the gripper machine and set a light load to start.
Wrap one or both hands around the handles with your wrist straight.
Squeeze the handles together as hard as you can.
Hold the squeeze for a second or two.
Open your hand slowly against the resistance and repeat.

name: Lever High Row
desc: A seated machine row where the handles come from above, so you pull down and back toward your upper chest. It works the upper back and rear shoulders, with the biceps helping.
ins: Sit in the machine with your chest against the pad and adjust the seat so the handles are above head height.
Reach up and grab the handles with straight arms.
Pull the handles down and back, bringing your elbows past your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end.
Let your arms extend slowly back up.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Lever Horizontal One Leg Press
desc: A one-leg press on a horizontal machine where you sit upright and push the footplate away. Working one leg at a time builds the glutes and quads evenly, with the hamstrings and calves assisting.
ins: Adjust the seat so your knee is bent about 90 degrees when your foot is on the plate.
Sit with your back flat on the pad and place one foot in the middle of the plate; rest the other on the floor or frame.
Hold the side handles and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and push the plate away until the leg is almost straight.
Breathe in and bend the knee to let the plate return slowly.
Finish the set and switch legs.

name: Lever Incline Chest Press (Wide Grip)
desc: A second version of the seated incline chest press machine, with a different handle and seat design but the same goal: pressing up and forward to build the upper chest with help from the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Adjust the seat and back pad so the handles start just above your shoulders.
Sit with your back and head against the pad and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the handles with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Breathe out and press up and away until your arms are nearly straight, without locking your elbows.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly back toward your upper chest.

name: Lever Kneeling Leg Curl
desc: A hamstring curl done one leg at a time on a kneeling leg curl machine. Training each leg separately lets you focus on the hamstring and spot strength differences between sides.
ins: Adjust the machine so your knee lines up with its pivot point and the pad sits on the back of your lower calf.
Kneel on the knee pad with your forearms on the support and your hips square.
Curl your heel toward your glutes, squeezing the hamstring.
Keep your hips still and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower the pad slowly until your leg is almost straight.
Breathe out as you curl; finish your reps, then switch legs.

name: Lever Kneeling Twist
desc: A machine twist done kneeling, where you rotate your hips and lower body against resistance while your chest stays facing forward. It targets the obliques with the lower back stabilizing.
ins: Adjust the machine, kneel on the pad and hold the handles with your chest facing forward.
Brace your abs and keep your shoulders square to the machine.
Breathe out and rotate your hips to one side as far as you can control.
Return slowly to the middle without letting the weight stack slam.
Finish your reps on that side, then switch the machine and work the other side.

name: Lever Lying Leg Curl
desc: A machine hamstring curl done lying face down, bending your knees to pull a padded lever toward your glutes. It isolates the hamstrings and is easy for beginners to learn.
ins: Adjust the machine so your knees are just off the end of the bench and the pad sits just above your heels.
Lie face down and hold the handles, hips pressed into the pad.
Curl the pad up toward your glutes as far as you can.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top and keep your hips down.
Lower the pad slowly until your legs are almost straight.
Breathe out as you curl and in as you lower.

name: Lever Lying Two-One Leg Curl
desc: A lying leg curl on a machine where you lift the pad with both legs and lower it with only one. The slow single-leg lowering overloads the hamstrings beyond what they could lift alone, with some help from the glutes.
ins: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees just off the bench edge.
Hold the handles and keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Breathe out and curl the pad up toward your glutes using both legs.
At the top, slide one leg out from under the pad.
Breathe in and lower the pad slowly with the remaining leg, taking three to four seconds.
Put both legs back under the pad and alternate the lowering leg each rep.

name: Lever Military Press
desc: A seated overhead press on a machine that moves the handles in a fixed path. It is a stable way to load the shoulders and triceps, with the upper chest helping.
ins: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height, and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing forward and plant your feet.
Breathe out and press the handles straight up until your arms are straight but not locked hard.
Keep your lower back on the pad.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly to shoulder height.

name: Lever Narrow Grip Seated Row
desc: A seated row machine using narrow, palms-facing-in handles, with the chest supported by a pad. It builds the upper back and lats, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest and sit with your chest on the pad.
Hold the narrow handles with your palms facing each other and arms straight.
Pull the handles back, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together without leaning back.
Return slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Lever Neck Extension (plate Loaded)
desc: A neck extension on a plate-loaded neck machine, pressing the back of the head against a pad. It strengthens the muscles at the back of the neck and upper traps.
ins: Sit in the machine facing forward and adjust the seat so the head pad sits against the back of your head.
Hold the handles and sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Start with your chin slightly tucked toward your chest.
Push your head back slowly against the pad until you are looking slightly up.
Pause, then return slowly; use a light weight and never jerk the neck.
Breathe out as you press back and in as you return.

name: Lever Neck Left Side Flexion (plate Loaded)
desc: A side bend of the neck to the left on a plate-loaded neck machine. It builds the muscles along the left side of the neck that help protect it from sideways force.
ins: Sit sideways in the neck machine so the head pad rests against the left side of your head.
Hold the handles and keep your torso upright and shoulders level.
Start with your head slightly tilted to the right.
Bend your neck slowly to the left, bringing your left ear toward your left shoulder against the pad.
Pause, then return slowly to the start; keep the weight light and the motion smooth.

name: Lever Neck Right Side Flexion (plate Loaded)
desc: A side bend of the neck to the right on a plate-loaded neck machine. It strengthens the right side of the neck and upper traps.
ins: Sit sideways in the machine so the head pad rests against the right side of your head.
Hold the handles and keep your shoulders level and your back straight.
Start with your head slightly tilted to the left.
Bend your neck slowly to the right against the pad, bringing your right ear toward your right shoulder.
Pause, then return slowly; do not let your shoulder rise to meet your ear.

name: Lever One Arm Bent Over Row
desc: A one-arm row using a barbell anchored at one end, pulling the free end up beside your body. It trains each side of the upper back, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Anchor one end of a barbell in a corner or landmine base and load the other end.
Stand beside the loaded end, hinge forward with a flat back and rest your free hand on your knee.
Hold the bar just behind the plates with the hand nearest to it.
Row the bar up toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower slowly to straight arm, finish your reps, then turn around for the other side.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Lever One Arm Lateral High Row
desc: A one-arm row on a lever machine pulled high and wide from the side. It targets the upper back and rear shoulder of each side separately.
ins: Sit on the machine facing the pad and take one handle with an overhand grip.
Start with your arm straight out in front of you at about shoulder height.
Pull the handle back with your elbow high and out to the side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back and breathe out.
Return slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Lever One Arm Lateral Wide Pulldown
desc: A single-arm wide pulldown on a plate-loaded or selectorised lever machine. It works each lat separately and lets you focus on pulling the elbow down to your side.
ins: Sit on the machine, secure your thighs under the pad and take one handle with an overhand grip.
Start with the arm straight overhead and slightly out to the side.
Pull the handle down in a wide arc until your elbow is beside your ribs.
Breathe out and squeeze your lat at the bottom.
Let the handle rise slowly to a full stretch.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: Lever One Arm Shoulder Press
desc: A machine shoulder press done one arm at a time. It lets you focus on each shoulder and even out differences between sides.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handle is at shoulder height and sit with your back against the pad.
Hold one handle with palm facing forward and rest your free hand on the seat or your thigh.
Breathe out and press the handle up until your arm is straight.
Keep your body square and don't lean away from the working arm.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: Lever Overhand Triceps Dip
desc: A seated dip machine exercise with an overhand grip where you push the handles down by straightening your arms. It builds the triceps with support for your back.
ins: Sit in the dip machine with your back against the pad and adjust the seat so the handles are about at chest height.
Grip the handles with palms facing down and your elbows bent and pointing back.
Breathe out and push the handles down until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Breathe in and let the handles rise slowly until your elbows are about 90 degrees.

name: Lever Preacher Curl
desc: A preacher curl on a machine with a fixed arm pad. It keeps your elbows in place and the resistance even, so the biceps work through the full range.
ins: Adjust the seat so your armpits sit snugly against the top of the pad and your elbows line up with the pivot.
Grab the handles with an underhand grip and arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the handles up toward your face.
Squeeze at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to almost straight arms.

name: Lever Preacher Curl (to Shoulders)
desc: A preacher curl on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine. The pad holds your upper arms still, so the biceps work through a smooth, guided path.
ins: Set the seat so your armpits sit at the top of the pad, then rest your upper arms on it.
Grip the handles underhand with your arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the handles toward your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly until your arms are almost straight.

name: Lever Pullover
desc: A pullover on a lever machine where you move a bar or pads from overhead down in an arc. It isolates the lats with little help from the biceps.
ins: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot and fasten the belt if there is one.
Reach up and place your hands or elbows on the bar or pads overhead.
Breathe out and pull the bar down in an arc toward your thighs, keeping your arms almost straight.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Let the bar return slowly overhead until you feel a stretch along your sides.

name: Lever Reverse Grip Lateral Pulldown
desc: A pulldown on a lever machine with an underhand grip. It builds the lats with strong help from the biceps and suits beginners.
ins: Adjust the seat and thigh pad so you are locked in with your arms reaching the handles.
Grip the handles with your palms facing you.
Pull the handles down to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Breathe out and squeeze your shoulder blades down.
Let the handles rise slowly to a full stretch.

name: Lever Reverse Grip Preacher Curl
desc: A machine preacher curl with an overhand, palms-down grip. It shifts more work to the brachialis and the forearm muscles while still training the biceps.
ins: Adjust the seat and place your upper arms flat on the pad.
Grip the handles with your palms facing down.
Breathe out and curl the handles up, keeping your wrists straight.
Pause at the top and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your arms are nearly straight.

name: Lever Reverse Grip Vertical Row
desc: A chest-supported machine row using an underhand grip. It trains the upper back and biceps without loading the lower back, which suits beginners.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and rest your chest on the pad.
Grip the handles with your palms facing up.
Pull the handles back, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Return slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your chest on the pad.

name: Lever Reverse Hyperextension
desc: A machine exercise where you lie face down with your hips at the edge of a pad and swing your legs up behind you against a lever. It strengthens the glutes, hamstrings and lower back while decompressing the spine.
ins: Lie face down on the pad with your hips at its edge and your legs hanging down, ankles under the roller or strap.
Hold the handles firmly to keep your upper body still.
Squeeze your glutes and raise your legs behind you until they are about level with your body.
Avoid swinging hard or over-arching your lower back at the top.
Lower your legs under control back to the hanging position.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Lever Rotary Calf
desc: A calf raise on a rotary calf machine, where a lever arm moves in an arc as you rise onto your toes. It works the calves and the muscles that keep the ankle stable.
ins: Adjust the machine so the pad sits firmly on your hips or thighs and your knees are slightly bent.
Place the balls of your feet on the footplate with your heels hanging off, and hold the handles.
Lower your heels slowly for a full stretch.
Rise onto your toes, pushing the lever arm through its arc as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower under control; breathe out on the way up.

name: Lever Seated Calf Press
desc: A seated calf raise on a lever machine with pads over the knees. Because the knees stay bent, it puts most of the work on the deeper calf muscle under the main one.
ins: Sit in the machine and adjust the knee pads so they rest snugly on your lower thighs.
Put the balls of your feet on the foot bar with your heels off the edge.
Lift slightly to release the safety lever, then lower your heels for a deep stretch.
Push through the balls of your feet to raise the pads as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second, lower slowly, and keep a steady breathing rhythm.
Put the safety lever back before you get up.

name: Lever Seated Calf Raise
desc: A calf raise on a seated calf machine, with pads resting on your lower thighs. The bent-knee position emphasizes the deep calf muscle that supports walking and running.
ins: Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the platform, heels off.
Adjust the knee pads so they sit snugly on your lower thighs.
Lift your heels slightly and release the safety lever.
Lower your heels as far as is comfortable for a full stretch.
Breathe out and press up onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly; reset the safety lever after the set.

name: Lever Seated Crunch (chest Pad)
desc: A seated ab crunch machine with a pad against your chest, letting you load the abs in a guided path. It is a good choice for beginners who want to add weight safely.
ins: Adjust the seat so the chest pad sits on your upper chest and hook your feet under the rollers if there are any.
Hold the handles lightly; do not pull with your arms.
Breathe out and crunch forward, curling your ribs down toward your hips.
Squeeze your abs at the bottom for a moment.
Return slowly until your back is upright, without letting the weights touch.

name: Lever Seated Crunch (Knees Up)
desc: A machine crunch in which your knees rise as your chest comes down, so both ends of your trunk curl in toward each other. It works the abs, with the obliques and hip flexors helping.
ins: Set the weight, sit on the machine and place your shins or feet behind the lower pads, holding the handles by your head or chest.
Sit tall with your abs tight and your lower back against the pad if there is one.
Breathe out and curl your chest down while drawing your knees up, squeezing your abs at the middle.
Pause for a second without pulling with your arms.
Breathe in and return slowly to the start, keeping the weight from slamming down.

name: Lever Seated Good Morning
desc: A good morning done on a seated machine: you lean forward from the hips against a pad and push back up to sitting. It trains the glutes, hamstrings and lower back in a controlled, supported path.
ins: Adjust the seat and pads so the upper pad sits across your upper back and your hips are against the seat back.
Sit tall, hold the handles and keep your feet flat.
Breathe in and lean forward from the hips, keeping your back flat.
Go until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, without rounding your back.
Breathe out and squeeze your glutes to push the pad back and return to upright.

name: Lever Seated Hip Abduction
desc: A seated machine exercise where you push your knees apart against padded arms. It strengthens the outer hips and side glutes that keep your knees and pelvis stable.
ins: Set the machine so the pads rest on the outside of your knees with your legs together.
Sit tall with your back against the pad and hold the handles.
Push your knees outward as far as you comfortably can.
Pause and squeeze the sides of your hips.
Let the pads come back together slowly without letting the weights touch.
Breathe out as you push out and in as you return.

name: Lever Seated Hip Adduction
desc: A seated machine exercise where you squeeze your knees together against padded arms. It isolates the inner thighs.
ins: Set the machine so your legs start open at a comfortable stretch with the pads on the inside of your knees.
Sit tall with your back against the pad and hold the handles.
Squeeze your knees together until the pads meet or nearly meet.
Pause and squeeze your inner thighs.
Let your legs open slowly back to the start, controlling the weight.
Breathe out as you squeeze and in as you open.

name: Lever Seated Leg Curl
desc: A hamstring curl done sitting on a machine, pulling a padded lever down and back under the seat. The seated position stretches the hamstrings at the hip, which makes this a very effective isolation exercise.
ins: Adjust the machine so your knees line up with the pivot and the lower pad sits just above your heels.
Sit with your back against the pad and lower the thigh pad until it holds your legs firmly.
Hold the handles and pull the pad down and back by bending your knees.
Squeeze your hamstrings when your knees are fully bent.
Let the pad return slowly until your legs are almost straight.
Breathe out as you curl and in as you return.

name: Lever Seated Leg Raise Crunch
desc: A seated machine movement that combines a knee raise with a crunch, bringing your knees and chest toward each other. It works the whole abdominal wall with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet or shins under the leg pads.
Hold the handles at your sides.
Breathe out and pull your knees up toward your chest while curling your upper body forward.
Squeeze for a second when your knees and chest are closest.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weight drop.

name: Lever Seated Reverse Fly
desc: A reverse fly on the pec deck machine using the horizontal handles with palms facing down. It isolates the rear shoulders while your chest stays supported.
ins: Set the handles to the rear position and adjust the seat so they are at shoulder height.
Sit facing the pad with your chest against it and grip the horizontal handles, palms facing down.
Breathe out and push the handles back with slightly bent elbows until your arms line up with your shoulders.
Keep your chest on the pad and your neck relaxed.
Breathe in and return slowly.

name: Lever Seated Reverse Fly (parallel Grip)
desc: A rear shoulder fly on the pec deck machine using the vertical handles, so your palms face each other. It targets the rear shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Set the machine handles to the rear position and sit facing the pad with your chest against it.
Grab the vertical handles with palms facing each other and arms straight at shoulder height.
Breathe out and sweep your arms back in a wide arc until they line up with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades for a second.
Breathe in and let the handles return slowly to the front.

name: Lever Seated Squat Calf Raise On Leg Press Machine
desc: A calf press done on a seated, horizontal leg press machine with your legs nearly straight. It targets the calves while your back stays supported against the seat.
ins: Sit in the leg press with your back against the pad and set the seat so your legs are almost straight.
Place only the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the footplate, heels off.
Press the plate out by straightening your legs, keeping a slight bend in the knees.
Let the plate bring your toes back toward you for a stretch.
Breathe out and push the plate away by pointing your toes, then pause.
Breathe in and return slowly, keeping your knees still the whole time.

name: Lever Shoulder Press (Converging Arc)
desc: A plate-loaded machine shoulder press where the handles move up and slightly inward in an arc. The converging path matches how the arms naturally press and works the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Set the seat so the handles start just above shoulder height and sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing forward and plant your feet.
Breathe out and press up and in until your arms are straight and your hands come closer together.
Pause briefly at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly along the same arc.

name: Lever Shoulder Press (Neutral Grip)
desc: A seated machine shoulder press using the neutral handles, so your palms face each other. The grip is easier on the shoulders and brings in more front shoulder and triceps.
ins: Adjust the seat so the neutral handles are at shoulder height and sit with your back against the pad.
Hold the handles with palms facing each other and elbows slightly in front of your body.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Breathe in and lower the handles slowly.

name: Lever Shrug
desc: A shrug on a leverage machine where you hold handles at your sides and lift along a fixed path. It isolates the upper traps, with the shoulders assisting.
ins: Stand or sit in the machine and take the handles at your sides with straight arms.
Stand tall with your chest up and chin level.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the top for a second.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Lever Sissy Squat With Dumbbell
desc: A knee-forward squat on a sissy-squat bench, holding a dumbbell at the chest while the ankles are locked in and the calves rest against the pad. The support lets you lean back safely and puts intense work on the quads, with the glutes, hamstrings and abs helping.
ins: Set the bench so your ankles fit snugly under the roller and your calves press against the pad.
Stand tall and hold a dumbbell upright against your chest.
Breathe in and bend your knees forward, letting your body lean back in a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor, keeping your stomach tight.
Breathe out and press your shins into the pad to straighten your knees and return to standing.

name: Lever Standing Chest Press
desc: A chest press on a standing machine, where you press handles forward from chest height while standing. It works the chest, shoulders and triceps and asks your legs and core to stay braced.
ins: Stand facing away from the machine and adjust the handles to line up with your mid-chest.
Grip the handles, take a short staggered stance and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight.
Keep your torso upright; do not lean forward to finish the press.
Breathe in and let the handles return slowly to your chest.

name: Lever Standing Gripless Shrug
desc: A shrug on a machine where the pads rest on your shoulders, so your hands do not have to grip. It isolates the traps without grip strength limiting the set.
ins: Adjust the machine so the pads sit on top of your shoulders while your knees are slightly bent.
Stand under the pads with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed.
Straighten your legs to take the weight, keeping your back tall.
Breathe out and lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold for a second at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.

name: Lever Standing Hip Extension
desc: A glute kickback on a standing hip extension machine, where you push a padded lever back with one leg. It isolates the glutes with help from the hamstrings and keeps the movement smooth and controlled.
ins: Set the pad so it sits behind your working leg, just above the knee or at the back of the thigh.
Stand facing the machine, hold the handles and keep a slight bend in the standing knee.
Brace your stomach and lean your chest forward a little.
Breathe out and push the lever back with your working leg by squeezing the glute.
Stop when your hip is fully open without arching your lower back.
Let the lever come forward slowly, then switch legs after your reps.

name: Lever T Bar Row
desc: A T-bar row on a machine with a chest pad, letting you row heavy weight while your lower back is supported. It builds thickness in the upper back with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Step onto the platform and rest your chest against the angled pad.
Grab the handles with the grip you prefer and lift the weight off its rest.
Let your arms hang straight with your shoulders reaching down.
Row the handles up toward your chest, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your back at the top, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you lower.

name: Lever T-Bar Reverse Grip Row
desc: A standing T-bar row on a lever machine using an underhand grip. It loads the upper back heavily and gives the biceps more work.
ins: Stand on the platform straddling the lever arm and bend your knees slightly.
Hinge forward with a flat back and take the handles with your palms facing up.
Pull the handles toward your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Lower slowly to a full stretch while keeping your back flat.

name: Lever Triceps Extension
desc: A triceps extension on a machine with an arm pad, where you push the handles away by straightening your elbows. It isolates the triceps along a guided path.
ins: Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest on the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Grip the handles with your elbows bent.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to push the handles down or forward.
Squeeze the triceps when your arms are straight.
Breathe in and return slowly to the bent-elbow position.

name: Lever Unilateral Row
desc: A machine row worked one arm at a time, with independent handles so each side has to pull its own share. It builds the upper back and helps fix strength differences between sides, with the biceps and forearms assisting.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest and rest your chest on the pad.
Hold one handle with your arm straight; you can brace your free hand on the machine.
Row the handle back until your elbow passes your side.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back, keeping your chest on the pad.
Return slowly to straight, finish your reps, then switch arms.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: London Bridge
desc: A rope drill where you start sitting under a hanging rope and climb hand over hand until you are standing, then walk your hands back down. It works the upper back, shoulders, biceps and grip.
ins: Sit on the floor under a hanging rope with your legs straight and heels on the ground.
Grab the rope above your head with both hands, one above the other.
Pull yourself up hand over hand, letting your heels stay put as your body rises.
Keep climbing until you are standing upright under the rope.
Reverse slowly, moving one hand down at a time until you are sitting again.
Keep your stomach tight and breathe steadily throughout.

name: Low Glute Bridge On Floor
desc: A basic glute bridge on the floor with a short, controlled lift of the hips. It is a gentle way to activate the glutes, with the hamstrings and core helping, and suits beginners or warm-ups.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat close to your glutes, arms by your sides.
Press your lower back gently toward the floor and tighten your stomach.
Breathe out and push through your heels to lift your hips a few centimeters off the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and hold for two seconds without arching your back.
Breathe in and lower your hips slowly to the floor.

name: Lower Back Curl
desc: A floor exercise lying face down where you lift the chest to strengthen the lower back. The glutes and hamstrings help hold the legs down.
ins: Lie face down on a mat with your legs straight and your arms by your sides, palms down.
Squeeze your glutes and press your hips into the floor.
Breathe out and lift your chest and shoulders a few centimetres off the mat.
Keep your neck long and look at the floor.
Hold for a second, then lower slowly.

name: Lunge (Dumbbell)
desc: A forward lunge holding a dumbbell in each hand. It strengthens the glutes and quads one leg at a time and improves balance and coordination.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and a dumbbell hanging at each side.
Step forward with one leg, landing heel first.
Lower your hips until both knees are bent to about 90 degrees and the back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your chest up and your front knee in line with your middle toes.
Push off the front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs, breathing in as you lower and out as you push back.

name: Lunge With Jump
desc: Jumping lunges: from a lunge you jump up and switch legs in the air, landing in a lunge on the other side. It builds explosive leg power in the glutes and quads and raises the heart rate fast.
ins: Start in a lunge with your right foot forward and both knees bent.
Swing your arms and jump straight up explosively.
Switch your legs in the air so the left foot lands in front.
Land softly in a lunge, letting the knees bend to absorb the impact.
Go straight into the next jump, breathing out on each jump, and keep alternating.

name: Lunge With Twist
desc: A forward lunge with a torso rotation over the front leg at the bottom. The twist works the abs and obliques, while the quads, glutes and hamstrings handle the lunge.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold your arms straight out in front of your chest, or clasp your hands.
Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees are bent at about a right angle.
At the bottom, turn your chest and arms toward the side of the front leg, keeping your hips facing forward.
Turn back to the center, keeping your front knee in line with your foot.
Push through the front heel to return to standing, then lunge with the other leg.
Breathe out as you twist and keep your abs tight throughout.

name: Lying (side) Quads Stretch
desc: A quad stretch done lying on your side, pulling your top heel toward your glutes. It lengthens the front of the thigh and hip and is easy on the balance.
ins: Lie on your side with your legs straight and rest your head on your lower arm.
Bend your top knee and hold that ankle or foot with your top hand.
Pull your heel gently toward your glutes, keeping your knees close together.
Push your hips slightly forward to feel the stretch along the front of the thigh.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Release, roll onto your other side and stretch the other leg.

name: Lying Elbow To Knee
desc: A floor crunch where you bring one elbow and the opposite knee together while the other leg straightens out. It works the abs and obliques, with the hip flexors and lower back helping to keep you steady.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat, and your hands lightly behind your head.
Tighten your abs and lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
Breathe out as you draw one knee in and turn to meet it with the opposite elbow, straightening the other leg just above the floor.
Return to the start with control.
Repeat with the other elbow and knee, alternating sides.

name: Lying Leg Raise Flat Bench
desc: A leg raise done lying on a flat bench, where you hold the bench behind your head and lift straight legs up. The bench lets your legs travel below level for a longer range for the lower abs and hip flexors.
ins: Lie on a flat bench with your hips near the end and hold the bench behind your head.
Stretch your legs out straight, level with the bench.
Breathe out and raise your legs until they point to the ceiling.
Lower them slowly to just below bench level, keeping your lower back pressed into the pad.
Keep your knees straight or very slightly soft.

name: Lying Leg-Hip Raise
desc: A floor exercise where you lift straight legs to vertical and then raise your hips off the floor. It focuses on the lower part of the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms flat beside you, palms down.
Tighten your abs and lift your legs together until they point at the ceiling.
Press your palms into the floor and curl your hips up off the mat, pushing your feet straight up.
Breathe out as your hips rise and keep the movement slow, without swinging.
Lower your hips first, then bring your legs down slowly, stopping just above the floor.

name: Machine Inner Chest Press
desc: A machine chest press where the handles travel inward toward each other as you press, so the chest gets a strong squeeze at the end of every rep.
ins: Set the seat so the handles sit at mid-chest height and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Hold the handles with your elbows bent and slightly below shoulder level.
Breathe out and press forward, bringing the handles in toward each other in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest hard for a second where the handles come closest together.
Breathe in and let the handles travel back out slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: March Sit (wall)
desc: A wall sit where you hold a seated position against a wall and lift one foot at a time in a slow march. Taking a foot off the floor makes the standing leg's quads and glutes work much harder.
ins: Stand with your back flat against a wall and walk your feet out about two foot-lengths.
Slide down until your knees are bent close to 90 degrees, with your knees over your ankles.
Press your back into the wall and tighten your core.
Lift one foot a few centimeters off the floor, hold for a moment and set it down.
Lift the other foot the same way, keeping your hips level and your thighs at the same height.
Keep marching for a set time, breathing steadily, then stand up by sliding back up the wall.

name: Medicine Ball Catch And Overhead Throw
desc: A power drill where you catch a medicine ball overhead and throw it back hard. It trains explosive pulling from the lats along with the shoulders and core.
ins: Stand facing a partner or a solid wall a few metres away, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the medicine ball overhead with both hands and tighten your stomach.
Throw the ball forward hard from overhead, snapping your arms down and breathing out.
Catch the return with your arms overhead, letting them give slightly to absorb it.
Reset your stance and throw again right away.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
desc: A two-hand throw where you pass a medicine ball from your chest to a partner or wall. It develops fast pushing power in the chest, shoulders and triceps.
ins: Stand facing a partner or a solid wall about 3 meters away, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ball at your chest.
Keep your elbows out and your thumbs behind the ball.
Step forward slightly and throw the ball by straightening your arms quickly, finishing with your palms facing out.
Breathe out sharply as you release.
Catch the return with soft arms, bring the ball back to your chest and reset before the next throw.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Push From 3 Point Stance
desc: An explosive medicine ball throw started from a low three-point stance, similar to a sprint or lineman start. You drive forward with the legs and push the ball out from the chest, training upper-body power that links to the legs.
ins: Place the ball on the floor in front of you and crouch over it with feet shoulder-width apart, hips back and knees bent.
Hold the ball against your chest with one hand and put the other hand on the floor so you are in a three-point stance.
Bring the free hand up to the ball as you drive forward and up through your legs.
Push the ball out from your chest with both hands as hard as you can, aiming forward and slightly up.
Follow the throw with a few running steps, then walk back, pick up the ball and reset.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Push Multiple Response
desc: A rapid chest push against a wall with a medicine ball, where you catch and throw again straight away. It trains fast, repeated pushing and quick hands.
ins: Stand about an arm's length plus a step from a solid wall, feet shoulder-width apart, holding a light medicine ball at your chest.
Push the ball into the wall by straightening your arms quickly.
Catch it as it bounces back, letting your elbows bend just enough to absorb it.
Push it back to the wall immediately with as little pause as possible.
Keep a steady rhythm and breathe out on each push; stop when your speed drops.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Push Single Response
desc: A medicine ball chest push done as single, maximal-effort throws with a full reset between each one. It builds peak pushing power in the chest, shoulders and triceps.
ins: Stand facing a wall or open space with feet shoulder-width apart and the ball held at your chest.
Bend your knees slightly and set your stomach tight.
Throw the ball forward from your chest as hard as you can, fully straightening your arms.
Breathe out sharply on the throw.
Let the ball drop or roll, collect it and take a moment to reset fully before the next throw.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Push With Run Release
desc: A power drill where you throw a medicine ball forward from your chest and sprint after it. It combines explosive chest pushing with acceleration from the legs.
ins: Stand in an open space with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ball at your chest.
Lean forward slightly and bend your knees as if about to sprint.
Drive off your legs and throw the ball forward from your chest with both hands.
Sprint after the ball as soon as it leaves your hands.
Pick up or catch the ball, walk back to the start and reset before the next rep.

name: Medicine Ball Close Grip Push Up
desc: A push-up with both hands on a medicine ball. The narrow, unstable base makes the triceps work hard and challenges your shoulders, chest and core to stay balanced.
ins: Place a medicine ball under your chest and put both hands on it, fingers spread around the sides.
Step your feet back into a plank with your body in a straight line.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the ball, keeping your elbows close to your ribs.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your stomach tight so your hips don't drop or pike up.

name: Medicine Ball Crunch
desc: A crunch where you hold a medicine ball with straight arms and push it up toward the ceiling as you rise. The extra weight and reach make the abs work harder, with the obliques, hip flexors and the muscles along the ribs helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a medicine ball with both hands above your chest, arms straight.
Tighten your abs and press your lower back into the floor.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders off the floor while pushing the ball straight up toward the ceiling.
Pause at the top with your arms still straight.
Breathe in and lower your shoulders slowly, keeping the ball over your chest.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Slam
desc: An explosive full-body move where you lift a medicine ball overhead and slam it into the floor. It works the upper back, shoulders and core and raises the heart rate.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Reach the ball overhead and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Breathe out and slam the ball straight down in front of you as hard as you can, bending your hips and knees.
Keep your back flat as you follow the ball down.
Pick up the ball, stand tall and repeat.

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw
desc: An explosive throw in which you swing a medicine ball from behind your head and release it forward. It builds power in the triceps, shoulders, chest and core.
ins: Stand facing a solid wall or a partner with your feet hip-width apart or in a short split stance.
Hold a medicine ball with both hands and raise it above and slightly behind your head.
Brace your stomach and throw the ball forward hard, snapping your arms straight as you release.
Breathe out sharply as you throw and follow through with your arms.
Catch the rebound or collect the ball, reset your stance and throw again.

name: Medicine Ball Supine Chest Throw
desc: An explosive pressing throw in which you lie on your back and push a medicine ball straight up, then catch it. It builds pressing power in the triceps, chest and shoulders.
ins: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows slightly tucked.
Breathe out and push the ball straight up as fast as you can, letting it leave your hands.
Catch it with soft arms and let it come back down to your chest.
Reset for a moment before the next throw.

name: Mixed Grip Chin-Up
desc: A chin-up with one palm facing you and the other facing away, a grip that is very secure on the bar. It builds the lats and biceps; switch which hand is under each set to keep both sides even.
ins: Grab the bar shoulder-width apart with one hand overhand and the other underhand.
Hang with straight arms and tighten your stomach and glutes.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar, keeping your body from twisting.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Change which hand is underhand on your next set.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Modified Hindu Push-Up
desc: A flowing push-up that starts with your hips high in an upside-down V, dips the chest forward close to the floor, then pushes back to the start. It works the chest, shoulders and triceps and adds mobility for the back and hips.
ins: Start in an upside-down V: hands and feet on the floor a bit wider than shoulder-width, hips high and arms straight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, sweeping your chest down and forward so it skims just above the floor between your hands.
Keep moving forward and straighten your arms, letting your hips lower toward the floor and your chest lift.
Breathe out and push your hips back up and back to return to the upside-down V.
Move smoothly and keep your stomach tight throughout.

name: Modified Push Up To Lower Arms
desc: A push-up variation done from the knees that moves between the hands and the forearms. It builds forearm, triceps, chest and shoulder strength along with core control.
ins: Start in a push-up position on your knees, hands under your shoulders and body straight from head to knees.
Lower your right forearm to the floor, then your left, so you rest on both forearms.
Keep your hips level and your stomach tight; do not let your back sag.
Press through your right palm to come back up onto your hand, then do the same with the left.
Alternate which arm leads each rep and breathe steadily throughout.

name: Monster Walk
desc: A walking drill with a resistance band around your legs, taking wide, diagonal steps in a half squat. It strengthens the side glutes and outer hips that keep your knees from caving in.
ins: Place a mini band just above your knees or around your ankles.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart, bend into a quarter squat and keep your chest up.
Step one foot forward and out at a diagonal, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the other foot forward and out the same way, never letting your feet come together.
Keep your knees pushed out and your hips level as you walk forward for 10 to 20 steps.
Walk backward the same way to return, breathing steadily.

name: Mountain Climber
desc: A fast plank-based drill where you drive your knees toward your chest one after the other. It builds cardio fitness while working the core, shoulders and arms.
ins: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Tighten your stomach and keep your hips level with your shoulders.
Drive your right knee toward your chest, then return it.
Switch legs quickly, bringing the left knee in as the right foot goes back.
Keep alternating at a steady pace, landing lightly on the balls of your feet.
Breathe rhythmically and keep your shoulders over your hands.

name: Muscle Up
desc: A strict, advanced bodyweight move that combines a powerful pull-up with a dip to get from hanging below the bar to pressing up above it. It works the lats, biceps, triceps, chest and shoulders.
ins: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip about shoulder-width, using a false grip if you can.
Pull explosively, bringing the bar down toward your lower chest rather than your chin.
As you reach the top of the pull, lean forward and rotate your wrists and elbows over the bar.
From the bottom of the dip position, press up until your arms are straight.
Lower back down under control to a full hang.
Breathe out on the pull and press, and take a breath at the hang.

name: Muscle-Up (on Vertical Bar)
desc: An advanced move that combines a pull-up and a dip to take you from hanging below the bar to supporting yourself above it. It builds the lats, biceps and triceps together.
ins: Hang from the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip, wrists set slightly over the bar.
Pull explosively, driving the bar toward your lower chest.
As your chest reaches the bar, lean forward and swing your elbows quickly over it.
Press down until your arms are straight and you are supported above the bar.
Lower back under the bar with control and reset before the next rep.

name: Narrow Push-Up On Exercise Ball
