desc: A narrow push-up with both hands on an exercise ball. The close hand position loads the triceps, and the rolling ball forces the shoulders, chest and core to work hard for balance.
ins: Kneel behind an exercise ball and place both hands on top of it close together, fingers pointing down the sides.
Step your feet back one at a time into a plank with your body straight.
Breathe in and lower your chest to the ball, keeping your elbows close to your ribs.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms.
Keep your stomach tight and the ball still under your hands.

name: Neck Bridge Prone
desc: An advanced neck strengthening exercise where you support part of your body weight on your forehead while facing the floor. It builds the front and side neck muscles but should only be done with care and no pain.
ins: Kneel on a mat and place a thick, soft pad in front of you.
Put your hands on the floor beside the pad and rest your forehead on it.
Tuck your chin slightly and tighten your abs.
Lift your knees and shift a little weight forward onto your forehead, using your hands to control the load.
Hold for a few seconds while breathing steadily, then shift back to take weight off.
Keep the movement small and stop right away if you feel any pain.

name: Neck Side Stretch
desc: A gentle stretch for the side of the neck, tilting the ear toward the shoulder. It eases tension in the muscles that lift the shoulder blade and the upper traps.
ins: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and down.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder, keeping your face looking forward.
For a deeper stretch, rest your right hand lightly on the left side of your head; do not pull hard.
Keep the left shoulder down and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly.
Bring your head back to center and repeat on the other side.

name: Negative Crunch
desc: A crunch that focuses on the lowering half, where you start at the top and take several seconds to roll down. Slow lowering builds ab strength and control.
ins: Sit with your knees bent and feet flat, arms crossed on your chest, as if at the top of a sit-up.
Brace your abs and round your lower back slightly.
Lower your back toward the floor very slowly, taking about four seconds.
Stop just before your shoulders touch down.
Use your hands or a small push to get back to the top, then lower again.

name: Oblique Crunch (Alternating Twist)
desc: A crunch on your back where you rotate as you rise, aiming one shoulder toward the opposite knee and switching sides each rep. It concentrates on the obliques along with the rest of the abs.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, fingertips resting lightly behind your ears.
Tighten your abs and press your lower back into the floor.
Breathe out as you lift your shoulder blades and turn, aiming one shoulder toward the opposite knee.
Hold the squeeze for a second, then lower slowly as you breathe in.
Turn toward the other side on the next rep, alternating throughout the set.

name: Oblique Crunches Floor
desc: A floor crunch done with your knees dropped to one side, so the curl comes from the side of your waist. It focuses on the obliques.
ins: Lie on your back, bend your knees and let both drop to your left side so they rest on the floor.
Keep your shoulders flat and place your fingertips by your ears.
Breathe out and lift your shoulders straight up toward the ceiling, feeling the right side of your waist work.
Lower slowly and keep a steady rhythm.
Finish your reps, then drop your knees to the right and repeat.

name: Olympic Barbell Hammer Curl
desc: A curl done holding an Olympic bar on its end, or a barbell gripped with palms facing in near the center, so the wrists stay neutral like a hammer curl. It builds the biceps, brachialis and forearms.
ins: Stand tall and hold the bar in front of your thighs with both palms facing each other, hands close together near the middle.
Keep the bar level and your elbows at your sides.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest with your thumbs leading.
Squeeze at the top without swinging.
Breathe in and lower slowly to straight arms.

name: Olympic Barbell Triceps Extension
desc: A standing overhead triceps extension with an Olympic barbell. It loads the triceps heavily through a long range and needs a stable, braced torso.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and press the bar overhead with a narrow overhand grip.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes to keep your back neutral.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head, upper arms close to your ears.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to bring the bar back overhead.
Use a lighter weight than you would for presses and move slowly.

name: One Arm Against Wall
desc: A simple standing exercise where one straight arm presses down against a wall to switch on the lat. It teaches beginners to feel the lats working.
ins: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away, feet hip-width apart.
Place one palm on the wall at about head height with your arm straight.
Without bending your elbow, press your hand down and into the wall as if pulling it toward your hip.
Feel the muscle under your armpit tighten and keep breathing.
Hold for 5 to 10 seconds, relax and repeat, then switch arms.

name: One Arm Chin-Up
desc: An advanced chin-up done with only one arm, demanding a lot of lat and biceps strength plus a strong grip. Build up to it with weighted and assisted one-arm work first.
ins: Grab the bar with one hand, palm facing you, directly above your shoulder.
Hang with the arm straight and your body tight; you can hold your working wrist with the other hand at first.
Pull your elbow down toward your hip and drive your chest up to the bar.
Resist turning by squeezing your stomach and glutes.
Lower slowly to a full hang, then switch arms.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: One Arm Dip
desc: A very advanced dip done on one arm, usually on a single parallel bar or sturdy handle. It demands strong triceps, chest and shoulders plus a lot of balance.
ins: Grip one dip handle and press up so that arm is straight, using your free hand on the other bar for balance at first.
Shift your body over the working hand and tighten your stomach.
Breathe in and bend the elbow to lower yourself a short distance, keeping the elbow close to your side.
Breathe out and press back up to a straight arm.
Increase the depth only as your strength and balance allow; switch arms after the set.

name: One Arm Overhead Shoulder (Dumbbell)
desc: A standing one-arm dumbbell press. It builds shoulder strength on each side and challenges your core to stop you leaning.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell at shoulder height, palm facing forward.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe out and press the dumbbell straight overhead until your arm is straight.
Keep your hips and shoulders level the whole time.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then switch arms after your set.

name: One Arm Slam (with Medicine Ball)
desc: A powerful one-arm throw where you lift a medicine ball overhead and slam it into the floor. It trains the abs to drive force, with the shoulders and back helping.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding a non-bouncing medicine ball in one hand at your shoulder.
Reach the ball up overhead, rising onto the balls of your feet.
Brace your abs and slam the ball forcefully into the floor beside your foot, bending your hips and knees.
Breathe out sharply as you throw.
Pick the ball up with a flat back, finish your reps, then switch arms.

name: One Arm Towel Row
desc: A one-arm bodyweight row using a towel looped around a sturdy post or door handle. Your body is the weight, and the towel adds grip work.
ins: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or the handle of a closed, locked door and hold both ends in one hand.
Step your feet close to the anchor and lean back until your arm is straight.
Keep your body straight from head to heels and your free arm by your side.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward your hand, driving your elbow back.
Lower yourself slowly until your arm is straight.
Finish the set and switch arms.

name: One Leg Donkey Calf Raise
desc: The bent-over donkey calf raise done on one leg at a time. It doubles the load on each calf and helps even out side-to-side differences.
ins: Stand on a step on one foot with your heel hanging off, the other foot hooked behind it.
Hinge at the hips and support your hands on a bench or rail in front of you.
Keep your back flat and your working knee nearly straight.
Let your heel drop for a full stretch.
Breathe out and drive up onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, and switch legs after the set.

name: One Leg Floor Calf Raise
desc: A single-leg calf raise on flat ground using only body weight. It builds calf strength and balance one side at a time.
ins: Stand next to a wall and rest one hand on it for balance.
Lift one foot off the floor by bending that knee.
Breathe out and rise onto the ball of your standing foot as high as possible.
Pause at the top, keeping the ankle straight and the knee soft.
Breathe in and lower your heel slowly to the floor.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: One Leg Squat
desc: A bodyweight squat on one leg while the other leg is held off the floor. It builds serious strength in the glutes and quads of the standing leg and demands good balance and ankle mobility.
ins: Stand on your right leg and lift your left foot a little off the floor in front of you.
Reach your arms forward to help you balance.
Breathe in and slowly bend your right knee, pushing your hips back, as low as you can control.
Keep the right knee in line with your toes and the heel flat on the floor.
Breathe out and push through the whole foot to stand back up.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Otis Up
desc: A weighted sit-up where you hold a plate at your chest and press it overhead as you reach the top. It works the abs and hip flexors under load, with the lower back helping control the descent.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet anchored, holding a weight plate against your chest.
Breathe out and sit up in one smooth movement.
As you reach the top, press the plate straight overhead.
Bring the plate back to your chest and lower your back slowly to the floor.
Choose a weight that lets you sit up without jerking.

name: Outside Leg Kick Push-Up
desc: A push-up combined with a sideways leg lift: after each push-up you sweep one straight leg out to the side. It works the chest and arms while adding work for the glutes, hips and core.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees, then press back up.
At the top, lift one straight leg off the floor and sweep it out to the side as far as you can without twisting your hips.
Bring the leg back in and set the foot down.
Do another push-up and sweep the other leg out.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you press; keep your core tight so your hips stay level.

name: Overhead Press (Barbell)
desc: The standing barbell overhead press, pushing the bar from your upper chest to overhead with no leg drive. It is a core strength lift for the shoulders and triceps and trains the whole body to stay tight.
ins: Set the bar in a rack at upper chest height and grip it just outside shoulder width.
Unrack it, step back and stand with feet hip-width apart, glutes squeezed and stomach braced.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly so it clears your chin.
Push your head through once the bar passes it, finishing with the bar over the middle of your feet.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your upper chest.

name: Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
desc: A standing dumbbell overhead press with both arms. It builds the shoulders and triceps and trains the whole body to stay stable under load.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes and keep your knees soft.
Breathe out and press both dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight.
Don't lean back or push with your legs.
Breathe in and lower slowly to shoulder height.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch
desc: A simple stretch for the back of the upper arm done by reaching one hand down behind your head and gently pressing the elbow with the other hand. It also loosens the shoulder.
ins: Stand or sit tall and raise your right arm overhead.
Bend the elbow so your right hand reaches down toward the middle of your upper back.
Place your left hand on your right elbow and gently press it back and down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly and keeping your head upright.
Release slowly and repeat on the other arm.

name: Palms Up Close Grip Pulldown (Biceps)
desc: A lat pulldown with the palms facing you, which lets the elbows stay close and brings the biceps in strongly. It builds the lats and lower lats in particular.
ins: Sit at the pulldown station and grab the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder-width.
Lift your chest and lean back only a little.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, keeping your elbows in front of your body and close.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom for a moment.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way up.

name: Pec Deck (Machine)
desc: A seated fly on a pec deck machine, where you bring the arms together in front of your chest against resistance. It isolates the chest with a stable, guided path that suits beginners.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles or pads are at chest height, then sit with your back against the pad.
Hold the handles with a slight bend in your elbows and your arms open to the sides.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a smooth arc.
Squeeze your chest for a moment when they meet.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch, breathing in, and breathe out as you close.

name: Pelvic Tilt
desc: A gentle floor exercise where you flatten your lower back into the floor by tightening your abs and tilting your pelvis. It teaches control of the deep abs and eases stiffness in the lower back.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms resting by your sides.
Notice the small gap between your lower back and the floor.
Breathe out and tighten your lower abs to tilt your pelvis back, pressing your lower back flat into the floor.
Hold for a few seconds without lifting your hips or pushing with your feet.
Breathe in and relax back to the starting position.

name: Pelvic Tilt Into Bridge
desc: A floor exercise that starts with a small tilt of the pelvis and rolls up into a full glute bridge. It wakes up the glutes and teaches you to control your lower back, with help from the hamstrings and core.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart, arms by your sides.
Flatten your lower back into the floor by tilting your pelvis up slightly.
Keep that tilt and peel your hips off the floor one section of the spine at a time.
Stop when your knees, hips and shoulders form a straight line and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe in at the top, then breathe out as you roll back down, lower back touching last.

name: Peroneals Stretch
desc: A rope-assisted stretch for the muscles on the outer side of the lower leg. You turn the sole of your foot inward while pulling it gently toward you.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and loop a rope around the ball of that foot.
Hold both ends of the rope, with more of the pull coming from the hand on the inner side of the leg.
Pull gently so your toes come toward you and the sole turns inward.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the outside of your shin and ankle.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds and breathe slowly.
Release and switch legs.

name: Pike-To-Cobra Push-Up
desc: A flowing bodyweight move that goes from a pike, with hips high, down through a push-up and up into a cobra with the chest lifted, then back again. It works the shoulders, triceps and core and strengthens and opens the hips and glutes.
ins: Start in a pike: hands and feet on the floor, hips high, body in an upside-down V.
Bend your elbows and swoop your chest down close to the floor between your hands.
Keep moving forward, straightening your arms and lifting your chest into a cobra with your hips low.
Breathe in as you open the chest, then breathe out and push your hips back up to the pike.
Move smoothly and keep your stomach tight throughout.

name: Plank
desc: A basic core hold where you support your body on your forearms and toes in a straight line. It builds abdominal endurance and teaches you to brace, with the shoulders, lower back and glutes helping to hold the position.
ins: Place your forearms on the floor with your elbows directly under your shoulders, hands facing forward.
Step your feet back so you rest on your toes, feet about hip-width apart.
Tighten your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Look at the floor just ahead of your hands to keep your neck in line.
Hold without letting your hips sag or pike up, breathing slowly and steadily throughout.

name: Plyo Push Up
desc: An explosive push-up where you drive your whole upper body off the floor so your hands leave the ground. It builds speed and power in the chest, triceps and shoulders.
ins: Start in a push-up position with your hands just wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest quickly but under control until it is close to the floor.
Explode upward so your hands lift off the floor.
Land with your hands in the same spot and your elbows soft to absorb the impact.
Go straight into the next rep, keeping your hips in line with your shoulders.

name: Posterior Step To Overhead Reach
desc: A reverse lunge combined with an overhead arm reach that lengthens the front of the body. It warms up the core, hips and legs and opens up the shoulders.
ins: Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
Step one foot back and lower into a lunge, landing on the ball of the back foot.
As you lower, sweep both arms up overhead and reach tall, keeping your ribs down and abs tight.
Hold for a breath, feeling the stretch in the front of the back hip.
Press through the front foot to step back to standing as you lower your arms, then switch legs.

name: Posterior Tibialis Stretch
desc: A rope-assisted stretch for the deep muscle behind the shin that supports the arch of the foot. You pull the foot up and turn the sole slightly outward.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and loop a rope around the ball of that foot.
Hold both ends, pulling a little more with the hand on the outer side of the leg.
Draw your toes toward you while letting the sole turn slightly outward.
Stop at a gentle stretch deep in the calf and along the inner ankle.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds with slow breathing.
Release and switch legs.

name: Potty Squat
desc: A deep bodyweight squat where you sit all the way down between your heels and pause, like sitting on a very low seat. It builds control through the abs and trunk while strengthening the quads and glutes and improving hip and ankle mobility.
ins: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and your toes turned slightly out.
Tighten your abs and reach your arms forward for balance.
Bend your knees and hips and sink as low as you can, keeping your heels down and your chest up.
Rest at the bottom for a few breaths, pressing your knees gently out with your elbows if that helps.
Push through your whole foot to stand back up, breathing out as you rise.

name: Potty Squat With Support
desc: A very deep, low squat held while gripping a support in front of you. It builds strength and mobility at the bottom of the squat, working the glutes, quads, hamstrings and calves.
ins: Stand facing a sturdy support such as a rack post or door frame and hold it with both hands.
Set your feet a little wider than your hips with toes turned slightly out.
Breathe in and sink down as low as you can, letting your hips drop between your heels.
Keep your heels down and use the support to keep your chest upright.
Hold the bottom for a few breaths, then breathe out and push up to standing.

name: Power Clean
desc: An Olympic-style lift that pulls the barbell explosively from the floor and catches it on the front of your shoulders in a partial squat. It develops total-body power, especially in the hamstrings, glutes and quads.
ins: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip-width apart, and grip it just outside your knees with a hook or overhand grip.
Set your back flat, shoulders slightly in front of the bar and arms long.
Push the floor away and lift the bar steadily past your knees, keeping it close.
When it reaches mid-thigh, jump your hips forward hard, extend fully and shrug.
Pull yourself under and whip your elbows forward to catch the bar on your shoulders in a quarter squat, then stand up.
Drop or lower the bar to the floor with control and reset; breathe and brace before every rep.

name: Power Point Plank
desc: A plank that moves between your hands and your forearms, lowering one arm at a time and pushing back up. It works the abs to stop your hips rocking, while the shoulders, triceps and glutes keep you stable.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet about hip-width apart.
Tighten your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body is straight.
Lower one forearm to the floor, then the other, until you are in a forearm plank.
Place one hand back under its shoulder, then the other, to push back up to the high plank.
Lead with the other arm on the next rep, keeping your hips as still as possible and breathing steadily.

name: Prancing
desc: A rhythmic in-place drill that alternates lifting one heel high while the other foot stays down, shifting weight like a light march on the toes. It works the calves and warms up the ankles and legs.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed.
Shift your weight to the right foot and rise high onto the ball of that foot, bending the right knee slightly.
Keep the left heel lightly on the floor as you rise on the right.
Lower the right heel as you shift your weight and rise onto the left forefoot.
Keep alternating in a smooth bouncing rhythm, with an upright chest and tight stomach.

name: Preacher Curl (Dumbbell)
desc: A one-arm preacher curl with a dumbbell. The pad stops your shoulder from helping and focuses the effort on the biceps.
ins: Rest the back of one upper arm on a preacher pad, armpit snug against the top.
Hold a dumbbell underhand with the arm nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, stopping just short of a locked elbow; switch arms after the set.

name: Preacher Curl (Machine)
desc: A machine preacher curl using handles with a neutral, thumbs-up grip. It trains the biceps along with the brachialis and forearms.
ins: Adjust the seat and rest the backs of your upper arms on the pad.
Hold the handles with your palms facing each other.
Breathe out and curl the handles up, keeping your thumbs pointing up.
Squeeze at the top without lifting your elbows off the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly to an almost straight arm.

name: Prisoner Half Sit-Up
desc: A half sit-up with your hands placed behind your head, which makes the upper body heavier to lift than with arms forward. It strengthens the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, and lace your fingers lightly behind your head.
Open your elbows wide and keep them there throughout.
Breathe out and curl up to about a 45-degree angle, leading with your chest, not your elbows.
Pause briefly without pulling your head forward.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your shoulders touch the floor.

name: Prone Twist On Stability Ball
desc: A back raise with a twist, done face down over a stability ball. The rotation works the obliques and abs, while the lower back lifts and holds your torso.
ins: Lie face down with your hips and stomach on a stability ball, toes on the floor and feet set wide for balance.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your ears.
Lift your chest off the ball until your body forms a straight line, without arching past that point.
Rotate your upper body to turn one shoulder up toward the ceiling, then come back to the center, breathing out as you turn.
Twist to the other side, and lower your chest back onto the ball at the end of the set.

name: Pull Up
desc: The standard pull-up with an overhand grip, one of the best bodyweight exercises for a wide, strong back. It works the lats first, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Grab the bar with your palms facing away, hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Hang with straight arms and squeeze your legs together.
Pull your shoulders down first, then pull your chest up toward the bar.
Go up until your chin passes the bar without kicking or swinging.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Pull Up (neutral Grip)
desc: A pull-up on parallel handles with the palms facing each other, usually easier on the wrists and shoulders. It trains the lats with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Grab the parallel handles with your palms facing each other, about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms, shoulders slightly drawn down.
Pull up by driving your elbows down beside your body.
Rise until your chin is above the handles.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Pull-In (on Stability Ball)
desc: A knee tuck in a push-up position with your shins on a stability ball, rolling the ball toward your chest. It works the abs and hip flexors while your shoulders hold you steady.
ins: Get into a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your shins resting on a stability ball.
Brace your abs so your body forms a straight line.
Breathe out and pull your knees toward your chest, letting the ball roll forward under your feet.
Pause with your hips over your shoulders.
Push your legs back out slowly to the straight plank without letting your hips sag.

name: Push And Pull Bodyweight
desc: A bodyweight push-up where you actively pull yourself down to the floor using your back muscles, then push back up. Controlling both directions works the chest, triceps and shoulders and teaches a stable shoulder position.
ins: Set up in a push-up position with your hands just wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Squeeze the floor with your hands and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Breathe in and pull yourself down toward the floor as if rowing your chest to your hands, keeping your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Stop with your chest just above the floor.
Breathe out and push the floor away to return to straight arms.

name: Push To Run
desc: A combination drill that joins one push-up with a burst of running knees in the plank position. It works the chest, arms and core while keeping the heart rate high.
ins: Start in a high plank with hands under your shoulders and body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows angled back, then press back up.
From the top, drive one knee toward your chest and switch legs quickly, as if running.
Do 4 to 6 fast knee drives while keeping your hips level.
Return to the plank and start the next push-up; breathe out as you press up.

name: Push Up
desc: The basic push-up on the floor, a bodyweight staple for the chest, triceps and shoulders. It also trains the core to hold the body straight.
ins: Place your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders and step your feet back into a high plank.
Tighten your stomach and glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest until it is just above the floor, elbows angled back at about 45 degrees.
Push the floor away to return to straight arms.
Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up; drop to your knees if you cannot keep good form.

name: Push Up On Bosu Ball
desc: A push-up with your hands gripping a BOSU ball turned flat side up. The wobbly platform makes the chest, shoulders and core work harder to keep you steady.
ins: Flip the BOSU so the flat side faces up and grip the edges of the platform with both hands.
Walk your feet back into a push-up position with your body straight from head to heels.
Keep the platform level and your stomach tight.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the platform by bending your elbows.
Breathe out and push back up to straight arms without letting the platform tip.

name: Push-Up (bosu Ball)
desc: A push-up with your hands gripping the edges of an upside-down BOSU-style half ball. The wobbly surface makes the chest, triceps, shoulders and core work harder to stay balanced.
ins: Turn the half ball so its flat side faces up and grip the edges with your hands.
Step your feet back into a straight plank, balancing the platform level.
Lower your chest toward the platform with control.
Press back up while keeping the platform from tipping.
Brace your stomach the whole time and breathe out as you push.

name: Push-Up (on Stability Ball)
desc: A push-up done with both hands on a stability ball, which rolls and shifts under you. Keeping the ball steady makes the chest, shoulders and core work much harder than a floor push-up.
ins: Kneel behind a stability ball and place your hands on its sides, a little narrower than shoulder width.
Straighten your legs behind you so you balance on your toes with your body in a straight line.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the top of the ball.
Push back up to straight arms, keeping the ball still.
Squeeze your stomach and glutes, and breathe out as you press.

name: Push-Up (on Stability Ball, Wide Feet)
desc: An advanced balance push-up with your hands placed on top of a stability ball. It builds chest and triceps strength while forcing your core and shoulder stabilisers to fight the ball's movement.
ins: Set the ball in front of you, place your palms on top of it and walk your feet back until your body is straight.
Spread your feet a little wider than usual for a steadier base.
Lower yourself slowly until your chest nearly touches the ball, elbows angled back.
Press up smoothly without letting the ball roll forward or sideways.
Hold your body rigid from head to heels and exhale on each press.

name: Push-Up (wall)
desc: A push-up done standing and leaning against a wall, the easiest push-up variation. It introduces the pushing pattern for the chest, triceps and shoulders with very little load.
ins: Stand about an arm's length from a wall and place your palms on it at shoulder height, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back slightly and tighten your stomach so your body is straight.
Lower your chest toward the wall by bending your elbows.
Press back to the starting position.
Breathe in as you lean in and out as you push; step further back to make it harder.

name: Push-Up (Wall, Close Grip)
desc: An easier version of the wall push-up with the hands placed lower and closer together, so the triceps help more. It is a gentle way to start building chest and arm strength.
ins: Stand facing a wall and place your hands on it at about chest height, shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet back a step so you are leaning into the wall with your body straight.
Bend your elbows close to your sides and bring your chest toward the wall.
Push the wall away until your arms are straight again.
Keep your heels down if you can and breathe out as you push.

name: Push-Up Close-Grip Off Dumbbell
desc: A close-grip push-up done with your hands gripping the handles of two dumbbells on the floor. The raised handles keep your wrists straight and let you lower a little deeper, focusing the work on the triceps.
ins: Place two dumbbells on the floor parallel to each other, just under your chest and close together.
Grip the handles and set up in a push-up position with your body in a straight line.
Breathe in and lower your chest between your hands, elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Make sure the dumbbells are stable and won't roll before each set.

name: Push-Up Inside Leg Kick
desc: A push-up followed by kicking one leg through under your body toward the opposite side. It combines chest and arm work with rotation through the hips and core.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Do a push-up, keeping your body in a straight line.
At the top, lift one hand and rotate onto the outside edge of the opposite foot.
Kick the free leg through under your body toward the lifted hand, reaching it out straight.
Pull the leg back, place the hand down and return to plank.
Do another push-up and kick through with the other leg, breathing out on each press and kick.

name: Push-Up Medicine Ball
desc: A push-up with one hand on a medicine ball and the other on the floor, rolling the ball across to switch sides between reps. The uneven position challenges each side of the chest and the core.
ins: Get into a push-up position with one hand on a medicine ball and the other on the floor.
Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your body straight and level.
Press back up to straight arms.
Roll the ball to your other hand and do the next rep with the hands switched.
Keep your stomach tight so your hips do not twist, and breathe out as you press.

name: Push-Up On Lower Arms
desc: A push-up that moves between a forearm plank and a straight-arm plank, often called a tiger push-up. Straightening the elbows from the forearms puts heavy work on the triceps, with the chest and shoulders assisting.
ins: Get into a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your body in one straight line.
Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.
Press your palms into the floor and straighten your elbows to lift your forearms off the ground into a high plank.
Lower back down with control until your forearms rest on the floor again.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Push-Up Plus
desc: A regular push-up with an extra push at the top where you spread your shoulder blades apart. It works the chest and triceps and adds direct work for the serratus muscles that support the shoulder blades.
ins: Start in a push-up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows at about 45 degrees.
Breathe out and push back up until your arms are straight.
Keep pushing the floor away so your shoulder blades spread apart and your upper back rounds slightly.
Relax the shoulder blades back to neutral before starting the next rep.

name: Push-Up To Side Plank
desc: A push-up followed by a turn into a side plank, alternating sides each rep. It trains the abs and obliques along with the chest, shoulders and triceps.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor and push back up.
At the top, rotate your body to the right, lift your right arm to the ceiling and stack your feet into a side plank.
Hold briefly with your hips high, then return to the plank.
Do another push-up and turn to the left side.

name: Quarter Sit-Up
desc: A very short sit-up where you rise only about a quarter of the way, just until your hands reach your knees. It is a beginner-friendly way to work the abs, with the hip flexors helping a little.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Rest your hands on the front of your thighs.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders up, sliding your hands until your fingertips reach your knees.
Hold briefly while keeping your lower back on the floor.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the floor.

name: Quick Feet Run
desc: Very fast, short steps on the spot, staying on the balls of the feet. It spikes the heart rate and sharpens foot speed and reaction.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees bent and chest slightly forward in an athletic stance.
Lift onto the balls of your feet.
Run in place with tiny, rapid steps, lifting the feet only a few centimeters.
Pump your arms quickly to match your feet and keep your core tight.
Breathe in a quick, steady rhythm and go for short bursts of 10 to 30 seconds.

name: Quick Feet Taps
desc: A fast footwork drill: run in place with very quick, short steps on the balls of your feet. It raises the heart rate and builds foot speed, working the quads and calves.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent and chest a little forward.
Lift onto the balls of your feet.
Start tapping your feet up and down as fast as you can, lifting them only a few centimeters.
Pump your arms in rhythm with your feet and keep your body light.
Breathe steadily and keep going for the set time, then slow down to a stop.

name: Raise Single Arm Push-Up
desc: A push-up where you lift one arm off the floor and reach it out at the top of each rep. Balancing on three points makes the chest, triceps, shoulders and core work harder against rotation.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet a little apart.
Do a full push-up, lowering your chest close to the floor and pressing back up.
At the top, lift one hand and reach that arm straight out to the side at shoulder height.
Hold for a second without letting your hips turn, then place the hand back down.
Do the next push-up and reach with the other arm, breathing out on each press.

name: Rear Axe Kick
desc: A kick in which the straight leg rises high in an arc and then drops down hard with the heel. It works the hamstrings and glutes and needs good hip flexibility and control.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with the right foot behind and your guard up.
Swing the straight right leg up in a small outward arc as high as you can control.
At the top, drive the heel straight down in front of you.
Keep your standing knee soft and your upper body upright for balance.
Land the foot back in stance under control and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Rear Decline Bridge
desc: A glute bridge done with your feet raised on a bench, so your shoulders are lower than your hips. The raised feet increase the range and put more work on the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie on your back with your heels on a bench or step and your knees bent to about 90 degrees.
Place your arms on the floor by your sides, palms down.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back.
Lower your hips slowly until they almost touch the floor.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Rear Deltoid Stretch
desc: A simple stretch where you pull one arm across your chest to lengthen the back of the shoulder. It also eases tightness in the upper back.
ins: Stand or sit tall and bring one arm straight across the front of your chest.
Hold it just above the elbow with your other hand.
Gently pull the arm closer to your chest until you feel a stretch in the back of your shoulder.
Keep your shoulder down and breathe slowly while you hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Release and repeat on the other arm.

name: Rear Leg Hook Kick
desc: A martial arts kick in which the rear leg swings around and the heel hooks back toward the target. Practised as a bodyweight drill, it builds the glutes and hamstrings, works the inner and outer thighs and core, and improves hip mobility and balance.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your left foot forward and your hands up to guard your face.
Pivot on the ball of your front foot so your heel turns toward the target.
Lift your right knee across your body and extend the leg slightly past the target.
Bend the knee sharply to sweep the heel back toward the target in a hooking path.
Bring the leg back in and set it down in your stance, keeping your hands up.
Repeat, then switch to the other stance.

name: Rear Pull-Up
desc: A wide-grip pull-up where you bring the bar behind your head instead of in front. It hits the lats and upper back hard but stresses the shoulders, so only do it if you have good shoulder mobility.
ins: Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Hang with straight arms and tilt your head slightly forward.
Pull up, keeping your elbows pointing down and slightly back, so the bar passes behind your head.
Stop when the bar reaches the base of your neck.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Reclining Big Toe Pose With Rope
desc: A yoga stretch done lying on your back with a rope looped around one foot to lift the leg. The rope lets you go deeper without straining, stretching the hamstrings and the calf.
ins: Lie on your back with legs straight and loop a rope around the ball of your right foot.
Hold one end of the rope in each hand with your elbows relaxed on the floor.
Breathe out and raise the right leg toward the ceiling, keeping it straight.
Walk your hands up the rope to bring the leg closer, keeping your left leg pressed into the floor.
Hold for 30 seconds or more with slow, even breaths.
Lower the leg slowly and repeat on the left side.

name: Resistance Band Foot Eversion
desc: A rehab exercise that tilts the sole of the foot outward against a resistance band. It builds the muscles that stop the ankle rolling inward and help prevent sprains.
ins: Sit on the floor or a chair with your heel resting on the ground.
Loop a band around the outer edge of your foot and anchor it toward the inner side.
Keep the heel in place and your leg still.
Tilt the outer edge of your foot up and out so the sole turns outward.
Hold for a second, return slowly, and switch sides after the set.

name: Resistance Band Foot External Rotation
desc: A rehab exercise that turns the whole foot outward from the ankle against a resistance band. It strengthens the muscles on the outer side of the lower leg that steady the ankle.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and loop a band around the front of one foot.
Anchor the other end to a sturdy object on the inner side of that foot, or hold it with the opposite foot.
Keep your knee and leg still, pointing straight up.
Rotate your foot outward, away from the other leg, against the band.
Hold for a moment, return slowly, and switch sides after the set.

name: Resistance Band Foot Inversion
desc: A rehab exercise that tilts the sole of the foot inward against a resistance band. It strengthens the muscles on the inner side of the ankle and lower leg.
ins: Sit with your leg straight or your heel on the floor, and loop a band around the inner edge of the foot.
Anchor the band toward the outer side so it pulls the foot outward.
Keep your heel and knee still.
Turn the sole of your foot inward toward the other foot against the band.
Pause, return slowly, and switch sides after the set.

name: Resistance Band Foot Plantar Flexion
desc: A rehab exercise that points the foot down against a resistance band, like pressing a pedal. It strengthens the calves and the muscles under the foot that support the arch.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and loop a band around the ball of that foot.
Hold both ends of the band in your hands with a little tension.
Start with your foot relaxed and toes pointing up.
Push the ball of your foot away from you, pointing the toes down against the band.
Hold briefly, return slowly to the start, and switch feet after the set.

name: Resistance Band Hip Thrusts On Knees
desc: A kneeling hip thrust with a loop band around the thighs: you sit back toward your heels and drive the hips forward. It targets the glutes, with some work for the hamstrings and quads, and needs no bench or weights.
ins: Kneel on a mat with knees hip-width apart and place a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
Keep your body upright and your hands on your hips.
Breathe in and sit your hips back toward your heels, keeping your chest up.
Breathe out and drive your hips forward until your body is straight from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top while pressing your knees out against the band.
Sit back slowly and repeat.

name: Resistance Band Horizontal Pallof Press
desc: A Pallof press performed from a half-kneeling position, pressing a side-anchored band straight forward while refusing to twist. Kneeling removes help from the legs so the abs and obliques work harder, while the glutes, shoulders, chest and triceps also contribute.
ins: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and kneel side-on to it, with the knee nearest the anchor down and the other foot forward.
Hold the band at your chest with both hands and move away until it is tight.
Tighten your abs and squeeze the glute of your down leg, keeping your torso tall.
Breathe out and press your hands straight forward, holding for two seconds without turning toward the anchor.
Bring your hands back to your chest slowly, and switch sides and legs after the set.

name: Resistance Band Leg Extension
desc: A leg extension done with a resistance band, sitting on a chair or bench and straightening the knee against the band. It isolates the quads and works well at home or as a light warm-up.
ins: Anchor a band low behind the chair or bench and loop the other end around one ankle.
Sit tall with your knees bent about 90 degrees and hold the sides of the seat.
Breathe out and straighten the knee, lifting the foot until the leg is straight.
Squeeze the front of the thigh for a second at the top.
Breathe in and bend the knee slowly back down, then switch legs after your reps.

name: Resistance Band Seated Biceps Curl
desc: A seated biceps curl using a resistance band looped under your feet. It is a simple, portable way to train the biceps, with tension that increases as you curl.
ins: Sit on the floor or a chair and loop the middle of the band under your feet.
Hold an end of the band in each hand with your arms straight and palms facing up.
Sit tall and keep your elbows close to your sides.
Breathe out and curl your hands up toward your shoulders.
Breathe in and lower slowly, keeping some tension in the band at the bottom.

name: Resistance Band Seated Chest Press
desc: A seated chest press with a resistance band wrapped behind you. It works the chest, shoulders and triceps and is easy to do at home or while travelling.
ins: Sit tall on a chair or bench and wrap the band around your upper back, holding one end in each hand.
Bring your hands beside your chest with your elbows bent and slightly below shoulder level.
Breathe out and press your hands forward until your arms are straight in front of your chest.
Squeeze your chest at the end without letting your shoulders shrug up.
Breathe in and return slowly, controlling the band as it pulls back.

name: Resistance Band Seated Hip Abduction
desc: A seated exercise where you push your knees apart against a loop band around your thighs. It strengthens the outer hips and glutes and is a good warm-up before squats.
ins: Place a loop band around your thighs just above the knees.
Sit on the edge of a bench or chair with feet flat and knees hip-width apart.
Sit tall or lean slightly forward with your hands on the bench.
Breathe out and press your knees out to the sides as far as you can against the band.
Hold for a second, then let the knees come back slowly without letting the band snap them in.

name: Resistance Band Seated Shoulder Press
desc: A seated overhead press with a resistance band looped under the bench or your seat. It is a simple, joint-friendly way to work the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Sit tall on a bench with the middle of a band under the seat or under your feet, holding an end in each hand at your shoulders.
Keep your palms forward and your stomach braced.
Breathe out and press your hands straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your back straight and don't lean back.
Breathe in and lower your hands slowly to your shoulders.

name: Resistance Band Seated Straight Back Row
desc: A seated row with a resistance band looped around your feet while you keep your back upright. It trains the upper back and is easy to do anywhere.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and loop the middle of the band around your feet.
Hold one end in each hand and sit tall with your chest up.
Breathe out and pull your elbows back past your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together without leaning back.
Let your arms extend forward slowly.

name: Resistance Band Shuttle
desc: A side shuffle in a half-squat with a loop band around the ankles, moving back and forth over a set distance. It strengthens the outer hips and glutes and helps keep the knees stable.
ins: Place a loop band around your ankles and stand with feet hip-width apart.
Bend into a quarter squat with your chest up and hands in front of you.
Step sideways with your right foot, keeping the band tight.
Follow with the left foot, but never let the feet come together.
Shuffle several steps to the right, then come back to the left, breathing steadily and staying low.

name: Reverse Crunch
desc: A crunch led by the hips: you curl your pelvis up off the floor instead of lifting your shoulders. It targets the lower part of the abs, with the hip flexors assisting.
ins: Lie on your back with your arms by your sides and lift your legs so your knees are bent at about a right angle over your hips.
Tighten your abs and press your palms lightly into the floor.
Breathe out and roll your hips off the mat, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Lift with your abs rather than swinging your legs.
Breathe in and lower your hips slowly back to the floor, keeping your knees bent.

name: Reverse Dip
desc: A dip done with your hands holding a waist-high bar or ledge behind your back and your feet on the floor in front. It works the triceps, with the chest and front shoulders helping.
ins: Stand with your back to a sturdy waist-high bar or ledge and grip it behind you with palms facing down, hands shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet forward so your weight is on your hands and your arms are straight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your body, keeping your elbows pointing straight back.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor or your shoulders feel tight.
Breathe out and press down through your hands to straighten your arms.

name: Reverse Fly (Dumbbell)
desc: A bent-over dumbbell fly with your palms facing behind you, which puts more emphasis on the rear shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
ins: Hinge forward with a flat back until your upper body is almost level with the floor, a dumbbell in each hand.
Turn your palms to face behind you and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Breathe out and sweep the dumbbells out to the sides up to shoulder height.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the start.

name: Reverse Grip Machine Lat Pulldown
desc: A lat pulldown machine used with an underhand grip, so the elbows stay close and the biceps help more. It builds the lats along a guided path.
ins: Adjust the seat and thigh pad, then sit with your feet flat.
Grab the handles with your palms facing you.
Pull the handles down toward your upper chest, elbows close to your body.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom without leaning far back.
Let the handles rise slowly to straight arms.
Breathe out as you pull and in as you return.

name: Reverse Grip Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up with the palms facing you, commonly called a chin-up, which brings the biceps in strongly. It trains the lats and is often easier than the overhand version.
ins: Grab the bar with your palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Hang with straight arms and a tight stomach.
Pull up, keeping your elbows in front of you and close.
Bring your chin above the bar and squeeze your back.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Reverse Hyper Extension (on Stability Ball)
desc: A reverse hyperextension done lying face down over a stability ball, lifting both legs behind you. It strengthens the glutes, hamstrings and lower back with equipment you can use at home.
ins: Lie face down with your hips on top of the ball and your hands on the floor in front of it, arms straight.
Let your legs hang down behind the ball with your toes resting on the floor.
Squeeze your glutes and lift both legs together until they line up with your body.
Keep your arms steady and avoid swinging or over-arching your back.
Lower your legs slowly until your toes nearly touch the floor.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Reverse Hyper On Flat Bench
desc: A reverse hyper done on a regular flat bench: you lie face down and lift your straight legs behind you. It targets the glutes and also works the hamstrings and lower back.
ins: Lie on your stomach along a flat bench so your hips sit at its end and your legs hang toward the floor.
Hold the sides or the front of the bench firmly.
Keep your legs straight and together, and breathe out as you raise them until they line up with your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top without arching your lower back hard.
Lower your legs slowly until your feet are just above the floor, breathing in.

name: Reverse Plank With Leg Lift
desc: A face-up plank on your hands and heels in which you lift one straight leg at a time. It works the abs to hold your body level, along with the glutes, hamstrings and shoulders.
ins: Sit with your legs straight and your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press through your hands and heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to heels.
Tighten your abs and glutes, then lift one straight leg as high as you can without letting your hips drop.
Lower the leg back down with control, breathing steadily.
Lift the other leg, alternating sides while keeping your hips up.

name: Ring Dips
desc: A dip done on gymnastic rings, which move freely and force you to stabilize at every point. It is an advanced exercise for the triceps, chest and shoulders.
ins: Set the rings at about hip height, grip them and jump or press up to a support position with straight arms at your sides.
Turn the rings slightly out and keep them close to your body.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower yourself until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Keep the rings tight to your sides so they don't drift apart.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms, turning the rings out at the top.

name: Rocking Frog Stretch
desc: A floor stretch on hands and knees with the knees spread wide, gently rocking the hips back and forth. It opens the inner thighs and hips and loosens the glutes.
ins: Start on your hands and knees, then slide your knees out wide to the sides.
Keep your shins parallel to each other, ankles in line with your knees and feet flexed.
Lower onto your forearms if that is comfortable.
Breathe out and slowly rock your hips back toward your heels until you feel the stretch in your inner thighs.
Breathe in and rock forward again, continuing the gentle motion for 30 to 60 seconds.

name: Rocky Pull-Up Pulldown
desc: A wide-grip pull-up that alternates between pulling to the front and pulling behind the head on each rep. It works the lats and upper back from two angles, with the biceps and forearms helping; skip the behind-the-head reps if they bother your shoulders.
ins: Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip and hang with straight arms.
Pull up in front until your upper chest is near the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
On the next rep, tilt your head forward and pull up so the bar passes behind your head.
Lower slowly again, and keep alternating front and back.
Breathe out on each pull and in on each lowering.

name: Roll Overs Into V Sits
desc: An advanced flowing exercise where you roll your legs back over your head and then roll forward into a balanced V-sit. It demands strong, controlled abs and also uses the hip flexors, inner thighs, glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight together and your arms by your sides, palms down.
Breathe in, lift your legs to vertical, then use your abs to roll your hips up and take your legs back over your head, keeping the weight on your upper back, not your neck.
Roll back down slowly, lowering your spine to the mat one part at a time.
As your hips touch down, carry the momentum forward and sit up into a V, balancing just behind your sit bones with legs and arms reaching forward.
Breathe out as you rise, hold the V briefly, then round your back and roll down with control to start again.

name: Roller Back Stretch
desc: A mobility drill lying back over a foam roller placed across the upper back. It opens the upper spine and helps with stiffness from sitting.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and place a foam roller across your back just below your shoulder blades.
Support your head with your hands and lift your hips slightly or keep them down.
Breathe out and let your upper back arch gently back over the roller.
Come back up, move the roller a little higher, and repeat.
Work along the upper back for about a minute, avoiding the lower back.

name: Roller Body Saw
desc: A forearm plank with your shins on a foam roller, sliding your body back and forth like a saw. It is a tough anti-extension exercise for the abs that also works the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Set up in a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your shins resting on a foam roller.
Tighten your abs and glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Push through your forearms to slide your body back, letting the roller move toward your ankles.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back sagging, breathing steadily.
Pull yourself forward again with your shoulders and abs until your elbows are back under your shoulders.

name: Roller Hip Lat Stretch
desc: A kneeling stretch with your hands on a foam roller, sitting the hips back while the roller rolls forward. It lengthens the lats along the sides of the back and opens the glutes and hips at the same time.
ins: Kneel on the floor and place a foam roller in front of you with both hands resting on it.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Roll the roller forward, letting your chest sink toward the floor and your arms stretch out.
Shift your hips slightly to the right to feel more stretch along the left side, then to the left.
Breathe deeply into the stretch, holding each side for 20 to 30 seconds.

name: Roller Hip Stretch
desc: A hip-opening stretch done lying on your back with a foam roller under your pelvis. Pulling one knee in while the other leg lengthens toward the floor stretches the front of the hip, with some release for the glutes and thighs.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent and place a foam roller across the floor under your pelvis.
Hug both knees toward your chest to find your balance on the roller.
Keep holding your right knee and slowly lower your left leg straight toward the floor.
Let the left leg hang and relax until you feel the stretch at the front of the left hip.
Breathe slowly for 20 to 30 seconds, then bring the leg back up and switch.

name: Roller Reverse Crunch
desc: A reverse crunch done lying lengthwise on a foam roller, which forces your core to keep you balanced. It targets the lower abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on a foam roller placed along your spine so your head and tailbone are supported, and rest your hands on the floor for balance.
Lift your feet with your knees bent at about a right angle over your hips.
Tighten your abs and breathe out as you curl your hips up, bringing your knees toward your chest.
Stay centered on the roller without tipping to either side.
Breathe in and lower your hips slowly to the start.

name: Roller Seated Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor
desc: A seated mobility drill with a foam roller held in both hands: you raise it overhead, then draw your shoulder blades down and back. It opens the chest and front shoulders and improves shoulder control.
ins: Sit tall on the floor or a bench with your legs straight out in front of you.
Hold a foam roller horizontally with both hands, arms straight in front of your chest.
Breathe in and slowly raise the roller overhead as far as you can without arching your lower back.
At the top, pull your shoulder blades down and back while keeping your arms long.
Breathe out and lower the roller back to chest height with control.

name: Roller Seated Single Leg Shoulder Flexor Depresor Retractor
desc: A seated foam roller shoulder drill done with one leg straight and the other bent, which makes it harder to cheat with the lower back. You raise the roller overhead and set the shoulder blades down and back to open the chest.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight and the other knee bent, foot flat beside the straight leg.
Hold a foam roller horizontally in both hands with arms straight in front of you.
Breathe in and lift the roller overhead slowly, keeping your torso upright and your ribs down.
Draw your shoulder blades down and back at the top and hold for a breath.
Breathe out and lower the roller to the start.
Switch which leg is straight halfway through.

name: Roller Side Lat Stretch
desc: A foam-roller drill lying on your side with the roller under your armpit. It loosens the lats and the back of the shoulder.
ins: Lie on your side with a foam roller under your armpit, roller across your body.
Reach your bottom arm straight overhead and bend your top leg to support yourself.
Roll slowly down a few centimetres toward your ribs and back up.
Pause on tender spots and breathe until they ease.
Roll for 30 to 60 seconds, then switch sides.

name: Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
desc: A hip hinge that lowers the barbell from standing down the front of your legs with only a slight knee bend. It is one of the best exercises for the hamstrings and glutes and also strengthens the lower back.
ins: Stand holding the bar at your thighs with an overhand grip, feet hip-width apart.
Unlock your knees slightly and keep that bend fixed.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, usually around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward and squeeze your glutes to stand back up.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.

name: Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
desc: A hip hinge holding a dumbbell in each hand, lowering the weights down the front of your legs with only a slight knee bend. It loads the glutes and hamstrings through a long stretch and trains the lower back to stay strong and flat.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees slightly and keep them at that angle for the whole set.
Breathe in and push your hips back, sliding the dumbbells down close to your legs.
Keep your back flat and your neck in line until you feel a strong stretch in the backs of your thighs.
Breathe out, squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall.

name: Rope Climb
desc: Climbing a hanging rope using the arms, with or without the help of the legs. It builds the upper back, grip, biceps and shoulders, and is an advanced skill that needs practice.
ins: Grab the rope as high as you can with both hands and hang with straight arms.
Lift your knees and wrap the rope around one leg, pinching it between your feet.
Stand up on the rope with your feet while reaching higher with your hands.
Repeat: pull, lift your knees, lock your feet, stand and reach.
Climb down slowly hand under hand, using your feet to control speed.
Never slide down with your hands; keep a steady breath throughout.

name: Roundhouse Kick
desc: A turning kick where the hips rotate and the shin or top of the foot swings around into the target. It trains the quads and glutes along with the inner and outer thighs, and builds rotational power and balance.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your guard up.
Lift your rear knee out to the side, raising it to the height you want to kick.
Pivot on your standing foot so your heel turns toward the target.
Rotate your hips over and snap the lower leg around, striking with the shin or top of the foot.
Bring the leg back the same way and land in your stance.
Repeat, then switch legs.

name: Rowing Machine
desc: Rowing on an indoor rowing machine: a leg drive, a lean back and an arm pull on every stroke. It works most of the body's big muscles while it builds endurance, and it is one of the eight HYROX stations.
ins: Sit on the seat, strap your feet in so the strap crosses the widest part of your foot, and take the handle with an overhand grip.
Start at the catch: shins about vertical, arms straight, and your body leaning slightly forward from the hips.
Drive with your legs first, pushing the footplate away while your arms stay straight and your back stays firm.
As your legs straighten, lean back a little and pull the handle to your lower ribs, elbows close to your body.
Return in the reverse order: arms forward, lean forward from the hips, then bend your knees to slide back to the catch.
Keep a smooth rhythm, breathing out on each drive; in HYROX the station is 1,000 m.

name: Run
desc: Steady running outdoors or on a track. It is one of the simplest ways to build endurance, heart health and leg stamina.
ins: Warm up with 5 minutes of brisk walking or light jogging.
Start running at a pace where you can still talk in short sentences.
Keep your posture tall, lean very slightly forward from the ankles and relax your hands.
Take light, quick steps and let your feet land under your hips.
Breathe in a steady rhythm through your nose and mouth.
Finish with a few minutes of easy walking to cool down.

name: Run (equipment)
desc: Running on a treadmill at a steady pace. It builds aerobic fitness and leg endurance with full control over speed and incline.
ins: Step onto the treadmill, clip on the safety key and start at a slow walk.
Raise the speed gradually over a few minutes until you reach an easy running pace.
Run tall with relaxed shoulders, eyes forward and arms swinging at your sides.
Land under your body with short, quick steps instead of long reaching strides.
Breathe steadily; you should be able to say a few words at a time.
Slow back to a walk for a few minutes before stopping.

name: Runners Stretch
desc: A half-kneeling stretch where you sit back over a straight front leg, popular with runners before and after a run. It stretches the hamstrings and calves of the front leg and the front of the back thigh.
ins: Kneel on your left knee with your right foot flat in front of you.
Place your hands on the floor on either side of the right foot.
Shift your hips back toward your left heel and straighten your right leg, pulling the toes up.
Keep your back long and fold gently over the right leg until you feel the stretch.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly, then switch legs.

name: Russian Twist
desc: A seated twist where you lean back with your feet up and rotate your torso from side to side. It works the obliques and the rest of the abs.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and lean back until your abs are tight.
Lift your feet a little off the floor and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Rotate your shoulders to the right and bring your hands beside your right hip.
Turn through the middle to the left side.
Keep your chest open and your back long, and breathe out on each turn.

name: Sandbag Lunge
desc: Walking lunges with a sandbag resting across your shoulders and upper back. A HYROX station that builds the quads and glutes under load and tests your balance and endurance.
ins: Lift the sandbag onto your shoulders behind your neck and hold it in place with both hands.
Stand tall, brace your stomach and take a long step forward.
Lower until your back knee lightly touches or hovers just above the floor, with your front shin close to upright.
Keep your chest up and your front knee in line with your toes.
Push through your front foot and bring your back foot forward straight into the next step.
Keep alternating legs as you walk forward for the set distance.

name: Scapula Dips
desc: A small movement on dip bars where you keep your arms straight and only move your shoulder blades up and down. It strengthens the traps and the muscles that control the shoulder blades.
ins: Support yourself on dip bars with your arms straight.
Let your shoulders rise toward your ears so your body sinks slightly, without bending your elbows.
Breathe out and push your shoulders down away from your ears to lift your body.
Hold the top for a second.
Lower slowly and repeat with straight arms the whole time.

name: Scapula Push-Up
desc: A push-up position drill where the arms stay straight and only the shoulder blades squeeze together and spread apart. It builds control and strength in the serratus muscles and helps keep the shoulders healthy.
ins: Get into a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Keep your arms straight and your stomach tight for the whole set.
Breathe in and let your chest drop slightly so your shoulder blades pinch together.
Breathe out and push the floor away so your shoulder blades spread apart and your upper back rises.
Pause briefly at the top, then repeat slowly.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
desc: A small pull-up movement where you hang from the bar and pull only your shoulder blades down and back, without bending your elbows. It strengthens the lower traps and the muscles that control the shoulder blades, preparing you for full pull-ups.
ins: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip at shoulder-width and straight arms.
Let your shoulders rise toward your ears in a relaxed hang.
Keeping your elbows straight, pull your shoulder blades down and together so your body lifts a few centimetres.
Hold the top position for a second or two.
Lower slowly back to the relaxed hang.
Breathe out as you pull down and in as you relax.

name: Scissor Jumps
desc: A jumping drill that switches the feet front and back in the air, like scissors opening and closing. It raises the heart rate and works the thighs and calves.
ins: Stand with one foot a step in front of the other, knees slightly bent.
Jump up and switch your legs in the air so the back foot lands in front.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
Spring straight into the next jump and switch again.
Swing your arms opposite to your legs, keep your chest up, and breathe steadily.

name: Seated Calf Stretch
desc: A floor stretch for the back of the lower leg, done sitting with one leg straight. It loosens the calf and also reaches into the hamstring.
ins: Sit on the floor with one leg straight in front of you and the other knee bent, foot flat.
Sit up tall and keep the knee of the straight leg pressed gently toward the floor.
Reach forward and hold the ball of the foot, then pull the toes back toward you.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly; do not bounce.
Let go, then switch legs.

name: Seated dip
desc: A machine dip performed seated, pushing the handles down until your arms are straight. It lets beginners train the triceps, chest and shoulders with a set load and a guided path.
ins: Set the seat so the handles sit at about chest height, then sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with palms facing in and your elbows pointing back.
Breathe out and push the handles down until your arms are straight, without locking the elbows hard.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up through the whole push.
Breathe in and let the handles come back up slowly until your elbows are at about a right angle.

name: Seated Glute Stretch
desc: A seated floor stretch where you cross one ankle over the other thigh and press the knee down. It opens up the glutes and the outside of the hip, with a light pull on the hamstrings.
ins: Sit on the floor with both legs straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and rest your right ankle on your left thigh just above the knee.
Put your right hand on the floor behind you and sit up tall.
Use your left hand to gently press your right knee down until you feel the stretch in the right glute.
Breathe slowly and hold for about 30 seconds, then switch sides.

name: Seated Leg Press (Machine)
desc: A leg press on a 45-degree sled machine, pushing the weighted platform away with both feet. It builds the glutes and quads with back support, making heavy leg training safer for beginners.
ins: Sit in the machine with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Push the platform up, release the safety handles and hold the side grips.
Bend your knees and lower the platform until your knees are near your chest, without your lower back lifting off the pad.
Press through your whole foot to push the platform back up, stopping just short of locking your knees.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you press; lock the safeties when finished.

name: Seated Leg Raise
desc: A seated floor exercise where you lean back on your hands and lift your straight legs. It is a simple way to train the lower abs and hip flexors.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and your hands on the floor slightly behind your hips.
Lean back a little and brace your abs, keeping your chest lifted.
Breathe out and raise both straight legs a few centimeters to a comfortable height.
Hold for a second, then lower slowly until your heels nearly touch the floor.

name: Seated Lower Back Stretch
desc: A gentle seated stretch where you fold forward to lengthen the lower back and the sides of the back. It also eases tension in the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Sit near the front of a chair with your feet flat and a little wider than hip-width.
Sit tall, then slowly bend forward from your hips.
Let your chest move toward your thighs and your arms hang down toward the floor.
Relax your neck and breathe slowly, feeling the stretch in your back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Roll back up slowly, one section of your spine at a time.

name: Seated Piriformis Stretch
desc: A figure-four stretch done sitting on a chair or bench, leaning forward over a crossed leg. It targets the piriformis deep in the hip and the glutes, and suits anyone who sits a lot.
ins: Sit tall on the front half of a chair or bench with both feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee and let the right knee drop out to the side.
Place your hands lightly on your right shin and knee.
Keeping your back straight, lean forward from the hips until you feel the stretch deep in the right glute.
Breathe slowly and hold for 30 seconds, then switch sides.

name: Seated Row (Cable)
desc: The standard seated cable row with a close handle, pulling toward the stomach. It is a staple for building the upper back and lats, with the biceps and forearms helping.
ins: Attach a close handle to the low pulley and sit with your feet on the platform.
Grab the handle and sit up tall with your arms straight and knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle to your stomach, driving your elbows back past your body.
Pause and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let the handle move forward slowly until your arms are straight, keeping your chest up.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Seated Row (Machine)
desc: A basic seated row on a lever machine. It trains the upper back and lats with the biceps assisting, and is easy for beginners to learn.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid chest, and press your chest lightly against the pad.
Grab the handles with your arms straight.
Pull the handles toward your body, driving your elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weight stack touch down.

name: Seated Side Crunch (wall)
desc: A side crunch done sitting on the floor with your back against a wall, which keeps you upright so the side of your waist does the bending. It targets the obliques.
ins: Sit on the floor with your back against a wall, knees bent and feet flat.
Place your fingertips by your ears with your elbows wide.
Breathe out and bend sideways, bringing your right elbow down toward your right hip while your back slides along the wall.
Come back to upright with control.
Repeat to the left side and keep alternating.

name: Seated Wide Angle Pose Sequence
desc: A seated yoga sequence with the legs spread wide, folding first toward the middle and then toward each leg. It stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs and improves hip flexibility.
ins: Sit on the floor and open your legs as wide as is comfortable, kneecaps and toes pointing up.
Sit up tall, using your hands behind you if your lower back rounds.
Breathe out and walk your hands forward between your legs, folding from the hips with a long back.
Hold for a few breaths, then walk your hands back up.
Turn your chest toward the right leg and fold over it for a few breaths.
Come back to the middle and repeat over the left leg.

name: Self Assisted Inverse Leg Curl
desc: A kneeling hamstring curl where you lower your body forward from the knees and use your hands to push yourself back up. It is a scaled version of the Nordic curl that builds very strong hamstrings, with help from the glutes and calves.
ins: Kneel on a soft mat and hook your heels under something heavy and stable, or have a partner hold your ankles.
Keep your body straight from knees to head and squeeze your glutes.
Breathe in and slowly lean forward from the knees, resisting with your hamstrings for as long as you can.
When you can no longer hold it, catch yourself with your hands like a push-up.
Give a small push off the floor and pull with your hamstrings to bring your body back up.
Breathe out as you return to the start.

name: Self Assisted Inverse Leg Curl (Hands on Bench)
desc: An easier Nordic-style hamstring curl where you hold onto a bench or box in front of you and use your arms to control the lowering and help you rise. It is a beginner step toward full inverse leg curls for the hamstrings, glutes and calves.
ins: Kneel on a mat with your heels anchored under a fixed object and place a bench or box in front of you.
Rest your hands on the bench and keep your body straight from knees to head.
Lean forward slowly from the knees, letting your hamstrings take as much of your weight as they can.
Walk your hands forward along the bench or let your arms bend to control the lowering.
Pull back up with your hamstrings, pushing with your arms only as much as you need.
Breathe out as you pull back to upright; keep your hips from bending.

name: Self Assisted Inverse Leg Curl (on Floor)
desc: A Nordic-style hamstring curl on the floor with your feet anchored, where you lower your body forward and push off the floor with your hands to help yourself back up. It builds eccentric hamstring strength, with help from the glutes and calves.
ins: Kneel on a mat with your heels hooked under a heavy, fixed object or held by a partner.
Keep a straight line from your knees to your head, glutes squeezed and arms ready in front of your chest.
Slowly lower your body forward, resisting with your hamstrings for as long as you can.
Catch yourself on your hands as you near the floor, landing in a push-up position.
Give a small push off the floor and pull with your hamstrings to return to tall kneeling.
Breathe out as you pull back up; use less hand push as you get stronger.
