name: Semi Squat Jump
desc: A small jump that starts from a half squat and lands back in it. It builds leg power and pushes the heart rate up.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and lower into a half squat, arms back.
Swing your arms forward and jump straight up, pushing through your feet.
Straighten your body fully in the air.
Land softly on the balls of your feet, rolling to the heels and sinking back into the half squat.
Reset your balance and jump again, breathing out on each jump.

name: Short Stride Run
desc: Running with short, quick strides and a high step rate instead of long reaching steps. It trains light, efficient footwork and is easier on the knees.
ins: Stand tall in an open space or on a treadmill, arms bent about 90 degrees.
Start jogging with short steps so each foot lands under your hips, not out in front.
Land lightly on the midfoot and keep your knees soft.
Increase your step rate while keeping the strides short.
Swing your arms in rhythm, stay relaxed through the shoulders, and breathe steadily.

name: Shoulder Grip Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up with the hands set at shoulder width. It is a balanced middle grip that trains the lats, biceps and forearms.
ins: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip directly above your shoulders.
Squeeze your legs together and tighten your stomach to stop swinging.
Breathe out and pull up until your chin is over the bar.
Keep your elbows pointing down and slightly forward.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

name: Shoulder Press (Plate Loaded)
desc: A basic seated machine shoulder press with an overhand grip. It is a safe, guided way for beginners to build the shoulders and triceps.
ins: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your shoulders, and sit with your back against the pad.
Hold the handles with an overhand grip just wider than your shoulders.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight.
Pause briefly without locking your elbows hard.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your hands are near shoulder height.

name: Shoulder Tap
desc: A high plank in which you lift one hand at a time to tap the opposite shoulder. It trains the abs to resist twisting while the shoulders and triceps hold you up.
ins: Get into a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet a little wider than hip-width.
Tighten your abs and glutes so your body is straight from head to heels.
Shift your weight slightly and lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Return the hand to the floor and tap with the other hand.
Keep your hips as still as possible, moving slowly and breathing steadily; widen your feet if your hips rock.

name: Shoulder Tap Push-Up
desc: A push-up followed by tapping each shoulder with the opposite hand while holding the plank. It builds the chest and triceps and trains the core to keep the hips square.
ins: Set up in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and feet about hip-width apart.
Lower your chest toward the floor and press back up.
At the top, lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder, then put it back down.
Tap your right shoulder with your left hand, then go into the next push-up.
Keep your hips as still as possible during the taps and breathe steadily.

name: Shuffle
desc: Quick sideways steps in a low athletic stance without crossing the feet. It trains lateral speed and hip strength and raises the heart rate.
ins: Stand with feet a bit wider than hips, knees bent, hips back and chest up.
Stay on the balls of your feet with your stomach tight.
Step sideways with the lead foot, then slide the trailing foot in without letting the feet touch or cross.
Keep your hips low and level and your knees in line with your toes.
After a few quick steps, plant the outside foot and shuffle back the other way, breathing in rhythm.

name: Side Bridge (on Forearm)
desc: A side plank held on your forearm, keeping your body in a straight line from head to feet. It builds endurance in the obliques and abs, with the glutes keeping the hips up.
ins: Lie on your side with your legs straight and stacked, and your elbow directly under your shoulder.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes.
Lift your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line.
Hold the position while breathing steadily, without letting your hips sink or roll backward.
Lower your hips, then repeat on the other side.

name: Side Bridge Hip Abduction
desc: A side plank on the forearm in which you lift the top leg up and down. It strengthens the outer hip and glutes while the obliques hold the plank steady.
ins: Lie on your right side and prop yourself on your right forearm, elbow under the shoulder.
Stack your legs and lift your hips so your body forms a straight line from head to feet.
Keep the hips high and lift your top leg toward the ceiling, keeping it straight.
Lower the leg with control without letting the hips drop.
Breathe steadily throughout, then switch sides after your reps.

name: Side Hip (on Parallel Bars)
desc: An advanced knee raise on parallel bars where you lift your knees up and to one side, twisting your hips. It focuses on the obliques with the hip flexors and abs helping.
ins: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms, shoulders pushed down and legs hanging.
Brace your abs and keep your upper body still.
Breathe out and raise your knees up and toward your right side, rotating your hips.
Lower your legs slowly to the center.
Repeat toward your left side and keep alternating.

name: Side Hip Abduction
desc: A standing body-weight exercise where you lift one straight leg out to the side. It strengthens the outer hip and side glutes that keep your pelvis level when you walk and run.
ins: Stand tall beside a wall or chair and rest one hand on it for balance.
Shift your weight onto the leg nearest the support, keeping a soft knee.
Lift the outside leg straight out to the side, toes pointing forward.
Stop before your upper body starts to lean away; keep your hips level.
Lower the leg slowly without letting it rest on the floor between reps.
Breathe out as you lift; finish your reps, then turn around for the other leg.

name: Side Kick
desc: A kick that drives the heel straight out to the side with the body turned sideways. It mainly strengthens the outer hip and glutes, with the quads, hamstrings, abs and obliques helping.
ins: Stand sideways to the target with your hands up.
Lift your lead knee up toward your chest, pointing it slightly across your body.
Turn your standing foot so the heel points toward the target.
Push the leg straight out, striking with the heel and the outer edge of the foot.
Breathe out on the kick, pull the knee back in and set the foot down.
Repeat, then switch sides.

name: Side Lying Floor Stretch
desc: A side-lying stretch on the floor that lengthens the lats and the side of the trunk, with a gentle pull through the outer hip.
ins: Lie on your side on a mat with your legs straight and your bottom arm under your head.
Cross your top leg behind your bottom leg and rest the foot on the floor.
Reach your top arm long over your head along the floor.
Let your top side lengthen from your hip to your fingertips.
Breathe into the stretch and hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch sides.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
desc: A side-lying exercise where you lift the bottom leg toward the ceiling with the top leg bent and placed in front. It strengthens the inner thigh, with some help from the glutes and hamstrings.
ins: Lie on your side with your head resting on your lower arm.
Bend your top knee and place that foot flat on the floor in front of your bottom knee.
Straighten the bottom leg and flex the foot.
Breathe out and lift the bottom leg as high as you can without rolling your hips.
Breathe in and lower it slowly, then switch sides after your reps.

name: Side Neck Stretch
desc: A side neck stretch where you tilt your ear toward your shoulder. It relieves tightness along the side of the neck and the upper traps.
ins: Sit or stand tall and let both arms hang relaxed.
Slowly tilt your head so your right ear moves toward your right shoulder.
Keep your left shoulder down; do not lift the right shoulder to meet your ear.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds and breathe slowly.
Return to center and repeat on the left side.

name: Side Plank Hip Adduction
desc: A hard side plank where the top foot rests on a bench and the bottom leg lifts up to meet it. It targets the inner thigh of the bottom leg, while the obliques and glutes keep the body lifted.
ins: Lie on your right side next to a bench and place your left foot on top of it.
Prop up on your right forearm with the elbow under your shoulder.
Squeeze the inner thigh of the top leg and lift your hips into a side plank.
Raise your bottom right leg up to touch the underside of the bench.
Lower the bottom leg slowly while keeping the hips up, breathing steadily.
Finish your reps, then turn around and switch sides.

name: Side Push Neck Stretch
desc: A deeper side neck stretch where one hand gently guides your head sideways while the opposite arm reaches toward the floor. It targets the upper traps and the muscles on the side of the neck.
ins: Sit tall and hold the edge of the seat with your left hand to anchor that shoulder.
Tilt your head to the right, bringing your ear toward your shoulder.
Place your right hand lightly on the left side of your head.
Let the weight of your hand add a gentle stretch; do not pull hard.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds with slow breathing.
Release slowly and switch sides.

name: Side Push-Up
desc: A push-up done lying on your side, pressing your upper body up with your top arm. It isolates the triceps of that arm using only body weight.
ins: Lie on your right side with your legs stacked and wrap your right arm around your waist or across your body.
Place your left palm on the floor in front of your right shoulder, fingers pointing toward your head.
Breathe out and press through your left hand to straighten the arm and lift your upper body off the floor.
Keep your hips and legs on the ground.
Breathe in and lower slowly; switch sides after the set.

name: Side Wrist Pull Stretch
desc: A simple stretch for the forearm and wrist where you use one hand to draw the other hand back while the arm is held out. It loosens tight forearms after grip-heavy training.
ins: Stand tall and hold one arm straight out in front of you at shoulder height.
Turn that palm to face away from you with the fingers pointing up.
With your other hand, gently pull the fingers back toward you.
Stop at a mild stretch along the inside of the forearm and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Breathe slowly and keep your elbow straight but relaxed.
Release and switch sides.

name: Side-To-Side Chin
desc: An advanced pull-up where you shift your body toward one hand at the top, then toward the other, moving side to side along the bar. It loads each lat more heavily in turn, with the biceps and forearms working hard.
ins: Grab the bar with a wide overhand grip and hang with straight arms.
Pull up until your chin is level with the bar.
At the top, move your chin toward your right hand, bending that arm more as the left arm straightens slightly.
Slide across toward your left hand while staying high.
Return to the centre and lower slowly to a full hang.
Breathe out as you pull up and keep breathing steadily as you move side to side.

name: Side-To-Side Toe Touch
desc: A standing side bend where you reach one hand down the outside of the leg toward your foot, then switch sides. It loosens the trunk and works the obliques, with the hip flexors helping you control the bend.
ins: Stand with your feet a bit wider than shoulder width and your arms out to the sides.
Keep your hips centered and your abs lightly braced.
Bend sideways, sliding one hand down the outside of that leg toward your foot as the other arm rises.
Go only as far as is comfortable without leaning forward or back, breathing out as you bend.
Return to standing and bend to the other side, alternating smoothly.

name: Single Arm Push-Up
desc: An advanced push-up performed on one hand, with the other arm behind your back. It demands high chest and triceps strength plus strong core control to stop the body from twisting.
ins: Get into a push-up position with your feet set wide and one hand placed under the centre of your chest.
Put your free hand behind your back or on your hip.
Lower your body slowly as far as you can control, keeping your hips and shoulders level.
Press back up through your working hand without twisting your torso.
Do all reps on one side before switching, and breathe out as you press; practise on an incline first if needed.

name: Single Leg Board Jump
desc: A forward hop on one leg to a marked spot or low board, landing and holding on the same leg. It builds single-leg power and teaches the knee and hip to stay stable on landing.
ins: Stand on your right leg facing a line or low board on the floor a short distance ahead.
Bend into a quarter squat on the standing leg and swing your arms back.
Swing your arms forward and hop forward off the right foot.
Land on the same foot with the knee bent, keeping it in line with your toes.
Hold the landing for two seconds before the next hop.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Single Leg Bridge With Outstretched Leg
desc: A one-leg glute bridge where the free leg stays straight and level with the working thigh. It loads one glute and hamstring at a time and challenges the core to keep the hips square.
ins: Lie on your back with your left knee bent and foot flat, and your right leg straight on the floor.
Lift the right leg until it lines up with the bent left thigh.
Breathe out and push through your left heel to raise your hips, keeping the right leg straight in the air.
Stop when your body is straight from shoulders to knee and squeeze the left glute.
Breathe in and lower your hips without letting them tilt to one side.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Single Leg Calf Raise (on A Dumbbell)
desc: A one-leg calf raise standing on the ball of your foot on a heavy dumbbell used as a small block. It adds range of motion and balance work for the calf and foot.
ins: Place a heavy hex dumbbell on the floor next to a wall so it cannot roll.
Step the ball of one foot onto the dumbbell's head with your heel off the back.
Hold the wall for balance and lift your other foot.
Lower your heel toward the floor until the calf stretches.
Breathe out and rise as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, and switch legs after the set.

name: Single Leg Platform Slide
desc: A reverse lunge where the back foot slides along the floor on a slider, towel or slide board instead of stepping. Sliding keeps constant tension on the front leg, working the hamstrings, glutes and quads.
ins: Stand tall with one foot on a slider or folded towel on a smooth floor and the other foot flat.
Brace your core and put most of your weight on the flat foot.
Slide the foot on the slider straight back as you bend the front knee and hinge slightly forward.
Lower until the front thigh is near parallel and you feel the glute and hamstring of the front leg working.
Pull the sliding foot back in by pushing through the front heel to stand.
Breathe out as you rise; finish one side, then switch.

name: Single Leg Squat (pistol)
desc: The pistol squat: a full-depth squat on one leg while the other leg is held straight out in front. It is an advanced test of glute and quad strength, balance and ankle and hip mobility.
ins: Stand on your right leg and lift your left leg straight out in front, heel just off the floor.
Reach both arms forward to counter your weight.
Breathe in and slowly sit down on the right leg, keeping the heel flat and the knee over the toes.
Lower until your hamstring rests on your calf while the left leg stays straight and off the floor.
Breathe out and push hard through the right foot to stand back up without bouncing.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.

name: Single Leg Vertical Jump
desc: A vertical jump from one leg, taking off and landing on the same foot. It is an advanced power drill for the quads, glutes and calves that also trains balance and landing control.
ins: Stand on your right foot with the left knee lifted slightly.
Bend the right knee into a quarter squat and swing your arms down and back.
Swing your arms up hard and jump straight up off the right foot.
Land softly on the same foot, letting the ankle, knee and hip bend together.
Steady yourself before the next jump, then switch legs after the set.

name: Sissy Squat
desc: A bodyweight squat where you rise onto your toes and lean back as your knees travel far forward. It puts heavy, focused work on the quads, with the calves and glutes helping to hold the position.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold a sturdy support with one hand.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Breathe in and bend your knees forward while leaning your upper body back, keeping a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower as far as you can control, letting your knees move well past your toes.
Breathe out and squeeze the quads to bring your knees back and return to standing.

name: Sit-Up (Slow Roll-Down)
desc: A full sit-up from the floor with your arms crossed on your chest, rising all the way to upright. It works the abs and hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and anchored, and your arms crossed on your chest.
Breathe out and curl your head and shoulders up first.
Keep rising until your torso is upright, leading with your chest.
Breathe in and roll down slowly, lowering your back one section at a time.

name: Sit-Up With Arms On Chest
desc: A standard sit-up with your arms crossed over your chest so your hands cannot pull on your head. It works the abs through a full range, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, anchoring your feet under something sturdy if needed.
Cross your arms over your chest with your hands on the opposite shoulders.
Breathe out and curl up, lifting your head, then shoulders, then lower back until you are sitting upright.
Keep your arms on your chest the whole time.
Breathe in and roll back down slowly to the floor.

name: Skater Hops
desc: Side-to-side bounds from one foot to the other, like a speed skater's stride. It builds leg power, balance and lateral control while raising the heart rate.
ins: Stand on your right leg with a slight bend in the knee and your left foot lifted behind you.
Push off the right foot and jump sideways to the left.
Land softly on the left foot, bending the knee and sweeping the right foot behind the left ankle.
Swing your arms across your body for balance and keep the landing knee over your toes.
Bound straight back to the right and keep alternating, breathing in rhythm.

name: Ski Ergometer
desc: A cardio machine that copies the double-pole action of cross-country skiing. Pulling the handles down works the triceps, shoulders and lats while the hips and legs join in, and it raises your heart rate quickly.
ins: Stand facing the machine with feet hip-width apart and take a handle in each hand above your head.
Pull the handles down in front of you by driving your arms down and hinging at your hips, bending your knees slightly.
Finish with your hands beside your thighs and your arms straight.
Stand back up and let your arms rise with the handles to the start.
Keep a steady rhythm and breathe out on each pull.

name: Ski Step
desc: Small side-to-side hops with the feet together, imitating a skier's motion. It raises the heart rate and trains ankle springiness and lateral control.
ins: Stand with feet together, knees slightly bent, and arms bent in front of you.
Hop sideways to the right, landing on both feet together.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
Immediately hop back to the left.
Keep your shoulders facing forward, hips loose, and breathe in rhythm as you hop quickly.

name: Skin The Cat
desc: An advanced shoulder mobility move on a bar or rings where you rotate your body backward between your arms and come back. It stretches the shoulders and builds upper back and core control.
ins: Hang from a bar or rings with a shoulder-width grip.
Tuck your knees to your chest and lift your hips up.
Keep rotating backward, passing your legs between your arms, until your feet point toward the floor behind you.
Lower only as far as your shoulders comfortably allow and breathe.
Reverse the movement slowly, tucking your knees to return to the hang.

name: Skips
desc: Skipping forward with a step-hop on each foot and a high knee drive, like a child's skip but more athletic. It is a warm-up and cardio drill that trains rhythm and leg drive.
ins: Stand tall with arms bent about 90 degrees and your eyes forward.
Step forward onto your left foot and do a small hop on it while driving your right knee up to hip height.
Swing the opposite arm forward with each knee drive.
Land lightly on the ball of the foot and step straight into the next hop on the other side.
Keep your chest up, contacts quick and breathing rhythmic as you travel forward.

name: Skullcrusher (Barbell)
ref: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension Skull Crusher
desc: The skull crusher: lying on a bench, you lower a barbell toward your forehead by bending only the elbows, then straighten your arms. It is a staple for triceps size and strength.
ins: Lie on a flat bench and hold a barbell straight above your chest with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Keep your upper arms still and pointing up for the whole set.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar slowly to just above your forehead.
Pause briefly without letting the bar touch your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms by squeezing the triceps.

name: Sled 45 Degrees One Leg Press
desc: A single-leg press on a 45-degree sled machine. Working one leg at a time builds the glutes and quads and shows up any strength gap between sides, with the hamstrings and calves helping.
ins: Sit in the sled with your back and hips flat against the pad and place one foot in the middle of the platform.
Press the platform up, release the safety handles and rest the other foot on the frame.
Breathe in and bend the working knee to lower the platform slowly toward your chest.
Stop before your lower back starts to lift off the pad.
Breathe out and push through the whole foot to straighten the leg without locking the knee.
Finish your reps, lock the safeties back in, then switch legs.

name: Sled 45° Calf Press
desc: A calf press on the 45-degree sled leg press, pushing the platform with only your ankles. It lets you load the calves heavily without putting weight on your spine.
ins: Sit in the 45-degree leg press and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Press the platform up until your legs are straight but not locked, then release the safety handles.
Keep your knees still and let the platform push your toes back toward you.
Breathe out and press the platform away by pointing your toes.
Pause, then breathe in and return slowly to a full stretch.
Lock the safety handles before you take your feet off.

name: Sled 45° Leg Press (back Pov)
desc: A two-leg press on the 45-degree sled, seen from behind, where it is easy to watch that the knees stay in line with the feet. It works the glutes and quads, with help from the hamstrings and calves.
ins: Sit back in the sled and press your lower back into the pad.
Place your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart with toes turned out slightly, then release the safeties.
Breathe in and lower the platform slowly, letting your knees travel in the same direction as your toes.
Do not let your knees fall inward as you go down or as you push.
Breathe out and drive the platform back up, keeping both feet pressing evenly.

name: Sled 45° Leg Press (side Pov)
desc: The standard 45-degree sled leg press, with both feet on the platform. It lets you push heavy weight for the glutes and quads with your back supported, and the hamstrings and calves help.
ins: Sit in the machine with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the middle of the platform.
Press the platform up slightly and release the safety handles.
Breathe in and bend your knees to bring the platform down until they reach about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and press the platform away through your heels and mid-foot, stopping just short of locking your knees.
Lock the safety handles back in when you finish.

name: Sled 45° Leg Wide Press
desc: A 45-degree leg press with your feet placed wide on the platform and toes turned out. The wide stance shifts more work to the glutes and inner thighs alongside the quads.
ins: Sit in the machine with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Place your feet wider than your shoulders on the platform, toes turned slightly out.
Push the platform up, release the safeties and hold the side grips.
Lower the platform, letting your knees travel out in line with your toes.
Stop before your lower back rounds off the pad, then press back up through your heels.
Breathe in on the way down and out as you push; re-engage the safeties at the end.

name: Sled Closer Hack Squat
desc: A hack squat on the sled machine with your feet placed close together. The narrow stance focuses the work on the quads, with the glutes helping.
ins: Step into the hack squat machine with your back against the pad and shoulders under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet close together, about hip-width or narrower, in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety handles and stand tall.
Bend your knees and lower slowly, letting your knees travel forward over your toes.
Go as deep as you can with your heels down, then push back up through your whole foot.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you press; lock the safeties when done.

name: Sled Forward Angled Calf Raise
desc: A standing calf raise on an angled calf sled, where you lean into shoulder pads while your feet push against the platform. The angle gives a smooth, back-friendly way to load the calves.
ins: Step onto the angled calf sled and place the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform.
Rest your shoulders under the pads and hold the handles.
Straighten your legs to free the sled, keeping knees soft.
Lower your heels for a full stretch.
Breathe out and push up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Sled Lying Calf Press
desc: A calf press done lying on your back in a sled machine, pushing the sled with the balls of your feet. Lying down takes load off the spine while the calves work hard.
ins: Lie on the sled machine's pad with your back flat and the balls of your feet on the lower part of the footplate.
Press the sled up until your legs are straight but not locked, then release the safety catch.
Let your heels move toward you slowly to stretch the calves.
Point your toes and push the sled as high as it will go.
Squeeze for a moment, lower slowly, and breathe out on each push.
Re-engage the safety catch before stepping off.

name: Sled Lying Squat
desc: A squat on a machine where you lie back on an angled pad with your shoulders under pads and push a platform with your feet. The supported position lets beginners load the glutes and quads with little stress on the spine.
ins: Lie back on the machine's pad with your shoulders snug under the shoulder pads.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate, toes slightly out, and hold the handles.
Push to straighten your legs and release the safety stop.
Bend your knees and let the sled come down until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees or a little deeper.
Press through your heels to straighten your legs without locking your knees hard.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you push; set the safety stop when finished.

name: Sled One Leg Calf Press On Leg Press
desc: A single-leg version of the leg press calf raise. Working one side at a time evens out strength differences between the calves.
ins: Sit in the leg press and place the ball of one foot on the lower edge of the platform; rest the other foot on the floor or tuck it away.
Straighten the working leg to lift the platform, keep a slight bend in the knee, and release the safety stops.
Lower the heel slowly until the calf is fully stretched.
Press through the ball of the foot to push the platform as high as you can.
Pause at the top, lower with control, and breathe out on each push.
Finish your set, lock the stops, then switch legs.

name: Sled Pull
desc: Pulling a loaded sled toward you with a rope, hand over hand, while you stay standing in one spot, as in the HYROX sled pull. It works the lats, upper back, biceps and grip, with your legs and core bracing to hold your position.
ins: Stand facing the sled with the rope stretched out in front of you, feet about shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Sit your hips back a little, brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Reach forward with one hand, grab the rope and pull it hard back to your hip.
As that hand finishes, reach past it with the other hand and pull again, hand over hand.
Let the rope pile up behind you and stay in your spot without walking backwards.
Keep pulling until the sled reaches you, for the set distance.

name: Sled Push
desc: Pushing a loaded sled across the floor by its upright poles, leaning in and driving with short, powerful steps. A HYROX station that builds leg drive in the quads, glutes and calves and tests your conditioning.
ins: Load the sled and grip its upright poles at about chest height, arms almost straight.
Lean in until your body makes a straight line from your head to your back heel, about 45 degrees to the floor.
Brace your stomach and drive one knee forward, pushing the floor away with the ball of your back foot.
Take short, quick, powerful steps, staying low and keeping your arms firm so the push comes from your legs.
Keep your head in line with your back and breathe steadily; don't let your hips rise above your shoulders.
Push for the set distance, then go round to the other end of the sled for the next length.

name: Sledge Hammer
desc: A conditioning exercise where you swing a sledgehammer down onto a large tire. It builds power through the abs and trunk, while the shoulders and forearms control the hammer.
ins: Stand facing a large tire with your feet shoulder-width apart, far enough back to strike its center, and make sure the area around you is clear.
Hold the handle with one hand near the end and the other higher up near the head.
Raise the hammer up and over your shoulder, keeping your back straight.
Swing it down onto the tire, sliding your top hand down the handle and bending your knees as it lands, breathing out hard.
Let the hammer bounce up, reset your grip and switch sides every few strikes.

name: Smith Back Shrug
desc: A shrug in the smith machine with the bar held behind your thighs instead of in front. Holding it behind pulls the shoulders slightly back, which shifts more work to the traps and upper back.
ins: Set the smith bar at about mid-thigh height and stand in front of it with your back to the bar.
Reach back and grab it with an overhand grip at shoulder-width, then unhook it.
Stand tall with your arms straight and the bar resting just behind your thighs.
Lift your shoulders straight up as high as you can.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Smith Behind Neck Press
desc: A seated press on the Smith machine where the bar is lowered behind your head. The guided bar adds stability, but the position still needs good shoulder mobility, so keep the weight light.
ins: Place an upright bench under the Smith bar so the bar runs just behind your head.
Sit tall, grip the bar wider than your shoulders and unrack it with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar behind your head to about ear level.
Breathe out and press it back up until your arms are straight.
Stop if you feel any pinching, and rack the bar by turning your wrists at the end.

name: Smith Bench Press
desc: A flat bench press done in a Smith machine, where the bar slides along fixed vertical tracks. The guided path makes it easy to learn and safer to train without a spotter.
ins: Place a flat bench under the Smith bar so the bar lines up with your mid-chest, then lie down.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and rotate it to unhook it.
Lower the bar slowly until it lightly touches your mid-chest.
Press it back up until your arms are straight, and rotate the bar to hook it when you finish.
Breathe in while lowering and out while pressing; set the safety stops just above chest level.

name: Smith Bent Knee Good Morning
desc: A good morning in the Smith machine with your knees clearly bent, hinging forward from the hips with the bar on your upper back. The guided bar and bent knees make it a stable way to train the glutes, hamstrings and lower back.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height, step under and rest it on your upper back.
Stand with your feet hip-width apart and unrack the bar.
Bend your knees noticeably and keep that bend throughout.
Push your hips back and lower your chest toward the floor with a flat back until your torso is near level.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand back up.
Breathe in as you hinge and out as you rise; rack the bar by turning it into the hooks.

name: Smith Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over row on the Smith machine. The fixed bar path helps you keep a steady line while you load the upper back.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and stand close to it.
Grip the bar overhand a little wider than shoulder width and unrack it.
Hinge at the hips with soft knees until your back is close to level, keeping it flat.
Pull the bar to your lower stomach and squeeze your shoulder blades together, breathing out.
Lower the bar slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Smith Chair Squat
desc: A Smith machine squat with your feet set slightly forward, sitting back as if into a chair until your thighs are parallel. The guided bar helps beginners keep a vertical shin and work the quads and glutes safely.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and rest it on your upper back.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart and a little in front of the bar.
Unrack the bar and brace your core.
Sit your hips back and down as if into a chair, keeping your shins close to vertical.
Stop when your thighs are parallel to the floor, then drive up through your heels.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise; rack the bar when done.

name: Smith Close-Grip Bench Press
desc: A close-grip bench press on a Smith machine. The fixed bar path lets you push hard with the triceps without worrying about balance.
ins: Set a flat bench under the Smith bar so it lines up with your lower chest.
Grip the bar a little narrower than shoulder width and unhook it by turning your wrists.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows tucked close.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight.
Re-hook the bar by turning your wrists at the end of the set.

name: Smith Deadlift
desc: A deadlift performed with the Smith machine bar, which moves on fixed rails. The guided path helps beginners learn the lift while working the glutes, hamstrings, quads and lower back.
ins: Set the Smith bar at its lowest safe position, around mid-shin, and stand close with your feet hip-width apart.
Hinge and bend your knees to grip the bar just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, lift your chest and brace.
Rotate the bar off the hooks and stand up by pushing through your feet and driving your hips forward.
Lower the bar by pushing your hips back, then bending your knees, until it is back at the start height.
Breathe out as you stand and in as you lower; hook the bar when finished.

name: Smith Decline Bench Press
desc: A decline bench press in a Smith machine that focuses on the lower chest. The fixed bar path lets you push hard with good stability.
ins: Set a decline bench under the Smith bar so the bar is over your lower chest, then secure your legs and lie back.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders and unhook it.
Lower it under control to your lower chest.
Press back up to straight arms without bouncing.
Exhale as you press and re-hook the bar before sitting up.

name: Smith Decline Reverse-Grip Press
desc: A decline Smith machine press using an underhand grip, palms facing you. The reverse grip keeps the elbows tucked and loads the lower chest and triceps.
ins: Lie on a decline bench under the Smith bar with your legs secured.
Grip the bar with palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart, and unhook it.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Press back up until your arms are extended.
Use a lighter weight than usual until you are comfortable with the grip, and breathe out on each press.

name: Smith Front Squat (clean Grip)
desc: A front squat on the Smith machine with the bar resting on the front of your shoulders in a clean-style grip. The upright torso puts the work on the glutes and quads, and the core has to stay braced.
ins: Set the bar at upper-chest height, step under it and rest it on the front of your shoulders.
Hold the bar with your fingertips just outside your shoulders and push your elbows forward and up.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly in front of the bar, then unhook it.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and sit straight down between your heels, keeping elbows high.
Go as low as you can with a straight back, then breathe out and drive up through your whole foot.
Rehook the bar when your set is done.

name: Smith Full Squat
desc: A full-depth back squat on the Smith machine. The guided bar path makes it easier to focus on going deep and staying balanced while the glutes and quads do the work, with help from the hamstrings and calves.
ins: Set the bar just below shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper back.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart, slightly in front of the bar, and unhook it.
Breathe in, brace your stomach and lower yourself by bending your knees and hips together.
Go down until your hips are below your knees, keeping your heels flat and back straight.
Breathe out and push up through your whole foot to standing.
Rehook the bar after the last rep.

name: Smith Hack Squat
desc: A Smith machine squat with a close stance and your feet set forward, leaning your back into the bar so your knees travel far forward. It mimics a hack squat and puts heavy focus on the quads, with the glutes assisting.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and rest it on your upper back.
Place your feet close together, about hip-width, and a step in front of the bar.
Unrack the bar, brace your core and lean your upper back into it.
Bend your knees and lower deep, letting your knees move forward while your torso stays upright.
Push through your whole foot to return to standing.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise; rack the bar at the end.

name: Smith Hip Raise
desc: A hip raise in the Smith machine with the bar across your hips and your upper back on a bench. It works the glutes and hamstrings while the abs keep your ribs and pelvis in line.
ins: Set a bench beside the Smith machine, sit on the floor with your upper back against the bench and the bar padded across your hips.
Plant your feet flat about shoulder width apart, knees bent, and hold the bar with both hands.
Brace your abs, tuck your chin slightly, and unhook the bar.
Breathe out and drive through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso are level.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower your hips slowly.

name: Smith Incline Reverse-Grip Press
desc: An incline Smith machine press with an underhand grip. The palms-up hand position tucks the elbows and shifts emphasis to the upper chest.
ins: Set an incline bench under the Smith bar and lie back with your feet flat.
Take an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart and unhook the bar.
Lower the bar to your upper chest with your elbows close to your body.
Press back up in a straight line.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows and breathe out on each press.

name: Smith Incline Shoulder Raises
desc: A small-range exercise on an incline bench in a Smith machine where you raise the bar using only your shoulder blades, arms kept straight. It strengthens the serratus muscles along the ribs and improves shoulder blade control.
ins: Set an incline bench under the Smith bar and lie back holding the bar with straight arms above your shoulders.
Lock your elbows and keep them locked for every rep.
Let your shoulder blades sink back so the bar lowers a short distance.
Push the bar up by spreading your shoulder blades and reaching your shoulders forward.
Pause at the top, lower slowly, and breathe out as you reach.

name: Smith Leg Press
desc: A leg press done lying on the floor under a Smith machine, pushing the bar up with the soles of your feet. It works the glutes and quads with your back fully supported, useful when no leg press machine is available.
ins: Set the Smith bar low and lie on your back under it on a mat, hips roughly below the bar.
Place the middle of both feet on the bar, shoulder-width apart, with your knees bent toward your chest.
Press the bar up a little and rotate it off the hooks with your hands, then hold the frame or rest your arms by your sides.
Lower the bar by bending your knees until they are near your chest, keeping your lower back on the floor.
Press through your heels to straighten your legs without locking your knees.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you press; set the safety stops before starting.

name: Smith Low Bar Squat
desc: A Smith machine squat with the bar sitting lower on the back, across the rear shoulders. The lower bar position lets you lean a little more and sit the hips back, so the glutes and hamstrings do more of the work along with the quads.
ins: Step under the bar and rest it across the back of your shoulders, just below the top of the traps.
Grip the bar wider than your shoulders and squeeze your shoulder blades together to make a shelf.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly forward, then unhook the bar.
Breathe in, brace, and push your hips back as you bend your knees, letting your chest tilt forward a little.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor while keeping your back flat.
Breathe out and drive your hips and shoulders up together to stand.

name: Smith Machine Bicep Curl
desc: A standing biceps curl using the Smith machine bar. The bar runs in a straight vertical track, so your elbows move slightly forward as you curl, and the hooks give a safe start and finish height.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height and grip it underhand at shoulder width.
Unhook the bar and stand tall, close to it, with your arms straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up toward your chest, letting your elbows travel slightly forward so the bar can rise straight up.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly, then rehook the bar when done.

name: Smith Machine Decline Close Grip Bench Press
desc: A close-grip bench press on a decline bench in a Smith machine. The narrow grip and fixed bar path focus on the triceps, with the lower chest and shoulders assisting.
ins: Set a decline bench under the Smith machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest, and lock your legs in.
Grip the bar with your hands about shoulder-width apart or slightly closer.
Unhook the bar and lower it to your lower chest, elbows tucked close to your sides.
Breathe out and press it up until your arms are straight.
Rotate the bar to re-hook it when your set is done.

name: Smith Machine Incline Tricep Extension
desc: A triceps extension performed on an incline bench in a Smith machine, lowering the bar toward your forehead with bent elbows. The guided bar lets you push the triceps hard with less balancing.
ins: Set an incline bench under the Smith machine so the bar travels over your upper face.
Grip the bar with your hands a little narrower than shoulder-width and unhook it with arms straight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows, letting them travel slightly forward, to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Stop a few centimeters above your head and keep your elbows narrow.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press the bar back up.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Decline Close Grip Bench Press
desc: A decline bench press on a Smith machine using a narrow, underhand grip. It works the lower chest and puts a heavy load on the triceps.
ins: Set a decline bench under the Smith bar so the bar lines up with your lower chest, then lie back with your feet hooked in.
Grip the bar with palms facing you and hands about shoulder-width or slightly narrower.
Unhook the bar and hold it over your lower chest with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly to your lower chest, keeping your elbows tucked close to your body.
Breathe out and press back up without letting your wrists bend back.
Rack the bar when you finish.

name: Smith Narrow Row
desc: A bent-over row in the smith machine using a narrow grip, with the bar on a fixed track. It trains the upper back and rear shoulders, with the biceps helping.
ins: Set the smith bar around knee height and stand close to it.
Grip the bar overhand with your hands a little narrower than your shoulders and unhook it.
Hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back until your chest is well forward.
Row the bar to your lower ribs, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Lower slowly to straight arms without changing your back angle.
Breathe out as you row and in as you lower.

name: Smith One Arm Row
desc: A one-arm row on the Smith machine, standing side-on to the bar. It works each side of the upper back separately.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and stand beside it.
Hinge forward with a flat back and place your free hand on your thigh or a bench.
Grip the middle of the bar with one hand and unrack it.
Pull the bar toward your hip, keeping your elbow close to your side, and breathe out.
Lower slowly to a straight arm.
Finish the set and switch sides.

name: Smith One Leg Floor Calf Raise
desc: A one-leg standing calf raise with the Smith bar across the back, done flat on the floor. The fixed bar path lets you load one calf heavily while staying balanced.
ins: Set the bar at shoulder height, step under it, and rest it across your upper back.
Unrack the bar and stand on one foot, hooking the other foot behind your ankle.
Keep your body tall and your standing knee straight but not locked.
Rise onto the ball of your foot as high as you can.
Hold for a second, then lower your heel slowly back to the floor.
Complete the set, rack the bar, and switch legs.

name: Smith Rear Delt Row
desc: A bent-over row on the Smith machine with a wide grip and flared elbows, pulled to the upper chest. The fixed bar path lets you focus on the rear shoulders and upper back.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and grip it with an overhand grip wider than your shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hinge forward with a flat back until your upper body is almost level with the floor.
Breathe out and pull the bar to your upper chest, keeping your elbows out wide.
Squeeze the back of your shoulders at the top.
Breathe in and lower the bar until your arms are straight.

name: Smith Reverse Calf Raises
desc: A calf raise done facing the Smith machine, holding the locked bar for balance while standing on a step. Using the bar for support lets you focus on a full, slow range for the calves.
ins: Lock the Smith bar at about chest height and place a step or plate just in front of it.
Face the bar, hold it with both hands, and put the balls of your feet on the edge of the step with your heels hanging off.
Let your heels sink below the step until you feel the calves stretch.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, using the bar only for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly; breathe out on the way up.

name: Smith Reverse Calf Raises (Bar on Front of Shoulders)
desc: A Smith machine calf raise with the bar held across the front of your shoulders instead of your back. Facing the bar keeps your torso upright and challenges the calves through a full range on a step.
ins: Set the Smith bar at upper-chest height and place a low step under it.
Stand facing the bar and rest it across the front of your shoulders, hands holding it lightly.
Place the balls of your feet on the step with your heels hanging off.
Unhook the bar and let your heels drop for a stretch.
Breathe out and rise as high as you can onto your toes, then pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly; rehook the bar when you finish.

name: Smith Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
desc: A bent-over Smith machine row with an underhand grip. It hits the upper back and gives extra work to the biceps.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and grip it with palms facing forward, shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hinge at the hips with soft knees and a flat back.
Pull the bar toward your belly button, elbows tucked in.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and breathe out.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Smith Reverse-Grip Press
desc: A flat bench press in a Smith machine using an underhand grip. It hits the chest, especially the upper part, while the tucked elbows bring the triceps in strongly.
ins: Lie on a flat bench under the Smith bar so it lines up with your lower chest.
Grip the bar underhand, palms facing your face, about shoulder-width apart, and unhook it.
Lower the bar to your lower chest with your elbows tucked in.
Press it back up until your arms are straight.
Start light while you learn the grip, and breathe out as you press.

name: Smith Seated One Leg Calf Raise
desc: A seated calf raise for one leg at a time, with the Smith bar resting on a padded knee. The bent knee shifts the work toward the deeper calf muscle.
ins: Place a bench under the Smith machine and a low step or plate in front of it.
Sit down, put the ball of one foot on the step, and lower the bar onto a pad across that thigh just above the knee.
Unrack the bar and let the heel drop below the step for a stretch.
Push through the ball of the foot to lift the bar as high as you can.
Squeeze at the top, lower slowly, and keep breathing steadily.
Rack the bar after the set and switch legs.

name: Smith Seated Shoulder Press
desc: A Smith machine shoulder press done sitting on a bench without leaning back, with the bar lowered in front of your face. It builds the shoulders and triceps on a guided path.
ins: Place a bench under the Smith bar so the bar comes down just in front of your face.
Sit tall, grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders and unrack it.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your upper chest or chin level.
Breathe out and press it straight up until your arms are straight.
Keep your back upright throughout and rack the bar when done.

name: Smith Seated Wrist Curl
desc: A seated wrist curl using the Smith machine bar, which stays on a fixed track. It strengthens the forearm flexors and grip with a stable, easy-to-load bar.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about knee height and place a bench in front of it.
Sit down and grab the bar with palms facing up, resting your forearms on your thighs and your wrists past your knees.
Unhook the bar and let it lower toward your fingertips.
Curl your wrists up as high as you can, keeping your forearms flat on your thighs.
Pause, then lower slowly; breathe out as you curl.
Rotate the bar to hook it back on the rack when the set is done.

name: Smith Shoulder Press
desc: A Smith machine shoulder press done with your back supported on an upright bench. The back pad and guided bar let you push the shoulders hard with little need for balance.
ins: Set a bench with a backrest almost upright under the Smith bar.
Sit with your back against the pad, grip the bar just wider than your shoulders and unrack it.
Breathe in and lower the bar until it is level with your chin.
Breathe out and press it up until your arms are straight.
Keep your lower back on the pad and rack the bar at the end of the set.

name: Smith Shrug
desc: A shrug in the smith machine with the bar in front of your thighs, where the fixed track lets you focus only on lifting the shoulders. It builds the upper traps.
ins: Set the smith bar at mid-thigh height and stand facing it.
Grab it overhand just outside your thighs and unhook it.
Stand tall with straight arms and your chest up.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Smith Sprint Lunge
desc: A Smith machine lunge that finishes in a sprinter's position: from the bottom of a split squat you drive up onto the front leg and bring the back knee forward to hip height. It builds single-leg strength and drive in the glutes and quads.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height, rest it on your upper back and unrack it.
Take a split stance with one foot forward and the other back on the ball of the foot.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor.
Drive through the front heel to stand and, in the same motion, bring the back knee forward and up to hip height.
Pause briefly balanced on one leg, then step the foot back into the split stance.
Breathe out as you drive up; finish one side before switching.

name: Smith Squat
desc: A back squat performed in the Smith machine, where the bar travels on fixed rails. It is a stable way for beginners to load the glutes and quads.
ins: Set the bar just below shoulder height and step under so it rests across your upper back.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart, slightly in front of the bar, toes turned a little out.
Unrack the bar by rotating it off the hooks and brace your core.
Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up.
Push through your feet to stand back up.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise; rotate the bar back onto the hooks when done.

name: Smith Standing Back Wrist Curl
desc: A behind-the-back wrist curl using the Smith machine bar, which moves on a fixed track. It isolates the forearm flexors and lets you handle a heavier load safely.
ins: Set the Smith bar at about mid-thigh height and stand with your back to it.
Reach behind you and grip the bar with palms facing backward, hands shoulder-width apart.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with your arms straight.
Let the bar roll toward your fingers so your wrists open.
Breathe out and curl the bar up by bending your wrists, keeping your arms still.
Lower slowly, then rehook the bar when the set is done.

name: Smith Standing Behind Head Military Press
desc: A standing military press on the Smith machine with the bar lowered behind your head. It hits the side and front shoulders hard and needs good mobility, so use a light weight.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and stand with the bar behind your head, feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar wider than your shoulders and unrack it.
Brace your stomach and press the bar up until your arms are straight, breathing out.
Breathe in and lower it behind your head to about ear level.
Keep your head slightly forward and stop if your shoulders pinch.

name: Smith Standing Military Press
desc: A standing military press on the Smith machine with the bar in front of your face. The guided path helps you press heavy with steady form.
ins: Set the Smith bar at upper chest height and stand facing it with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar just outside shoulder width and unrack it at your upper chest.
Brace your stomach, squeeze your glutes and press up until your arms are straight, breathing out.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your upper chest.
Stand still without bending your knees to help.

name: Smith Sumo Squat
desc: A wide-stance squat on the Smith machine with the toes turned out. The sumo stance shifts more work to the glutes and inner thighs while the quads and hamstrings still help, and the fixed track makes it easy to learn.
ins: Set the bar at shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper back.
Place your feet well wider than shoulder-width with toes turned out about 45 degrees.
Unhook the bar and brace your stomach.
Breathe in and lower straight down, pushing your knees out over your toes.
Go until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, then breathe out and drive up through your heels.
Rehook the bar after your last rep.

name: Smith Toe Raise
desc: A standing calf raise with both feet flat on the floor and the Smith bar across the upper back. It strengthens the calves and the small muscles that steady the ankle.
ins: Set the bar just below shoulder height, step under it, and rest it on your upper back.
Unrack the bar and stand with your feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Keep your knees straight but soft and your core tight.
Rise up onto your toes, pressing evenly through the big and little toe.
Hold briefly, then lower your heels slowly to the floor.
Breathe out as you rise and in as you lower.

name: Smith Upright Row
desc: An upright row on the Smith machine. The fixed path makes it easy to focus on lifting with your elbows to work the side shoulders and traps.
ins: Set the Smith bar at mid-thigh height and grip it with an overhand grip about shoulder width.
Unrack it and stand tall with the bar against your thighs.
Breathe out and lift your elbows up and out to bring the bar toward your chest.
Stop when your elbows reach shoulder height.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly.

name: Smith Wide Grip Bench Press
desc: A flat bench press on a Smith machine using a grip wider than shoulder-width. The guided bar and wide hands put the emphasis on the chest.
ins: Place a flat bench under the Smith bar so the bar lines up with your mid-chest, and lie back with your feet flat.
Grip the bar about one and a half times shoulder-width and pull your shoulder blades together.
Twist the bar to unhook it and hold it over your chest with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar to your mid-chest under control.
Breathe out and press it back up, stopping just before your elbows lock.
Twist the bar back onto the hooks when the set is done.

name: Smith Wide Grip Decline Bench Press
desc: A decline bench press on a Smith machine with a wide grip. The decline angle and wide hands focus the work on the lower chest.
ins: Set a decline bench under the Smith bar so the bar is over your lower chest, then lie back with your feet hooked in.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder-width and set your shoulder blades back and down.
Unhook the bar and hold it over your lower chest with straight arms.
Breathe in and lower the bar slowly until it lightly touches your lower chest.
Breathe out and press it back up, keeping your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Rack the bar before sitting up.

name: Snatch Pull
desc: A pulling drill for the snatch: you lift the barbell from the floor with a wide grip and finish with a violent hip extension and shrug, without catching it overhead. It builds pulling power in the quads, hamstrings, glutes and upper back.
ins: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and grip it wide, with hands far enough apart that the bar would sit in your hip crease when standing.
Set your hips lower than in a deadlift, chest up, back flat and arms straight.
Push the floor away and lift the bar smoothly past your knees, keeping it close.
As it reaches your upper thighs, extend your hips, knees and ankles explosively and shrug your shoulders up.
Keep your arms long; let the bar float, then lower it back to the floor with control.
Brace before each pull and breathe out after the finish.

name: Spell Caster
desc: A standing dumbbell move where you sweep both weights from one hip across your body to the other in a rotating arc, as if casting a spell. It trains the obliques and abs, with the lower back controlling the turn.
ins: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart, holding a light dumbbell in each hand beside your right hip.
Brace your abs and keep your knees soft.
Rotate to the left, sweeping both dumbbells up across your body to about shoulder height on the left side.
Let your right foot pivot as your hips turn.
Bring the dumbbells back to your left hip, then sweep them across to the right side.

name: Sphinx
desc: A gentle back bend lying face down and propped on the forearms. It eases the spine into extension and is a good warm-up for the lower back.
ins: Lie face down on a mat with your legs straight and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Place your elbows under your shoulders and your forearms flat on the floor.
Press through your forearms to lift your chest, keeping your hips on the mat.
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears and relax your glutes.
Breathe slowly and hold for 20 to 40 seconds, then lower down.

name: Spider Crawl Push Up
desc: A push-up where you bring one knee up toward the elbow on the same side as you lower, like a crawling spider. It works the chest and arms and adds hip mobility and core work, with the glutes stabilizing.
ins: Start in a high plank with your hands a little wider than your shoulders.
As you bend your elbows to lower, lift one foot and bring that knee out to the side toward the same elbow.
Keep the knee off the floor and your hips low and level.
Press back up and return the foot to the plank.
Repeat with the other knee on the next push-up.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you press.

name: Spin Back Kick
desc: A powerful spinning kick where you turn your back and drive the heel straight back into the target. It works the glutes and hamstrings hard and needs core control to stay balanced through the turn.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your left foot forward and guard up.
Turn on the front foot and spin backward, looking over your right shoulder at the target.
Bring your right knee up close to your chest as you turn.
Drive the heel straight back toward the target, keeping the foot flat and the toes pointing down.
Pull the leg back in, finish the turn and land facing forward in your stance.
Repeat, then practise on the other side.

name: Spin Hook Kick
desc: An advanced spinning kick: you turn your back to the target and whip the heel around in a hooking arc. It demands strong glutes, hamstrings and core plus very good balance and coordination.
ins: Stand in a fighting stance with your left foot forward and hands up.
Turn on the ball of your front foot and spin your body backward, looking over your right shoulder.
As you turn, lift your right leg and extend it outward.
Keep spinning and bend the knee to whip the heel through the target.
Finish the turn and land back in your stance, facing forward.
Practise slowly first, then add speed.

name: Spine Stretch
desc: A seated stretch where you round the spine forward over straight legs. It mobilises the back and stretches the hamstrings and glutes.
ins: Sit tall on a mat with your legs straight and a little wider than hip-width.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height.
Breathe out and roll forward one part of your spine at a time, starting with your head.
Reach toward your feet while pulling your stomach in.
Breathe in and roll back up slowly to sitting tall.

name: Spine Twist
desc: A seated mobility exercise where you rotate your upper body from side to side while sitting tall. It loosens the spine and trains the obliques and lower back to control rotation.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you, toes pointing up, a little wider than hip-width.
Sit up tall and stretch your arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Breathe out and turn your upper body to one side, keeping your hips still and your arms in line with your shoulders.
Breathe in and come back to the center, growing taller.
Turn to the other side, alternating smoothly.

name: Split Squats
desc: A stationary lunge where you keep your feet in a split stance and move straight up and down. It builds the quads and glutes one leg at a time, with the hamstrings and calves helping you balance.
ins: Stand tall and take a long step forward with your right foot, back heel lifted.
Put your hands on your hips and keep your chest up.
Breathe in and lower straight down until your back knee is just above the floor.
Keep your front knee over your ankle and your weight in the front heel.
Breathe out and push up through the front foot without moving your feet.
Finish the set, then switch the front leg.

name: Squat (Bodyweight)
desc: The basic bodyweight squat, the foundation of most leg training. It builds the quads and glutes, with the hamstrings helping, and teaches the pattern for every loaded squat.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out slightly.
Hold your arms out in front of you or clasp your hands at your chest.
Breathe in and sit your hips back and down as if lowering onto a chair.
Keep your heels down, chest up and knees in line with your toes as you go below parallel if you can.
Breathe out and push through your whole foot to stand up.

name: Squat Jerk
desc: An Olympic overhead lift where you drive the barbell up from your shoulders and catch it at arm's length in a full squat, then stand. It demands leg power from the quads and glutes plus strong, mobile shoulders and core.
ins: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders with a full grip, feet hip-width apart.
Take a breath, brace and dip a short distance straight down by bending your knees.
Drive up hard through your legs to launch the bar off your shoulders.
Push yourself down under the bar into a deep squat as your arms lock out overhead.
Stabilize with the bar over the middle of your feet, then stand up with it.
Lower the bar to your shoulders with control, breathing out once it is secured.

name: Squat On Bosu Ball
desc: A bodyweight squat performed on an unstable BOSU, flat side up. The wobble makes the quads, glutes and the small stabilizing muscles around the ankles and knees work harder to keep you balanced.
ins: Place the BOSU flat side up and step onto it carefully, feet near the outer edges.
Find your balance with your arms reaching forward and your stomach tight.
Breathe in and sit your hips back and down into a squat, keeping the platform level.
Go only as low as you can stay steady, with knees in line with your toes.
Breathe out and push through your heels to stand, then step off carefully when finished.

name: Squat To Overhead Reach
desc: A bodyweight squat that finishes with the arms reaching overhead, linking the lower and upper body. It warms up the quads, glutes and hamstrings and opens the shoulders and upper back.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and toes turned out a little.
Sit down into a deep squat, keeping your heels down and your chest up.
At the bottom, place your elbows inside your knees for a moment to open the hips.
Breathe in and raise both arms overhead as you stay low, lifting your chest.
Breathe out and stand up while keeping the arms reaching high, then lower them and repeat.

name: Squat To Overhead Reach With Twist
desc: A deep bodyweight squat with an overhead reach and a twist of the upper body to each side. It mobilizes the hips, quads and hamstrings and adds rotation for the upper back and core.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down as deep as you comfortably can.
Keep your heels flat and rest your left hand on the floor in front of you.
Rotate your chest to the right and reach your right arm up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Bring the arm back down, then twist to the left and reach the left arm up.
Return to the middle and stand up with both arms reaching overhead, breathing out as you rise.

name: Stability Ball Crunch (full Range Hands Behind Head)
desc: A crunch done lying back over a stability ball, which lets your spine extend backward before you curl up, giving a longer range than a floor crunch. It targets the abs, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Sit on a stability ball and walk your feet forward until your lower and middle back rest on it, feet flat and wide apart.
Rest your fingertips behind your head with your elbows open.
Breathe in and let your upper back extend back over the ball for a gentle stretch.
Breathe out and curl your chest up toward your hips, squeezing your abs without pulling your neck.
Lower slowly back over the ball to the stretched position.

name: Stalder Press
desc: An advanced gymnastics press that lifts you from a straddle seat on the floor into a handstand with straight arms. It requires very strong triceps and shoulders, along with core control and flexibility.
ins: Sit on the floor with your legs straight and wide apart, and place your palms on the floor between your legs.
Lean your shoulders forward over your hands and press down hard to lift your hips off the floor.
Keep your arms straight and keep shifting forward while lifting your hips higher than your shoulders.
Once your hips are over your hands, raise your straddled legs slowly up and bring them together into a handstand.
Lower back down the same way with control; practice the parts against a wall until you have the strength.

name: Standing Archer
desc: A standing mobility drill that copies drawing a bow, rotating the upper body as one arm reaches forward and the other pulls back. It opens the upper back and shoulders.
ins: Stand with your feet a little wider than your hips and knees soft.
Reach both arms straight forward at shoulder height.
Turn your upper body to one side while pulling that elbow back as if drawing a bow, the other arm staying straight.
Follow your back hand with your eyes and breathe out as you turn.
Return to the centre and repeat to the other side, alternating.

name: Standing Behind Neck Press
desc: A standing barbell press where the bar is lowered behind your head. It works the side and front shoulders hard and is only for lifters with good shoulder mobility.
ins: Take a barbell from a rack onto your upper back, gripping it wider than your shoulders.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and brace your stomach.
Breathe out and press the bar straight up until your arms are straight.
Breathe in and lower it behind your head to about ear level.
Use a light weight and stop if you feel pinching in the shoulder.

name: Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
desc: The basic standing calf raise with a barbell on your back. It builds strength and size in the calves and improves ankle power for running and jumping.
ins: Rest a barbell across your upper back and stand with feet hip-width apart, toes on a low step.
Brace your stomach and keep your chest up.
Let your heels drop slightly below the step.
Breathe out and press through your big toes to raise your heels as high as possible.
Pause at the top and squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly without letting the bar shift.

name: Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
desc: A standing calf raise holding a dumbbell in each hand. It is an easy-to-set-up way to strengthen the calves and ankles.
ins: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and stand on the edge of a step with your heels off.
Stand tall with your shoulders back and knees slightly soft.
Lower your heels until your calves stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause for a second at the top.
Breathe in and lower slowly; lightly touch a wall if you need balance.

name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
desc: A calf raise on a standing calf machine with shoulder pads carrying the load. The straight-leg position works the main calf muscle hard.
ins: Set the shoulder pads so you have to bend your knees slightly to get under them.
Step in, place the balls of your feet on the platform and rest the pads on your shoulders.
Straighten your legs to lift the weight, keeping knees soft.
Lower your heels until the calves are fully stretched.
Breathe out and drive up onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in and lower slowly without bouncing.

name: Standing Calf Raise (on A Staircase)
desc: A bodyweight calf raise on the edge of a stair, which lets the heels drop below the step for a longer range of motion.
ins: Stand on the bottom stair facing up, holding the rail for balance.
Slide back so only the balls of your feet are on the step.
Let your heels sink below the step until the calves stretch.
Push up onto your toes as high as you can.
Pause, then lower slowly through the full range; breathe out on the way up.

name: Standing Calf Raise (Smith Machine)
desc: A standing calf raise using the Smith machine bar across your back. The fixed track removes the need to balance, so you can focus on the calves.
ins: Set the Smith bar at shoulder height and place a low block or plate under it.
Step under the bar, rest it across your upper back and put the balls of your feet on the block.
Unhook the bar and stand tall with knees straight but soft.
Lower your heels until you feel a stretch in the calves.
Breathe out and push up onto your toes as high as you can, then pause.
Breathe in, lower slowly, and rehook the bar after the set.

name: Standing Calves
desc: The basic calf raise with no added weight, standing on flat ground. A good starting point for calf strength and ankle control.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart; lightly touch a wall if you need balance.
Tighten your stomach and keep your knees straight but not locked.
Push through the balls of your feet and lift your heels as high as you can.
Hold the top for a second without letting your ankles roll outward.
Lower your heels slowly back to the floor and repeat.

name: Standing Calves Calf Stretch
desc: A standing stretch for the calf that props the toes up against the base of a wall. It lengthens the calf muscle and the tissue behind the ankle.
ins: Stand facing a wall about a foot away.
Place the ball of one foot up against the wall with the heel on the floor.
Keep that leg straight and slowly move your hips toward the wall.
Stop when you feel a clear pull in the calf and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Breathe slowly, step back, and switch sides.

name: Standing Hamstring And Calf Stretch With Strap
desc: A standing stretch that uses a strap around the front of the foot to pull the toes toward you as you lean forward. It stretches the hamstrings and the calf of the same leg at once.
ins: Stand tall and place your right heel about half a step in front of you with the leg straight.
Loop a strap around the ball of your right foot and hold both ends.
Bend your left knee slightly and push your hips back.
Pull the strap gently so your right toes come up toward you.
Keep your back flat and hold for 20 to 30 seconds when you feel the stretch behind the thigh and in the calf.
Switch legs.

name: Standing Lateral Stretch
desc: A standing side bend with one arm reaching overhead to stretch the side of the body. It lengthens the lats and obliques and loosens the shoulders.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your knees soft.
Raise your right arm straight overhead and rest your left hand on your hip.
Lean slowly to the left, reaching your right arm up and over.
Keep your hips centred and avoid leaning forward or back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing slowly, then return to standing.
Switch arms and stretch the other side.

name: Standing Pelvic Tilt
desc: A standing drill where you rock the pelvis forward and back. It teaches control of the lower back and wakes up the stomach muscles.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, knees soft and hands on your hips.
Tighten your stomach and tuck your tailbone under so your lower back flattens.
Then tip your pelvis the other way so your lower back arches slightly.
Move slowly and keep your chest and shoulders still.
Breathe steadily and repeat for 10 to 15 slow rocks.

name: Standing Single Leg Curl
desc: A standing body-weight hamstring curl where you bend one knee to bring your heel toward your glutes. It is a simple beginner exercise for the hamstrings that can be made harder with an ankle weight.
ins: Stand tall holding a wall or chair for balance, feet hip-width apart.
Shift your weight onto one leg with a soft knee.
Keeping your thighs side by side, bend the other knee and bring your heel up toward your glutes.
Squeeze the back of your thigh at the top without letting the knee move forward.
Lower the foot slowly to just above the floor.
Breathe out as you curl; finish your reps, then switch legs.

name: Standing Wheel Rollerout
desc: An ab wheel rollout started from standing, one of the hardest anti-extension core exercises. It needs very strong abs plus stable shoulders and lower back.
ins: Stand with your feet hip width apart and hold the ab wheel with both hands.
Bend forward and place the wheel on the floor in front of your feet, keeping your knees straight or barely bent.
Brace hard and roll the wheel forward slowly, letting your body lengthen toward the floor.
Stop at the furthest point you can hold without your lower back sagging.
Pull the wheel back toward your feet using your abs, breathing out as you return.

name: Star Jump
desc: An explosive jump from a squat in which the arms and legs spread wide into a star shape in the air. It builds leg power and works the whole body as cardio.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart and drop into a quarter squat with your hands near your knees.
Jump up as high as you can.
In the air, spread your arms and legs wide so your body forms an X.
Bring your legs back together before landing and land softly with bent knees.
Reset into the squat and jump again; breathe out as you explode up.

name: Stationary Bike Run
desc: Steady cycling on a stationary bike for low-impact cardio. It raises the heart rate while working the thighs and calves without pounding the joints.
ins: Set the seat so your knee is only slightly bent when the pedal is at the bottom.
Sit tall, hold the handlebars lightly, and strap your feet in if the pedals have straps.
Warm up for a few minutes at an easy pace and low resistance.
Raise the resistance or speed to a level where you can still talk in short sentences.
Keep your hips still on the seat and push through the whole pedal circle.
Ease off for the last few minutes to cool down before stopping.

name: Stationary Bike Walk
desc: Easy, low-resistance pedaling on a stationary bike at a walking-like effort. It is a gentle way to warm up, recover or build basic endurance.
ins: Adjust the seat so your knee stays slightly bent when the pedal is at its lowest point.
Sit tall, hold the handlebars lightly and strap your feet in if the pedals have straps.
Set a low resistance and start pedaling at a relaxed, steady speed.
Push through the middle of your foot and keep your knees in line with your toes.
Breathe easily; you should be able to hold a normal conversation.
Keep going for the planned time, then slow down gradually.

name: Stepdown Squat
desc: A single-leg squat done standing on a step, slowly lowering the other heel toward the floor. It builds quad and glute strength and knee control, and is often used in knee rehab and training.
ins: Stand on a low step on your right foot with the left foot hanging off the side.
Put your hands on your hips or reach them forward for balance.
Breathe in and bend the right knee slowly, pushing your hips back, until the left heel lightly touches the floor.
Keep the right knee in line with your toes; do not let it cave inward.
Breathe out and push through the right foot to straighten back up.
Finish the set, then switch legs.

name: Stiff Leg Deadlift (Barbell)
desc: A deadlift done with your legs almost straight, lowering the barbell toward the floor by hinging at the hips. It targets the hamstrings hard and also works the glutes and lower back.
ins: Hold the bar at your thighs with an overhand grip, feet hip-width apart.
