Keep your legs nearly straight with just a slight softness in the knees.
Push your hips back and lower the bar close to your legs, keeping your back flat.
Go down until your hamstrings are fully stretched or the bar is near your feet, without rounding your back.
Pull back up by driving your hips forward and squeezing your glutes.
Breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.

name: Stiff Leg Deadlift (Dumbbell)
desc: A deadlift with dumbbells and your knees kept almost straight, reaching the weights low toward your feet. It gives the hamstrings a deep stretch and works the glutes and lower back.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Straighten your legs, leaving only a slight bend in the knees, and keep it fixed.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells in front of your legs toward your feet.
Keep your back flat and go only as low as your hamstring flexibility allows.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand up.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise.

name: Straddle Maltese
desc: An elite strength hold where you support your body level with and just above the floor or rings, with your arms spread wide and your legs straddled. It puts extreme demands on the abs, shoulders and chest.
ins: Place your hands on parallettes or hold rings, arms straight and set much wider than your shoulders.
Turn your hands slightly out, lock your elbows and tighten your whole body.
Lean forward and lift your legs, spreading them wide as your body lowers toward horizontal.
Hold your body flat and close to hand level, abs and glutes tight, breathing steadily.
Lower your feet with control. Only attempt this after mastering the straddle planche.

name: Straddle Planche
desc: An advanced hold where you balance your body horizontally above the floor on straight arms, with your legs spread wide. Spreading the legs shortens the lever compared with the full version; it builds huge strength in the abs, shoulders, chest and triceps.
ins: Place your hands on the floor or on parallettes about shoulder-width apart, fingers turned slightly out.
Lock your elbows, push the floor away and round your upper back slightly.
Lean your shoulders forward past your hands until your feet become light.
Lift your legs off the floor, spread them wide and straighten your body until it is level with the floor.
Tighten your abs and glutes to stop your hips from sagging, hold while breathing steadily, then lower your feet with control.

name: Straight Leg Deadlift (Band)
desc: A hip hinge with a resistance band under your feet, keeping the legs nearly straight to stretch the back of the thighs. It strengthens the lower back muscles along the spine, the hamstrings and the glutes.
ins: Stand on the middle of a band with your feet hip-width apart and hold the ends in front of your thighs.
Keep your legs almost straight with only a slight knee bend.
Push your hips back and lower your hands down your legs with a flat back.
Go down until you feel a strong pull behind your thighs, without rounding your back.
Squeeze your glutes and drive your hips forward to stand tall.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand.

name: Straight Leg Hip Bridge
desc: A hip bridge with the legs straight and heels on the floor, lifting the body into a straight plank-like line. It puts most of the work on the hamstrings, with the glutes, abs and calves helping.
ins: Lie on your back with legs straight, heels on the floor and toes pointing up.
Cross your arms over your chest or rest them by your sides.
Tighten your stomach and breathe out as you dig your heels into the floor to lift your hips.
Rise until your body is straight from shoulders to heels, without bending your knees.
Hold for a second, then breathe in and lower slowly.

name: Straight Leg Outer Hip Abductor
desc: A side-lying leg raise with a straight leg that strengthens the outer hip and thigh. It also brings in the glutes, which help keep the pelvis steady when you walk and run.
ins: Lie on your side with both legs straight and stacked, head resting on your lower arm.
Place your top hand on the floor in front of your chest for balance.
Point your top toes slightly forward and keep the leg straight.
Breathe out and raise the top leg toward the ceiling, leading with the heel, without rolling your hips back.
Lower it slowly to just above the bottom leg, then finish the set and switch sides.

name: Strongman Car Flip
desc: A strongman event where you lift one side of a car frame or similar heavy object from the ground and push it over onto its side. It is a maximal full-body effort for the glutes, legs, back, traps and grip.
ins: Stand close to the edge of the frame with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down to grip under it.
Set your back flat, chest up, and take a big breath to brace.
Drive through your legs and hips to lift the edge off the ground.
As it rises, step in, switch to a pushing grip and keep driving it upward.
Push it past its balance point until it tips over, breathing out as you push.
Reset your feet and grip before the next flip.

name: Strongman Fingal's Fingers
desc: A strongman event where you lift the free end of a long hinged pole and push it up and over until it tips to the other side. It is driven by the glutes and legs and also loads the shoulders, traps and grip.
ins: Stand at the free end of the pole with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down to grip under it.
Brace your stomach and keep your back flat.
Drive up with your legs and hips to lift the end of the pole to chest height.
Quickly switch your hands under it and press it overhead.
Walk forward under the pole, pushing it higher until it passes upright and falls the other way.
Move to the other side, reset and repeat.

name: Strongman Keg Toss
desc: A strongman throw where you swing a weighted keg between your legs and launch it up and back over your head. It builds explosive hip power through the glutes and hamstrings, with the shoulders, traps and abs helping.
ins: Make sure the area behind you is completely clear, then stand with feet shoulder-width apart, the keg between your feet.
Bend your knees and hinge at the hips with a flat back to grip the keg by its handles or rims.
Swing it back between your legs to load your hips.
Drive your hips forward and stand up explosively, pulling the keg up past your face with straight arms.
Let go when it is above your head so it flies up and back over you.
Breathe out hard on the throw, then turn to watch where it lands before the next rep.

name: Superman Push-Up
desc: An explosive push-up where you push off so hard that your hands and feet leave the floor, briefly stretching your arms forward like a flying superhero. It builds power in the chest and shoulders and needs a strong core.
ins: Start in a push-up position with your body straight and stomach braced.
Lower your chest quickly toward the floor.
Push up explosively, driving through your hands and toes so your whole body leaves the ground.
While in the air, shoot your arms forward and your legs slightly back.
Bring your hands and feet back under you and land softly with bent elbows, breathing out on each push.

name: Suspended Abdominal Fallout
desc: A standing rollout on a suspension trainer where you lean forward and let your arms travel overhead while your body stays straight. It challenges the abs and obliques to stop your back from arching.
ins: Set the suspension straps at about waist height and stand facing away from the anchor, holding the handles in front of you.
Step back so you lean slightly forward with your arms straight and your body in one line.
Brace your abs and let your arms rise overhead as your body leans further toward the floor.
Go only as far as you can keep your hips from sagging.
Press the straps down and back to pull yourself to the start, breathing out on the way up.

name: Suspended Push-Up
desc: A push-up with your hands holding the handles of suspension straps, which swing freely. The instability makes the chest, triceps, shoulders and core work much harder to control the movement.
ins: Set the straps to hang about knee to mid-shin height, grip the handles and walk your feet back into a leaning plank.
Hold your arms straight under your shoulders and brace your stomach.
Lower your chest between your hands, keeping the straps from flaring out to the sides.
Press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your body rigid and breathe out as you press; walk your feet forward to make it easier.

name: Suspended Reverse Crunch
desc: A reverse crunch done in a plank with your feet in suspension straps, pulling your knees to your chest. It works the lower abs and hip flexors while your shoulders and core keep you stable.
ins: Put your feet in the foot cradles of a suspension trainer and walk your hands out into a high plank.
Brace your abs so your body is straight from head to heels.
Breathe out and pull your knees in toward your chest, rounding your lower back slightly.
Extend your legs back slowly to the plank without letting your hips drop.
Keep your hands under your shoulders throughout.

name: Suspended Row
desc: A row using rings or suspension straps where you pull your body toward your hands while keeping it straight. It builds the upper back and challenges the shoulders and core, with the biceps assisting.
ins: Set the rings or straps at about chest height and hold one in each hand.
Lean back with straight arms and walk your feet forward until your body is angled.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so your body stays in a straight line.
Pull yourself up until your hands are beside your chest, elbows driving back.
Lower slowly to straight arms; lower the angle to make it harder.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the way down.

name: Swimmer Kicks (Face Down)
desc: A face-down exercise where you lift your chest and legs off the floor and flutter-kick the legs in small, fast movements. It works the glutes and the whole back of the body, with the hamstrings and calves helping.
ins: Lie face down on a mat with your arms stretched out in front of you.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your chest, arms and legs slightly off the floor.
Keep your legs straight and kick them up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
Keep your neck long by looking at the floor just ahead of you.
Breathe steadily and continue for the set time, then lower everything to the floor and rest.

name: Swing 360
desc: A standing drill that swings the arms in big circles while the torso turns with them. It warms up the shoulders and spine and lightly raises the heart rate.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Raise your arms in front of you at shoulder height.
Swing both arms in a wide circle to one side, letting your torso and hips turn with them.
Let your heels pivot naturally so your knees and lower back are not twisted.
Keep the motion smooth and continuous, breathing freely, then switch direction.

name: Three Bench Dip
desc: An advanced dip using three benches: two parallel benches for your hands and a third in front for your heels. The raised feet and deeper range make the triceps carry more of your bodyweight.
ins: Place two benches side by side about shoulder-width apart and a third in front of them.
Put one hand on each of the side benches and your heels on the front bench with legs straight.
Lower your body by bending your elbows straight back until they reach about a right angle.
Keep your torso upright and shoulders down.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Tire Flip
desc: Flipping a heavy tire end over end by driving it up from the ground and pushing it over. It is a full-body power exercise led by the glutes and legs, with the hamstrings, quads, back and core all working hard.
ins: Stand close to the tire with feet shoulder-width apart and squat down to grip under the edge with palms up.
Put your chest against the tire, keep your back flat and brace your stomach.
Drive with your legs and hips to push the tire up and forward at an angle.
As it rises, step in and switch your hands to a palms-forward push position.
Push the tire over with your arms and body, breathing out hard.
Walk up to it and reset your stance for the next flip.

name: Toe Touch Sit (wall)
desc: A single-leg balance exercise near a wall where you sit your hips back on one leg and reach toward the toes of the other, lifted leg. It works the abs for balance and the legs and glutes for strength, with the upper back holding your posture.
ins: Stand with your back lightly touching a wall and your feet a short step in front of it.
Brace your abs, shift your weight onto one leg and lift the other straight out in front of you.
Sit your hips back and down on the standing leg while reaching both hands toward the toes of the lifted leg.
Keep your chest lifted and the standing knee pointing over your toes.
Push through the standing heel to rise, then finish your reps and switch legs.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
desc: A deadlift with a hexagonal trap bar, standing inside the frame and holding handles at your sides. The centered load makes it easier on the lower back and works the glutes, hamstrings and quads.
ins: Step into the middle of the trap bar with your feet hip-width apart.
Bend your hips and knees to grab the center of each handle.
Flatten your back, lift your chest and take a big breath to brace.
Push the floor away with your legs and stand up tall, keeping your arms straight.
Lower the bar by sitting your hips back and bending your knees until the plates touch the floor.
Breathe out at the top or after setting the bar down.

name: Treadmill Run
desc: Running on a treadmill at a steady pace or in intervals. It builds cardiovascular fitness and leg endurance with an easy-to-control speed.
ins: Step on with your feet on the side rails, clip on the safety key, and start the belt slowly.
Walk for a few minutes, then raise the speed to a light jog.
Run tall in the middle of the belt with short, light steps landing under your hips.
Keep your arms bent and swinging, and do not hold the rails while running.
Set the speed to an effort you can sustain, breathing in a steady rhythm.
Slow to a walk for a few minutes before stopping the belt.

name: Treadmill Walk
desc: Walking on a treadmill at a brisk pace. It is easy-to-control, low-impact cardio that suits beginners, warm-ups and recovery days.
ins: Stand on the side rails, attach the safety key, and start the belt at a slow speed.
Step onto the belt and begin walking near the middle.
Increase the speed to a brisk walk that raises your breathing.
Stand tall, swing your arms naturally, and avoid leaning on the rails.
Lower the speed for the last few minutes, then stop the belt before stepping off.

name: Triceps Dip
desc: A dip on parallel bars with the torso kept upright to focus on the triceps. It is one of the best bodyweight exercises for arm strength.
ins: Grip the parallel bars and press up so your arms are straight and your body hangs between them.
Keep your torso upright and your elbows pointing back.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower yourself until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Breathe out and press back up until your arms are straight.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid swinging your legs.

name: Triceps Dip (Assisted)
desc: A dip on the assisted dip machine done kneeling on the pad, where the counterweight takes part of your body weight. It lets beginners build triceps strength before doing full dips.
ins: Pick an assist weight on the stack, step up and kneel on the pad with your hands on the dip handles.
Straighten your arms so you start at the top with your chest up and shoulders down.
Bend your elbows and lower yourself slowly, keeping the elbows pointing back rather than out.
Stop when your upper arms are about level with the floor or your shoulders start to feel strained.
Breathe out and push the handles down until your arms are straight again.

name: Triceps Dip (bench Leg)
desc: A bench dip with your legs straight and heels on the floor, which puts more of your weight on your arms than the bent-knee version. It builds the triceps.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench, place your hands beside your hips and grip the edge.
Walk your feet out until your legs are straight and only your heels touch the floor, hips just in front of the bench.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your hips, keeping your back close to the bench.
Stop when your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Triceps Dip (between Benches)
desc: A dip with your hands on one bench and your heels resting on a second bench in front of you. Raising the feet makes it harder and loads the triceps more.
ins: Place two benches parallel, about a leg's length apart.
Sit on the edge of one with your hands beside your hips and rest your heels on the other bench, legs straight.
Slide your hips forward off the bench so your arms hold your weight.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor, back close to the bench.
Breathe out and push through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Triceps Dips Floor
desc: A dip done from the floor: sitting with your hands behind you, you lift and lower your hips by bending and straightening your arms. It is an easy way to train the triceps with no equipment.
ins: Sit on the floor with knees bent, feet flat and hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward you.
Press into your hands to lift your hips a little off the floor.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your hips toward the floor without touching down.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to lift back up.
Keep your elbows pointing back rather than out to the sides.

name: Triceps Extension
desc: The standard triceps pushdown on a high cable with a straight bar. It is a simple, joint-friendly way to build the triceps.
ins: Attach a straight bar to a high pulley and grab it overhand at about shoulder width.
Stand close with feet hip-width apart, knees soft and elbows tucked to your sides.
Breathe out and press the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Hold the bottom for a moment and squeeze.
Breathe in and let the bar come up to about chest height, keeping your elbows fixed.

name: Triceps Extension (Barbell)
desc: A standing overhead triceps extension with a barbell. It trains the triceps, especially the long head, and asks your core to keep you upright.
ins: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, brace your stomach and press a barbell overhead with a narrow overhand grip.
Keep your upper arms close to your ears.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower the bar behind your head.
Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.
Breathe out and straighten your arms to press the bar back up.

name: Triceps Extension (Cable)
desc: An overhead cable triceps extension with a rope, done standing with your back to the machine. It stretches and strengthens the long head of the triceps.
ins: Attach a rope to a low or mid pulley, grab the ends and turn away from the machine, bringing the rope over your head.
Take a staggered stance and lean forward slightly with your elbows pointing forward beside your head.
Breathe out and straighten your arms forward and up, spreading the rope at the end.
Keep your upper arms still; only your forearms move.
Breathe in and let your hands return behind your head under control.

name: Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
desc: A seated one-arm overhead triceps extension with a dumbbell. Sitting with back support keeps your torso still so the triceps of one arm do all the work.
ins: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in one hand straight overhead.
Keep the upper arm close to your head with the elbow pointing up.
Breathe in and bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Breathe out and straighten the arm back overhead.
Finish your reps, then switch arms.

name: Triceps Press
desc: A bodyweight triceps extension done leaning on a bench or bar: you bend your elbows to bring your head toward your hands, then press back by straightening your arms. It isolates the triceps without weights.
ins: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the edge of a sturdy bench or a bar set at about hip height.
Walk your feet back into an inclined plank with your body straight.
Breathe in and bend only your elbows, letting your forehead travel down toward the edge between your hands.
Keep your elbows pointing down and your body rigid.
Breathe out and press through your palms to straighten your arms and return.

name: Triceps Stretch
desc: A triceps stretch using a wall: with your elbow bent overhead and resting on the wall, you lean in to stretch the back of the arm and the shoulder.
ins: Stand facing a wall or the side of a door frame, about a step away.
Raise one arm, bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head, and rest the elbow on the wall above you.
Lean your chest gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch along the back of the arm.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly.
Ease off and repeat with the other arm.

name: Tuck Crunch
desc: A crunch where you lift your shoulders and pull your knees in at the same time so they meet over your stomach. It works the whole front of the abs, with help from the hip flexors.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your feet just off the floor, hands resting lightly behind your ears.
Tighten your abs and press your lower back into the mat.
Breathe out and lift your shoulders while drawing your knees toward your chest so they meet in the middle.
Squeeze your abs for a second at the top without pulling on your neck.
Breathe in and lower your shoulders and push your feet back out with control, keeping your feet off the floor.

name: Twin Handle Parallel Grip Lat Pulldown
desc: A lat pulldown using a close double handle with the palms facing each other. The neutral grip lets you pull strongly through a long range, working the lats with help from the biceps, rear shoulders and mid back.
ins: Attach the twin parallel handle to the high pulley and sit with your thighs secured.
Hold the handles with your palms facing each other and arms straight.
Lean back slightly and lift your chest.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest, elbows close and driving down.
Squeeze your back, then let the handle rise slowly.
Breathe out on the pull and in on the return.

name: Twist Hip Lift
desc: A glute bridge with a twist: from the top of the bridge you rotate your hips from side to side. It works the glutes and hamstrings and adds a strong demand on the obliques.
ins: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and arms spread out on the floor.
Breathe out and lift your hips into a bridge so your knees, hips and shoulders line up.
Keeping the hips up, slowly rotate them toward the right so the left hip lifts higher.
Return to the middle, then rotate toward the left.
Keep your glutes squeezed so your hips do not sag while you twist.
Lower your hips to the floor at the end of the set.

name: Twisted Leg Raise
desc: A floor exercise that combines a knee-in leg raise with a twist of the hips, sending your knees toward one side of your chest and then the other. It targets the obliques and lower abs, with the hip flexors assisting.
ins: Lie flat on your back with your arms spread wide on the floor for support.
Lift your legs with your knees bent so your feet hover just above the floor.
Breathe out and pull your knees in while rotating your hips, aiming your knees at one shoulder.
Breathe in and extend your legs back out to the hovering position.
Pull in again toward the opposite shoulder, keeping your upper back flat on the floor throughout.

name: Twisted Leg Raise (Bent Knees)
desc: A lying leg raise where you bring your bent knees up and rotate your hips toward one side, alternating sides each rep. It works the lower abs and the obliques, with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms out to the sides, palms pressing into the floor.
Tighten your abs and bend your knees as you lift your feet off the floor.
Breathe out and draw your knees up toward your chest while turning your hips so your knees angle toward one shoulder.
Lower your legs slowly back toward the floor without letting them touch down.
Lift again and turn the other way, alternating sides.

name: Two Toe Touch
desc: A standing forward bend reaching both hands toward your toes. It loosens the spine and stretches the hamstrings and glutes.
ins: Stand tall with your feet together or hip-width apart.
Raise your arms overhead and breathe in.
Breathe out and fold forward from the hips, reaching both hands toward your toes.
Keep your knees soft if you need to and let your head hang.
Pause for a moment, then roll up slowly to standing.

name: Upper Back Stretch
desc: A standing stretch where you clasp your hands in front and round your upper back. It loosens the muscles between and around the shoulder blades.
ins: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Interlace your fingers and push your palms forward at chest height.
Round your upper back and let your head drop gently between your arms.
Feel your shoulder blades spread apart and keep breathing slowly.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then relax.

name: Upward Facing Dog
desc: A yoga back bend lifting the chest from a face-down position with straight arms. It opens the chest and stretches the spine into extension.
ins: Lie face down with your legs straight and the tops of your feet on the mat.
Place your hands on the floor beside your lower ribs.
Breathe in and press your arms straight, lifting your chest and thighs off the floor.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears and look forward.
Hold for a few breaths, then lower down slowly.

name: V-Sit On Floor
desc: A harder variation of the L-sit where you lift your straight legs higher, so your body forms a V while you balance on your hands. It demands strong abs and hip flexors and good hamstring flexibility.
ins: Sit on the floor with legs straight and hands planted beside or slightly behind your hips.
Press down hard through straight arms to lift your hips off the floor.
Lean your shoulders back a little and raise your straight legs as high as you can toward your face.
Keep your knees locked and your abs pulled in, holding while breathing steadily.
Lower your legs and hips with control. Work from a solid L-sit before trying this.

name: Vertical Leg Raise (on Parallel Bars)
desc: A leg raise done while supported on your forearms or hands in a dip station or captain's chair, lifting your legs in front of you. It targets the lower abs with the hip flexors helping.
ins: Support yourself on the parallel bars or a captain's chair with your back against the pad and your legs hanging straight.
Push your shoulders down away from your ears and brace your abs.
Breathe out and raise your straight legs until they are level with your hips, or higher if you can curl your pelvis up.
Lower your legs slowly without swinging.
Bend your knees to make it easier if needed.

name: Walk Elliptical Cross Trainer
desc: Walking on an elliptical cross trainer, where the feet move in a smooth oval and the arms push and pull the handles. It gives full-body cardio with very little impact on the knees.
ins: Step onto the pedals one foot at a time while holding the fixed handles.
Start striding slowly, then take hold of the moving handles.
Stand upright and keep your whole foot on the pedal instead of rising onto your toes.
Push and pull the handles in rhythm with your legs.
Choose a resistance that makes you breathe harder but still lets you talk.
Slow down gradually before stepping off.

name: Walk Wave Machine
desc: Walking on a wave machine, a cardio machine whose pedals swing side to side. It raises the heart rate and works the hips and inner and outer thighs along with the legs.
ins: Set a low resistance and a small stride on the console.
Step onto the pedals with feet centered and hold the handles lightly.
Start a smooth side-to-side stepping rhythm, pressing through your whole foot.
Keep your knees in line with your toes and your hips facing forward.
Stand tall with relaxed shoulders and breathe in a steady rhythm.
Increase speed or resistance gradually, and slow down for the last minutes.

name: Walking (outdoor)
desc: Brisk walking outdoors, the simplest form of cardio. It improves heart health and endurance and gently works the legs and glutes.
ins: Wear supportive shoes and pick a safe route.
Stand tall with your shoulders relaxed and eyes looking ahead.
Start at an easy pace for a few minutes to warm up.
Pick up to a brisk pace where you breathe faster but can still talk.
Swing your arms naturally and land heel first, rolling through to the toes.
Slow down for the last few minutes to cool down.

name: Walking High Knees Lunge
desc: A walking lunge with a knee lift between steps: drive the back knee up high before stepping into the next lunge. It works the legs and glutes, challenges balance and raises the heart rate.
ins: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or ready to swing.
Step forward with your right foot and lower into a lunge until both knees are bent about 90 degrees.
Push through the right heel to stand up and drive your left knee up to hip height.
Pause briefly in balance, then step the left foot forward into the next lunge.
Keep your chest up and front knee over the ankle, and breathe out as you rise.

name: Walking Lunge
desc: A bodyweight lunge where each step carries you forward across the floor. It builds the glutes and quads, works the hamstrings and calves, and challenges balance as you move.
ins: Stand tall with feet together and hands on your hips or at your sides.
Take a long step forward with your right foot.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees and the back knee hovers just above the floor.
Keep your chest up and your front knee in line with your toes.
Push through the front heel and bring the back foot forward straight into the next step.
Keep alternating legs as you walk forward.

name: Walking On Incline Treadmill
desc: Walking on a treadmill set to an uphill incline. It raises the heart rate like a light jog while working the glutes, hamstrings and calves with low impact.
ins: Step onto the treadmill and start walking at a slow speed on a flat setting.
Raise the incline gradually to a level that makes you breathe harder.
Stand tall, lean only slightly forward from the ankles, and take full steps.
Let your arms swing naturally instead of holding the rails.
Keep a steady pace for your planned time, then lower the incline and speed to cool down.

name: Walking On Stepmill
desc: Climbing on a stepmill, a machine with a moving staircase. It is demanding cardio that strongly works the glutes, thighs and calves.
ins: Hold the side rails and step onto the stairs, then start at a slow speed.
Stand upright and place your whole foot on each step.
Push through the heel and midfoot to climb, letting your glutes and thighs do the work.
Use the rails only for light balance; do not lean on them or hang your weight off them.
Raise the speed gradually and keep your breathing steady.
Slow down for the last minutes before stopping and stepping off.

name: Wall Ball
desc: A full squat with a medicine ball held at your chest, finished by throwing the ball up to a target on the wall and catching it into the next squat. A HYROX and CrossFit staple that works the quads, glutes and shoulders and drives your heart rate up.
ins: Stand about an arm's length from the wall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the medicine ball at your chest with both hands under it and elbows down.
Brace your stomach and squat until your hips are below your knees, keeping your chest up and the ball close.
Drive up hard through your whole foot and, as your legs straighten, push the ball up and slightly forward with both arms.
Throw it to hit the target (in HYROX about 3 m for men and 2.7 m for women).
Catch the ball at your chest as it comes down and sink straight into the next squat.
Breathe out on each throw and keep a steady rhythm for the set number of reps.

name: Weighted Bench Dip
desc: A bench dip with a weight plate resting on your lap to add resistance. It builds triceps strength once bodyweight bench dips become easy.
ins: Sit on the edge of a bench with your hands beside your hips and walk your feet out, legs straight or slightly bent.
Have a partner place a weight plate on your thighs, or set it there before you slide off the bench.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your hips, keeping your back close to the bench.
Stop when your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight, keeping the plate steady.

name: Weighted Close Grip Chin-Up On Dip Cage
desc: An advanced close-grip chin-up with added weight, done on the pull-up handles of a dip station. It builds strength in the lats and biceps.
ins: Attach a weight to a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Hang from the pull-up handles of the dip cage with your hands close together and palms facing you.
Pull your shoulders down and tighten your stomach to keep the weight still.
Breathe out and pull until your chin is above the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang without letting the weight swing.

name: Weighted Cossack Squats
desc: A wide-stance side-to-side squat holding a weight at your chest, sitting deep over one leg while the other stays straight. It builds the glutes and quads and improves inner-thigh and hip mobility.
ins: Stand with your feet very wide, toes slightly out, holding a weight against your chest.
Shift your weight to the right and bend the right knee, sitting your hips back and down.
Keep the left leg straight and let its toes point up as you go deeper.
Keep your right heel flat and your chest up at the bottom.
Breathe out and push through the right foot to come back to the middle.
Repeat to the left side and keep alternating.

name: Weighted Crunch
desc: A floor crunch done while holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your chest to make the abs work harder. The obliques assist.
ins: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a weight plate or dumbbell on your chest.
Brace your abs and tuck your chin slightly.
Breathe out and curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly.
Increase the weight only when you can keep the curl smooth.

name: Weighted Crunch (behind Head)
desc: A crunch with a light weight plate held behind your head to add load. It targets the abs, while the upper back and shoulders work to hold the plate steady.
ins: Lie on your back on a mat or flat bench with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a light plate behind your head with both hands, elbows pointing slightly forward.
Tighten your abs and breathe out as you curl your shoulder blades off the surface, moving your ribs toward your hips.
Keep your chin slightly tucked and let your abs lift the weight, not your arms.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your shoulder blades touch down.

name: Weighted Decline Sit-Up
desc: A sit-up on a decline bench while holding a weight plate at your chest, making it one of the harder sit-up variations. It builds strong abs, with the hip flexors and lower back working too.
ins: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back, holding a plate flat against your chest.
Tighten your abs and tuck your chin slightly.
Breathe out and curl up until your chest is close to your thighs, keeping the plate pressed to your chest.
Pause briefly at the top without jerking.
Breathe in and lower slowly until your back is close to the bench, keeping tension in your abs.

name: Weighted Donkey Calf Raise
desc: The bent-over donkey calf raise with extra load, usually a weight hung from a dip belt or a plate on your lower back. It builds the calves with a long stretch under heavy resistance.
ins: Put on a dip belt with a plate attached, or have a partner place a weight on your lower back.
Stand on a step with the balls of your feet, heels hanging off.
Hinge forward and support your hands on a bench in front of you, back flat.
Lower your heels into a deep stretch.
Breathe out and rise onto your toes as high as you can, then squeeze.
Breathe in and lower slowly without rounding your back.

name: Weighted Drop Push Up
desc: An advanced plyometric push-up done with added weight, such as a vest: you drop your hands from two low platforms to the floor, absorb the landing and push explosively back up onto the platforms.
ins: Put on a weight vest and set two low steps or plates just wider than shoulder-width apart.
Start in a push-up position with your hands on the platforms and your body straight.
Lift your hands off the platforms and drop them to the floor between them.
Land with soft elbows and let your chest sink into a push-up to absorb the drop.
Push explosively so your hands rise high enough to land back on the platforms.
Rest between reps if needed to keep every rep fast and controlled.

name: Weighted Front Plank
desc: A forearm plank with a weight plate resting on your upper back to make the hold harder. It builds abdominal endurance, with the shoulders and lower back working to keep you straight.
ins: Get into a forearm plank with your elbows under your shoulders and your feet about hip-width apart.
Have a partner place a plate across your upper back, between your shoulder blades.
Tighten your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Hold the position without letting your hips sag or rise, breathing steadily.
When time is up, have the plate removed before you lower your knees to the floor.

name: Weighted Front Raise
desc: A front raise holding a weight plate with both hands. It works the front shoulders and your grip at the same time.
ins: Stand tall and hold a weight plate by the sides with both hands in front of your thighs.
Brace your stomach and keep your elbows slightly bent.
Breathe out and raise the plate in front of you to eye level.
Pause briefly without leaning back.
Breathe in and lower the plate slowly.

name: Weighted Hanging Leg-Hip Raise
desc: A hanging leg raise with extra weight held between your feet or strapped to your ankles, finishing by curling your hips up. It is a demanding move for the abs, with the hip flexors and lower back also working.
ins: Hold a light dumbbell between your feet or wear ankle weights, then grab a pull-up bar with palms facing away, hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
Hang with straight arms, draw your shoulders slightly down and stop any swinging.
Tighten your abs and raise your legs in front of you until they are at least level with the floor.
Keep going by tilting your hips up toward your chest, breathing out as you lift.
Lower your legs slowly under control so your body does not swing.

name: Weighted Hyperextension (on Stability Ball)
desc: A back extension done face down over a stability ball while holding a weight plate or dumbbell. It strengthens the lower back muscles along the spine, with the glutes and hamstrings helping, and the ball adds a balance challenge.
ins: Lie face down over a stability ball with it under your hips and stomach.
Press your feet against a wall or spread them wide for balance.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Let your upper body curl down over the ball, then lift it until your body is straight.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly.
Breathe out as you lift and in as you lower.

name: Weighted Kneeling Step With Swing
desc: A kneeling drill where you step one foot forward into a half kneel while swinging a weight from your hips up overhead with straight arms. It works the shoulders, triceps and core, along with balance.
ins: Kneel tall on a mat holding a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands in front of your hips.
Brace your stomach and keep your back straight.
Step one foot forward into a half kneel while swinging the weight up and overhead with straight arms.
Lower the weight back to your hips as you bring the foot back to kneeling.
Repeat with the other foot forward and keep alternating.

name: Weighted Lunge With Swing
desc: A forward lunge with an added swing: as you lower, the weight swings down beside the front knee, and as you stand it swings back up. It builds the glutes and legs and adds coordination and core control.
ins: Stand tall holding a dumbbell or kettlebell with both hands at chest height.
Step forward into a lunge with your right foot.
As you lower, swing the weight down and across to the outside of your right knee, keeping your back straight.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to stand, swinging the weight back up to your chest.
Repeat on the other leg, swinging to the outside of the left knee.

name: Weighted Lying Neck Extension (with Head Harness)
desc: A neck extension lying face down on a bench with a weight hung from a head harness. It strengthens the back of the neck and upper back.
ins: Put on a head harness with a light plate attached.
Lie face down on a flat bench with your head and neck past the end and your hands holding the bench.
Let your head lower slowly until your chin moves toward your chest.
Raise your head back up until you are looking forward, without arching the lower back.
Pause, then lower slowly; breathe out as you lift.
Start very light and stop if you feel any sharp pain.

name: Weighted Lying Neck Flexion (with Head Harness)
desc: A neck flexion lying on your back on a bench with a weight hung from a head harness. It trains the muscles on the front and sides of the neck.
ins: Fit the head harness and attach a light weight, then lie on your back on a flat bench with your head past the end.
Hold the weight or harness lightly with your hands to guide it as you settle in.
Let your head lower slowly back until it is in line with the bench.
Curl your chin toward your chest by lifting your head.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly; breathe out as you lift.
Keep your shoulders on the bench and use a very light load at first.

name: Weighted Lying Side Lifting Head (with Head Harness)
desc: A neck strengthening exercise where you lie on your side and raise your head sideways against a weight hung from a head harness. It builds the muscles on the side of the neck and the upper traps.
ins: Attach a light plate to a head harness and fit it snugly on your head.
Lie on your side on a flat bench with your head just past the end and the weight hanging toward the floor.
Hold the bench with your hands and keep your shoulders and hips stacked.
Breathe out and lift your head sideways toward your top shoulder until it lines up with your body.
Pause, then breathe in and lower slowly without twisting your head.
Finish the set, then turn over and work the other side.

name: Weighted Muscle Up
desc: An advanced muscle-up done with extra weight, moving from a hang below the bar to a support above it. It builds explosive pulling and pressing strength.
ins: Wear a dip belt or weighted vest with a light load you can control.
Hang from the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Pull explosively toward your lower chest, keeping your body tight.
As you reach the bar, lean forward and turn your elbows over it quickly.
Press up to straight arms above the bar and breathe out.
Lower under control back to a hang.

name: Weighted Muscle Up (on Bar)
desc: An advanced weighted muscle-up on a straight bar, taking you from a hang to a support above the bar with extra load. It builds explosive strength in the lats, arms and shoulders.
ins: Attach a light weight with a belt or vest and grip the bar overhand at shoulder width.
Start from a dead hang with your body tight.
Pull explosively, bringing the bar toward your hips while your body leans back slightly.
Lean your chest over the bar and turn your elbows over quickly.
Press to straight arms above the bar and breathe out.
Lower under control to the hang.

name: Weighted One Hand Pull Up
desc: An elite one-arm pull-up done with added weight. It demands very high lat, biceps and grip strength and should only be tried after mastering bodyweight one-arm pull-ups.
ins: Add a small weight with a belt or vest.
Hang from the bar with one hand, palm facing you or to the side, and your free arm by your side.
Pull your shoulder down and tighten your whole body to stop spinning.
Breathe out and pull until your chin clears the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Switch arms after each set.

name: Weighted Overhead Crunch (on Stability Ball)
desc: A crunch on a stability ball while holding a weight overhead with straight arms, which makes the abs work against a long lever. It trains the abs with the obliques and lower back stabilizing on the ball.
ins: Lie back on a stability ball with it under your middle back and your feet planted wide.
Hold a light plate or dumbbell with both hands and stretch your arms straight above your head.
Breathe out and curl up, keeping your arms in line with your ears as your shoulders lift.
Pause when your abs are fully tight.
Lower slowly back over the ball, keeping your arms straight.

name: Weighted Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up with extra weight hanging from a belt or held between the feet, for people who can already do many bodyweight reps. It builds strength in the lats, with the biceps and forearms working hard.
ins: Attach a weight to a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hang with straight arms and keep the weight still.
Pull up until your chin passes the bar, leading with your chest.
Lower slowly and with control to a full hang.
Breathe out on the way up and in on the way down.

name: Weighted Round Arm
desc: Arm circles done with light weights held out to the sides at shoulder height. Holding the arms up keeps the side shoulders working the whole time and builds endurance.
ins: Stand tall with a light weight in each hand.
Raise your arms out to the sides to shoulder height with your elbows almost straight.
Draw small, controlled circles forward with your hands.
After your set time or count, reverse the direction of the circles.
Keep your shoulders down, breathe steadily, and lower your arms when finished.

name: Weighted Russian Twist
desc: A Russian twist holding a plate or dumbbell, with your heels on the floor for a steadier base. It works the obliques and abs while the lower back keeps your spine long.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and heels down, holding a weight at your chest.
Lean back until your abs engage, keeping your back straight.
Rotate your shoulders to one side and bring the weight toward the floor beside your hip.
Turn back through the middle to the other side.
Move at a controlled pace and breathe out on each turn.

name: Weighted Russian Twist (legs Up)
desc: A weighted Russian twist done with your feet held off the floor, which makes balancing part of the challenge. It works the obliques and abs, with the hip flexors holding your legs up.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent, holding a weight plate or dumbbell at your chest.
Lean back with a straight spine and lift your feet off the floor.
Rotate your shoulders to the right and bring the weight beside your right hip.
Rotate through the middle to your left hip.
Keep your feet up and your legs steady while only your torso turns.

name: Weighted Russian Twist (No Floor Touch)
desc: A seated rotation holding a weight, done with your heels resting on the floor for a steadier base than the feet-up version. It works the obliques and the rest of the abs, with the lower back helping to hold your posture.
ins: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your heels on the ground, holding a plate, dumbbell or medicine ball at your chest.
Lean back slightly with a straight back until you feel your abs switch on.
Breathe out and turn your shoulders to one side, bringing the weight beside your hip.
Turn back through the center and over to the other side, moving the weight with your torso, not just your arms.
Keep your chest lifted and your knees still throughout the set.

name: Weighted Seated Bicep Curl (on Stability Ball)
desc: A biceps curl with a medicine ball done sitting on a stability ball. Balancing on the ball works your core while the biceps lift the weight.
ins: Sit on a stability ball with feet flat and wide for balance.
Hold a medicine ball in both hands with palms facing up, arms straight in front of your thighs.
Breathe out and curl the ball up toward your chest, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze the biceps at the top while sitting tall.
Breathe in and lower the ball slowly to straight arms.

name: Weighted Seated Neck Extension (with Head Harness)
desc: A seated neck extension where you lift your head back against a weight hanging from a head harness. It strengthens the muscles along the back of the neck and the upper traps.
ins: Fit a head harness with a light plate attached and sit on the end of a bench.
Lean your torso forward slightly and rest your hands on your knees, keeping your back flat.
Let your chin drop toward your chest so the weight hangs in front of you.
Breathe out and raise your head back until you are looking straight ahead or slightly up.
Pause, then breathe in and lower your chin slowly.
Move smoothly; never jerk the weight.

name: Weighted Seated Twist (on Stability Ball)
desc: A seated twist on a stability ball while holding a weight, where the unstable seat adds a balance challenge. It works the obliques and abs, with the lower back keeping you upright.
ins: Sit tall on a stability ball with your feet flat and wide on the floor.
Hold a light plate or dumbbell in both hands at chest height, arms slightly bent.
Brace your abs and rotate your shoulders to one side while your hips stay still on the ball.
Return to the middle and rotate to the other side.
Keep the movement slow so the ball stays steady under you.

name: Weighted Side Bend (on Stability Ball)
desc: A side crunch done lying sideways over a stability ball while holding a weight plate against your chest. It strengthens the obliques and the muscles along the lower back.
ins: Lie on your side over a stability ball with the ball under your hip and your feet staggered against a wall or the floor for balance.
Hold a weight plate flat against your chest with both hands.
Let your upper body drape down over the ball until you feel a stretch along your side.
Squeeze your side muscles to lift your shoulder up toward your hip, breathing out as you rise.
Pause briefly, then lower slowly back over the ball while breathing in.
Finish your set, then switch to the other side.

name: Weighted Sissy Squat
desc: A sissy squat holding a weight plate to your chest: you rise onto your toes, lean back and push your knees forward to lower. It puts intense, isolated work on the quads and needs strong, healthy knees.
ins: Stand with your feet hip-width apart next to a sturdy support, holding a plate against your chest with one arm and the support with the other hand.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Push your knees forward and lean your body back, keeping a straight line from your knees to your head.
Lower as far as you can control, until your knees are deeply bent and close to the floor.
Squeeze your quads to drive your knees back and return to standing on your toes.
Breathe in as you lower and out as you rise; start with body weight before adding a plate.

name: Weighted Squat
desc: A body-weight squat made harder with a weighted vest. Keeping your hands free lets you focus on squat form while the extra load builds the glutes and quads.
ins: Put on a weighted vest and fasten it snugly so it does not bounce.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out, arms out in front for balance.
Breathe in, brace and sit your hips back and down.
Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest up and heels flat.
Drive through your feet to stand up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Breathe out as you rise.

name: Weighted Standing Curl
desc: A standing curl holding a single weight plate with both hands. It trains the biceps and challenges your grip.
ins: Stand tall and hold a weight plate at its sides with both hands, palms facing in or slightly up, arms straight.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Breathe out and curl the plate up toward your chest.
Squeeze the biceps at the top without leaning back.
Breathe in and lower the plate slowly to straight arms.

name: Weighted Standing Hand Squeeze
desc: A grip-strength exercise where you squeeze a hand gripper as hard as you can and hold it closed. It trains the fingers and forearms for a stronger crushing grip.
ins: Stand tall and hold a hand gripper in one hand, arm relaxed at your side or bent in front of you.
Set the gripper deep in your palm with the handle across your fingers.
Breathe out and squeeze until the handles touch or as far as you can.
Hold the squeeze for 2 to 5 seconds.
Open your hand slowly under control.
Finish the set, then switch hands.

name: Weighted Standing Neck Extension (with Head Harness)
desc: A neck extension done standing and bent forward, with a weight hanging from a head harness. It strengthens the back of the neck, traps and upper back.
ins: Put on a head harness with a light weight attached.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bend forward at the hips, and rest your hands on your knees with a flat back.
Let your head drop slowly so your chin moves toward your chest.
Lift your head until it lines up with your spine or looks slightly ahead.
Pause, then lower slowly; keep your back still and breathe steadily.

name: Weighted Straight Bar Dip
desc: A dip on a single straight bar with extra weight hung from a belt or held between the legs. It is a heavy strength exercise for the chest, triceps and front shoulders.
ins: Attach a plate or dumbbell to a dip belt around your hips.
Grip the straight bar in front of you at shoulder-width and press up so you are supported on straight arms with the bar at your hips.
Lean your chest forward over the bar and bring your legs slightly forward for balance.
Breathe in and bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the bar under control.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms.
Step down carefully, and only add weight once bodyweight bar dips feel solid.

name: Weighted Stretch Lunge
desc: A deep forward lunge holding a weight, pausing at the bottom so the back hip gets a strong stretch. It builds the glutes and quads of the front leg and improves hip flexibility.
ins: Stand tall holding a dumbbell or weight plate in each hand or at your chest.
Take a long step forward with your right foot.
Lower until your back knee is just above the floor and sink your hips slightly forward to feel a stretch at the front of the back hip.
Hold the bottom for two seconds, breathing steadily, with your chest up.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs each rep.

name: Weighted Svend Press
desc: A standing chest exercise where you squeeze a weight plate between your palms and press it straight out from your chest. Constant inward pressure keeps the inner chest working hard.
ins: Stand tall and hold a weight plate between your flat palms in front of your chest, fingers pointing forward.
Squeeze your palms together as hard as you can.
Press the plate straight out in front of you until your arms are almost straight.
Bring it slowly back to your chest while keeping the squeeze.
Breathe out as you press and keep your shoulders down away from your ears.

name: Weighted Three Bench Dips
desc: The three-bench dip with a weight plate resting on your lap. The added load makes it a heavy triceps builder for people who can already do many bodyweight reps.
ins: Set two benches side by side for your hands and a third in front for your heels.
Get into position with legs straight, then have a partner place a plate on your thighs, or set it there yourself.
Bend your elbows straight back and lower your body until your elbows reach about a right angle.
Keep the plate steady and your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight.

name: Weighted Tricep Dips
desc: A dip on parallel bars with extra weight hung from a belt or held between your feet. Keeping your torso upright focuses the work on the triceps, with the chest and shoulders helping.
ins: Attach a weight to a dip belt or hold a dumbbell between your feet.
Grab the bars and lift yourself up with your arms straight and your body upright.
Breathe in and sink down, bending at the elbows, until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Keep your elbows pointing back and your shoulders down.
Breathe out and press up until your arms are straight.

name: Weighted Triceps Dip On High Parallel Bars
desc: A weighted dip on high parallel bars where your feet hang well clear of the floor. The extra load and full hang make it a demanding triceps exercise that also works the chest and shoulders.
ins: Fasten a weight to a dip belt, step up and grab the high bars.
Support yourself with straight arms, legs hanging and knees slightly bent or crossed.
Breathe in and lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about level with the floor.
Keep your torso upright and avoid swinging the weight.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms.

name: Wheel Run
desc: An advanced ab wheel rollout done from the feet, rolling the wheel far out in front and pulling it back. It hammers the core and also loads the shoulders and arms.
ins: Stand with feet hip-width apart, bend down and place both hands on the ab wheel in front of your feet.
Tighten your stomach and glutes so your back stays flat.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, letting your body lower toward the floor as your arms reach out.
Go only as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull the wheel back toward your feet using your core, breathing out as you return.
Beginners can build up to this by starting from the knees.

name: Wide Grip Pull-Up
desc: A pull-up with the hands placed wide on the bar. The wide grip shifts most of the work onto the lats and gives the back a broader look.
ins: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip clearly wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulders down and tighten your stomach.
Breathe out and pull your chest toward the bar until your chin is above it.
Think about driving your elbows down to your sides.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.

name: Wide Grip Rear Pull-Up
desc: An advanced pull-up with a wide overhand grip where you pull the bar behind your head. It works the lats and upper back hard but needs good shoulder mobility.
ins: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip well wider than your shoulders.
Lean your head slightly forward and set your shoulders down.
Pull yourself up until the bar is behind your head at about the base of your neck.
Breathe out at the top and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
Switch to front pull-ups if you feel any pinching in your shoulders.

name: Wide Hand Push Up
desc: A push-up with the hands placed well outside shoulder-width. The wider position puts more stretch and work on the chest and less on the triceps.
ins: Place your hands on the floor about one and a half times shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward or slightly out.
Step your feet back so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Breathe in and lower your chest toward the floor, letting your elbows travel out to the sides.
Stop when your chest is a few centimeters above the floor.
Breathe out and press back up, keeping your hips from sagging.

name: Wide-Grip Chest Dip On High Parallel Bars
desc: A chest-focused dip on high parallel bars set wider than usual. The wide grip and forward lean put a big stretch and load on the chest, with the triceps and shoulders helping.
ins: Grip high parallel bars that are wider than your shoulders and lift yourself to straight arms with your feet off the floor.
Bend your knees, let your feet drift back and lean your chest forward.
Breathe in and lower yourself by bending your elbows, letting them point out to the sides.
Go down until you feel a deep stretch in your chest, without letting your shoulders roll forward.
Breathe out and press back up to straight arms, keeping the forward lean.

name: Wind Sprints
desc: Short, all-out runs over a set distance with easy recovery in between. They build speed and conditioning, working the legs hard while your core keeps your body stable.
ins: Mark a straight stretch of about 30 to 50 meters on a track, field or other open space.
Warm up first with a few minutes of easy jogging.
Start with one foot in front of the other, lean forward slightly and drive off hard.
Run at full effort, pumping your arms and staying tall with your abs tight.
Slow down gradually after the line, then walk back to the start to recover.
Start the next sprint once your breathing has settled.

name: World Greatest Stretch
desc: A flowing mobility drill that combines a deep lunge, an elbow drop, an upper-body twist and a hamstring stretch. It loosens the hips, hamstrings, glutes and quads in one move and makes a great warm-up.
ins: Step your right foot forward into a long lunge and put both hands on the floor inside the right foot.
Keep the back leg straight and drop your right elbow toward the inside of your right ankle.
Place the right hand back down, then rotate your chest open and reach your right arm to the ceiling.
Bring the hand down, shift your hips back and straighten the front leg, pulling the toes up.
Return to the lunge, step back to standing and repeat on the other side, breathing steadily.

name: Wrist Circles
desc: A simple mobility drill that rolls the wrists through slow circles. It warms up the wrists and hands before lifting, push-ups or typing.
ins: Stand or sit and hold your arms out in front of you, elbows straight or slightly bent.
Make loose fists or keep your fingers relaxed.
Slowly turn your hands in large circles in one direction, moving only at the wrists.
After 10 to 15 circles, switch to the other direction.
Keep the movement smooth and stay inside a pain-free range.

name: Wrist Rollerer
desc: A forearm builder where you wind a weight up and down on a cord attached to a handle. It works both sides of the forearm and the grip with a long, steady burn.
ins: Stand tall holding the wrist roller with both hands, palms down, arms straight out in front at shoulder height.
Let the weight hang at the end of the cord near the floor.
Turn the handle by rolling one wrist forward, then the other, to wind the weight up.
Keep your arms straight and your shoulders down while you roll.
When the weight reaches the handle, unwind it slowly the same way.
Breathe steadily; try palms-up rolling on another set.

name: Zigzag Hops
desc: Quick diagonal hops forward in a zigzag pattern, often around cones or over a line. It builds springy calves, leg power and side-to-side control.
ins: Set up a line or a row of cones and stand to one side of it with knees slightly bent.
Hop diagonally forward across the line, landing on the balls of both feet.
Land softly, bending the ankles, knees and hips, with knees over the toes.
Bounce straight into the next diagonal hop back across the line.
Swing your arms for rhythm, keep hops low and quick, and breathe steadily.
Walk back to the start and rest before the next round.
